questions.question_text: A transformer steps up \( 220 \, \text{V} \) to \( 440 \, \text{V} \). If the primary current is \( 10 \, \text{A} \), what is the secondary current?
questions.explanation: Power input = Power output: \( V_p I_p = V_s I_s \). \( I_s = \frac{V_p I_p}{V_s} = \frac{220 \times 10}{440} = 5 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: What is the behavior of the impedance in a series LCR circuit at very high frequencies?
questions.explanation: At very high frequencies, \( X_L = \omega L \) becomes very large, while \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \) becomes very small. The impedance \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} \) is dominated by \( X_L \), making the circuit behave as predominantly inductive.

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with only an inductor, what is the instantaneous power when the current is at its maximum?
questions.explanation: In a purely inductive circuit, current lags voltage by 90°. When the current is at its maximum, the voltage is zero (since voltage leads by 90°), making the instantaneous power (\( P = V I \)) zero at that instant.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 550 \), \( N_s = 1100 \). If \( V_p = 110 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 110 \times \frac{1100}{550} = 220 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 100 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 130 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 70 \, \Omega \) has a \( 300 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the power dissipated?
A \( 85 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 85 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.085 = 26.69 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{230}{26.69} \approx 8.62 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 8.62 \approx 12.19 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: In a series LCR circuit, under what condition does the circuit behave as if it has only resistance?
options: When inductive and capacitive reactances are equal
questions.explanation: In a series LCR circuit, the circuit behaves as purely resistive at resonance, where the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance (\( X_L = X_C \)). This cancels the reactive components, leaving only the resistance to determine the impedance.

questions.question_text: A \( 254.6 \, \text{V} \) (peak) AC source is connected to a \( 90 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{254.6}{1.414} \approx 180 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{180}{90} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 90 = 360 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 60 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 60 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.06 = 18.84 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{220}{18.84} \approx 11.68 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: In a series LCR circuit at resonance, what is the relationship between the inductive and capacitive reactances?
questions.explanation: At resonance in a series LCR circuit, the inductive reactance (\( X_L \)) equals the capacitive reactance (\( X_C \)). This balance cancels out the reactive components, making the impedance purely resistive and maximizing the current.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 80 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 100 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 40 \, \Omega \) has a \( 240 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the power dissipated?
A \( 45 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 45 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 45 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 59 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{110}{59} \approx 1.864 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 1.864 \approx 2.64 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: What happens to the average power dissipated in an AC circuit with only a capacitor over one complete cycle?
options: It is half of the peak power
questions.explanation: In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the current leads the voltage by 90°. The instantaneous power alternates between positive and negative, and over a complete cycle, these values cancel out, resulting in zero average power dissipation. The capacitor stores and releases energy without dissipating it as heat.

questions.question_text: A \( 15 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 15 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 15 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 177 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{110}{177} \approx 0.621 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with only a resistor, how does the current behave relative to the applied voltage?
options: It is in phase with the voltage
It is 180° out of phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: In a purely resistive AC circuit, the current and voltage oscillate in phase, meaning they reach their peak, zero, and minimum values simultaneously. This occurs because a resistor does not introduce any phase shift between voltage and current.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 300 \), \( N_s = 150 \). If \( V_s = 120 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the primary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_p = V_s \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} = 120 \times \frac{300}{150} = 240 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: What is the significance of the rms value in specifying AC quantities?
options: It represents the equivalent DC value for power
questions.explanation: The rms (root mean square) value of an AC quantity (e.g., voltage or current) is the equivalent DC value that produces the same average power in a resistive load. It accounts for the time-varying nature of AC, making it a standard measure for power calculations.

questions.question_text: A \( 200 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source supplies a \( 80 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{200}{80} = 2.5 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 2.5 \approx 3.535 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 70 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi f \). \( f = 50 \, \text{Hz} \), \( L = 70 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( \omega = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.07 = 21.98 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A \( 226.3 \, \text{V} \) (peak) AC source is connected to a \( 80 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{226.3}{1.414} \approx 160 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{160}{80} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 80 = 320 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 12 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 12 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 12 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 265.3 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: In a step-up transformer, how does the current in the secondary coil compare to the primary coil, assuming ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: In an ideal step-up transformer (where \( V_s > V_p \) and \( N_s > N_p \)), power is conserved (\( V_p I_p = V_s I_s \)). Since the secondary voltage is higher, the secondary current must be lower than the primary current (\( I_s = I_p \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} \)), where \( \frac{N_p}{N_s} < 1 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 55 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 55 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.055 = 17.27 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{230}{17.27} \approx 13.32 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 150 \, \Omega \) resistor is connected to a \( 300 \, \text{V} \) (peak) AC supply. What is the rms current in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Peak voltage: \( v_m = 300 \, \text{V} \). RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{300}{1.414} \approx 212.1 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{212.1}{150} \approx 1.414 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 160 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source supplies a \( 80 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{160}{80} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 80 = 320 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 120 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi f \). \( f = 50 \, \text{Hz} \), \( L = 120 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( \omega = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.12 = 37.68 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( L = 3.5 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 8 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
questions.explanation: \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L C}} \). \( L = 3.5 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 8 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3.5 \times 8 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{28 \times 10^{-6}}} \approx 188.98 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the current leads the voltage by what phase angle?
questions.explanation: For a capacitor, \( i = i_m \sin (\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}) \), \( v = v_m \sin \omega t \). Phase difference: \( \phi = \frac{\pi}{2} \), so current leads voltage by \( 90^\circ \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 40 \, \Omega \), \( L = 5 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 80 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant frequency in Hz?
questions.explanation: \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L C}} \). \( L = 5 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 80 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5 \times 80 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 \times 10^{-4}}} = 50 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( f_0 = \frac{50}{2 \times 3.14} \approx 7.96 \, \text{Hz} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with a series combination of resistor, inductor, and capacitor, what is the condition for the circuit to be purely resistive?
options: When inductive and capacitive reactances cancel
questions.explanation: For an LCR series circuit to be purely resistive, the net reactance must be zero (\( X_L - X_C = 0 \)), which occurs at resonance when \( X_L = X_C \). This makes the impedance equal to the resistance (\( Z = R \)), and the circuit behaves as if only resistance is present.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 400 \), \( N_s = 800 \). If \( V_p = 120 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 120 \times \frac{800}{400} = 240 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 100 \, \Omega \) resistor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC supply. What is the average power consumed?
In an AC circuit with only a capacitor, why does the current lead the voltage?
options: Because current charges the capacitor before voltage builds
questions.explanation: In a capacitor, current flows to charge or discharge the plates before the voltage across it changes. This causes the current to reach its maximum 90° ahead of the voltage, as the voltage builds up after the current starts flowing.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 40 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 50 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 30 \, \Omega \) has a \( 120 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the power dissipated?
A \( 60 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 40 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the impedance?
A \( 14 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 14 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 14 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 227.5 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{230}{227.5} \approx 1.01 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 100 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 50 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the impedance?
A \( 9 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 9 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 9 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 353.7 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 400 \), \( N_s = 800 \). If \( V_p = 120 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 120 \times \frac{800}{400} = 240 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: In a series LCR circuit, what happens to the total voltage across the inductor and capacitor at resonance?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( X_L = X_C \), and the voltages across the inductor (\( V_L = I X_L \)) and capacitor (\( V_C = I X_C \)) are equal in magnitude but 180° out of phase. Thus, they cancel each other, making the net voltage across the LC combination zero.

questions.question_text: A \( 70 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 70 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.07 = 26.38 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{230}{26.38} \approx 8.72 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 8.72 \approx 12.33 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 20 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 35 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 55 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{55 - 35}{20} = 1 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A transformer steps down \( 440 \, \text{V} \) to \( 220 \, \text{V} \). If the secondary current is \( 8 \, \text{A} \), what is the primary current?
questions.explanation: \( V_p I_p = V_s I_s \). \( I_p = \frac{V_s I_s}{V_p} = \frac{220 \times 8}{440} = 4 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: An AC source provides a peak voltage of \( 424.2 \, \text{V} \) to a \( 200 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{424.2}{1.414} = 300 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{300}{200} = 1.5 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = (1.5)^2 \times 200 = 2.25 \times 200 = 450 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 27 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 27 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 27 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 117.8 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{220}{117.8} \approx 1.867 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 25 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 25 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 25 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 106.2 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{110}{106.2} \approx 1.036 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 40 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 60 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 20 \, \Omega \). What is the power factor?
A \( 10 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC supply. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 10 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 265.4 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{110}{265.4} \approx 0.414 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 0.414 \approx 0.585 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 85 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi f \). \( f = 50 \, \text{Hz} \), \( L = 85 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( \omega = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.085 = 26.69 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 110 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 90 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 70 \, \Omega \). What is the impedance?
In an AC circuit with a series combination of resistor and capacitor, what happens to the phase difference if the frequency approaches infinity?
questions.explanation: In an RC series circuit, \( \phi = \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{X_C}{R} \right) \), where \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \). As frequency (\( \omega \)) approaches infinity, \( X_C \) approaches zero, making \( \phi \) approach 0°, so the circuit becomes nearly resistive.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 25 \, \Omega \) is at resonance with a \( 200 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( Z = R = 25 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{200}{25} = 8 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 18 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 18 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 18 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 147.3 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{110}{147.3} \approx 0.747 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 100 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 80 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 60 \, \Omega \). What is the impedance?
A \( 30 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 30 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 30 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 106.1 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{220}{106.1} \approx 2.074 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 2.074 \approx 2.93 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: What is the effect on the power factor of an LCR series circuit when the frequency is decreased below resonance?
questions.explanation: Below resonance, \( X_C > X_L \), making the circuit capacitive. The phase angle \( \phi = \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} \right) \) is positive, and the power factor \( \cos \phi \) decreases (less than 1) as the circuit becomes less resistive.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 100 \) and \( N_s = 200 \). If the primary voltage is \( 220 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 220 \times \frac{200}{100} = 440 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 50 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), where \( \omega = 2\pi f \). \( f = 60 \, \text{Hz} \), \( L = 50 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( \omega = 2 \times 3.14 \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.05 = 18.84 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: What is the average power dissipated in a purely capacitive circuit over one complete cycle?
questions.explanation: Power: \( p_C = i v = i_m v_m \cos (\omega t) \sin (\omega t) = \frac{i_m v_m}{2} \sin (2\omega t) \). Average over a cycle: \( P_C = \frac{i_m v_m}{2} \langle \sin (2\omega t) \rangle = 0 \), since \( \langle \sin (2\omega t) \rangle = 0 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 80 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 80 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.08 = 30.14 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{230}{30.14} \approx 7.63 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with a resistor and inductor in series, what happens to the power factor if the inductance is increased?
questions.explanation: In an RL series circuit, power factor \( \cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} \), where \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} \) and \( X_L = \omega L \). Increasing inductance increases \( X_L \), which increases \( Z \), reducing \( \cos \phi \) (closer to 0), as the circuit becomes more inductive.

questions.question_text: A \( 8 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 8 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 8 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 331.6 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: What happens to the current in a purely inductive AC circuit when the frequency of the source decreases?
questions.explanation: In a purely inductive circuit, \( X_L = \omega L \), and current \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} \). Decreasing frequency reduces \( \omega \), lowering \( X_L \), which increases the current since \( I \) is inversely proportional to \( X_L \).

questions.question_text: A sinusoidal voltage of peak value \( 283 \, \text{V} \) is applied to a \( 5 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{283}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 200 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{200}{5} = 40 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: What is the key requirement for an AC circuit to exhibit resonance?
options: Presence of both inductance and capacitance
questions.explanation: Resonance in an AC circuit requires both inductance and capacitance to be present (e.g., in an LCR circuit). This allows the inductive and capacitive reactances to balance at a specific frequency, a condition not possible with only one reactive component.

questions.question_text: A \( 15 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 15 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 15 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 212 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A \( 55 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 55 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.055 = 20.72 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{110}{20.72} \approx 5.31 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 5.31 \approx 7.51 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: What is the role of a capacitor in improving the power factor of an AC circuit with an inductive load?
questions.explanation: An inductive load causes the current to lag the voltage, reducing the power factor. Adding a capacitor in parallel introduces a leading current that counteracts the lagging current, bringing the net phase difference closer to zero, thus improving the power factor.

questions.question_text: A \( 90 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 90 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.09 = 33.91 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{220}{33.91} \approx 6.49 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( L = 4 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 10 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
questions.explanation: \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L C}} \). \( L = 4 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 10 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 \times 10^{-5}}} \approx 158.1 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the physical significance of the term "wattless current" in an AC circuit?
options: It is the current with maximum power
It is the current in a resistive circuit
It is the current that heats the circuit
It is the current that does not contribute to average power
questions.explanation: "Wattless current" refers to the component of current in a purely reactive (inductive or capacitive) AC circuit that is 90° out of phase with the voltage. It does not contribute to average power dissipation, as power is zero when \( \cos 90° = 0 \), hence "wattless."

questions.question_text: A \( 90 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi f \). \( f = 50 \, \text{Hz} \), \( L = 90 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( \omega = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.09 = 28.26 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( L = 8 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 5 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
questions.explanation: \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L C}} \). \( L = 8 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{8 \times 5 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{40 \times 10^{-6}}} \approx 158.1 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 40 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 65 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 25 \, \Omega \). What is the power factor?
A \( 40 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 40 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 40 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 79.6 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A \( 16 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 16 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 16 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 199 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{230}{199} \approx 1.156 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 1.156 \approx 1.63 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 95 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi f \). \( f = 50 \, \text{Hz} \), \( L = 95 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( \omega = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.095 = 29.83 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 30 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 50 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 20 \, \Omega \). What is the power factor?
questions.explanation: \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{30^2 + (50 - 20)^2} = \sqrt{900 + 900} = \sqrt{1800} \approx 42.43 \, \Omega \). Power factor: \( \cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{30}{42.43} \approx 0.707 \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 30 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 40 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 60 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{60 - 40}{30} = \frac{20}{30} = 0.667 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(0.667) \approx 33.7^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 90 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 70 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 50 \, \Omega \). What is the impedance?
In an AC circuit with only an inductor, what is the phase relationship between the current and the voltage?
options: Current is in phase with voltage
Current is 180° out of phase with voltage
questions.explanation: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current lags the voltage by 90°. This is because the inductor opposes changes in current, causing the current to reach its peak after the voltage.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 500 \), \( N_s = 250 \). If \( V_s = 120 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the primary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_p = V_s \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} = 120 \times \frac{500}{250} = 240 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 60 \, \Omega \) is at resonance with a \( 240 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( Z = R = 60 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{240}{60} = 4 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 800 \), \( N_s = 400 \). If \( V_s = 110 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the primary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_p = V_s \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} = 110 \times \frac{800}{400} = 220 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 70 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 30 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the impedance?
A \( 230 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source supplies a \( 115 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{230}{115} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 2 \approx 2.828 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 22 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 22 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 22 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 144.7 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{220}{144.7} \approx 1.52 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 35 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 60 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 25 \, \Omega \). What is the power factor?
questions.explanation: \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{35^2 + (60 - 25)^2} = \sqrt{1225 + 1225} = \sqrt{2450} \approx 49.5 \, \Omega \). Power factor: \( \cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{35}{49.5} \approx 0.707 \).

questions.question_text: In an LCR series circuit, what happens to the circuit’s behavior when the frequency is significantly above the resonant frequency?
questions.explanation: Above resonance, \( X_L = \omega L \) becomes much larger than \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), making the net reactance positive. The circuit behaves as predominantly inductive, with the current lagging the voltage.

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with only a capacitor, what happens to the impedance if the capacitance is decreased?
questions.explanation: In a purely capacitive circuit, impedance is \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \). Decreasing capacitance (\( C \)) increases \( X_C \) because they are inversely proportional, thus increasing the impedance.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 450 \), \( N_s = 900 \). If \( V_p = 120 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 120 \times \frac{900}{450} = 240 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 65 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 65 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.065 = 24.49 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{110}{24.49} \approx 4.49 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 21 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 21 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 21 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 151.6 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{230}{151.6} \approx 1.517 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 100 \, \text{W} \) bulb is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC supply. What is the resistance of the bulb?
A series LCR circuit has \( L = 2 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 50 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
questions.explanation: Resonant frequency: \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L C}} \). \( L = 2 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 50 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-4}}} = 100 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 130 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 110 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 90 \, \Omega \). What is the impedance?
A \( 80 \, \Omega \) resistor is connected to a \( 160 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} \). Given: \( V = 160 \, \text{V} \), \( R = 80 \, \Omega \). \( I = \frac{160}{80} = 2 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: In a series LCR circuit at resonance, the power dissipated is \( 4800 \, \text{W} \) with \( R = 3 \, \Omega \). What is the rms current?
What is the primary reason AC voltage is preferred over DC voltage for long-distance power transmission?
options: It can be transformed to different voltages easily
questions.explanation: AC voltage is preferred for long-distance power transmission because it can be easily stepped up or down using transformers. This allows for high-voltage transmission to reduce energy losses due to resistance, followed by stepping down to safer levels for distribution.

questions.question_text: Why does an AC circuit with only an inductor exhibit a "wattless" current?
options: Because the inductor has high resistance
questions.explanation: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current lags the voltage by 90°. The power factor (\( \cos 90^\circ = 0 \)) is zero, meaning no average power is dissipated; the current is "wattless" because it only stores and releases energy without consuming it.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 50 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 30 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 20 \, \Omega \) is connected to an AC source. What is the impedance?
A series LCR circuit has \( R = 35 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 55 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 75 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{75 - 55}{35} = \frac{20}{35} \approx 0.571 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(0.571) \approx 29.74^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A \( 30 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 30 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 30 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 106.1 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{230}{106.1} \approx 2.17 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 210 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source supplies a \( 105 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{210}{105} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 2 \approx 2.828 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 65 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 65 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.065 = 20.41 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{230}{20.41} \approx 11.27 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 11.27 \approx 15.94 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 350 \), \( N_s = 700 \). If \( V_s = 420 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the primary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_p = V_s \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} = 420 \times \frac{350}{700} = 210 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: What is the condition for maximum power dissipation in a series LCR circuit?
options: When the circuit is at resonance
questions.explanation: Maximum power dissipation in a series LCR circuit occurs at resonance, where \( X_L = X_C \), making the impedance equal to the resistance (\( Z = R \)). At this point, the power factor (\( \cos \phi \)) is 1, and power (\( P = I^2 R \)) is maximized.

questions.question_text: Why does the current amplitude in a series LCR circuit peak at the resonant frequency?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( X_L = X_C \), so the impedance \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} \) reduces to \( R \), the minimum possible value. Since \( I = \frac{V}{Z} \), the current amplitude peaks when \( Z \) is minimized.

questions.question_text: A \( 20 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC supply. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 20 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 20 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 159.2 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{220}{159.2} \approx 1.38 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 19 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 19 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 19 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 167.5 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{220}{167.5} \approx 1.313 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: Why does the voltage across an inductor in a series LCR circuit potentially exceed the source voltage at resonance?
questions.explanation: At resonance, current is maximized (\( I = \frac{V}{R} \)), and the voltage across the inductor (\( V_L = I X_L \)) can exceed the source voltage if \( X_L > R \). This is possible because \( V_L \) and \( V_C \) are out of phase with the source voltage, and their vector sum with \( V_R \) equals the source voltage.

questions.question_text: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current lags the voltage by what phase angle?
questions.explanation: For a pure inductor, \( i = i_m \sin (\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2}) \), while \( v = v_m \sin \omega t \). Phase difference: \( \phi = -\frac{\pi}{2} \), meaning current lags voltage by \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) or \( 90^\circ \).

questions.question_text: Why does the voltage across the inductor in a series LCR circuit equal the voltage across the capacitor at resonance, despite their phase difference?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( X_L = X_C \), and since \( V_L = I X_L \) and \( V_C = I X_C \) with the same current \( I \), their magnitudes are equal. However, they are 180° out of phase, so their vector sum is zero, not their magnitudes.

questions.question_text: In a series LCR circuit, why does resonance not occur if either the inductor or capacitor is absent?
options: Because there’s no balancing of reactive components
questions.explanation: Resonance in a series LCR circuit requires both an inductor and capacitor to create a condition where \( X_L = X_C \), canceling the reactive components. Without either, there’s no opposing reactance to balance, preventing resonance.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 15 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 25 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 40 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{40 - 25}{15} = 1 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 90 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 120 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 60 \, \Omega \) has a \( 270 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the power dissipated?
A \( 100 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi f \). \( f = 50 \, \text{Hz} \), \( L = 100 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( \omega = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.1 = 31.4 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 10 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 15 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 5 \, \Omega \). What is the power factor?
A \( 35 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 35 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.035 = 13.19 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{110}{13.19} \approx 8.34 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 198.1 \, \text{V} \) (peak) AC source is connected to a \( 70 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{198.1}{1.414} \approx 140 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{140}{70} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 70 = 280 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 50 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 50 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 63.7 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{220}{63.7} \approx 3.45 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 3.45 \approx 4.88 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 20 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 40 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 60 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{60 - 40}{20} = 1 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 50 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 80 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 60 \, \Omega \). What is the power factor?
questions.explanation: \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{50^2 + (80 - 60)^2} = \sqrt{2500 + 400} = \sqrt{2900} \approx 53.85 \, \Omega \). Power factor: \( \cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{50}{53.85} \approx 0.928 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 20 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 20 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 20 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 159.2 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{230}{159.2} \approx 1.445 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 1.445 \approx 2.04 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: What is the role of resonance in the operation of a radio receiver?
questions.explanation: In a radio receiver, resonance in an LCR circuit is used to tune to a specific frequency. By adjusting the capacitance or inductance, the circuit’s resonant frequency matches the desired station’s signal, amplifying it while filtering out others.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( L = 5 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 20 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
A \( 180 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source supplies a \( 90 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{180}{90} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 2 \approx 2.828 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a purely capacitive AC circuit not dissipate power despite having current flow?
options: Because energy is stored and returned without loss
questions.explanation: In a purely capacitive circuit, the current leads the voltage by 90°. The instantaneous power oscillates, but the average power over a cycle is zero because the energy is stored during one half-cycle and returned during the other, with no net dissipation.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 50 \, \Omega \) is at resonance with a \( 230 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( Z = R = 50 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{230}{50} = 4.6 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with only a capacitor, what is the nature of the current when the voltage is at its peak?
options: It is in phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: In a purely capacitive circuit, the current leads the voltage by 90°. When the voltage is at its peak (maximum positive or negative), the current is zero because it reaches its peak 90° earlier and crosses zero at the voltage peak.

questions.question_text: A \( 212.1 \, \text{V} \) (peak) AC source is connected to a \( 75 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{212.1}{1.414} = 150 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{150}{75} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 75 = 300 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 45 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 18 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the impedance?
In an AC circuit with only a resistor, what is the value of the power factor?
questions.explanation: In a purely resistive AC circuit, the voltage and current are in phase (phase angle \( \phi = 0^\circ \)). The power factor is defined as \( \cos \phi \), so \( \cos 0^\circ = 1 \), indicating maximum power transfer.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 70 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 90 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 40 \, \Omega \) has a \( 210 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the power dissipated?
questions.explanation: \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{70^2 + (90 - 40)^2} = \sqrt{4900 + 2500} = \sqrt{7400} \approx 86 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{Z} = \frac{210}{86} \approx 2.442 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 R = (2.442)^2 \times 70 \approx 417.6 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with a resistor and capacitor in series, why can the sum of individual voltages exceed the source voltage?
options: Because voltages are out of phase
questions.explanation: In an RC series circuit, the voltages across the resistor and capacitor are 90° out of phase. The algebraic sum of their magnitudes can exceed the source voltage, but the source voltage is the vector sum (\( V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + V_C^2} \)), accounting for the phase difference.

questions.question_text: A \( 80 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 25 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the impedance?
A \( 25 \, \Omega \) resistor is connected to a \( 125 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} \). Given: \( V = 125 \, \text{V} \), \( R = 25 \, \Omega \). \( I = \frac{125}{25} = 5 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 141.4 \, \text{V} \) (peak) AC source is connected to a \( 50 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{141.4}{1.414} = 100 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{100}{50} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 50 = 200 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A light bulb rated at \( 100 \, \text{W} \) operates on a \( 220 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC supply. What is the peak voltage across the bulb?
questions.explanation: Peak voltage: \( v_m = \sqrt{2} V \). Given: \( V = 220 \, \text{V} \) (rms). \( v_m = 1.414 \times 220 = 311.08 \, \text{V} \approx 311 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with a capacitor and resistor in series, how does the phase difference between voltage and current change if the capacitance is increased?
questions.explanation: In an RC series circuit, the phase angle \( \phi = \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{X_C}{R} \right) \), where \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \). Increasing capacitance decreases \( X_C \), reducing the phase angle, meaning the current leads the voltage by a smaller angle.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 25 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 50 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 70 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{70 - 50}{25} = \frac{20}{25} = 0.8 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(0.8) \approx 38.66^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A \( 110 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the inductive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi f \). \( f = 50 \, \text{Hz} \), \( L = 110 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( \omega = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.11 = 34.54 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: What is the significance of the phase difference being 90° in a purely reactive AC circuit?
questions.explanation: A 90° phase difference (in purely inductive or capacitive circuits) means the power factor (\( \cos 90^\circ = 0 \)) is zero, indicating no average power is dissipated. Energy oscillates between the source and the reactive element without being converted to heat.

questions.question_text: Why does the impedance of an AC circuit with only an inductor increase with frequency?
options: Because inductive reactance increases with frequency
questions.explanation: The impedance in a purely inductive circuit is the inductive reactance (\( X_L = \omega L \)), where \( \omega = 2\pi f \). As frequency (\( f \)) increases, \( \omega \) increases linearly, causing \( X_L \) (and thus impedance) to increase proportionally.

questions.question_text: A \( 200 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 15 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the voltage across the capacitor?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{314 \times 15 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 212.3 \, \Omega \). \( Z = \sqrt{200^2 + 212.3^2} \approx 291.5 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{Z} = \frac{220}{291.5} \approx 0.755 \, \text{A} \). Voltage across capacitor: \( V_C = I X_C = 0.755 \times 212.3 \approx 160.3 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a transformer not work with direct current (DC)?
options: Because DC does not produce a changing magnetic flux
questions.explanation: A transformer relies on a changing magnetic flux to induce voltage in the secondary coil via mutual induction. DC provides a constant current, producing a steady magnetic field with no flux change, so no voltage is induced.

questions.question_text: A \( 20 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 20 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 20 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 132.7 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{110}{132.7} \approx 0.829 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 0.829 \approx 1.17 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 75 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 75 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.075 = 28.26 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{110}{28.26} \approx 3.89 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: An AC voltage \( v = 141.4 \sin (100\pi t) \) V is applied across a \( 50 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the rms current through the resistor?
questions.explanation: Given: \( v = v_m \sin \omega t \), where \( v_m = 141.4 \, \text{V} \), \( R = 50 \, \Omega \). RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{141.4}{\sqrt{2}} = 100 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{100}{50} = 2 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 20 \, \Omega \) resistor is connected to a \( 100 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} \). Given: \( V = 100 \, \text{V} \), \( R = 20 \, \Omega \). \( I = \frac{100}{20} = 5 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( L = 3 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 12 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
questions.explanation: \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L C}} \). \( L = 3 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 12 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3 \times 12 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{36 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{10^3}{6} \approx 166.67 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 20 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 30 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 50 \, \Omega \). What is the power factor?
questions.explanation: \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{20^2 + (30 - 50)^2} = \sqrt{400 + 400} = \sqrt{800} \approx 28.28 \, \Omega \). Power factor: \( \cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{20}{28.28} \approx 0.707 \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with a series combination of resistor and inductor, what happens to the impedance if the frequency decreases?
questions.explanation: In an RL series circuit, impedance \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} \), where \( X_L = \omega L \). Decreasing frequency reduces \( \omega \), lowering \( X_L \), which decreases the impedance since \( R \) remains constant.

questions.question_text: A \( 60 \, \Omega \) resistor is connected to a \( 180 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} \). Given: \( V = 180 \, \text{V} \), \( R = 60 \, \Omega \). \( I = \frac{180}{60} = 3 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with a series combination of resistor and capacitor, what determines whether the circuit is predominantly capacitive?
options: The relative magnitude of capacitive reactance to resistance
questions.explanation: In an RC series circuit, the circuit is predominantly capacitive if the capacitive reactance (\( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \)) is greater than the resistance (\( R \)). This makes the impedance \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2} \) dominated by \( X_C \), and the current leads the voltage significantly.

questions.question_text: A \( 200 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source supplies a \( 100 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the peak voltage?
questions.explanation: Peak voltage: \( v_m = \sqrt{2} V \). \( V = 200 \, \text{V} \). \( v_m = 1.414 \times 200 = 282.8 \, \text{V} \approx 283 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 60 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 80 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 20 \, \Omega \) has a \( 180 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the power dissipated?
A \( 130 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source supplies a \( 65 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{130}{65} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 65 = 260 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary energy loss mechanism in a real transformer that reduces its efficiency?
questions.explanation: In a real transformer, energy losses occur due to resistance in the windings (\( I^2 R \) losses), flux leakage, eddy currents, and hysteresis. Among these, resistance in the windings (copper loss) is a primary mechanism, converting electrical energy into heat.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 700 \), \( N_s = 350 \). If \( V_p = 280 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 280 \times \frac{350}{700} = 140 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 11 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 11 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 11 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 241.2 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 200 \), \( N_s = 400 \). If \( V_p = 110 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 110 \times \frac{400}{200} = 220 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 30 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 45 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 15 \, \Omega \). What is the power factor?
questions.explanation: \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{30^2 + (45 - 15)^2} = \sqrt{900 + 900} = \sqrt{1800} \approx 42.43 \, \Omega \). Power factor: \( \cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{30}{42.43} \approx 0.707 \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with a resistor and inductor in series, what determines the magnitude of the phase difference between voltage and current?
options: The ratio of inductive reactance to resistance
questions.explanation: In an RL series circuit, the phase angle \( \phi = \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{X_L}{R} \right) \). The magnitude of this angle depends on the ratio of inductive reactance (\( X_L = \omega L \)) to resistance (\( R \)), as it reflects the relative contributions of inductance and resistance.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 250 \), \( N_s = 500 \). If \( V_s = 440 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the primary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_p = V_s \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} = 440 \times \frac{250}{500} = 220 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 25 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 25 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 25 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 127.4 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{230}{127.4} \approx 1.805 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 1.805 \approx 2.55 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 6 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 6 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 6 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 530.5 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: What is the effect on an ideal transformer’s secondary voltage if the number of turns in the secondary coil is halved?
questions.explanation: In an ideal transformer, \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). If the number of secondary turns (\( N_s \)) is halved, the secondary voltage (\( V_s \)) becomes half its original value, assuming primary voltage (\( V_p \)) remains constant.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 300 \), \( N_s = 150 \). If \( V_p = 240 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 240 \times \frac{150}{300} = 120 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 40 \, \Omega \) resistor is connected to a \( 120 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} \). Given: \( V = 120 \, \text{V} \), \( R = 40 \, \Omega \). \( I = \frac{120}{40} = 3 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 30 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 30 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.03 = 9.42 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{220}{9.42} \approx 23.35 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 150 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source supplies a \( 75 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{150}{75} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 75 = 4 \times 75 = 300 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 50 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 50 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.05 = 15.7 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{220}{15.7} \approx 14.01 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 14.01 \approx 19.81 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 28 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 28 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 28 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 113.6 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{220}{113.6} \approx 1.936 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 50 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 20 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the impedance?
A series LCR circuit with \( R = 40 \, \Omega \) is at resonance with a \( 200 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( Z = R = 40 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{200}{40} = 5 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 10 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 20 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 30 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{30 - 20}{10} = 1 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 300 \), \( N_s = 150 \). If \( V_s = 115 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the primary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_p = V_s \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} = 115 \times \frac{300}{150} = 230 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 16 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 16 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{376.8 \times 16 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 165.8 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: What happens to the current in a purely capacitive AC circuit when the frequency of the source increases?
questions.explanation: In a purely capacitive circuit, the capacitive reactance (\( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \)) decreases as the frequency (\( f \), where \( \omega = 2\pi f \)) increases. Since current is inversely proportional to reactance (\( I = \frac{V}{X_C} \)), the current increases.

questions.question_text: A \( 190 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source supplies a \( 95 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{190}{95} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 2 \approx 2.828 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 250 \), \( N_s = 500 \). If \( V_s = 440 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the primary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_p = V_s \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} = 440 \times \frac{250}{500} = 220 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 95 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 95 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 314 \times 0.095 = 29.83 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{220}{29.83} \approx 7.375 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 7.375 \approx 10.43 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 175 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source supplies a \( 35 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{175}{35} = 5 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 5^2 \times 35 = 875 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 110 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 140 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 80 \, \Omega \) has a \( 330 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the power dissipated?
A series LCR circuit has \( R = 15 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 30 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 45 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{45 - 30}{15} = 1 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 120 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 100 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 80 \, \Omega \). What is the impedance?
In an AC circuit with a pure inductor, why is the average power dissipated zero over a complete cycle?
options: Because the inductor has high resistance
Because energy is stored and returned without dissipation
questions.explanation: In a pure inductor, the current lags the voltage by 90°. The instantaneous power oscillates between positive (energy stored) and negative (energy returned), averaging to zero over a cycle because the inductor does not dissipate energy as heat but stores and releases it.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 600 \), \( N_s = 1200 \). If \( V_s = 480 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the primary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_p = V_s \times \frac{N_p}{N_s} = 480 \times \frac{600}{1200} = 240 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary factor determining the resonant frequency in a series LCR circuit?
questions.explanation: The resonant frequency in a series LCR circuit is determined by the inductance (\( L \)) and capacitance (\( C \)), given by \( f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{L C}} \). Resistance affects damping but not the resonant frequency itself.

questions.question_text: In an LCR series circuit, if the frequency is below the resonant frequency, which component dominates the circuit's behavior?
questions.explanation: Below resonance, \( \omega \) is low, making \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \) larger than \( X_L = \omega L \). Thus, the capacitive reactance dominates, and the circuit behaves as predominantly capacitive, with current leading voltage.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( L = 6 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 10 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
questions.explanation: \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L C}} \). \( L = 6 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 10 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6 \times 10^{-5}}} \approx 129.1 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: Why does an ideal transformer maintain constant power across its primary and secondary coils?
questions.explanation: In an ideal transformer, there are no losses (e.g., resistance, flux leakage). Energy conservation dictates that input power (\( V_p I_p \)) equals output power (\( V_s I_s \)), so the power remains constant despite changes in voltage and current.

questions.question_text: A \( 15 \, \Omega \) resistor is connected to a \( 75 \, \text{V} \) (rms) AC source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} \). Given: \( V = 75 \, \text{V} \), \( R = 15 \, \Omega \). \( I = \frac{75}{15} = 5 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 169.7 \, \text{V} \) (peak) AC source is connected to a \( 60 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the average power consumed?
questions.explanation: RMS voltage: \( V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{169.7}{1.414} \approx 120 \, \text{V} \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{120}{60} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Average power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 60 = 240 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 50 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 70 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 30 \, \Omega \) has a \( 200 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the power dissipated?
questions.explanation: \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{50^2 + (70 - 30)^2} = \sqrt{2500 + 1600} = \sqrt{4100} \approx 64 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{Z} = \frac{200}{64} \approx 3.125 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 R = (3.125)^2 \times 50 \approx 488.28 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 240 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source supplies a \( 120 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{240}{120} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 2 \approx 2.828 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 80 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 60 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 40 \, \Omega \). What is the impedance?
A \( 50 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 20 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the voltage across the resistor?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{314 \times 20 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 159.2 \, \Omega \). \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2} = \sqrt{50^2 + 159.2^2} \approx 166.6 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{Z} = \frac{110}{166.6} \approx 0.66 \, \text{A} \). Voltage across resistor: \( V_R = I R = 0.66 \times 50 \approx 33 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 50 \, \Omega \) is at resonance with a \( 250 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( Z = R = 50 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{250}{50} = 5 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: What is the significance of the power factor being zero in an AC circuit?
questions.explanation: A power factor of zero (\( \cos \phi = 0 \)) means the phase difference between voltage and current is 90°, as in purely inductive or capacitive circuits. This indicates no average power is dissipated, as energy is only stored and released, not consumed.

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 20 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 40 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 60 \, \Omega \). What is the phase angle?
questions.explanation: \( \tan \phi = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = \frac{60 - 40}{20} = 1 \). \( \phi = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ \). Since \( X_C > X_L \), the circuit is capacitive, and current leads voltage.

questions.question_text: A transformer has \( N_p = 600 \), \( N_s = 300 \). If \( V_p = 240 \, \text{V} \) (rms), what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: \( \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \). \( V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 240 \times \frac{300}{600} = 120 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( L = 2.5 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 40 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
In an AC circuit with a series LCR combination, why does the power dissipated depend only on the resistive component?
options: Because only resistance converts energy to heat
questions.explanation: Power dissipation in an AC circuit (\( P = I^2 R \cos \phi \)) occurs only through resistance, as inductors and capacitors store and release energy without converting it to heat. The reactive components affect the current and phase, but only \( R \) dissipates power.

questions.question_text: A \( 13 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 13 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 13 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 245.1 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A \( 60 \, \Omega \) resistor and \( 15 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor are in series with a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the impedance?
A series LCR circuit has \( R = 200 \, \Omega \), \( C = 15 \, \mu\text{F} \), and is connected to a \( 220 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) AC source. What is the impedance?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \), \( C = 15 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 15 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 212.3 \, \Omega \). No inductor, so \( X_L = 0 \). Impedance: \( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2} = \sqrt{200^2 + 212.3^2} \approx 291.5 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A \( 200 \, \text{V} \) (rms) source supplies a \( 100 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{200}{100} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 2 \approx 2.828 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit with \( R = 100 \, \Omega \), \( L = 1 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 1 \, \mu\text{F} \) is at resonance. What is the impedance?
questions.explanation: At resonance, \( X_L = X_C \), so \( Z = R \). Given: \( R = 100 \, \Omega \). Impedance \( Z = 100 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( R = 60 \, \Omega \), \( X_L = 50 \, \Omega \), \( X_C = 30 \, \Omega \). What is the impedance?
A \( 60 \, \text{mH} \) inductor is connected to a \( 110 \, \text{V} \), \( 60 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the peak current?
questions.explanation: \( X_L = \omega L \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 60 = 376.8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( L = 60 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H} \). \( X_L = 376.8 \times 0.06 = 22.61 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} = \frac{110}{22.61} \approx 4.87 \, \text{A} \). Peak current: \( i_m = \sqrt{2} I = 1.414 \times 4.87 \approx 6.88 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A series LCR circuit has \( L = 4 \, \text{H} \), \( C = 25 \, \mu\text{F} \). What is the resonant angular frequency?
A \( 26 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 26 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 26 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 122.4 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{230}{122.4} \approx 1.879 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC circuit with a resistor and capacitor in series, what happens to the total voltage across the components compared to the source voltage?
options: It is less than the source voltage
It equals the source voltage when added vectorially
It is greater than the source voltage
questions.explanation: In an RC series circuit, the voltages across the resistor (\( V_R \)) and capacitor (\( V_C \)) are 90° out of phase. The total source voltage is the vector sum, \( V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + V_C^2} \), which equals the applied voltage, not the algebraic sum, due to the phase difference.

questions.question_text: What happens to the current in an AC circuit containing only an inductor when the source frequency approaches zero?
questions.explanation: In a purely inductive circuit, \( X_L = \omega L \), and \( I = \frac{V}{X_L} \). As frequency (\( f \)) approaches zero, \( \omega = 2\pi f \) also approaches zero, making \( X_L \) very small. Thus, the current increases significantly, approaching a maximum limited only by resistance (which is zero in an ideal inductor).

questions.question_text: A \( 24 \, \mu\text{F} \) capacitor is connected to a \( 230 \, \text{V} \), \( 50 \, \text{Hz} \) source. What is the rms current?
questions.explanation: \( X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} \), \( \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 314 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( C = 24 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F} \). \( X_C = \frac{1}{314 \times 24 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 132.6 \, \Omega \). RMS current: \( I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{230}{132.6} \approx 1.734 \, \text{A} \).
