tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
tests.title: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory Chapter-Wise Test 3

questions.question_text: What is the total internal energy of 1 mole of a triatomic gas at 300 K with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Triatomic gas: 6 degrees of freedom (3 translational + 3 rotational). \(U = 3 R T = 3 \times 8.31 \times 300 = 7479 \, \text{J} \approx 7.48 \, \text{kJ}\).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of 0.2 moles of a diatomic gas by 10 K at constant volume, with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Diatomic gas: 5 degrees of freedom, \(C_v = \frac{5}{2} R\). \(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.2 \times \frac{5}{2} \times 8.31 \times 10 = 83.1 \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: What is the collision frequency of a gas molecule with a mean free path of \(3.0 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) and average speed of 600 m/s?
questions.explanation: Collision frequency = \(\frac{ }{l}\). \(\frac{600}{3.0 \times 10^{-7}} = 2.0 \times 10^9 \, \text{s}^{-1}\).

questions.question_text: At STP, 22.4 litres of oxygen gas (\(O_2\)) is present. What is the mass of this gas? (Molecular mass of \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\), \(1 \, \text{u} = 1 \, \text{g/mol}\))
questions.explanation: At STP (273 K, 1 atm), 1 mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 litres (molar volume). Given volume = 22.4 litres, so number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \( \frac{22.4}{22.4} = 1 \, \text{mol} \). Mass = \(\mu \times \text{molecular mass} = 1 \times 32 = 32 \, \text{g} \).

questions.question_text: A gas occupies 67.2 litres at STP. How many molecules are present? (\(N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \, \text{mol}^{-1}\), molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres)
questions.explanation: Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \(\frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Molar volume}} = \frac{67.2}{22.4} = 3.0 \, \text{mol}\). Number of molecules = \(\mu \times N_A = 3.0 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 1.806 \times 10^{24}\).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of 0.4 moles of a triatomic gas by 15 K at constant volume, with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Triatomic gas: 6 degrees of freedom, \(C_v = 3 R\). \(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.4 \times 3 \times 8.31 \times 15 = 149.58 \, \text{J} \approx 149.6 \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: A gas occupies a volume of 11.2 litres at STP. How many molecules are present in this gas? (\(N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \, \text{mol}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres/mol. Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \( \frac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5 \, \text{mol} \). Number of molecules = \(\mu \times N_A = 0.5 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 3.01 \times 10^{23} \).

questions.question_text: A gas at 3 atm and 400 K has a volume of 15 litres. If the pressure drops to 1.5 atm at constant temperature, what is the new volume?
A gas occupies 56.0 litres at STP. How many moles are present? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres)
questions.explanation: Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \(\frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Molar volume}}\). \(\mu = \frac{56.0}{22.4} = 2.5 \, \text{mol}\).

questions.question_text: At what temperature is the rms speed of helium molecules 1500 m/s? (Atomic mass of He = 4 u, \(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))

tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
tests.title: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory Chapter-Wise Test 4

questions.question_text: A gas at 2 atm and 400 K has a volume of 10 litres. If the temperature decreases to 100 K at constant pressure, what is the new volume?
A gas at 2.5 atm and 500 K has a density of \(0.96 \, \text{kg m}^{-3}\). What is its molecular mass? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), 1 atm = \(1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\))
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\rho R T}{M}\), \(M = \frac{\rho R T}{P}\). \(P = 2.5 \times 1.01 \times 10^5 = 2.525 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\). \(M = \frac{0.96 \times 8.31 \times 500}{2.525 \times 10^5} = 0.0158 \, \text{kg/mol} \approx 15.8 \, \text{g/mol} \approx 16 \, \text{g/mol}\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 1 atm and 273 K has a volume of 8 litres. If the pressure increases to 4 atm at constant temperature, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law: \(P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2\). \(P_1 = 1 \, \text{atm}\), \(V_1 = 8 \, \text{litres}\), \(P_2 = 4 \, \text{atm}\). \(V_2 = \frac{P_1 V_1}{P_2} = \frac{1 \times 8}{4} = 2 \, \text{litres}\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 1 atm and 300 K has a volume of 10 litres. If the volume is reduced to 5 litres at constant temperature, what is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law: \(P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2\). \(P_1 = 1 \, \text{atm}\), \(V_1 = 10 \, \text{litres}\), \(V_2 = 5 \, \text{litres}\). \(P_2 = \frac{P_1 V_1}{V_2} = \frac{1 \times 10}{5} = 2 \, \text{atm} \).

questions.question_text: A mixture of 0.2 moles of helium and 0.8 moles of oxygen is at 300 K in a 10-litre container. What is the total pressure? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). Total moles = \(0.2 + 0.8 = 1.0\), \(V = 10 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{1.0 \times 8.31 \times 300}{10 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.493 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 2.49 \, \text{atm}\).

questions.question_text: A solid has a molar specific heat capacity of \(25.5 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). How many degrees of freedom per atom does it have? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(C = f \times \frac{R}{2}\), \(25.5 = f \times \frac{8.31}{2}\). \(f = \frac{25.5 \times 2}{8.31} \approx 6.14 \approx 6\).

questions.question_text: A gas occupies 5.6 litres at STP. How many moles of the gas are present? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres)
questions.explanation: Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \(\frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Molar volume}}\). \(\mu = \frac{5.6}{22.4} = 0.25 \, \text{mol}\).

questions.question_text: A gas mixture contains 8 g of helium and 8 g of oxygen. What is the ratio of their partial pressures?
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\mu RT}{V}\), \(\frac{P_{\text{He}}}{P_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{\mu_{\text{He}}}{\mu_{\text{O}_2}}\). \(\mu_{\text{He}} = \frac{8}{4} = 2 \, \text{mol}\), \(\mu_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{8}{32} = 0.25 \, \text{mol}\). Ratio = \(\frac{2}{0.25} = 8:1\).

questions.question_text: What is the heat required to raise the temperature of 0.2 moles of a triatomic gas by 10 K at constant volume? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), no vibrational modes)
questions.explanation: Triatomic gas: 6 degrees of freedom (3 translational + 3 rotational). \(C_v = 3R\), \(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.2 \times 3 \times 8.31 \times 10 = 49.86 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A gas at 3 atm and 600 K has a density of \(0.96 \, \text{kg m}^{-3}\). What is its molecular mass? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), 1 atm = \(1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\))
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\rho R T}{M}\), \(M = \frac{\rho R T}{P}\). \(P = 3 \times 1.01 \times 10^5 = 3.03 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\). \(M = \frac{0.96 \times 8.31 \times 600}{3.03 \times 10^5} = 0.0158 \, \text{kg/mol} \approx 15.8 \, \text{g/mol} \approx 16 \, \text{g/mol}\).

tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
tests.title: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory Chapter-Wise Test 5

questions.question_text: A gas has a molar specific heat at constant volume of \(20.8 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is its \(C_p\)? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
A gas mixture has equal masses of helium and oxygen. What is the ratio of their number of molecules?
questions.explanation: Let mass = \(m\). \(N = \frac{m}{M} \times N_A\). For He (\(M = 4\)): \(N_{\text{He}} = \frac{m}{4} \times N_A\). For \(O_2\) (\(M = 32\)): \(N_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{m}{32} \times N_A\). Ratio \(\frac{N_{\text{He}}}{N_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{\frac{m}{4}}{\frac{m}{32}} = \frac{32}{4} = 8:1\).

questions.question_text: A gas has a volume of 22.4 litres at STP. How many moles are present if the temperature is raised to 546 K at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: At STP, 22.4 litres = 1 mole. Charles’ law: \(\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2}\), but moles remain constant at constant \(P\). Initial \(\mu = 1 \, \text{mol}\), remains 1 mole as \(V\) adjusts with \(T\).

questions.question_text: A gas has a \(C_v\) of \(27.0 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is its \(C_p\)? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
What is the collision frequency of a gas molecule with a mean free path of \(1.2 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) and average speed of 480 m/s?
questions.explanation: Collision frequency = \(\frac{ }{l}\). \(\frac{480}{1.2 \times 10^{-7}} = 4.0 \times 10^9 \, \text{s}^{-1}\).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of a gas is 550 m/s at 275 K. At what temperature will the rms speed be 1100 m/s?
A gas has a \(C_v\) of \(17.1 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is its \(C_p\)? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
What is the temperature at which the rms speed of nitrogen molecules is 1032 m/s? (Molecular mass of \(N_2 = 28 \, \text{u}\), \(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
The mean free path of a gas is \(1.2 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) with a number density of \(4.0 \times 10^{25} \, \text{m}^{-3}\). What is the molecular diameter?
What is the average translational kinetic energy of a nitrogen molecule (\(N_2\)) at 300 K? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE per molecule = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). Substitute: \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 300 = 6.21 \times 10^{-21} \, \text{J} \).

tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
tests.title: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory Chapter-Wise Test 6

questions.question_text: The rms speed of oxygen molecules at a certain temperature is 500 m/s. What is the rms speed of hydrogen molecules at the same temperature? (Molecular mass of \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\), \(H_2 = 2 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3k_B T}{m}}\), so \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\). Ratio: \(\frac{v_{\text{rms,H}_2}}{v_{\text{rms,O}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{O_2}}{m_{H_2}}} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{2}} = \sqrt{16} = 4\). \(v_{\text{rms,H}_2} = 4 \times 500 = 2000 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the collision frequency of a gas molecule with a mean free path of \(1.0 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) and average speed of 400 m/s?
questions.explanation: Collision frequency = \(\frac{ }{l}\). \(\frac{400}{1.0 \times 10^{-7}} = 4.0 \times 10^9 \, \text{s}^{-1}\).

questions.question_text: A solid has a molar specific heat capacity of \(24.9 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is the energy per degree of freedom per atom? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(C = f \times \frac{R}{2}\), \(24.9 = f \times \frac{8.31}{2}\), \(f = \frac{24.9 \times 2}{8.31} \approx 6\). Energy per degree of freedom = \(\frac{1}{2} k_B T\), per mole = \(\frac{1}{2} R T\). For 1 degree of freedom, energy per mole = \(\frac{8.31}{2} = 4.155 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A gas mixture contains 2 g of hydrogen and 32 g of oxygen. What is the ratio of their partial pressures?
A gas mixture contains 4 g of helium and 32 g of oxygen. What is the total pressure if the volume is 22.4 litres at 273 K? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(\mu_{\text{He}} = \frac{4}{4} = 1 \, \text{mol}\), \(\mu_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{32}{32} = 1 \, \text{mol}\). Total moles = \(1 + 1 = 2 \, \text{mol}\), \(V = 22.4 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V} = \frac{2 \times 8.31 \times 273}{22.4 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.02 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 2 \, \text{atm} \).

questions.question_text: A gas mixture has equal masses of hydrogen and argon at 300 K. What is the ratio of their rms speeds? (Molecular mass: \(H_2 = 2 \, \text{u}\), Ar = 39.9 u)
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{H}_2}}{v_{\text{Ar}}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{Ar}}}{m_{\text{H}_2}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{H}_2}}{v_{\text{Ar}}} = \sqrt{\frac{39.9}{2}} \approx \sqrt{19.95} \approx 4.47\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 2 atm and 400 K has a volume of 8 litres. If the temperature decreases to 200 K at constant pressure, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Charles’ law: \(\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2}\). \(V_1 = 8 \, \text{litres}\), \(T_1 = 400 \, \text{K}\), \(T_2 = 200 \, \text{K}\). \(V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 8 \times \frac{200}{400} = 4 \, \text{litres}\).

questions.question_text: The number density of a gas is \(2.5 \times 10^{25} \, \text{m}^{-3}\). If the molecular diameter is \(2 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{m}\), what is the mean free path?
A gas has a \(C_v\) of \(20.4 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is its \(C_p\)? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
What is the total internal energy of 0.5 moles of a monatomic gas at 600 K? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Monatomic gas: \(U = \frac{3}{2} \mu R T\). \(U = \frac{3}{2} \times 0.5 \times 8.31 \times 600 = 3741.75 \, \text{J} \approx 3.74 \, \text{kJ}\).

tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
tests.title: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory Chapter-Wise Test 7

questions.question_text: The mean free path of a gas is \(5 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) with a number density of \(2 \times 10^{25} \, \text{m}^{-3}\). What is the molecular diameter?
A gas mixture contains 4 g of helium and 16 g of oxygen. What is the ratio of their partial pressures?
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\mu RT}{V}\), \(\frac{P_{\text{He}}}{P_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{\mu_{\text{He}}}{\mu_{\text{O}_2}}\). \(\mu_{\text{He}} = \frac{4}{4} = 1 \, \text{mol}\), \(\mu_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{16}{32} = 0.5 \, \text{mol}\). Ratio = \(\frac{1}{0.5} = 2:1\).

questions.question_text: What is the ratio of \(C_p\) to \(C_v\) for a gas with 3 translational and 2 rotational degrees of freedom?
questions.explanation: Degrees of freedom = \(3 + 2 = 5\). \(C_v = \frac{5}{2} R\), \(C_p = C_v + R = \frac{5}{2} R + R = \frac{7}{2} R\). \(\gamma = \frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac{\frac{7}{2} R}{\frac{5}{2} R} = \frac{7}{5} = 1.4\).

questions.question_text: What is the average translational kinetic energy of an argon atom at 500 K? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 500 = 1.035 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: What is the total internal energy of 0.3 moles of a triatomic gas at 300 K with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Triatomic gas: 6 degrees of freedom, \(U = 3 \mu R T\). \(U = 3 \times 0.3 \times 8.31 \times 300 = 2243.7 \, \text{J} \approx 2.24 \, \text{kJ}\).

questions.question_text: A mixture of 2 moles of helium and 3 moles of nitrogen is at 400 K in a 50-litre container. What is the total pressure? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). Total moles = \(2 + 3 = 5\), \(V = 50 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{5 \times 8.31 \times 400}{50 \times 10^{-3}} = 3.324 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 3.32 \, \text{atm}\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 2 atm and 400 K has a volume of 6 litres. If the pressure decreases to 1 atm at constant temperature, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law: \(P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2\). \(P_1 = 2 \, \text{atm}\), \(V_1 = 6 \, \text{litres}\), \(P_2 = 1 \, \text{atm}\). \(V_2 = \frac{P_1 V_1}{P_2} = \frac{2 \times 6}{1} = 12 \, \text{litres}\).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of 0.1 moles of a monatomic gas by 30 K at constant volume? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Monatomic gas: \(C_v = \frac{3}{2} R\). \(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.1 \times \frac{3}{2} \times 8.31 \times 30 = 37.395 \, \text{J} \approx 37.4 \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of a gas is 300 m/s at 150 K. At what temperature will the rms speed be 600 m/s?
A gas at 4 atm and 500 K has a volume of 20 litres. If the pressure increases to 8 atm at constant temperature, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law: \(P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2\). \(P_1 = 4 \, \text{atm}\), \(V_1 = 20 \, \text{litres}\), \(P_2 = 8 \, \text{atm}\). \(V_2 = \frac{P_1 V_1}{P_2} = \frac{4 \times 20}{8} = 10 \, \text{litres}\).

tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
tests.title: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory Chapter-Wise Test 8

questions.question_text: A gas has a \(C_v\) of \(20.8 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is the ratio of specific heats (\(\gamma\))? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
At what temperature is the rms speed of oxygen molecules 964 m/s? (Molecular mass of \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\), \(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
The mean free path of air molecules at STP is \(2.9 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\). If temperature doubles at constant pressure, what is the new mean free path?
questions.explanation: \(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\), \(n = \frac{N}{V}\), and \(PV = Nk_B T\). At constant \(P\), \(V \propto T\), so \(n \propto \frac{1}{T}\). If \(T\) doubles, \(n\) halves, \(l\) doubles. New \(l = 2 \times 2.9 \times 10^{-7} = 5.8 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the average translational kinetic energy of a hydrogen molecule at 700 K? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 700 = 1.449 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 1.5 atm and 300 K has a density of \(1.2 \, \text{kg m}^{-3}\). What is its molecular mass? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), 1 atm = \(1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\))
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\rho R T}{M}\), \(M = \frac{\rho R T}{P}\). \(P = 1.5 \times 1.01 \times 10^5 = 1.515 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\). \(M = \frac{1.2 \times 8.31 \times 300}{1.515 \times 10^5} = 0.01975 \, \text{kg/mol} \approx 19.75 \, \text{g/mol} \approx 20 \, \text{g/mol}\).

questions.question_text: The mean free path of a gas molecule is \(1.0 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}\) at 0.5 atm. What will it be at 2 atm if temperature remains constant?
questions.explanation: \(l \propto \frac{1}{n}\), \(n \propto P\). If \(P\) increases by 4 times (\(0.5 \, \text{to} \, 2\)), \(n\) increases 4 times, \(l\) reduces to \(\frac{1}{4}\). New \(l = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-6}}{4} = 2.5 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\).

questions.question_text: What is the total internal energy of 0.4 moles of a diatomic gas at 400 K with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Diatomic gas: 5 degrees of freedom, \(U = \frac{5}{2} \mu R T\). \(U = \frac{5}{2} \times 0.4 \times 8.31 \times 400 = 3324 \, \text{J} \approx 3.32 \, \text{kJ}\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 1.5 atm and 300 K has a volume of 12 litres. If the temperature increases to 450 K at constant pressure, what is the new volume?
The mean free path of a gas molecule is \(1.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}\) at 0.2 atm. What will it be at 0.8 atm if temperature remains constant?
questions.explanation: \(l \propto \frac{1}{n}\), \(n \propto P\). If \(P\) increases by 4 times (\(0.2 \, \text{to} \, 0.8\)), \(n\) increases 4 times, \(l\) reduces to \(\frac{1}{4}\). New \(l = \frac{1.5 \times 10^{-6}}{4} = 3.75 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\).

questions.question_text: A mixture of 0.1 moles of helium and 0.9 moles of oxygen is at 500 K in a 30-litre container. What is the total pressure? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). Total moles = \(0.1 + 0.9 = 1.0\), \(V = 30 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{1.0 \times 8.31 \times 500}{30 \times 10^{-3}} = 1.385 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 1.39 \, \text{atm}\).

tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
tests.title: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory Chapter-Wise Test 9

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of 0.15 moles of a triatomic gas by 25 K at constant volume, with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Triatomic gas: 6 degrees of freedom, \(C_v = 3 R\). \(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.15 \times 3 \times 8.31 \times 25 = 93.4875 \, \text{J} \approx 93.5 \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of 0.3 moles of a triatomic gas by 15 K at constant volume, ignoring vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Triatomic gas: 6 degrees of freedom, \(C_v = 3R\). \(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.3 \times 3 \times 8.31 \times 15 = 112.185 \, \text{J} \approx 112.2 \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: A gas mixture has equal volumes of helium and argon at the same temperature and pressure. What is the ratio of their rms speeds? (Atomic mass: He = 4 u, Ar = 39.9 u)
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{He}}}{v_{\text{Ar}}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{Ar}}}{m_{\text{He}}}} = \sqrt{\frac{39.9}{4}} \approx \sqrt{10} \approx 3.16\).

questions.question_text: What is the average translational kinetic energy of a nitrogen molecule at 1000 K? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 1000 = 2.07 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: A mixture of 0.3 moles of nitrogen and 0.7 moles of argon is at 350 K in a 20-litre container. What is the total pressure? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). Total moles = \(0.3 + 0.7 = 1.0\), \(V = 20 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{1.0 \times 8.31 \times 350}{20 \times 10^{-3}} = 1.45575 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 1.46 \, \text{atm}\).

questions.question_text: At what temperature is the rms speed of argon molecules 860 m/s? (Atomic mass of Ar = 39.9 u, \(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
A gas mixture contains 8 g of helium and 64 g of oxygen. What is the ratio of their partial pressures?
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\mu RT}{V}\), \(\frac{P_{\text{He}}}{P_{\text{O}_2}} = \frac{\mu_{\text{He}}}{\mu_{\text{O}_2}}\). \(\mu_{\text{He}} = \frac{8}{4} = 2 \, \text{mol}\), \(\mu_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{64}{32} = 2 \, \text{mol}\). Ratio = \(\frac{2}{2} = 1:1\).

questions.question_text: A gas mixture contains 16 g of oxygen and 4 g of hydrogen. What is the ratio of their partial pressures?
A gas at 2.5 atm and 500 K has a volume of 12 litres. If the pressure increases to 5 atm at constant temperature, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law: \(P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2\). \(P_1 = 2.5 \, \text{atm}\), \(V_1 = 12 \, \text{litres}\), \(P_2 = 5 \, \text{atm}\). \(V_2 = \frac{P_1 V_1}{P_2} = \frac{2.5 \times 12}{5} = 6 \, \text{litres}\).

questions.question_text: A monatomic gas has a molar specific heat at constant pressure of \(20.8 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is the value of \(C_v\)?
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas: \(C_p - C_v = R\), where \(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). \(C_v = C_p - R = 20.8 - 8.31 = 12.49 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \approx 12.5 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \).

tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory

questions.question_text: A gas mixture has equal masses of neon and nitrogen at 300 K. What is the ratio of their rms speeds? (Atomic mass: Ne = 20.2 u, \(N_2 = 28 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{Ne}}}{v_{\text{N}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{N}_2}}{m_{\text{Ne}}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{Ne}}}{v_{\text{N}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{28}{20.2}} \approx \sqrt{1.386} \approx 1.18\).

questions.question_text: A gas occupies 33.6 litres at STP. How many molecules are present? (\(N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \, \text{mol}^{-1}\), molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres)
questions.explanation: Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \(\frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Molar volume}} = \frac{33.6}{22.4} = 1.5 \, \text{mol}\). Number of molecules = \(\mu \times N_A = 1.5 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 9.03 \times 10^{23}\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 1 atm and 273 K has a density of \(1.43 \, \text{kg m}^{-3}\). What is its molecular mass? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), 1 atm = \(1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\))
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\rho R T}{M}\), \(M = \frac{\rho R T}{P}\). \(M = \frac{1.43 \times 8.31 \times 273}{1.01 \times 10^5} = 0.0321 \, \text{kg/mol} \approx 32.1 \, \text{g/mol}\).

questions.question_text: What is the collision frequency of a gas molecule if its mean free path is \(2 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) and average speed is 500 m/s?
questions.explanation: Collision frequency = \(\frac{ }{l}\). \(\frac{500}{2 \times 10^{-7}} = 2.5 \times 10^9 \, \text{s}^{-1}\).

questions.question_text: How many degrees of freedom does a diatomic molecule have if its vibrational mode is active?
questions.explanation: Diatomic molecule: 3 translational + 2 rotational + 1 vibrational (2 modes: KE and PE). Total degrees of freedom = \(3 + 2 + 2 = 7\).

questions.question_text: A vessel contains 1 mole of a diatomic gas at 300 K. What is its total internal energy if vibrational modes are not excited? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: For diatomic gas (rigid rotator): \(U = \frac{5}{2} \mu R T\). \(U = \frac{5}{2} \times 1 \times 8.31 \times 300 = 6232.5 \, \text{J} \approx 6.23 \, \text{kJ} \).

questions.question_text: What is the average translational kinetic energy of a neon atom at 800 K? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 800 = 1.656 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: What is the time between collisions for a gas molecule with a mean free path of \(4.5 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) and average speed of 450 m/s?
How much heat is required to raise the temperature of 0.5 moles of neon by 25 K at constant volume? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: For monatomic gas, \(C_v = \frac{3}{2} R\). \(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.5 \times \frac{3}{2} \times 8.31 \times 25 = 155.8125 \, \text{J} \approx 155.8 \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: A gas has a \(C_v\) of \(21.0 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is its \(C_p\)? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))

questions.question_text: The rms speed of nitrogen molecules is 516 m/s at 300 K. What is the rms speed of oxygen molecules at the same temperature? (Molecular mass: \(N_2 = 28 \, \text{u}\), \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{O}_2}}{v_{\text{N}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{N}_2}}{m_{\text{O}_2}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{O}_2}}{516} = \sqrt{\frac{28}{32}} = \sqrt{0.875} \approx 0.935\). \(v_{\text{O}_2} = 516 \times 0.935 \approx 482 \, \text{m/s}\).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of helium molecules is 1370 m/s at 300 K. What is the rms speed of argon molecules at the same temperature? (Atomic mass: He = 4 u, Ar = 39.9 u)
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{Ar}}}{v_{\text{He}}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{He}}}{m_{\text{Ar}}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{Ar}}}{1370} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{39.9}} \approx \sqrt{0.1} \approx 0.316\). \(v_{\text{Ar}} = 1370 \times 0.316 \approx 433 \, \text{m/s}\).

questions.question_text: A solid has a molar specific heat capacity of \(24.5 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). How many degrees of freedom per atom does it have? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(C = f \times \frac{R}{2}\), \(24.5 = f \times \frac{8.31}{2}\). \(f = \frac{24.5 \times 2}{8.31} \approx 5.9 \approx 6\).

questions.question_text: A gas has a density of \(0.8 \, \text{kg m}^{-3}\) at 1 atm and 300 K. What is its molecular mass? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), 1 atm = \(1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\))
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\rho R T}{M}\), so \(M = \frac{\rho R T}{P}\). \(M = \frac{0.8 \times 8.31 \times 300}{1.01 \times 10^5} = 0.01975 \, \text{kg/mol} = 19.75 \, \text{g/mol} \approx 20 \, \text{g/mol} \).

questions.question_text: The mean free path of a gas is \(1.8 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) with a number density of \(3.0 \times 10^{25} \, \text{m}^{-3}\). What is the molecular diameter?
A gas at 3 atm and 600 K has a volume of 15 litres. If the pressure decreases to 1.5 atm at constant temperature, what is the new volume?
What is the average translational kinetic energy of a nitrogen molecule at 450 K? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 450 = 9.315 \times 10^{-21} \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: What is the volume of 0.6 moles of an ideal gas at 3 atm and 527°C? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
At what temperature is the rms speed of hydrogen molecules 2000 m/s? (Molecular mass of \(H_2 = 2 \, \text{u}\), \(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
What is the pressure of 0.4 moles of an ideal gas in a 4-litre container at 327°C? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). \(T = 327 + 273 = 600 \, \text{K}\), \(V = 4 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{0.4 \times 8.31 \times 600}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = 4.986 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 5.0 \, \text{atm} (1 \, \text{atm} \approx 10^5 \, \text{Pa})\).

questions.question_text: What is the total internal energy of 1.5 moles of a monatomic gas at 250 K? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))

questions.question_text: A gas has a \(C_v\) of \(12.5 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is the ratio of specific heats (\(\gamma\))? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
A mixture of 1 mole of neon and 2 moles of argon is at 500 K in a 30-litre container. What is the total pressure? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))

questions.question_text: A gas occupies 28.0 litres at STP. How many moles are present? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres)

questions.question_text: At what temperature is the rms speed of oxygen molecules 600 m/s? (Molecular mass of \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\), \(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
A container holds 0.5 moles of an ideal gas at 2 atm pressure and 27°C. What is the volume of the gas? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Ideal gas equation: \(PV = \mu R T\). \(T = 27 + 273 = 300 \, \text{K}\), \(P = 2 \times 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} = 2.02 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\), \(\mu = 0.5 \, \text{mol}\). \(V = \frac{\mu R T}{P} = \frac{0.5 \times 8.31 \times 300}{2.02 \times 10^5} = 6.17 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3 = 6.17 \, \text{litres} \).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of nitrogen molecules is 516 m/s at 300 K. What is the rms speed of argon molecules at the same temperature? (Molecular mass: \(N_2 = 28 \, \text{u}\), Ar = 39.9 u)
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{Ar}}}{v_{\text{N}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{N}_2}}{m_{\text{Ar}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{Ar}}}{516} = \sqrt{\frac{28}{39.9}} \approx \sqrt{0.7017} \approx 0.8375\). \(v_{\text{Ar}} = 516 \times 0.8375 \approx 432 \, \text{m/s}\).

questions.question_text: What is the pressure of 0.25 moles of an ideal gas in a 5-litre container at 227°C? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). \(T = 227 + 273 = 500 \, \text{K}\), \(V = 5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{0.25 \times 8.31 \times 500}{5 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.0775 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 2.08 \, \text{atm} (1 \, \text{atm} \approx 10^5 \, \text{Pa})\).

questions.question_text: A vessel contains helium gas at 27°C with a pressure of 2 atm. If the temperature increases to 127°C at constant volume, what is the final pressure?
The mean free path of a gas molecule is \(2 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) at a certain pressure. If the pressure is doubled, what is the new mean free path? (Assume constant temperature)
questions.explanation: Mean free path \(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\), where \(n \propto P\) at constant \(T\). If \(P\) doubles, \(n\) doubles, so \(l\) halves. New \(l = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7}}{2} = 1 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m} \).

tests.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory

questions.question_text: A solid has a molar specific heat capacity of \(25 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\) at room temperature. How many degrees of freedom does each atom have?
questions.explanation: For a solid, \(C = f \times \frac{R}{2} \times N_A = f \times \frac{R}{2} \times 1 = f \times \frac{R}{2}\). Given \(C = 25 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), \(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). \(25 = f \times \frac{8.31}{2}\), \(f = \frac{25 \times 2}{8.31} \approx 6\).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of argon molecules is 430 m/s at 300 K. What is the rms speed of nitrogen molecules at the same temperature? (Atomic mass: Ar = 39.9 u, \(N_2 = 28 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{N}_2}}{v_{\text{Ar}}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{Ar}}}{m_{\text{N}_2}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{N}_2}}{430} = \sqrt{\frac{39.9}{28}} \approx \sqrt{1.425} \approx 1.193\). \(v_{\text{N}_2} = 430 \times 1.193 \approx 513 \, \text{m/s}\).

questions.question_text: A gas mixture contains 12 g of helium and 28 g of nitrogen. What is the ratio of their partial pressures?
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\mu RT}{V}\), \(\frac{P_{\text{He}}}{P_{\text{N}_2}} = \frac{\mu_{\text{He}}}{\mu_{\text{N}_2}}\). \(\mu_{\text{He}} = \frac{12}{4} = 3 \, \text{mol}\), \(\mu_{\text{N}_2} = \frac{28}{28} = 1 \, \text{mol}\). Ratio = \(\frac{3}{1} = 3:1\).

questions.question_text: What is the molar specific heat at constant volume (\(C_v\)) for a diatomic gas with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: For a diatomic gas (rigid rotator), 5 degrees of freedom (3 translational + 2 rotational). \(C_v = \frac{5}{2} R = \frac{5}{2} \times 8.31 = 20.775 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \approx 20.8 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of a gas is 450 m/s at 225 K. At what temperature will the rms speed be 900 m/s?
How much heat is required to raise the temperature of 0.25 moles of a diatomic gas by 20 K at constant volume, with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Diatomic gas: 5 degrees of freedom, \(C_v = \frac{5}{2} R\). \(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.25 \times \frac{5}{2} \times 8.31 \times 20 = 207.75 \, \text{J} \approx 207.8 \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: A gas has a \(C_p\) of \(29.8 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is the ratio of specific heats (\(\gamma\))? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
A gas mixture has equal numbers of oxygen and argon molecules at 300 K. What is the ratio of their rms speeds? (Molecular mass: \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\), Ar = 39.9 u)
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{O}_2}}{v_{\text{Ar}}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{Ar}}}{m_{\text{O}_2}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{O}_2}}{v_{\text{Ar}}} = \sqrt{\frac{39.9}{32}} \approx \sqrt{1.247} \approx 1.117\).

questions.question_text: What is the average translational kinetic energy of a helium atom at 1000 K? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 1000 = 2.07 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: What is the total internal energy of 0.7 moles of a diatomic gas at 200 K with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Diatomic gas: 5 degrees of freedom, \(U = \frac{5}{2} \mu R T\). \(U = \frac{5}{2} \times 0.7 \times 8.31 \times 200 = 2908.5 \, \text{J} \approx 2.91 \, \text{kJ}\).

questions.question_text: A gas has a \(C_p\) of \(35.4 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is its \(C_v\)? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
What is the total internal energy of 2 moles of a monatomic gas at 400 K? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: For monatomic gas, \(U = \frac{3}{2} \mu R T\). \(U = \frac{3}{2} \times 2 \times 8.31 \times 400 = 9972 \, \text{J} \approx 9.97 \, \text{kJ} \).

questions.question_text: The mean free path of a gas molecule is \(3.0 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}\) at 0.25 atm. What will it be at 1 atm if temperature remains constant?
questions.explanation: \(l \propto \frac{1}{n}\), \(n \propto P\). If \(P\) increases by 4 times (\(0.25 \, \text{to} \, 1\)), \(n\) increases 4 times, \(l\) reduces to \(\frac{1}{4}\). New \(l = \frac{3.0 \times 10^{-6}}{4} = 7.5 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\).

questions.question_text: A gas occupies 89.6 litres at STP. How many moles are present? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres)
questions.explanation: Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \(\frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Molar volume}}\). \(\mu = \frac{89.6}{22.4} = 4.0 \, \text{mol}\).

questions.question_text: What is the volume of 0.5 moles of an ideal gas at 2 atm and 627°C? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
What is the temperature at which the average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is \(1.035 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\)? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(1.035 \times 10^{-20} = \frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times T\). \(T = \frac{1.035 \times 10^{-20} \times 2}{3 \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23}} = 500 \, \text{K} \).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of oxygen molecules is 482 m/s at 300 K. What is the rms speed of methane molecules at the same temperature? (Molecular mass: \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\), \(CH_4 = 16 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{CH}_4}}{v_{\text{O}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{O}_2}}{m_{\text{CH}_4}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{CH}_4}}{482} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{16}} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414\). \(v_{\text{CH}_4} = 482 \times 1.414 \approx 682 \, \text{m/s}\).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of nitrogen molecules is 516 m/s at 300 K. What will it be at 600 K? (Molecular mass of \(N_2 = 28 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T}\), \(\frac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\frac{T_2}{T_1}}\). \(\frac{v_2}{516} = \sqrt{\frac{600}{300}} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414\). \(v_2 = 516 \times 1.414 \approx 729 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A gas at 1.5 atm and 300 K has a volume of 18 litres. If the pressure decreases to 0.75 atm at constant temperature, what is the new volume?
A gas mixture has equal masses of helium and nitrogen at 300 K. What is the ratio of their rms speeds? (Atomic mass: He = 4 u, \(N_2 = 28 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{He}}}{v_{\text{N}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{N}_2}}{m_{\text{He}}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{He}}}{v_{\text{N}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{28}{4}} = \sqrt{7} \approx 2.645\).

questions.question_text: A mixture of 1 mole of argon and 0.5 moles of nitrogen is at 450 K in a 15-litre container. What is the total pressure? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). Total moles = \(1 + 0.5 = 1.5\), \(V = 15 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{1.5 \times 8.31 \times 450}{15 \times 10^{-3}} = 3.74 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 3.74 \, \text{atm}\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 400 K has a pressure of 1 atm. If the temperature is reduced to 200 K at constant volume, what is the new pressure?
What is the pressure of 0.8 moles of an ideal gas in a 16-litre container at 427°C? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). \(T = 427 + 273 = 700 \, \text{K}\), \(V = 16 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{0.8 \times 8.31 \times 700}{16 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.90625 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 2.91 \, \text{atm} (1 \, \text{atm} \approx 10^5 \, \text{Pa})\).

questions.question_text: A mixture of 0.5 moles of helium and 1.5 moles of oxygen is at 350 K in a 25-litre container. What is the total pressure? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(PV = \mu R T\), \(P = \frac{\mu R T}{V}\). Total moles = \(0.5 + 1.5 = 2\), \(V = 25 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3\). \(P = \frac{2 \times 8.31 \times 350}{25 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.326 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \approx 2.33 \, \text{atm}\).

questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 600 = 1.242 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: A gas has a density of \(1.2 \, \text{kg m}^{-3}\) at 2 atm and 400 K. What is its molecular mass? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), 1 atm = \(1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\))
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\rho R T}{M}\), \(M = \frac{\rho R T}{P}\). \(P = 2 \times 1.01 \times 10^5 = 2.02 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\). \(M = \frac{1.2 \times 8.31 \times 400}{2.02 \times 10^5} = 0.01975 \, \text{kg/mol} = 19.75 \, \text{g/mol} \approx 20 \, \text{g/mol} \).

questions.question_text: A gas has a \(C_p\) of \(20.8 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is the ratio of specific heats (\(\gamma\))? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))

questions.question_text: A gas has a \(C_v\) of \(24.93 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is the ratio of specific heats (\(\gamma\))? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
What is the average speed of a molecule if its mean free path is \(4 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) and time between collisions is \(8 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{s}\)?

What is the average translational kinetic energy of an argon atom at 900 K? (\(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Average translational KE = \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\). \(\frac{3}{2} \times 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 900 = 1.863 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\).

questions.question_text: A solid has a molar specific heat capacity of \(24.4 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). How many degrees of freedom per atom does it have? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(C = f \times \frac{R}{2}\), \(24.4 = f \times \frac{8.31}{2}\). \(f = \frac{24.4 \times 2}{8.31} \approx 5.87 \approx 6\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 2 atm and 400 K has a density of \(0.8 \, \text{kg m}^{-3}\). What is its molecular mass? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), 1 atm = \(1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\))
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\rho R T}{M}\), \(M = \frac{\rho R T}{P}\). \(P = 2 \times 1.01 \times 10^5 = 2.02 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\). \(M = \frac{0.8 \times 8.31 \times 400}{2.02 \times 10^5} = 0.01318 \, \text{kg/mol} \approx 13.2 \, \text{g/mol}\).

questions.question_text: A gas mixture has equal numbers of helium and nitrogen molecules at 400 K. What is the ratio of their rms speeds? (Atomic mass: He = 4 u, \(N_2 = 28 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{He}}}{v_{\text{N}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{N}_2}}{m_{\text{He}}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{He}}}{v_{\text{N}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{28}{4}} = \sqrt{7} \approx 2.65\).

questions.question_text: The ratio of specific heats (\(\gamma\)) for a triatomic gas with no vibrational modes is:
questions.explanation: Triatomic gas: 3 translational + 3 rotational = 6 degrees of freedom. \(C_v = 3R\), \(C_p = C_v + R = 4R\). \(\gamma = \frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac{4R}{3R} = \frac{4}{3} = 1.33\).

questions.question_text: What is the collision frequency of a gas molecule with a mean free path of \(2.4 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) and average speed of 480 m/s?
questions.explanation: Collision frequency = \(\frac{ }{l}\). \(\frac{480}{2.4 \times 10^{-7}} = 2.0 \times 10^9 \, \text{s}^{-1}\).

questions.question_text: What is the total internal energy of 0.5 moles of a diatomic gas at 200 K with no vibrational modes? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Diatomic gas: 5 degrees of freedom (3 translational + 2 rotational). \(U = \frac{5}{2} \mu R T = \frac{5}{2} \times 0.5 \times 8.31 \times 200 = 2077.5 \, \text{J} \approx 2.08 \, \text{kJ}\).

questions.explanation: \(C = f \times \frac{R}{2}\), \(24.9 = f \times \frac{8.31}{2}\). \(f = \frac{24.9 \times 2}{8.31} \approx 5.99 \approx 6\).

questions.question_text: The molar specific heat at constant pressure for a polyatomic gas with 2 vibrational modes is: (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: Polyatomic gas: 3 translational + 3 rotational + 2 vibrational modes. Total degrees of freedom = \(3 + 3 + 2 \times 2 = 10\). \(C_v = 5R\), \(C_p = C_v + R = 6R = 6 \times 8.31 = 49.86 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: The mean free path of a gas is \(3 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) with a number density of \(3 \times 10^{25} \, \text{m}^{-3}\). What is the molecular diameter?

A gas at 2 atm and 300 K occupies 20 litres. If the pressure is increased to 4 atm at constant temperature, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law: \(P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2\). \(P_1 = 2 \, \text{atm}\), \(V_1 = 20 \, \text{litres}\), \(P_2 = 4 \, \text{atm}\). \(V_2 = \frac{P_1 V_1}{P_2} = \frac{2 \times 20}{4} = 10 \, \text{litres}\).

questions.question_text: A gas mixture has equal numbers of hydrogen and oxygen molecules at 300 K. What is the ratio of their rms speeds? (Molecular mass: \(H_2 = 2 \, \text{u}\), \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\))

questions.question_text: The rms speed of helium molecules is 1370 m/s at 300 K. What is the rms speed of oxygen molecules at the same temperature? (Atomic mass: He = 4 u, \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\))
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{O}_2}}{v_{\text{He}}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{He}}}{m_{\text{O}_2}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{O}_2}}{1370} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{32}} = \sqrt{0.125} \approx 0.3535\). \(v_{\text{O}_2} = 1370 \times 0.3535 \approx 484 \, \text{m/s}\).

A gas mixture has 2 g of helium and 16 g of oxygen. What is the ratio of their partial pressures?
A gas at 2 atm and 300 K has a volume of 5 litres. If the temperature rises to 600 K at constant pressure, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Charles’ law: \(\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2}\). \(V_1 = 5 \, \text{litres}\), \(T_1 = 300 \, \text{K}\), \(T_2 = 600 \, \text{K}\). \(V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 5 \times \frac{600}{300} = 10 \, \text{litres}\).

questions.question_text: A solid has a molar specific heat capacity of \(26.5 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). How many degrees of freedom per atom does it have? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.explanation: \(C = f \times \frac{R}{2}\), \(26.5 = f \times \frac{8.31}{2}\). \(f = \frac{26.5 \times 2}{8.31} \approx 6.38 \approx 6\).

questions.question_text: A gas at 3 atm and 600 K has a density of \(1.44 \, \text{kg m}^{-3}\). What is its molecular mass? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\), 1 atm = \(1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\))
questions.explanation: \(P = \frac{\rho R T}{M}\), \(M = \frac{\rho R T}{P}\). \(P = 3 \times 1.01 \times 10^5 = 3.03 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\). \(M = \frac{1.44 \times 8.31 \times 600}{3.03 \times 10^5} = 0.0237 \, \text{kg/mol} \approx 23.7 \, \text{g/mol} \approx 24 \, \text{g/mol}\).

questions.question_text: The rms speed of oxygen molecules is 482 m/s at 300 K. What is the rms speed of helium molecules at the same temperature? (Molecular mass: \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\), He = 4 u)
questions.explanation: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\), \(\frac{v_{\text{He}}}{v_{\text{O}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{O}_2}}{m_{\text{He}}}}\). \(\frac{v_{\text{He}}}{482} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{4}} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.828\). \(v_{\text{He}} = 482 \times 2.828 \approx 1363 \, \text{m/s}\).

questions.question_text: What is the volume of 0.2 moles of an ideal gas at 1.5 atm and 227°C? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
A gas has a \(C_p\) of \(28.8 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is its \(C_v\)? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))
A wire of length \( 2 \, \text{m} \) and resistance \( 4 \, \Omega \) is stretched to \( 4 \, \text{m} \). What is the new resistance?
questions.explanation: Volume constant: \( l A = l' A' \Rightarrow A' = \frac{A}{2} \). New resistance: \( R' = \frac{\rho l'}{A'} = \frac{\rho (2l)}{\frac{A}{2}} = 4 \frac{\rho l}{A} = 4R = 4 \times 4 = 16 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: What ensures that the total voltage drop across a series circuit equals the source voltage?
questions.explanation: Kirchhoff’s loop rule (conservation of energy) ensures that the sum of potential drops across all elements in a closed loop equals the supplied voltage, as energy is conserved in the circuit.

questions.question_text: Why does the resistance of a metallic conductor increase with temperature?
questions.explanation: Resistance (\( R = \rho l / A \)) depends on resistivity (\( \rho \)), which is \( \rho = m / (n e^2 \tau) \). As temperature increases, the average time between collisions (\( \tau \)) decreases due to increased lattice vibrations, leading to higher \( \rho \) and thus higher \( R \).

questions.question_text: A nichrome wire has a resistance of \( 60 \, \Omega \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \) and \( \alpha = 1.7 \times 10^{-4} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \). What is its resistance at \( 330^\circ \text{C} \)?
A Wheatstone bridge has \( R_1 = 14 \, \Omega \), \( R_2 = 28 \, \Omega \), \( R_3 = 10 \, \Omega \). What is \( R_4 \) for balance?
questions.explanation: Balance condition: \( \frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{R_3}{R_4} \). Substitute: \( \frac{14}{28} = \frac{10}{R_4} \). Solve: \( 0.5 = \frac{10}{R_4} \Rightarrow R_4 = \frac{10}{0.5} = 20 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: In a circuit with a battery and a resistor, if the internal resistance of the battery equals the external resistance, what fraction of the total power is dissipated in the external resistor?
questions.explanation: Let emf = \( \varepsilon \), internal resistance = \( r \), external resistance = \( R = r \). Total resistance = \( r + R = 2r \). Current = \( I = \varepsilon / (2r) \). Power in external resistor = \( I^2 R = (\varepsilon / 2r)^2 r = \varepsilon^2 r / (4 r^2) = \varepsilon^2 / (4 r) \). Total power = \( \varepsilon I = \varepsilon \cdot \varepsilon / (2r) = \varepsilon^2 / (2r) \). Fraction = \( (\varepsilon^2 / 4r) / (\varepsilon^2 / 2r) = 1/2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 16 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 2 \, \Omega \) internal resistance delivers a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \) to a resistor. What is the resistance of the resistor?
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage: \( V = \varepsilon - I r = 16 - 2 \times 2 = 12 \, \text{V} \). Resistance: \( R = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{12}{2} = 6 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: What causes the resistivity of a conductor to deviate from Ohm’s law at very high electric fields?
questions.explanation: At high fields, resistivity (\( \rho = m / (n e^2 \tau) \)) may change as \( \tau \) or \( n \) varies (e.g., due to electron saturation or heating), making the \( I \)-versus-\( V \) relationship non-linear and violating Ohm’s law.

questions.question_text: What causes the potential difference across a resistor to drop when current flows through it?
questions.explanation: Current through a resistor (\( I = V / R \)) causes a potential drop (\( V = I R \)) as electrical energy is converted to thermal energy due to collisions with lattice ions.

questions.question_text: A conductor has a resistivity of \( 4 \times 10^{-8} \, \Omega \text{m} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) and a temperature coefficient of \( 4 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \). What is its resistivity at \( 60^\circ \text{C} \)?
questions.explanation: Use: \( \rho_t = \rho_0 [1 + \alpha (T - T_0)] \). Given: \( \rho_0 = 4 \times 10^{-8} \, \Omega \text{m} \), \( \alpha = 4 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \), \( T = 60^\circ \text{C} \), \( T_0 = 20^\circ \text{C} \). Substitute: \( \rho_t = 4 \times 10^{-8} [1 + 4 \times 10^{-3} (60 - 20)] \). Calculate: \( \rho_t = 4 \times 10^{-8} [1 + 0.16] = 4 \times 10^{-8} \times 1.16 = 4.64 \times 10^{-8} \, \Omega \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of cross-sectional area \( 6 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}^2 \) carries a current of \( 1.8 \, \text{A} \). If \( n = 8.5 \times 10^{28} \, \text{m}^{-3} \) and \( e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \), what is the drift speed?
questions.explanation: Drift speed: \( v_d = \frac{I}{n e A} \). Substitute: \( v_d = \frac{1.8}{8.5 \times 10^{28} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 6 \times 10^{-7}} \). Calculate: \( v_d = \frac{1.8}{8.16 \times 10^3} \approx 2.21 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In a Wheatstone bridge, if the bridge is unbalanced, what determines the direction of current through the galvanometer?
questions.explanation: When unbalanced (\( R_1 / R_2 \neq R_3 / R_4 \)), the potentials at the galvanometer’s nodes differ. The current flows from the higher-potential node to the lower one, determined by the relative voltage drops across the bridge arms.

questions.question_text: A nichrome wire has a resistance of \( 80 \, \Omega \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) and \( \alpha = 1.7 \times 10^{-4} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \). What is its resistance at \( 300^\circ \text{C} \)?
In a metallic conductor, if the temperature increases significantly, what happens to the conductivity of the material?
questions.explanation: Conductivity (\( \sigma = 1 / \rho \)) is inversely proportional to resistivity (\( \rho = m / (n e^2 \tau) \)). As temperature increases, the relaxation time (\( \tau \)) decreases due to more frequent collisions, increasing \( \rho \) and thus decreasing \( \sigma \).

questions.question_text: A circuit has a \( 18 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 3 \, \Omega \) internal resistance and three resistors \( 4 \, \Omega \), \( 8 \, \Omega \), \( 16 \, \Omega \) in parallel. What is the current through the \( 8 \, \Omega \) resistor?
questions.explanation: Parallel resistance: \( \frac{1}{R_p} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{4 + 2 + 1}{16} = \frac{7}{16} \Rightarrow R_p = \frac{16}{7} \approx 2.29 \, \Omega \). Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 3 + 2.29 = 5.29 \, \Omega \). Total current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{18}{5.29} \approx 3.4 \, \text{A} \). Voltage across parallel: \( V = I R_p = 3.4 \times 2.29 \approx 7.79 \, \text{V} \). Current through \( 8 \, \Omega \): \( I_8 = \frac{V}{8} = \frac{7.79}{8} \approx 0.97 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 45 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a cubical network of 12 resistors, each \( 5 \, \Omega \). What is the total current?
questions.explanation: Equivalent resistance: \( R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{5}{6} R = \frac{5}{6} \times 5 = \frac{25}{6} \approx 4.17 \, \Omega \). Total current: \( I = \frac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{45}{\frac{25}{6}} = 45 \times \frac{6}{25} = 10.8 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A wire has a resistance of \( 30 \, \Omega \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 31.5 \, \Omega \) at \( 75^\circ \text{C} \). What is the temperature coefficient of resistivity?
questions.explanation: Use: \( R_t = R_0 [1 + \alpha (T - T_0)] \). Substitute: \( 31.5 = 30 [1 + \alpha (75 - 25)] \). Solve: \( 31.5 = 30 + 1500\alpha \Rightarrow 1500\alpha = 1.5 \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{1.5}{1500} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 10 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a \( 2 \, \Omega \) and \( 3 \, \Omega \) resistor in series. What is the power dissipated in the \( 3 \, \Omega \) resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R = 2 + 3 = 5 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{10}{5} = 2 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 R = 2^2 \times 3 = 12 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: In a circuit with a battery, if the external resistance is reduced to zero, what limits the current?
questions.explanation: When external resistance \( R = 0 \), total resistance becomes the battery’s internal resistance (\( r \)). Current is then \( I = \varepsilon / r \), limited solely by \( r \).

questions.question_text: A wire has a resistance of \( 15 \, \Omega \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 16.5 \, \Omega \) at \( 70^\circ \text{C} \). What is the temperature coefficient of resistivity?
questions.explanation: Use: \( R_t = R_0 [1 + \alpha (T - T_0)] \). Substitute: \( 16.5 = 15 [1 + \alpha (70 - 20)] \). Solve: \( 16.5 = 15 + 750\alpha \Rightarrow 750\alpha = 1.5 \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{1.5}{750} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A circuit has a \( 28 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 4 \, \Omega \) internal resistance and three resistors \( 4 \, \Omega \), \( 8 \, \Omega \), \( 16 \, \Omega \) in parallel. What is the current through the \( 8 \, \Omega \) resistor?
questions.explanation: Parallel resistance: \( \frac{1}{R_p} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{4 + 2 + 1}{16} = \frac{7}{16} \Rightarrow R_p = \frac{16}{7} \approx 2.29 \, \Omega \). Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 4 + 2.29 = 6.29 \, \Omega \). Total current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{28}{6.29} \approx 4.45 \, \text{A} \). Voltage across parallel: \( V = I R_p = 4.45 \times 2.29 \approx 10.19 \, \text{V} \). Current through \( 8 \, \Omega \): \( I_8 = \frac{V}{8} = \frac{10.19}{8} \approx 1.27 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 6 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 0.5 \, \Omega \) internal resistance is connected to a \( 5.5 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the power dissipated in the external resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 5.5 + 0.5 = 6 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{6}{6} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 R = 1^2 \times 5.5 = 5.5 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 18 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a \( 6 \, \Omega \) and \( 12 \, \Omega \) resistor in series. What is the power dissipated in the \( 6 \, \Omega \) resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R = 6 + 12 = 18 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{18}{18} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 R = 1^2 \times 6 = 6 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 10 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 1 \, \Omega \) internal resistance is connected to a \( 9 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the power dissipated in the internal resistance?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 9 + 1 = 10 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{10}{10} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 r = 1^2 \times 1 = 1 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: In a circuit with two resistors of different resistances in series, which resistor dissipates more power if the same current flows through both?
questions.explanation: Power \( P = I^2 R \). With the same current (\( I \)) in series, power is proportional to resistance (\( R \)). The resistor with higher resistance dissipates more power.

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 3 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) has a resistance of \( 5 \, \Omega \). What is the resistivity of the material?
questions.explanation: Resistance: \( R = \frac{\rho l}{A} \). Rearrange: \( \rho = \frac{R A}{l} \). Given: \( R = 5 \, \Omega \), \( A = 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \), \( l = 3 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( \rho = \frac{5 \times 3 \times 10^{-6}}{3} = 5 \times 10^{-6} \, \Omega \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A cell of emf \( 7 \, \text{V} \) and internal resistance \( 1 \, \Omega \) is connected to a \( 6 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the terminal voltage?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 6 + 1 = 7 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{7}{7} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Terminal voltage: \( V = \varepsilon - I r = 7 - 1 \times 1 = 6 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A circuit has a \( 16 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 2 \, \Omega \) internal resistance and three resistors \( 2 \, \Omega \), \( 4 \, \Omega \), \( 8 \, \Omega \) in parallel. What is the current through the \( 2 \, \Omega \) resistor?
questions.explanation: Parallel resistance: \( \frac{1}{R_p} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{4 + 2 + 1}{8} = \frac{7}{8} \Rightarrow R_p = \frac{8}{7} \approx 1.14 \, \Omega \). Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 2 + 1.14 = 3.14 \, \Omega \). Total current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{16}{3.14} \approx 5.10 \, \text{A} \). Voltage across parallel: \( V = I R_p = 5.10 \times 1.14 \approx 5.81 \, \text{V} \). Current through \( 2 \, \Omega \): \( I_2 = \frac{V}{2} = \frac{5.81}{2} \approx 2.91 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: Two cells of emf \( 2.5 \, \text{V} \) and \( 3.5 \, \text{V} \) with internal resistances \( 0.5 \, \Omega \) and \( 1 \, \Omega \) are connected in series. What is the equivalent emf?
questions.explanation: For series: \( \varepsilon_{\text{eq}} = \varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 = 2.5 + 3.5 = 6.0 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5 \, \Omega \) resistor carries a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \) for \( 10 \, \text{s} \). How much energy is dissipated as heat?
questions.explanation: Energy dissipated: \( W = I^2 R t \). Given: \( I = 2 \, \text{A} \), \( R = 5 \, \Omega \), \( t = 10 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( W = (2)^2 \times 5 \times 10 = 4 \times 50 = 200 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A Wheatstone bridge with \( R_1 = 4 \, \Omega \), \( R_2 = 8 \, \Omega \), \( R_3 = 6 \, \Omega \), \( R_4 = 12 \, \Omega \) has a \( 12 \, \text{V} \) battery across AC and a galvanometer (\( 2 \, \Omega \)) across BD. What is the current through the galvanometer?
questions.explanation: Check balance: \( \frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{4}{8} = 0.5 \), \( \frac{R_3}{R_4} = \frac{6}{12} = 0.5 \). Bridge is balanced. Since balanced, \( I_g = 0 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A circuit has a \( 12 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 1 \, \Omega \) internal resistance and two resistors \( 2 \, \Omega \) and \( 6 \, \Omega \) in parallel. What is the total current?
questions.explanation: Parallel resistance: \( \frac{1}{R_p} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3 + 1}{6} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow R_p = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5 \, \Omega \). Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 1 + 1.5 = 2.5 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{12}{2.5} = 4.8 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A wire has a resistance of \( 12 \, \Omega \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 13.2 \, \Omega \) at \( 85^\circ \text{C} \). What is the temperature coefficient of resistivity?
questions.explanation: Use: \( R_t = R_0 [1 + \alpha (T - T_0)] \). Substitute: \( 13.2 = 12 [1 + \alpha (85 - 25)] \). Solve: \( 13.2 = 12 + 720\alpha \Rightarrow 720\alpha = 1.2 \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{1.2}{720} \approx 1.67 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 12 \, \Omega \) resistor dissipates \( 48 \, \text{W} \) of power. What is the voltage across it?
questions.explanation: Power: \( P = \frac{V^2}{R} \). Rearrange: \( V = \sqrt{P R} \). Substitute: \( V = \sqrt{48 \times 12} = \sqrt{576} = 24 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A Wheatstone bridge with \( R_1 = 16 \, \Omega \), \( R_2 = 32 \, \Omega \), \( R_3 = 24 \, \Omega \), \( R_4 = 48 \, \Omega \) has a \( 20 \, \text{V} \) battery across AC and a galvanometer (\( 5 \, \Omega \)) across BD. What is the current through the galvanometer?
questions.explanation: Check balance: \( \frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{16}{32} = 0.5 \), \( \frac{R_3}{R_4} = \frac{24}{48} = 0.5 \). Bridge is balanced. Since balanced, \( I_g = 0 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 18 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a cubical network of 12 resistors, each \( 3 \, \Omega \). What is the total current?
questions.explanation: Equivalent resistance: \( R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{5}{6} R = \frac{5}{6} \times 3 = 2.5 \, \Omega \). Total current: \( I = \frac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{18}{2.5} = 7.2 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A Wheatstone bridge with \( R_1 = 10 \, \Omega \), \( R_2 = 20 \, \Omega \), \( R_3 = 15 \, \Omega \), \( R_4 = 30 \, \Omega \) has a \( 15 \, \text{V} \) battery across AC and a galvanometer (\( 10 \, \Omega \)) across BD. What is the current through the galvanometer?
questions.explanation: Check balance: \( \frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{10}{20} = 0.5 \), \( \frac{R_3}{R_4} = \frac{15}{30} = 0.5 \). Bridge is balanced. Since balanced, \( I_g = 0 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: Why does the drift velocity of electrons in a conductor remain much smaller than their thermal velocity?
questions.explanation: Drift velocity (\( v_d = e E \tau / m \)) is small because \( E \) is typically weak and \( \tau \) is short due to frequent collisions, whereas thermal velocity arises from random motion at high speeds (proportional to \( \sqrt{k T / m} \)), unaffected by the field.

questions.question_text: A cell of emf \( 5 \, \text{V} \) and internal resistance \( 0.5 \, \Omega \) is connected to a \( 4.5 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the current in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 4.5 + 0.5 = 5 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{5}{5} = 1 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a non-ohmic device, like a diode, exhibit a non-linear current-voltage relationship?
questions.explanation: In a diode, resistance depends on the direction and magnitude of the applied voltage due to its semiconductor junction properties. Forward bias reduces resistance, while reverse bias increases it, leading to a non-linear \( I \)-versus-\( V \) curve.

questions.question_text: A \( 24 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a cubical network of 12 resistors, each \( 4 \, \Omega \). What is the total current?
questions.explanation: Equivalent resistance: \( R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{5}{6} R = \frac{5}{6} \times 4 = \frac{20}{6} = \frac{10}{3} \approx 3.33 \, \Omega \). Total current: \( I = \frac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{24}{\frac{10}{3}} = 24 \times \frac{3}{10} = 7.2 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 20 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 2 \, \Omega \) internal resistance delivers a current of \( 2.5 \, \text{A} \) to a resistor. What is the resistance of the resistor?
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage: \( V = \varepsilon - I r = 20 - 2.5 \times 2 = 15 \, \text{V} \). Resistance: \( R = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{15}{2.5} = 6 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A \( 4 \, \Omega \) resistor dissipates \( 16 \, \text{W} \) of power. What is the voltage across it?
questions.explanation: Power: \( P = \frac{V^2}{R} \). Rearrange: \( V = \sqrt{P R} \). Substitute: \( V = \sqrt{16 \times 4} = \sqrt{64} = 8 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire carries \( 3 \, \text{A} \) with a drift speed of \( 9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{m/s} \). If \( n = 8.5 \times 10^{28} \, \text{m}^{-3} \) and \( e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \), what is the cross-sectional area?
questions.explanation: Drift speed: \( v_d = \frac{I}{n e A} \). Rearrange: \( A = \frac{I}{n e v_d} \). Substitute: \( A = \frac{3}{8.5 \times 10^{28} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 9 \times 10^{-5}} \). Calculate: \( A = \frac{3}{1.224 \times 10^5} \approx 2.45 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 15 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a \( 3 \, \Omega \) and \( 12 \, \Omega \) resistor in series. What is the power dissipated in the \( 12 \, \Omega \) resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R = 3 + 12 = 15 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{15}{15} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 R = 1^2 \times 12 = 12 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 8 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 1 \, \Omega \) internal resistance is connected to a \( 7 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the power dissipated in the internal resistance?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 7 + 1 = 8 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{8}{8} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 r = 1^2 \times 1 = 1 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 12 \, \Omega \) resistor dissipates \( 48 \, \text{W} \) of power. What is the current through it?
questions.explanation: Power: \( P = I^2 R \). Rearrange: \( I = \sqrt{\frac{P}{R}} \). Substitute: \( I = \sqrt{\frac{48}{12}} = \sqrt{4} = 2 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 5 \, \text{m} \) and resistance \( 20 \, \Omega \) is stretched to \( 10 \, \text{m} \). What is the new resistance?
questions.explanation: Volume constant: \( l A = l' A' \Rightarrow A' = \frac{A}{2} \). New resistance: \( R' = \frac{\rho l'}{A'} = \frac{\rho (2l)}{\frac{A}{2}} = 4 \frac{\rho l}{A} = 4R = 4 \times 20 = 80 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A \( 20 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a \( 5 \, \Omega \) and \( 15 \, \Omega \) resistor in series. What is the power dissipated in the \( 15 \, \Omega \) resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R = 5 + 15 = 20 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{20}{20} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 R = 1^2 \times 15 = 15 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: A Wheatstone bridge with \( R_1 = 9 \, \Omega \), \( R_2 = 18 \, \Omega \), \( R_3 = 12 \, \Omega \), \( R_4 = 24 \, \Omega \) has a \( 20 \, \text{V} \) battery across AC and a galvanometer (\( 5 \, \Omega \)) across BD. What is the current through the galvanometer?
questions.explanation: Check balance: \( \frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{9}{18} = 0.5 \), \( \frac{R_3}{R_4} = \frac{12}{24} = 0.5 \). Bridge is balanced. Since balanced, \( I_g = 0 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 5 \, \text{m} \) and resistance \( 10 \, \Omega \) is stretched to \( 10 \, \text{m} \). What is the new resistance?
questions.explanation: Volume constant: \( l A = l' A' \Rightarrow A' = \frac{A}{2} \). New resistance: \( R' = \frac{\rho l'}{A'} = \frac{\rho (2l)}{\frac{A}{2}} = 4 \frac{\rho l}{A} = 4R = 4 \times 10 = 40 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A conductor has a resistivity of \( 9 \times 10^{-8} \, \Omega \text{m} \) and \( \alpha = 4 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is its resistivity at \( 60^\circ \text{C} \)?
questions.explanation: Use: \( \rho_t = \rho_0 [1 + \alpha (T - T_0)] \). Substitute: \( \rho_t = 9 \times 10^{-8} [1 + 4 \times 10^{-3} (60 - 20)] \). Calculate: \( \rho_t = 9 \times 10^{-8} [1 + 0.16] = 9 \times 10^{-8} \times 1.16 = 1.044 \times 10^{-7} \, \Omega \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A Wheatstone bridge with \( R_1 = 12 \, \Omega \), \( R_2 = 24 \, \Omega \), \( R_3 = 18 \, \Omega \), \( R_4 = 36 \, \Omega \) has a \( 12 \, \text{V} \) battery across AC and a galvanometer (\( 5 \, \Omega \)) across BD. What is the current through the galvanometer?
questions.explanation: Check balance: \( \frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{12}{24} = 0.5 \), \( \frac{R_3}{R_4} = \frac{18}{36} = 0.5 \). Bridge is balanced. Since balanced, \( I_g = 0 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A nichrome wire has a resistance of \( 70 \, \Omega \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \) and \( \alpha = 1.7 \times 10^{-4} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \). What is its resistance at \( 270^\circ \text{C} \)?
A \( 14 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 2 \, \Omega \) internal resistance delivers a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \) to a resistor. What is the resistance of the resistor?
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage: \( V = \varepsilon - I r = 14 - 2 \times 2 = 10 \, \text{V} \). Resistance: \( R = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{10}{2} = 5 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: Why does a conductor’s current density increase when its length is halved while keeping the potential difference constant?
questions.explanation: Resistance \( R = \rho l / A \). Halving length (\( l' = l/2 \)) halves \( R \) (\( R' = R/2 \)). Current \( I = V / R \), so \( I' = V / (R/2) = 2I \). Current density \( j = I / A \), so \( j' = 2I / A = 2j \).

questions.question_text: Two cells of emf \( 4 \, \text{V} \) and \( 5 \, \text{V} \) with internal resistances \( 0.5 \, \Omega \) and \( 1 \, \Omega \) are connected in series with a \( 5.5 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the current through the circuit?
questions.explanation: Equivalent emf: \( \varepsilon_{\text{eq}} = 4 + 5 = 9 \, \text{V} \). Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 0.5 + 1 + 5.5 = 7 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon_{\text{eq}}}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{9}{7} \approx 1.29 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 15 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a \( 3 \, \Omega \) and \( 9 \, \Omega \) resistor in series. What is the power dissipated in the \( 9 \, \Omega \) resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R = 3 + 9 = 12 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{15}{12} = 1.25 \, \text{A} \). Power: \( P = I^2 R = (1.25)^2 \times 9 = 1.5625 \times 9 = 14.06 \, \text{W} \approx 14 \, \text{W} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a battery’s emf remain constant even when it delivers a large current?
questions.explanation: Emf is the potential difference across the battery terminals when no current flows, determined by the chemical reactions inside. It’s an intrinsic property, independent of current, though terminal voltage drops due to internal resistance.

questions.question_text: A nichrome wire has a resistance of \( 90 \, \Omega \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) and \( \alpha = 1.7 \times 10^{-4} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \). What is its resistance at \( 260^\circ \text{C} \)?
A wire of length \( 2 \, \text{m} \) and resistance \( 5 \, \Omega \) is stretched to \( 4 \, \text{m} \). What is the new resistance?
questions.explanation: Volume constant: \( l A = l' A' \Rightarrow A' = \frac{A}{2} \). New resistance: \( R' = \frac{\rho l'}{A'} = \frac{\rho (2l)}{\frac{A}{2}} = 4 \frac{\rho l}{A} = 4R = 4 \times 5 = 20 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: Two cells in parallel have emf \( 12 \, \text{V} \) and \( 3 \, \text{V} \) with internal resistances \( 4 \, \Omega \) and \( 1 \, \Omega \). What is the equivalent emf?
questions.explanation: For parallel: \( \varepsilon_{\text{eq}} = \frac{\varepsilon_1 r_2 + \varepsilon_2 r_1}{r_1 + r_2} \). Substitute: \( \varepsilon_{\text{eq}} = \frac{12 \times 1 + 3 \times 4}{4 + 1} = \frac{12 + 12}{5} = \frac{24}{5} = 4.8 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 10 \, \text{V} \) battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to a cubical network of 12 resistors, each \( 1.5 \, \Omega \). What is the current through one edge from a corner?
questions.explanation: Equivalent resistance: \( R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{5}{6} R = \frac{5}{6} \times 1.5 = 1.25 \, \Omega \). Total current: \( I_{\text{total}} = \frac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{10}{1.25} = 8 \, \text{A} \). Corner current: \( I = \frac{I_{\text{total}}}{3} = \frac{8}{3} \approx 2.67 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of cross-sectional area \( 8 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}^2 \) carries a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \). If \( n = 8.5 \times 10^{28} \, \text{m}^{-3} \) and \( e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \), what is the drift speed?
questions.explanation: Drift speed: \( v_d = \frac{I}{n e A} \). Substitute: \( v_d = \frac{2}{8.5 \times 10^{28} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 8 \times 10^{-7}} \). Calculate: \( v_d = \frac{2}{1.088 \times 10^4} \approx 1.84 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A wire has a resistance of \( 24 \, \Omega \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 25.8 \, \Omega \) at \( 75^\circ \text{C} \). What is the temperature coefficient of resistivity?
questions.explanation: Use: \( R_t = R_0 [1 + \alpha (T - T_0)] \). Substitute: \( 25.8 = 24 [1 + \alpha (75 - 25)] \). Solve: \( 25.8 = 24 + 1200\alpha \Rightarrow 1200\alpha = 1.8 \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{1.8}{1200} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A nichrome wire has a resistance of \( 60 \, \Omega \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) and \( \alpha = 1.7 \times 10^{-4} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \). What is its resistance at \( 225^\circ \text{C} \)?

A conductor has a resistivity of \( 1.2 \times 10^{-7} \, \Omega \text{m} \) and \( \alpha = 4 \times 10^{-3} \, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is its resistivity at \( 80^\circ \text{C} \)?
A \( 18 \, \text{V} \) battery with \( 3 \, \Omega \) internal resistance delivers a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \) to a resistor. What is the resistance of the resistor?
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage: \( V = \varepsilon - I r = 18 - 2 \times 3 = 12 \, \text{V} \). Resistance: \( R = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{12}{2} = 6 \, \Omega \).

questions.question_text: A cell of emf \( 10 \, \text{V} \) and internal resistance \( 1 \, \Omega \) is connected to a \( 9 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the terminal voltage?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 9 + 1 = 10 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{10}{10} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Terminal voltage: \( V = \varepsilon - I r = 10 - 1 \times 1 = 9 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A cell of emf \( 6 \, \text{V} \) and internal resistance \( 1.5 \, \Omega \) is connected to a \( 4.5 \, \Omega \) resistor. What is the terminal voltage?
questions.explanation: Total resistance: \( R_{\text{total}} = 4.5 + 1.5 = 6 \, \Omega \). Current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{6}{6} = 1 \, \text{A} \). Terminal voltage: \( V = \varepsilon - I r = 6 - 1 \times 1.5 = 4.5 \, \text{V} \).
