questions.question_text: A circular coil of radius 5 cm and 100 turns is rotated in a 0.1 T magnetic field at 50 rad/s. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: Maximum emf: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega \). \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.05)^2 = 0.00785 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = 100 \times 0.1 \times 0.00785 \times 50 = 3.925 \, \text{V} \approx 3.93 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of 0.3 m × 0.45 m moves out of a 0.5 T field at 0.9 m/s along its shorter side. What is the emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = B l v \), \( l = 0.45 \, \text{m} \). \( \varepsilon = 0.5 \times 0.45 \times 0.9 = 0.2026 \, \text{V} \approx 0.203 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with mutual inductance 0.22 H has a current change of 7 A/s in the primary coil. What is the induced emf in the secondary coil?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{dI}{dt} = 0.22 \times 7 = 1.54 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil with \( L = 0.2 \, \text{H} \) has its current increased from 0 to 5 A in 0.5 s. What is the energy stored?
A circular coil of radius 8 cm and 240 turns rotates at 45 rad/s in a 0.04 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.08)^2 = 0.0201 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 240 \times 0.04 \times 0.0201 \times 45 = 8.676 \, \text{V} \approx 8.68 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 140 turns and area 0.045 m² is in a field that decreases from 0.07 T to 0 in 0.35 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.07 \times 0.045 = 0.00315 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 140 \times \frac{0.00315}{0.35} = 140 \times 0.009 = 1.26 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 600 turns per meter and area 0.012 m² has a current change from 4 A to 1 A in 0.2 s. What is the self-induced emf? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (600)^2 \times 0.012 \times 1 = 0.00543 \, \text{H} \). \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = 0.00543 \times \frac{1 - 4}{0.2} = 0.00543 \times (-15) = 0.08145 \, \text{V} \approx 0.081 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A rod of length 0.8 m moves at 1.5 m/s in a 0.4 T field perpendicular to its length. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = B l v = 0.4 \times 0.8 \times 1.5 = 0.48 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A wheel with 4 spokes of 0.5 m each rotates at 48 rpm in a 0.8 T field. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi \times \frac{48}{60} = 1.6\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.8 \times 1.6\pi \times (0.5)^2 = 0.5024 \, \text{V} \approx 0.5 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of sides 15 cm and 6 cm moves out of a 0.4 T field at 1.5 m/s perpendicular to the shorter side. What is the motional emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = B l v \), \( l = 0.15 \, \text{m} \). \( \varepsilon = 0.4 \times 0.15 \times 1.5 = 0.09 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 800 turns/m and area 0.01 m² has \( \mu_r = 1 \). What is its self-inductance? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_r \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 1 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (800)^2 \times 0.01 \times 1 = 0.00804 \, \text{H} \approx 0.008 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with mutual inductance 0.3 H has a current change of 5 A/s in the primary coil. What is the induced emf in the secondary coil?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{dI}{dt} = 0.3 \times 5 = 1.5 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A rod rotates at 20 rad/s in a 0.4 T field. If the length from the axis to the tip is 0.5 m, what is the emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.4 \times 20 \times (0.5)^2 = 5 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: When a bar magnet is moved towards a stationary coil, the induced current flows in a direction that opposes the magnet’s motion. This is an example of which fundamental principle?
questions.explanation: The phenomenon where induced current opposes the change causing it is Lenz’s law, which ensures conservation of energy by resisting the magnet’s motion through a repulsive force.

questions.question_text: A conducting rod is moved perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The emf induced across its ends depends on which of the following factors?
options: Magnetic field strength, length of the rod, and velocity
Mass of the rod and magnetic field
questions.explanation: The motional emf is given by \( \varepsilon = B l v \), where \( B \) is the magnetic field strength, \( l \) is the length of the rod, and \( v \) is its velocity, all of which are critical factors.

questions.question_text: A metal ring is placed near a solenoid. When an AC current flows through the solenoid, the ring experiences a force. This is primarily due to what?
options: Interaction of induced currents with the magnetic field
questions.explanation: The AC current creates a varying magnetic field, inducing currents in the ring that generate an opposing field, leading to a repulsive or attractive force based on Lenz’s law.

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of sides 30 cm and 12 cm moves out of a 0.6 T field at 1 m/s perpendicular to the shorter side. What is the motional emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = B l v \), \( l = 0.3 \, \text{m} \). \( \varepsilon = 0.6 \times 0.3 \times 1 = 0.18 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil is rotated in a magnetic field such that the flux through it changes from maximum to zero. At what position does the rate of change of flux reach its peak?
questions.explanation: The rate of change of flux (\( \frac{d\Phi}{dt} = N B A \omega \sin\theta \)) is maximum when \( \sin\theta = 1 \), i.e., at \( \theta = 90^\circ \), where the coil is perpendicular to the field.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet is moved towards a coil of 50 turns at a constant speed. The magnetic flux through the coil increases from 0 to 0.02 Wb in 0.1 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf in the coil?
questions.explanation: Given: \( N = 50 \), \( \Delta \Phi_B = 0.02 - 0 = 0.02 \, \text{Wb} \), \( \Delta t = 0.1 \, \text{s} \). Using Faraday's law: \( \varepsilon = -N \frac{\Delta \Phi_B}{\Delta t} \). \( \varepsilon = 50 \times \frac{0.02}{0.1} = 50 \times 0.2 = 10 \, \text{V} \). Magnitude of emf = 10 V.

questions.question_text: A circular coil of radius 7 cm and 180 turns rotates at 20 rad/s in a 0.07 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.07)^2 = 0.0154 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 180 \times 0.07 \times 0.0154 \times 20 = 3.88 \, \text{V} \approx 3.9 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A square loop of side 15 cm rotates at 15 rad/s in a 0.2 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = (0.15)^2 = 0.0225 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 1 \times 0.2 \times 0.0225 \times 15 = 0.0675 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 300 turns rotates at 100 rad/s in a 0.05 T field. If the area is 0.01 m², what is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 300 \times 0.05 \times 0.01 \times 100 = 15 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A square loop of side 20 cm is rotated in a 0.2 T field at 10 rad/s. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega \), \( N = 1 \), \( A = (0.2)^2 = 0.04 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = 1 \times 0.2 \times 0.04 \times 10 = 0.08 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A conducting loop is rotated in a non-uniform magnetic field. The induced emf is more complex than in a uniform field because of what factor?
questions.explanation: In a non-uniform field, the magnetic field strength varies across the loop, causing the flux change rate to depend on position, leading to a non-sinusoidal emf.

questions.question_text: A coil of 160 turns and area 0.06 m² is in a field that decreases from 0.08 T to 0 in 0.4 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.08 \times 0.06 = 0.0048 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 160 \times \frac{0.0048}{0.4} = 160 \times 0.012 = 1.92 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 750 turns/m and area 0.02 m² has \( \mu_r = 1 \). What is its self-inductance? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_r \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 1 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (750)^2 \times 0.02 \times 1 = 0.01414 \, \text{H} \approx 0.014 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 550 turns and length 1.1 m induces an emf of 1.65 V in a nearby coil when its current changes from 0 to 3 A in 0.3 s. What is the mutual inductance?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 3 - 0 = 3 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.3 \, \text{s} \). \( M = \frac{\varepsilon}{\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}} = \frac{1.65}{\frac{3}{0.3}} = \frac{1.65}{10} = 0.165 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 90 turns and area 0.03 m² is in a field that increases from 0 to 0.06 T in 0.3 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.06 \times 0.03 = 0.0018 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 90 \times \frac{0.0018}{0.3} = 90 \times 0.006 = 0.54 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil is placed in a magnetic field that increases in strength. The energy stored in the coil’s magnetic field comes from what source?
options: Work done by an external source
questions.explanation: The energy stored (\( \frac{1}{2} L I^2 \)) comes from the work done by the external source (e.g., a battery) against the back emf to establish the current.

questions.question_text: A coil of self-inductance 0.8 H has its current decreased from 6 A to 3 A in 0.2 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 3 - 6 = -3 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.2 \, \text{s} \). \( \varepsilon = 0.8 \times \frac{-3}{0.2} = 0.8 \times (-15) = -12 \, \text{V} \), magnitude = 12 V.

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 900 turns/m and area 0.015 m² has \( \mu_r = 2 \). What is its self-inductance? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_r \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 2 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (900)^2 \times 0.015 \times 1 = 0.0305 \, \text{H} \approx 0.03 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A square loop of side 18 cm rotates at 10 rad/s in a 0.25 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = (0.18)^2 = 0.0324 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 1 \times 0.25 \times 0.0324 \times 10 = 0.081 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A loop of 0.45 m × 0.2 m moves out of a 0.6 T field at 1.5 m/s along its longer side. How long does the emf last?
questions.explanation: Time = distance/velocity, distance = width along motion = 0.2 m. \( t = \frac{0.2}{1.5} = 0.1333 \, \text{s} \approx 0.13 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius 11 cm is deformed into a straight wire in a 0.2 T field in 0.5 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: Initial flux: \( \Phi = B A = 0.2 \times \pi \times (0.11)^2 = 0.0076 \, \text{Wb} \). Final flux = 0. \( \varepsilon = \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \frac{0.0076}{0.5} = 0.0152 \, \text{V} \approx 0.015 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 220 turns rotates at 70 rad/s in a 0.05 T field. If the area is 0.025 m², what is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 220 \times 0.05 \times 0.025 \times 70 = 19.25 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of sides 40 cm and 20 cm moves out of a 0.9 T field at 1 m/s perpendicular to the longer side. What is the motional emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = B l v \), \( l = 0.2 \, \text{m} \). \( \varepsilon = 0.9 \times 0.2 \times 1 = 0.18 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 250 turns and length 0.8 m induces an emf of 0.75 V in a nearby coil when its current changes from 0 to 2.5 A in 0.25 s. What is the mutual inductance?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 2.5 - 0 = 2.5 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.25 \, \text{s} \). \( M = \frac{\varepsilon}{\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}} = \frac{0.75}{\frac{2.5}{0.25}} = \frac{0.75}{10} = 0.075 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 100 turns and area 0.02 m² is rotated at 50 Hz in a 0.05 T field. What is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi v = 2\pi \times 50 = 100\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 100 \times 0.05 \times 0.02 \times 100\pi = 31.4 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 450 turns per meter and area 0.018 m² has a current change from 5 A to 2 A in 0.15 s. What is the self-induced emf? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (450)^2 \times 0.018 \times 1 = 0.00458 \, \text{H} \). \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = 0.00458 \times \frac{2 - 5}{0.15} = 0.00458 \times (-20) = 0.0916 \, \text{V} \approx 0.092 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil with \( L = 0.4 \, \text{H} \) has its current increased from 0 to 7 A in 0.7 s. What is the energy stored?
A circular coil of radius 9 cm and 200 turns rotates at 50 rad/s in a 0.03 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.09)^2 = 0.0254 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 200 \times 0.03 \times 0.0254 \times 50 = 7.62 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 150 turns and area 0.05 m² is in a field that increases from 0 to 0.06 T in 0.3 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.06 \times 0.05 = 0.003 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 150 \times \frac{0.003}{0.3} = 150 \times 0.01 = 1.5 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 280 turns rotates at 80 rad/s in a 0.06 T field. If the area is 0.01 m², what is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 280 \times 0.06 \times 0.01 \times 80 = 13.44 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil is placed near a current-carrying solenoid. The induced emf in the coil is zero when the solenoid’s current is in what state?
questions.explanation: A constant current produces a steady magnetic field, resulting in no change in flux through the coil and thus no induced emf.

questions.question_text: A coil of 130 turns experiences a magnetic flux change from 0 to 0.06 Wb in 0.12 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta \Phi = 0.06 \, \text{Wb} \), \( \Delta t = 0.12 \, \text{s} \), \( N = 130 \). \( \varepsilon = 130 \times \frac{0.06}{0.12} = 130 \times 0.5 = 65 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A conducting loop is rotated in a uniform magnetic field. The induced emf depends on the rate of change of what physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Faraday’s law states that the induced emf is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop, which varies as the loop rotates.

questions.question_text: A coil of 50 turns and area 0.06 m² is in a 0.15 T field that drops to zero in 0.3 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.15 \times 0.06 = 0.009 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 50 \times \frac{0.009}{0.3} = 50 \times 0.03 = 1.5 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 200 turns is placed in a field that decreases from 0.05 T to 0 in 0.4 s. If the area is 0.02 m², what is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.05 \times 0.02 = 0.001 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 200 \times \frac{0.001}{0.4} = 0.5 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil is placed near a current-carrying wire. If the current in the wire is suddenly switched off, what happens to the magnetic flux through the coil?
questions.explanation: When the current is switched off, the magnetic field due to the wire collapses, reducing the magnetic flux through the coil from some value to zero.

questions.question_text: A coil of 150 turns and area 0.01 m² is rotated at 40 Hz in a 0.06 T field. What is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi v = 2\pi \times 40 = 80\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 150 \times 0.06 \times 0.01 \times 80\pi = 22.62 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A conducting loop is twisted in a uniform magnetic field. The induced emf arises primarily from what change?
options: Change in flux due to orientation
questions.explanation: Twisting changes the orientation of the loop’s area vector relative to the field, altering the magnetic flux and inducing an emf.

questions.question_text: A coil of 50 turns has an area of 0.03 m² in a 0.2 T field. If the field drops to zero in 0.1 s, what is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.2 \times 0.03 = 0.006 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 50 \times \frac{0.006}{0.1} = 3 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A rod of length 0.6 m moves at 2.5 m/s in a 0.25 T field perpendicular to its length. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = B l v = 0.25 \times 0.6 \times 2.5 = 0.375 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 600 turns and length 0.8 m induces an emf of 2 V in a nearby coil when its current changes from 1 A to 4 A in 0.2 s. What is the mutual inductance?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 4 - 1 = 3 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.2 \, \text{s} \). \( M = \frac{\varepsilon}{\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}} = \frac{2}{\frac{3}{0.2}} = \frac{2}{15} = 0.133 \, \text{H} \approx 0.13 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A rod rotates at 25 rad/s in a 0.3 T field. If the length from the axis to the tip is 0.8 m, what is the emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.3 \times 25 \times (0.8)^2 = 2.4 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A loop of 0.3 m × 0.12 m moves out of a 0.4 T field at 2 m/s along its longer side. How long does the emf last?
questions.explanation: Time = distance/velocity, distance = width along motion = 0.12 m. \( t = \frac{0.12}{2} = 0.06 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A wheel with 6 spokes of 0.6 m each rotates at 45 rpm in a 0.5 T field. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi \times \frac{45}{60} = 1.5\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times 1.5\pi \times (0.6)^2 = 0.8478 \, \text{V} \approx 0.85 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of self-inductance 1.2 H has its current increased from 2 A to 6 A in 0.4 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 6 - 2 = 4 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.4 \, \text{s} \). \( \varepsilon = 1.2 \times \frac{4}{0.4} = 1.2 \times 10 = 12 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil with \( L = 0.5 \, \text{H} \) has its current increased from 0 to 6 A in 0.6 s. What is the energy stored?
A square loop of side 16 cm rotates at 18 rad/s in a 0.2 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = (0.16)^2 = 0.0256 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 1 \times 0.2 \times 0.0256 \times 18 = 0.09216 \, \text{V} \approx 0.092 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius 13 cm is deformed into a straight wire in a 0.18 T field in 0.6 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: Initial flux: \( \Phi = B A = 0.18 \times \pi \times (0.13)^2 = 0.00956 \, \text{Wb} \). Final flux = 0. \( \varepsilon = \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \frac{0.00956}{0.6} = 0.01593 \, \text{V} \approx 0.016 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 75 turns and area 0.05 m² is in a 0.12 T field that drops to zero in 0.25 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.12 \times 0.05 = 0.006 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 75 \times \frac{0.006}{0.25} = 75 \times 0.024 = 1.8 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A conducting loop is compressed in a uniform magnetic field. The induced current flows to maintain what quantity against the compression?
questions.explanation: The current opposes the decrease in flux by maintaining the original flux direction, resisting the reduction in area per Lenz’s law.

questions.question_text: A coil of self-inductance 1.8 H has its current increased from 3 A to 7 A in 0.5 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 7 - 3 = 4 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.5 \, \text{s} \). \( \varepsilon = 1.8 \times \frac{4}{0.5} = 1.8 \times 8 = 14.4 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A conducting rod moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field with constant velocity. What is true about the induced emf across its ends?
questions.explanation: The induced emf (\( \varepsilon = B l v \)) remains constant because the velocity, magnetic field, and rod length are constant, leading to a steady flux change rate.

questions.question_text: A conducting loop is stationary in a uniform magnetic field that increases in strength. The induced emf is generated by what field component?
questions.explanation: A changing magnetic field induces an electric field (per Maxwell’s equations), which drives the emf in the stationary loop.

questions.question_text: A rod rotates at 10 rad/s in a 0.5 T field. If the length from the axis to the tip is 0.6 m, what is the emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times 10 \times (0.6)^2 = 0.9 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius 14 cm is deformed into a straight wire in a 0.15 T field in 0.5 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: Initial flux: \( \Phi = B A = 0.15 \times \pi \times (0.14)^2 = 0.00923 \, \text{Wb} \). Final flux = 0. \( \varepsilon = \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \frac{0.00923}{0.5} = 0.01846 \, \text{V} \approx 0.018 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 320 turns rotates at 65 rad/s in a 0.08 T field. If the area is 0.015 m², what is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 320 \times 0.08 \times 0.015 \times 65 = 24.96 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 260 turns rotates at 75 rad/s in a 0.05 T field. If the area is 0.018 m², what is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 260 \times 0.05 \times 0.018 \times 75 = 17.55 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A conducting disc rotates in a uniform magnetic field parallel to its axis. The induced emf between the center and rim arises due to what?
questions.explanation: Rotation causes radial charge separation via the magnetic force (\( F = q v \times B \)), inducing an emf from the center to the rim.

questions.question_text: A wheel with 9 spokes of 0.5 m each rotates at 55 rpm in a 0.6 T field. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi \times \frac{55}{60} = \frac{11\pi}{6} \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.6 \times \frac{11\pi}{6} \times (0.5)^2 = 0.4328 \, \text{V} \approx 0.43 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 40 turns experiences a magnetic flux change from 0 to 0.01 Wb in 0.05 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta \Phi = 0.01 \, \text{Wb} \), \( \Delta t = 0.05 \, \text{s} \), \( N = 40 \). \( \varepsilon = 40 \times \frac{0.01}{0.05} = 40 \times 0.2 = 8 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of self-inductance 0.5 H has its current increased from 1 A to 4 A in 0.25 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 4 - 1 = 3 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.25 \, \text{s} \). \( \varepsilon = 0.5 \times \frac{3}{0.25} = 0.5 \times 12 = 6 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A conducting rod is stationary in a varying magnetic field. The induced emf in the rod arises due to which component of the force on its charges?
options: Electric field due to changing magnetic field
questions.explanation: For a stationary rod (\( v = 0 \)), the emf is induced by the electric field generated by the time-varying magnetic field, not the magnetic force (\( q v \times B \)), which requires motion.

questions.question_text: A coil with \( L = 0.1 \, \text{H} \) has its current increased from 0 to 4 A in 0.2 s. What is the energy stored?
questions.explanation: Energy: \( W = \frac{1}{2} L I^2 \). \( W = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.1 \times (4)^2 = 0.05 \times 16 = 0.8 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 350 turns and length 0.7 m induces an emf of 1.2 V in a nearby coil when its current changes from 1 A to 4 A in 0.3 s. What is the mutual inductance?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 4 - 1 = 3 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.3 \, \text{s} \). \( M = \frac{\varepsilon}{\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}} = \frac{1.2}{\frac{3}{0.3}} = \frac{1.2}{10} = 0.12 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with mutual inductance 0.2 H has a current change of 5 A/s in the primary coil. What is the induced emf in the secondary coil?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{dI}{dt} = 0.2 \times 5 = 1 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil with \( L = 0.6 \, \text{H} \) has its current increased from 0 to 5 A in 0.5 s. What is the energy stored?
A magnet is moved towards a coil, inducing a current. If the magnet’s speed increases, what happens to the induced current?
questions.explanation: Faster motion increases the rate of flux change, resulting in a larger induced emf and, assuming constant resistance, a larger induced current.

questions.question_text: A magnet is dropped through a vertical copper tube. The magnet’s fall is slower than expected due to what effect?
options: Opposing magnetic field due to induced currents
questions.explanation: The falling magnet induces currents in the copper tube, which create a magnetic field opposing the magnet’s motion, slowing its fall. This is an application of Lenz’s law.

questions.question_text: A coil of 130 turns and area 0.08 m² is in a 0.12 T field that drops to zero in 0.4 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.12 \times 0.08 = 0.0096 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 130 \times \frac{0.0096}{0.4} = 130 \times 0.024 = 3.12 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius 10 cm is deformed into a straight wire in a 0.1 T field. If the flux change occurs in 0.2 s, what is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: Initial flux: \( \Phi = B A = 0.1 \times \pi \times (0.1)^2 = 0.00314 \, \text{Wb} \). Final flux = 0. \( \varepsilon = \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \frac{0.00314}{0.2} = 0.0157 \, \text{V} \approx 0.016 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil is wound tightly around a core material. If the current through it changes rapidly, the induced emf opposing this change is an example of which phenomenon?
questions.explanation: This is self-induction, where a changing current in a coil induces an emf that opposes the change, proportional to the coil’s self-inductance.

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 400 turns and length 0.5 m induces an emf of 0.8 V in a nearby coil when its current changes from 2 A to 4 A in 0.2 s. What is the mutual inductance?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 4 - 2 = 2 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.2 \, \text{s} \). \( M = \frac{\varepsilon}{\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}} = \frac{0.8}{\frac{2}{0.2}} = \frac{0.8}{10} = 0.08 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A coil with \( L = 0.3 \, \text{H} \) has its current increased from 0 to 6 A in 0.6 s. What is the energy stored?
A circular coil of radius 8 cm and 150 turns rotates at 25 rad/s in a 0.06 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.08)^2 = 0.0201 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 150 \times 0.06 \times 0.0201 \times 25 = 4.5225 \, \text{V} \approx 4.52 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 230 turns rotates at 85 rad/s in a 0.03 T field. If the area is 0.02 m², what is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 230 \times 0.03 \times 0.02 \times 85 = 11.73 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 170 turns and area 0.07 m² is in a field that decreases from 0.1 T to 0 in 0.5 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.1 \times 0.07 = 0.007 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 170 \times \frac{0.007}{0.5} = 170 \times 0.014 = 2.38 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A wheel with 7 spokes of 0.45 m each rotates at 36 rpm in a 0.6 T field. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi \times \frac{36}{60} = 1.2\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.6 \times 1.2\pi \times (0.45)^2 = 0.383 \, \text{V} \approx 0.38 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A square loop of side 20 cm rotates at 20 rad/s in a 0.15 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = (0.2)^2 = 0.04 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 1 \times 0.15 \times 0.04 \times 20 = 0.12 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius 12 cm is deformed into a straight wire in a 0.2 T field in 0.5 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: Initial flux: \( \Phi = B A = 0.2 \times \pi \times (0.12)^2 = 0.00904 \, \text{Wb} \). Final flux = 0. \( \varepsilon = \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \frac{0.00904}{0.5} = 0.01808 \, \text{V} \approx 0.018 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 70 turns experiences a magnetic flux change from 0 to 0.02 Wb in 0.04 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta \Phi = 0.02 \, \text{Wb} \), \( \Delta t = 0.04 \, \text{s} \), \( N = 70 \). \( \varepsilon = 70 \times \frac{0.02}{0.04} = 70 \times 0.5 = 35 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 500 turns per meter and area 0.01 m² has a current change from 3 A to 0 A in 0.5 s. What is the self-induced emf? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (500)^2 \times 0.01 \times 1 = 0.00314 \, \text{H} \). \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = 0.00314 \times \frac{0 - 3}{0.5} = 0.01884 \, \text{V} \approx 0.019 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid’s current is switched off suddenly. What causes sensitive instruments nearby to be at risk of damage?
questions.explanation: The sudden drop in current induces a high emf due to self-inductance, which can generate significant currents or voltages in nearby circuits, risking damage.

questions.question_text: A coil of self-inductance 1.0 H has its current decreased from 5 A to 2 A in 0.15 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 2 - 5 = -3 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.15 \, \text{s} \). \( \varepsilon = 1.0 \times \frac{-3}{0.15} = 1.0 \times (-20) = -20 \, \text{V} \), magnitude = 20 V.

questions.question_text: A coil of 130 turns and area 0.03 m² is rotated at 30 Hz in a 0.08 T field. What is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi v = 2\pi \times 30 = 60\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 130 \times 0.08 \times 0.03 \times 60\pi = 58.62 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A wheel with 5 spokes of 0.4 m each rotates at 30 rpm in a 0.7 T field. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi \times \frac{30}{60} = \pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.7 \times \pi \times (0.4)^2 = 0.1759 \, \text{V} \approx 0.176 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC generator, slip rings are used instead of a split ring commutator. What is the primary reason for this design choice?
options: To convert AC to DC output
questions.explanation: Slip rings allow continuous contact with the coil, preserving the alternating nature of the emf, unlike a split ring commutator which rectifies it to DC.

questions.question_text: A coil of 80 turns is placed in a magnetic field that increases from 0 to 0.03 Wb/m² in 0.2 s. If the coil area is 0.05 m², what is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: Flux change: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.03 \times 0.05 = 0.0015 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 80 \times \frac{0.0015}{0.2} = 80 \times 0.0075 = 0.6 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius 15 cm is deformed into a straight wire in a 0.15 T field in 0.6 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: Initial flux: \( \Phi = B A = 0.15 \times \pi \times (0.15)^2 = 0.0106 \, \text{Wb} \). Final flux = 0. \( \varepsilon = \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \frac{0.0106}{0.6} = 0.01767 \, \text{V} \approx 0.018 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A conducting loop is placed in a magnetic field that remains constant in magnitude and direction. No emf is induced because of what condition?
questions.explanation: Emf is induced only when magnetic flux changes. A constant field with a stationary loop results in no flux change, hence no emf.

questions.question_text: A coil of 130 turns and area 0.04 m² is in a field that increases from 0 to 0.05 T in 0.2 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.05 \times 0.04 = 0.002 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 130 \times \frac{0.002}{0.2} = 130 \times 0.01 = 1.3 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 550 turns per meter and area 0.016 m² has a current drop from 7 A to 4 A in 0.3 s. What is the self-induced emf? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (550)^2 \times 0.016 \times 1 = 0.00608 \, \text{H} \). \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = 0.00608 \times \frac{4 - 7}{0.3} = 0.00608 \times (-10) = 0.0608 \, \text{V} \approx 0.061 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 700 turns/m and area 0.008 m² has \( \mu_r = 1 \). What is its self-inductance? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_r \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 1 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (700)^2 \times 0.008 \times 1 = 0.00492 \, \text{H} \approx 0.005 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 1000 turns/m and area 0.01 m² has \( \mu_r = 2 \). What is its self-inductance? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_r \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 2 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (1000)^2 \times 0.01 \times 1 = 0.02513 \, \text{H} \approx 0.025 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 120 turns and area 0.04 m² is in a 0.09 T field that drops to zero in 0.3 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.09 \times 0.04 = 0.0036 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 120 \times \frac{0.0036}{0.3} = 120 \times 0.012 = 1.44 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 700 turns per meter and area 0.015 m² has a current drop from 8 A to 5 A in 0.3 s. What is the self-induced emf? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (700)^2 \times 0.015 \times 1 = 0.00923 \, \text{H} \). \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = 0.00923 \times \frac{5 - 8}{0.3} = 0.00923 \times (-10) = 0.0923 \, \text{V} \approx 0.092 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 300 turns rotates at 70 rad/s in a 0.07 T field. If the area is 0.012 m², what is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 300 \times 0.07 \times 0.012 \times 70 = 17.64 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A loop of 0.2 m × 0.1 m moves out of a 0.5 T field at 2 m/s along its longer side. How long does the emf last?
questions.explanation: Time = distance/velocity, distance = width along motion = 0.1 m. \( t = \frac{0.1}{2} = 0.05 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A wheel with 8 spokes of 0.55 m each rotates at 50 rpm in a 0.4 T field. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi \times \frac{50}{60} = \frac{5\pi}{3} \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.4 \times \frac{5\pi}{3} \times (0.55)^2 = 0.3166 \, \text{V} \approx 0.317 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 170 turns and area 0.015 m² is rotated at 35 Hz in a 0.1 T field. What is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi v = 2\pi \times 35 = 70\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 170 \times 0.1 \times 0.015 \times 70\pi = 56.03 \, \text{V} \approx 56 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A rod rotates at 15 rad/s in a 0.3 T field. If the length from the axis to the tip is 0.4 m, what is the emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 \). \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.3 \times 15 \times (0.4)^2 = 0.36 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil with high self-inductance is suddenly disconnected from a battery. The resulting high voltage spike is due to what?
questions.explanation: The rapid current drop induces a large back emf (\( \varepsilon = -L \frac{dI}{dt} \)) due to self-inductance, causing a voltage spike.

questions.question_text: A conducting loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field with its plane parallel to the field lines. Why is no emf induced when the field strength changes?
options: Due to zero flux through the loop
questions.explanation: When the plane is parallel to the field, the flux through the loop is zero (\( \Phi = B A \cos 90^\circ = 0 \)), so changing the field strength does not alter the flux, resulting in no emf.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with mutual inductance 0.25 H has a current change of 4 A/s in the primary coil. What is the induced emf in the secondary coil?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{dI}{dt} = 0.25 \times 4 = 1 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of 0.1 m × 0.2 m moves out of a 0.4 T field at 0.5 m/s along its shorter side. What is the emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = B l v \), \( l = 0.2 \, \text{m} \). \( \varepsilon = 0.4 \times 0.2 \times 0.5 = 0.04 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of self-inductance 0.6 H has its current decreased from 4 A to 1 A in 0.15 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 1 - 4 = -3 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.15 \, \text{s} \). \( \varepsilon = 0.6 \times \frac{-3}{0.15} = 0.6 \times (-20) = -12 \, \text{V} \), magnitude = 12 V.

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 450 turns and length 0.9 m induces an emf of 1.8 V in a nearby coil when its current changes from 2 A to 5 A in 0.3 s. What is the mutual inductance?
questions.explanation: \( \varepsilon = M \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \). \( \Delta I = 5 - 2 = 3 \, \text{A} \), \( \Delta t = 0.3 \, \text{s} \). \( M = \frac{\varepsilon}{\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}} = \frac{1.8}{\frac{3}{0.3}} = \frac{1.8}{10} = 0.18 \, \text{H} \).

questions.question_text: A circular coil of radius 10 cm and 220 turns rotates at 60 rad/s in a 0.02 T field. What is the maximum emf induced?
questions.explanation: \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.1)^2 = 0.0314 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 220 \times 0.02 \times 0.0314 \times 60 = 8.2992 \, \text{V} \approx 8.3 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 80 turns and area 0.05 m² is in a 0.1 T field that drops to zero in 0.25 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.1 \times 0.05 = 0.005 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 80 \times \frac{0.005}{0.25} = 80 \times 0.02 = 1.6 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: In a system of two coils, the mutual inductance depends on which property of the setup?
options: Geometry and medium between the coils
questions.explanation: Mutual inductance depends on the geometry (e.g., coil sizes, separation, orientation) and the medium’s permeability, affecting how much flux from one coil links with the other.

questions.question_text: A coil of 180 turns and area 0.02 m² is rotated at 45 Hz in a 0.08 T field. What is the maximum emf?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 2\pi v = 2\pi \times 45 = 90\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 180 \times 0.08 \times 0.02 \times 90\pi = 81.43 \, \text{V} \approx 81.4 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: In an AC generator, what happens to the induced emf when the rotational speed of the coil doubles?
questions.explanation: The emf is proportional to the angular speed (\( \varepsilon = N B A \omega \)), so doubling the rotational speed doubles the emf.

questions.question_text: A metal ring is placed in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its plane. If the field strength decreases, the induced current in the ring flows in a direction to produce a magnetic field that does what?
options: Has no effect on the field
questions.explanation: According to Lenz’s law, the induced current opposes the decrease in magnetic flux by generating a magnetic field in the same direction as the original field.

questions.question_text: A solenoid of 800 turns per meter and area 0.013 m² has a current change from 9 A to 6 A in 0.2 s. What is the self-induced emf? (\( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{H/m} \))
questions.explanation: \( L = \mu_0 n^2 A l \), assume \( l = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( L = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (800)^2 \times 0.013 \times 1 = 0.01045 \, \text{H} \). \( \varepsilon = L \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = 0.01045 \times \frac{6 - 9}{0.2} = 0.01045 \times (-15) = 0.15675 \, \text{V} \approx 0.157 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: A coil of 60 turns and area 0.04 m² is in a 0.1 T field that drops to zero in 0.2 s. What is the induced emf?
questions.explanation: \( \Delta \Phi = B A = 0.1 \times 0.04 = 0.004 \, \text{Wb} \). \( \varepsilon = N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = 60 \times \frac{0.004}{0.2} = 60 \times 0.02 = 1.2 \, \text{V} \).

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has a frequency of \( 60 \, \text{MHz} \). What is its wavelength? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))
questions.explanation: Using \( v \lambda = c \), we have \( \lambda = \frac{c}{v} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{60 \times 10^6} = 5 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: What explains the effectiveness of infrared waves in remote sensing applications?

questions.question_text: What is the relationship between the amplitudes of electric and magnetic fields in an electromagnetic wave in vacuum? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has an electric field amplitude of \( 45 \, \text{V/m} \). What is the magnetic field amplitude? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has a wavelength of \( 12 \, \text{m} \). What is its frequency? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

questions.question_text: Which type of electromagnetic waves are produced by the rapid acceleration and deceleration of electrons in aerials?

questions.question_text: In a circuit with a capacitor, if the rate of change of electric flux is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{Vm/s} \), what is the displacement current? (Given \( \varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \, \text{F/m} \))
questions.explanation: Displacement current \( i_d = \varepsilon_0 \frac{d \Phi_E}{dt} \). Substituting the values, \( i_d = (8.85 \times 10^{-12}) \times (2 \times 10^{11}) = 1.77 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: Why are radio waves effective for long-distance communication?

questions.question_text: Why are microwaves used in domestic microwave ovens?

questions.question_text: Which frequency range corresponds to short wave bands used for radio communication?

questions.question_text: What is the frequency range of visible light?

questions.question_text: In electromagnetic wave propagation, what ensures that the electric and magnetic fields sustain each other?

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used to detect X-rays?

questions.question_text: What is the approximate wavelength range of ultraviolet rays as per the document?

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave has a magnetic field amplitude of \( B_0 = 8 \times 10^{-8} \, \text{T} \). What is the electric field amplitude? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

questions.question_text: In electromagnetic theory, what explains the constant ratio of electric to magnetic field amplitudes in a wave?

questions.question_text: Why are UV rays harmful in large quantities?
options: They have harmful effects on humans
questions.explanation: The document mentions that UV rays in large quantities have harmful effects on humans, such as damaging skin cells and inducing excessive melanin production.

questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate area \( A = 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \) and separation \( d = 2 \, \text{mm} \) is being charged at a rate of \( \frac{dQ}{dt} = 0.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the displacement current between the plates? (Given \( \varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \, \text{F/m} \))
questions.explanation: Displacement current \( i_d = \varepsilon_0 \frac{d \Phi_E}{dt} \). Since \( \Phi_E = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0} \), we have \( \frac{d \Phi_E}{dt} = \frac{1}{\varepsilon_0} \frac{dQ}{dt} \). But in a capacitor, \( i_d = \frac{dQ}{dt} \). Thus, \( i_d = 0.5 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: What makes electromagnetic waves capable of carrying energy over long distances?

questions.explanation: The document highlights that electromagnetic waves carry energy from one place to another, a capability stemming from their oscillating electric and magnetic fields.

questions.question_text: Why are infrared waves important for maintaining Earth's average temperature?

questions.question_text: Why does the absence of conduction current in certain regions necessitate the concept of displacement current?

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has a wavelength of \( 5 \, \text{m} \). What is its frequency? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave has a wave number \( k = 3 \, \text{rad/m} \). What is its wavelength in vacuum?

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has an electric field amplitude of \( 30 \, \text{V/m} \). What is the magnetic field amplitude? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

questions.question_text: What precaution must be taken when using X-rays in medical applications?

questions.question_text: What is the approximate wavelength range of microwaves as per the document?

questions.question_text: According to Maxwell's equations, what is the speed of electromagnetic waves in a medium with permittivity \( \varepsilon \) and permeability \( \mu \)?

questions.question_text: What insight does the Ampere-Maxwell law provide about the symmetry of electromagnetic fields?

questions.question_text: Why does the speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum remain constant irrespective of their source’s motion?

It varies with the source’s velocity
It depends on the medium’s density

questions.question_text: Which frequency range corresponds to the ultrahigh frequency (UHF) band used by cellular phones?

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave propagates in the \( z \)-direction with electric field along the \( x \)-axis. In which direction is the magnetic field oriented?

If \( \mathbf{E} \) is along \( x \)-axis and propagation is along \( z \)-axis, then \( \mathbf{B} \) must be along the \( y \)-axis (since \( \mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B} \) gives the direction of propagation).

questions.question_text: What is the typical wavelength range of X-rays as per the document?

questions.question_text: What enables electromagnetic waves to propagate through vacuum?

questions.question_text: What did Maxwell's unification of electricity, magnetism, and light lead to?

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has a magnetic field amplitude of \( B_0 = 4 \times 10^{-8} \, \text{T} \). What is the electric field amplitude? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

They are not absorbed by any material

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has a wavelength of \( 6 \, \text{m} \). What is its frequency? (Given \( c = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s} \))

questions.question_text: What physical implication arises from the fact that electromagnetic waves are transverse in nature?

questions.question_text: Infrared waves are often called heat waves because:

questions.question_text: What enables electromagnetic waves to propagate through vacuum without a medium?

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave has a wave number \( k = 4 \, \text{rad/m} \). What is its wavelength in vacuum?

questions.question_text: An electromagnetic wave has an angular frequency \( \omega = 8 \times 10^{11} \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its frequency in Hz?

questions.question_text: What property of electromagnetic waves explains their ability to travel at the same speed in vacuum regardless of their frequency?
questions.explanation: The speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum depends only on the permittivity (\( \varepsilon_0 \)) and permeability (\( \mu_0 \)) of free space, given by \( c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}} \), which is constant.

questions.question_text: What does Gauss's Law for electricity state in Maxwell's equations?

questions.question_text: In electromagnetic theory, what explains the ability of waves to exhibit coherence?

questions.question_text: Why are electromagnetic waves classified into different types in the spectrum?
