questions.question_text: Why is the gravitational force between two point masses always attractive?
questions.explanation: Newton’s universal law of gravitation (\( F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2} \)) is always positive since masses are positive, and the force vector is directed toward the other mass, making it attractive.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about a satellite in elliptical orbit?
questions.explanation: In an elliptical orbit, speed varies (faster at perihelion, slower at aphelion) due to conservation of angular momentum, making option 3 correct.

questions.question_text: What determines the escape speed from a planet?
What is the minimum speed required to escape from a point \( R_E \) above Earth’s surface? (\( R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M_E}{R_E + h}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 g R_E^2}{2 R_E}} = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E}{2}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{2}} = \sqrt{3.136 \times 10^7} \). \( v_e \approx 5.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} = 5.6 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: Why does the gravitational potential energy of two masses become more negative as they get closer?
questions.explanation: \( V = -\frac{G M m}{r} \). As \( r \) decreases, the term \( -\frac{G M m}{r} \) becomes larger in magnitude (more negative), reflecting increased binding energy due to stronger attraction.

questions.question_text: Three masses of \( 15 \, \text{kg} \) each form an equilateral triangle with side \( 10 \, \text{m} \). What is the net force on one mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Force between two masses: \( F = G \frac{m^2}{r^2} = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \frac{15 \times 15}{10^2} = 1.50 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \). Two forces at 60°: \( F_R = \sqrt{F^2 + F^2 + 2 F^2 \cos 60^\circ} \). \( F_R = \sqrt{(1.50 \times 10^{-10})^2 (1 + 1 + 1)} = 1.50 \times 10^{-10} \sqrt{3} \). \( F_R \approx 2.60 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What happens to the gravitational force on a point mass inside a hollow spherical shell?
options: It increases with distance from the center
It depends on the shell’s thickness
questions.explanation: The gravitational force on a point mass inside a hollow spherical shell of uniform density is zero. This is because forces from all parts of the shell cancel out due to symmetry, leaving no net force.

questions.question_text: A satellite orbits a planet at \( 4 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center with a period of 8 hours. What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Why can’t the gravitational force on a point mass outside a spherical shell be zero?
options: The force acts as if from the center
The shell’s thickness cancels the force
questions.explanation: Outside a spherical shell, the gravitational force acts as if all the mass is concentrated at the center. Since the mass is non-zero and the distance is finite, the force (\( F = \frac{G M m}{r^2} \)) cannot be zero.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect about escape speed?
options: It is independent of the object’s mass
It depends on the planet’s mass
It is independent of the planet
questions.explanation: Escape speed (\( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \)) is independent of the object’s mass (option 1 correct), depends on \( M \) and \( R \) (option 2 correct), and decreases with altitude (option 4 correct). Option 3 is incorrect as it does depend on the planet.

questions.question_text: What does Kepler’s third law reveal about the motion of planets farther from the Sun?
questions.explanation: Kepler’s third law (\( T^2 \propto a^3 \)) shows that planets farther from the Sun (larger semi-major axis \( a \)) have longer orbital periods (\( T \)), as the period increases with the distance cubed.

questions.question_text: Why can’t a satellite in a circular orbit have zero total energy?
options: It is bound with negative energy
questions.explanation: \( E = -\frac{G M m}{2 r} \) for a circular orbit, which is negative due to the bound state. Zero total energy implies the satellite could escape to infinity, which contradicts a stable orbit.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect about acceleration due to gravity?
options: It is zero at Earth’s center
It is maximum below the surface
questions.explanation: \( g \) decreases above (option 1 correct) and below (option 3 correct) the surface, and is zero at the center (option 2 correct). Option 4 is incorrect as \( g \) is maximum at the surface, not below.

questions.question_text: A satellite orbits a planet at \( 2.5 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center with a period of 5 hours. What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Three masses of \( 18 \, \text{kg} \) each form an equilateral triangle with side \( 12 \, \text{m} \). What is the net force on one mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Force between two masses: \( F = G \frac{m^2}{r^2} = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \frac{18 \times 18}{12^2} = 1.50 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \). Two forces at 60°: \( F_R = \sqrt{F^2 + F^2 + 2 F^2 \cos 60^\circ} \). \( F_R = \sqrt{(1.50 \times 10^{-10})^2 (1 + 1 + 1)} = 1.50 \times 10^{-10} \sqrt{3} \). \( F_R \approx 2.60 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the kinetic energy of a \( 800 \, \text{kg} \) satellite at \( 10 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( K = \frac{G M_E m}{2 r} \). \( r = 10 R_E = 6.4 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( K = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 800}{2 \times 6.4 \times 10^7} \). \( K = \frac{3.202 \times 10^{17}}{1.28 \times 10^8} \approx 2.50 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A satellite near Earth has a period of 90 minutes. What is its period at \( h = 3 R_E \)? (\( R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
A satellite orbits Earth at \( 17 R_E \) from the center. What is its orbital speed? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E^2}{r}} \). \( r = 17 R_E \), \( v = \sqrt{\frac{9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{17}} \). \( v = \sqrt{3.694 \times 10^6} \approx 1.92 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A planet orbits the Sun with a period of 6 years. If Earth’s orbital radius is \( 1.5 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \), what is its semi-major axis?

A planet has an orbital period of 4 years around the Sun. If Earth’s orbital radius is \( 1.5 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \), what is the planet’s semi-major axis? (\( 1 \, \text{year} = 3.156 \times 10^7 \, \text{s} \))
Which of Kepler’s laws implies that the gravitational force acting on a planet is a central force?
questions.explanation: Kepler’s second law (law of areas) states that the line joining a planet to the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal times. This is a consequence of the conservation of angular momentum, which holds true for a central force directed along the line joining the two bodies (e.g., the Sun and planet). A central force ensures no torque, preserving angular momentum.

questions.question_text: What role does the Sun play in planetary motion according to Kepler’s laws?
questions.explanation: The Sun is at one focus of the elliptical orbits (first law) and provides the central gravitational force driving the equal-area sweep (second law) and period-distance relation (third law).

questions.question_text: A body weighs \( 245 \, \text{N} \) on Earth’s surface. What is its weight at a depth \( d = R_E/5 \)? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

What is the gravitational potential due to Earth at \( 1.92 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Four \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) masses form a square of side \( 5 \, \text{m} \). What is the potential energy of the system? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

A moon orbits a planet with a period of 9 days and radius \( 6 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))
What does the heliocentric model, supported by Kepler’s laws, improve over the geocentric model?
questions.explanation: The heliocentric model (Sun at the center) simplifies planetary motion descriptions compared to the geocentric model (Earth at the center), which required complex epicycles. Kepler’s laws align with heliocentric orbits.

questions.question_text: A planet orbits the Sun with a period of 7 years. If Earth’s orbital radius is \( 1.5 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \), what is its semi-major axis?
A satellite orbits Earth at \( 7 R_E \) from the center. What is its orbital speed? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E^2}{r}} \). \( r = 7 R_E \), \( v = \sqrt{\frac{9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{7}} \). \( v = \sqrt{8.966 \times 10^6} \approx 2.99 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Four \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) masses form a square of side \( 6 \, \text{m} \). What is the potential energy of the system? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

What is the gravitational force on a \( 12 \, \text{kg} \) mass \( 10 \, \text{m} \) from the center of a spherical shell of mass \( 600 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 8 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
What does Kepler’s third law imply about the relationship between orbital period and distance?
questions.explanation: Kepler’s third law: the square of the orbital period (\( T^2 \)) is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis (\( a^3 \)), i.e., \( T^2 \propto a^3 \). This relates time and distance for planetary motion.

questions.question_text: A projectile launched at \( 10 \, \text{km/s} \) from Earth reaches a maximum distance of? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))

How much energy is required to move a \( 600 \, \text{kg} \) satellite from \( 10 R_E \) to \( 20 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta E = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 6.4 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 1.28 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta E = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 600 \left(\frac{1}{1.28 \times 10^8} - \frac{1}{6.4 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta E = -2.401 \times 10^{17} (-7.8125 \times 10^{-9}) \approx 1.88 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: What is the escape speed from a planet with \( g = 4.9 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) and radius \( 3.2 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \)?
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{2 g R} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{2 \times 4.9 \times 3.2 \times 10^6} = \sqrt{3.136 \times 10^7} \). \( v_e \approx 5.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} = 5.6 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: A body is projected from Earth with \( 13 \, \text{km/s} \). What is its speed far away? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s} \))
Why is the gravitational potential energy negative in a bound system?
options: Work is required to reach infinity
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy as \( V = -\frac{G M m}{r} \), with zero at infinity. For a bound system (e.g., orbit), the negative value indicates that work must be done to separate the objects to infinity, reflecting gravitational attraction.

questions.question_text: Why does a satellite in a circular orbit have negative total energy?
options: It is moving away from Earth
questions.explanation: The total energy \( E = -\frac{G M m}{2 r} \) is negative because the potential energy (\( -\frac{G M m}{r} \)) is negative and twice the magnitude of the positive kinetic energy (\( \frac{G M m}{2 r} \)). This negative value indicates a bound system.

questions.question_text: What is the gravitational potential due to Earth at \( 3.84 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Why does Kepler’s first law indicate that planetary orbits are not perfectly circular?
options: The Sun is not at the center
Orbits are elliptical with the Sun at one focus
questions.explanation: Kepler’s first law (law of orbits) describes planetary orbits as ellipses with the Sun at one focus, not circles (a special case of an ellipse). This deviation from circular motion reflects the real dynamics of gravitational interaction.

questions.question_text: What ensures that a satellite remains in a stable circular orbit?
options: Balance of gravitational and centripetal forces
questions.explanation: A stable circular orbit requires the gravitational force (\( \frac{G M_E m}{r^2} \)) to equal the centripetal force (\( \frac{m v^2}{r} \)), balancing the forces to maintain constant radius and speed.

questions.question_text: Three \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) masses form an equilateral triangle of side \( 1 \, \text{m} \). What is the potential energy? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

A moon orbits a planet with a period of 13 days and radius \( 1.0 \times 10^9 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))

What is the kinetic energy of a \( 300 \, \text{kg} \) satellite at \( 5 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( K = \frac{G M_E m}{2 r} \). \( r = 5 R_E = 3.2 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( K = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 300}{2 \times 3.2 \times 10^7} \). \( K = \frac{1.201 \times 10^{17}}{6.4 \times 10^7} \approx 1.88 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A satellite near Earth has a period of 82 minutes. What is its period at \( h = 9 R_E \)? (\( R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))

Two masses \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) are \( 6 \, \text{m} \) apart. What is the gravitational potential at a point \( 2 \, \text{m} \) from the \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) mass on the line joining them? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
What is the minimum speed to escape from \( 8 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 g R_E^2}{8 R_E}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{8}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{1.568 \times 10^7} \approx 3.96 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \approx 4.0 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: Why is the value of \( g \) maximum at Earth’s surface?
options: All mass contributes at the surface
It is zero at the surface
questions.explanation: At the surface. Above, \( g \) decreases with \( 1/(R_E + h)^2 \); below, only inner mass contributes, reducing \( g \) linearly as \( g(d) = g (1 - d/R_E) \). Thus, \( g \) peaks at \( r = R_E \).

questions.question_text: What is the escape speed from a planet with mass \( 4.5 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 6 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 4.5 \times 10^{24}}{6 \times 10^6}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{1.0005 \times 10^8} \approx 1.00 \times 10^4 \, \text{m/s} = 10.0 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: Four \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) masses form a square of side \( 8 \, \text{m} \). What is the potential energy of the system? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

What is the gravitational potential energy of a \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) mass at a height of \( 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \) above Earth’s surface? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Distance from center: \( r = R_E + h = 6.4 \times 10^6 + 6.4 \times 10^6 = 1.28 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( V = -\frac{G M_E m}{r} = -\frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 2}{1.28 \times 10^7} \). \( V = -\frac{8.004 \times 10^{14}}{1.28 \times 10^7} = -6.25 \times 10^7 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) mass is moved from \( 5 R_E \) to \( 10 R_E \) from Earth’s center. What is the change in potential energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta V = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 3.2 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 6.4 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta V = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 5 \left(\frac{1}{6.4 \times 10^7} - \frac{1}{3.2 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta V = -2.001 \times 10^{15} (-1.5625 \times 10^{-8}) \approx 3.13 \times 10^7 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: What is the minimum speed to escape from \( 7 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 g R_E^2}{7 R_E}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{7}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{1.79 \times 10^7} \approx 4.23 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \approx 4.2 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: A moon orbits a planet with period 8 days and radius \( 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))

What is the gravitational potential due to Earth at \( 5.12 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Which of the following statements is correct about gravitational potential energy?
options: It is zero at Earth’s surface
It is zero at infinite separation
It increases as objects get closer
questions.explanation: \( V = -\frac{G M m}{r} \) is defined with zero at infinity, and work is needed to separate masses, making option 2 correct.

questions.question_text: What is the kinetic energy of a \( 200 \, \text{kg} \) satellite at \( 4 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( K = \frac{G M_E m}{2 r} \). \( r = 4 R_E = 2.56 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( K = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 200}{2 \times 2.56 \times 10^7} \). \( K = \frac{8.004 \times 10^{16}}{5.12 \times 10^7} \approx 1.56 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: How much energy is required to move a \( 300 \, \text{kg} \) satellite from \( 7 R_E \) to \( 14 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta E = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 4.48 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 8.96 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta E = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 300 \left(\frac{1}{8.96 \times 10^7} - \frac{1}{4.48 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta E = -1.201 \times 10^{17} (-1.116 \times 10^{-8}) \approx 1.34 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A planet orbits the Sun with a period of 12 years. If Earth’s orbital radius is \( 1.5 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \), what is its semi-major axis?

A \( 1000 \, \text{kg} \) satellite orbits Earth at \( 16 R_E \) from the center. What is its total energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
A projectile is launched at \( 5 \, \text{km/s} \) from Earth’s surface. What is its maximum distance from the center? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
Which of the following statements is correct about Kepler’s third law?
options: Period squared is proportional to distance cubed
Period is constant for all orbits
questions.explanation: \( T^2 \propto a^3 \), meaning the period squared is proportional to the semi-major axis cubed, making option 2 correct.

questions.question_text: What is the escape speed from a planet with mass \( 2.4 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 2.4 \times 10^{24}}{4 \times 10^6}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{8.002 \times 10^7} \approx 8.95 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \approx 8.95 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: Three masses of \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) each form an equilateral triangle with side \( 6 \, \text{m} \). What is the net force on one mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Force between two masses: \( F = G \frac{m^2}{r^2} = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \frac{8 \times 8}{6^2} = 1.185 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \). Two forces at 60°: \( F_R = \sqrt{F^2 + F^2 + 2 F^2 \cos 60^\circ} \). \( F_R = \sqrt{(1.185 \times 10^{-10})^2 (1 + 1 + 1)} = 1.185 \times 10^{-10} \sqrt{3} \). \( F_R \approx 2.05 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the gravitational force on a \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) mass \( 6 \, \text{m} \) from the center of a spherical shell of mass \( 300 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 4 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Outside shell: \( F = \frac{G M m}{r^2} \). \( F = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 300 \times 7}{6^2} \). \( F = \frac{1.401 \times 10^{-8}}{36} \approx 3.89 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 600 \, \text{kg} \) satellite orbits Earth at \( 8 R_E \) from the center. What is its total energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
A satellite orbits at \( 3 R_E \) from Earth’s center. What is its speed? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E^2}{r}} \). \( r = 3 R_E \), \( v = \sqrt{\frac{9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{3}} \). \( v = \sqrt{2.09 \times 10^7} \approx 4.57 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) mass is moved from \( 8 R_E \) to \( 16 R_E \) from Earth’s center. What is the change in potential energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta V = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 5.12 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 1.024 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta V = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 8 \left(\frac{1}{1.024 \times 10^8} - \frac{1}{5.12 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta V = -3.202 \times 10^{15} (-9.766 \times 10^{-9}) \approx 3.13 \times 10^7 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: At what height above Earth’s surface is \( g \) reduced to \( 6.12 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)? (\( g_0 = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))

A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) mass is moved from \( R_E \) to \( 2 R_E \) from Earth’s center. What is the work done? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
A body is launched from Earth at \( 12.5 \, \text{km/s} \). What is its speed at infinity? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s} \))

A \( 700 \, \text{kg} \) satellite orbits Earth at \( 10 R_E \) from the center. What is its total energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
A body is launched from Earth at \( 11.5 \, \text{km/s} \). What is its speed at infinity? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s} \))

Energy required to move a \( 300 \, \text{kg} \) satellite from \( 3 R_E \) to \( 6 R_E \) is? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta E = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 3 R_E = 1.92 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 6 R_E = 3.84 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta E = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 300 \left(\frac{1}{3.84 \times 10^7} - \frac{1}{1.92 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta E = -1.201 \times 10^{17} (-2.604 \times 10^{-8}) \approx 3.13 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 900 \, \text{kg} \) satellite orbits Earth at \( 14 R_E \) from the center. What is its total energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

A \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) mass is moved from \( 7 R_E \) to \( 14 R_E \) from Earth’s center. What is the change in potential energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta V = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 4.48 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 8.96 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta V = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 7 \left(\frac{1}{8.96 \times 10^7} - \frac{1}{4.48 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta V = -2.801 \times 10^{15} (-1.116 \times 10^{-8}) \approx 3.13 \times 10^7 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: The time period of a satellite near Earth’s surface is 84 minutes. What is its time period at a height \( h = R_E \)? (\( R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))

A satellite of mass \( 500 \, \text{kg} \) orbits Earth at \( 2 R_E \) from the center. What is its kinetic energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( K = \frac{G M_E m}{2 r} \). \( r = 2 R_E = 2 \times 6.4 \times 10^6 = 1.28 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( K = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 500}{2 \times 1.28 \times 10^7} \). \( K = \frac{2.001 \times 10^{17}}{2.56 \times 10^7} \approx 7.82 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: Three masses of \( 12 \, \text{kg} \) each form an equilateral triangle with side \( 9 \, \text{m} \). What is the net force on one mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Force between two masses: \( F = G \frac{m^2}{r^2} = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \frac{12 \times 12}{9^2} = 1.185 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \). Two forces at 60°: \( F_R = \sqrt{F^2 + F^2 + 2 F^2 \cos 60^\circ} \). \( F_R = \sqrt{(1.185 \times 10^{-10})^2 (1 + 1 + 1)} = 1.185 \times 10^{-10} \sqrt{3} \). \( F_R \approx 2.05 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: How much energy is required to move a \( 100 \, \text{kg} \) satellite from \( 4 R_E \) to \( 8 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta E = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 2.56 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 5.12 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta E = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 100 \left(\frac{1}{5.12 \times 10^7} - \frac{1}{2.56 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta E = -4.002 \times 10^{16} (-1.953 \times 10^{-8}) \approx 7.82 \times 10^8 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: What is the escape speed from a planet with mass \( 3.6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 3.6 \times 10^{24}}{5 \times 10^6}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{9.607 \times 10^7} \approx 9.80 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \approx 9.8 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: Why is the gravitational force on a point mass outside a hollow spherical shell equivalent to that of a point mass at its center?
options: Symmetry causes forces to cancel radially
Mass is distributed evenly at the center
questions.explanation: For a uniform spherical shell, the gravitational forces from all parts of the shell combine such that the net force on an external point acts as if the shell’s entire mass is concentrated at its center, due to symmetry.

questions.question_text: Why does the gravitational potential energy approach zero as the distance between two masses increases?
options: It is defined as zero at infinity
questions.explanation: \( V = -\frac{G M m}{r} \), with the convention that \( V = 0 \) at \( r \to \infty \). As \( r \) increases, \( \frac{1}{r} \) decreases, making \( V \) less negative and approaching zero.

questions.question_text: What does the variation of \( g \) with altitude indicate about gravitational force?
Why does the gravitational potential energy depend on the inverse of distance?
options: Energy is zero at the surface

questions.question_text: What is the gravitational potential at a point \( 9.6 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \) from Earth’s center due to Earth? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Why does a satellite in a higher orbit have a longer orbital period?
questions.explanation: \( T^2 \propto r^3 \) for satellites. A higher orbit (larger \( r \)) increases \( T^2 \) by \( r^3 \), so the period \( T \) increases as the radius grows, reflecting weaker gravitational pull at greater distances.

questions.question_text: Why does the gravitational potential decrease (become less negative) as altitude increases?
questions.explanation: As altitude increases, \( r \) (distance from Earth’s center) increases, reducing the magnitude of the negative term \( -\frac{G M m}{r} \), making \( V \) less negative.

questions.question_text: A moon orbits a planet with a period of 12 days and radius \( 9 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))

A moon orbits a planet with a period of 11 days and radius \( 8 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))

A moon orbits a planet with a period of 6 days and radius \( 4 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))
What is the significance of the Cavendish experiment in understanding gravity?

What is the total energy of a \( 100 \, \text{kg} \) satellite orbiting Earth at \( 3 R_E \) from the center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( E = -\frac{G M_E m}{2 r} \). \( r = 3 R_E = 3 \times 6.4 \times 10^6 = 1.92 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( E = -\frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 100}{2 \times 1.92 \times 10^7} \). \( E = -\frac{4.002 \times 10^{16}}{3.84 \times 10^7} \approx -1.04 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about the gravitational force inside a hollow spherical shell?
options: It depends on the shell’s thickness
It acts outward from the center
questions.explanation: The net gravitational force inside a uniform hollow spherical shell is zero due to symmetry, making option 2 correct.

questions.question_text: What is the significance of the negative sign in the gravitational potential energy formula \( V = -\frac{G M m}{r} \)?
options: It shows the force is repulsive
It indicates energy is zero at infinity
It implies energy increases with distance
questions.explanation: The negative sign indicates that gravitational potential energy is zero at infinite separation (\( r \to \infty \)) and decreases (becomes more negative) as objects approach each other. It reflects the attractive nature of gravity, where work must be done to separate masses.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 1 \, \text{km/s} \) from Earth’s surface. What is its maximum distance from the center? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
Why does the total energy of a satellite in an elliptical orbit remain constant?
questions.explanation: Gravity is a conservative force, so the total mechanical energy (\( E = KE + PE \)) is conserved in an elliptical orbit, with kinetic and potential energies trading off but summing to a constant.

questions.question_text: A satellite orbits Earth at \( 11 R_E \) from the center. What is its orbital speed? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E^2}{r}} \). \( r = 11 R_E \), \( v = \sqrt{\frac{9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{11}} \). \( v = \sqrt{5.698 \times 10^6} \approx 2.39 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Four \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) masses form a square of side \( 7 \, \text{m} \). What is the potential energy of the system? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
A projectile is launched at \( 9 \, \text{km/s} \) from Earth’s surface. What is its maximum distance from the center? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))

A \( 250 \, \text{kg} \) satellite orbits Earth at \( 6 R_E \) from the center. What is its total energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
At what height above Earth’s surface is \( g \) reduced to \( 7.84 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)? (\( g_0 = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
A satellite orbits Earth at \( 19 R_E \) from the center. What is its orbital speed? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E^2}{r}} \). \( r = 19 R_E \), \( v = \sqrt{\frac{9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{19}} \). \( v = \sqrt{3.301 \times 10^6} \approx 1.82 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1100 \, \text{kg} \) satellite orbits Earth at \( 18 R_E \) from the center. What is its total energy? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

Four equal masses of \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) are at the vertices of a square with side \( 2 \, \text{m} \). What is the net force on one mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Force from adjacent: \( F_1 = G \frac{m^2}{r^2} = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \frac{3 \times 3}{2^2} = 1.50 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \) (2 forces at 90°). Force from diagonal: \( F_2 = G \frac{m^2}{(2\sqrt{2})^2} = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \frac{9}{8} = 7.50 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N} \). Resultant of two \( F_1 \): \( F_R = \sqrt{2} \times 1.50 \times 10^{-10} \approx 2.12 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \). Net force (vector sum with \( F_2 \)): \( F = \sqrt{(2.12 \times 10^{-10})^2 + (7.50 \times 10^{-11})^2} \approx 2.25 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the key assumption about Earth’s density in calculating \( g \) below its surface?
options: It is zero at the center
questions.explanation: Considering the Earth has uniform density to simplify the mass contributing to gravity inside (\( M_r = M_E \frac{r^3}{R_E^3} \)), leading to \( g(d) = g (1 - d/R_E) \). Non-uniform density would complicate this.

questions.question_text: Two identical masses of \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) each are placed at the vertices A and B of an equilateral triangle ABC with side length \( 2 \, \text{m} \). What is the gravitational force on a \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) mass at vertex C? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Force due to A on C: \( F_{AC} = G \frac{m_A m_C}{r^2} = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \frac{5 \times 10}{2^2} = 8.34 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \). Force due to B on C: \( F_{BC} = 8.34 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \) (equal magnitude, 60° apart). Resultant: \( F_R = \sqrt{F_{AC}^2 + F_{BC}^2 + 2 F_{AC} F_{BC} \cos 60^\circ} \). \( F_R = \sqrt{(8.34 \times 10^{-10})^2 + (8.34 \times 10^{-10})^2 + 2 (8.34 \times 10^{-10})^2 (0.5)} \). \( F_R = 8.34 \times 10^{-10} \sqrt{1 + 1 + 1} = 1.44 \times 10^{-9} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched from Earth with a speed of \( 15 \, \text{km/s} \). What is its speed at infinity? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s} \))
At what height above Earth’s surface is \( g \) reduced to \( 8.82 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)? (\( g_0 = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))

How much energy is required to move a \( 500 \, \text{kg} \) satellite from \( 5 R_E \) to \( 10 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta E = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 3.2 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 6.4 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta E = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 500 \left(\frac{1}{6.4 \times 10^7} - \frac{1}{3.2 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta E = -2.001 \times 10^{17} (-1.5625 \times 10^{-8}) \approx 3.13 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: What is the gravitational force on a \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) mass \( 8 \, \text{m} \) from the center of a spherical shell of mass \( 450 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 6 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Outside shell: \( F = \frac{G M m}{r^2} \). \( F = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 450 \times 10}{8^2} \). \( F = \frac{3.0015 \times 10^{-8}}{64} \approx 4.69 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: Two masses \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 20 \, \text{kg} \) are \( 20 \, \text{m} \) apart. What is the gravitational potential at a point \( 9 \, \text{m} \) from the \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Which of the following statements is incorrect about gravitational force?
options: It can be zero at some points
It decreases with the square of distance
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is always attractive (option 2 is correct), follows the inverse-square law (option 3 is correct), and acts between all masses (option 4 is correct). Option 1 is incorrect as it can be zero inside a shell.

questions.question_text: What is the gravitational potential due to Earth at \( 1.28 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Which of the following statements is incorrect about gravitational potential energy?
options: It is negative for bound objects
It is zero at infinite distance
questions.explanation: It’s negative (option 1 correct), zero at infinity (option 2 correct), and conservative (option 3 correct). Option 4 is incorrect as it depends on distance, not mass alone.

questions.question_text: Four \( 9 \, \text{kg} \) masses form a square of side \( 9 \, \text{m} \). What is the potential energy of the system? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
What is the escape speed from a planet of mass \( 4.8 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 4.8 \times 10^{24}}{5 \times 10^6}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{6.403 \times 10^7} \approx 8.0 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} = 8.0 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: What causes the variation in kinetic energy of a satellite in an elliptical orbit?
questions.explanation: In an elliptical orbit, total energy is constant, but kinetic energy (\( KE = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 \)) varies as speed changes with distance from the center (faster closer, slower farther), balancing the changing potential energy.

questions.question_text: What property of the gravitational force allows Newton’s law to apply to extended objects?
questions.explanation: The gravitational force obeys the principle of superposition, meaning the total force on a body is the vector sum of forces from individual point masses. This allows the law to extend to composite objects by summing contributions.

questions.question_text: What causes the elliptical shape of planetary orbits according to Newton’s theory?
questions.explanation: The inverse-square law (\( F \propto 1/r^2 \)) leads to elliptical orbits as a general solution to the two-body problem, matching Kepler’s first law, unlike a linear force which would produce circular orbits.

questions.question_text: What is the primary reason the gravitational force inside a uniform spherical shell is zero?
questions.explanation: Inside a uniform spherical shell, the gravitational forces from all mass elements cancel out due to symmetry, resulting in a net force of zero at any internal point.

questions.question_text: Two masses \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) are \( 8 \, \text{m} \) apart. What is the gravitational potential at a point \( 3 \, \text{m} \) from the \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))

What is the gravitational force on a \( 13 \, \text{kg} \) mass \( 11 \, \text{m} \) from the center of a spherical shell of mass \( 700 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 9 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Outside shell: \( F = \frac{G M m}{r^2} \). \( F = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 700 \times 13}{11^2} \). \( F = \frac{6.0689 \times 10^{-8}}{121} \approx 5.02 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: Why is the escape speed independent of the mass of the object being launched?
options: Mass cancels out in the energy equation
It depends on the launch angle
It is due to Earth’s rotation
questions.explanation: Escape speed as \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \). The mass \( m \) of the object cancels out in the energy conservation equation (\( \frac{1}{2} m v_e^2 = \frac{G M m}{R} \)), making \( v_e \) dependent only on the planet’s mass \( M \) and radius \( R \).

questions.question_text: How much energy is required to move a \( 700 \, \text{kg} \) satellite from \( 11 R_E \) to \( 22 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta E = -G M_E m \left(\frac{1}{r_2} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) \). \( r_1 = 7.04 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \), \( r_2 = 1.408 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta E = -6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 700 \left(\frac{1}{1.408 \times 10^8} - \frac{1}{7.04 \times 10^7}\right) \). \( \Delta E = -2.801 \times 10^{17} (-7.102 \times 10^{-9}) \approx 1.99 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A moon orbits a planet with a period of 7 days and radius \( 5 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))
What is the minimum speed to escape from \( 3 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 g R_E^2}{3 R_E}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{3}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{4.181 \times 10^7} \approx 6.47 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \approx 6.5 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect about \( g \) variation?
options: It is zero at Earth’s center
questions.explanation: \( g \) decreases with altitude (option 1 correct), depth (option 2 correct), and is zero at the center (option 4 correct). Option 3 is incorrect as \( g \) decreases, not increases, below the surface.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum speed to escape from \( 10 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 g R_E^2}{10 R_E}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{10}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{1.254 \times 10^7} \approx 3.54 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \approx 3.5 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: A planet has a moon with an orbital radius of \( 5 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \) and a period of 10 days. What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))
Why did Newton conclude that the gravitational force decreases with the square of the distance?
options: Due to the Moon’s orbit compared to Earth’s gravity
Due to experimental data from Cavendish
questions.explanation: Newton observed that the centripetal acceleration of the Moon (\( a_m = \frac{V^2}{R_m} \)) was much smaller than the acceleration due to gravity on Earth’s surface (\( g \)), and their ratio matched the inverse square of their distances from Earth’s center (\( \frac{g}{a_m} \approx \frac{R_m^2}{R_E^2} \)).

questions.question_text: A satellite orbits Earth at a height equal to \( R_E/2 \). What is its orbital speed? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( r = R_E + \frac{R_E}{2} = 1.5 R_E \). \( v = \sqrt{\frac{G M_E}{r}} = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E^2}{1.5 R_E}} = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E}{1.5}} \). \( v = \sqrt{\frac{9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{1.5}} = \sqrt{4.181 \times 10^7} \). \( v \approx 6.47 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Why does an object require more energy to escape from a higher altitude than to reach that altitude?
questions.explanation: Escape energy from altitude \( h \) is \( \frac{G M m}{R + h} \), while energy to reach \( h \) from the surface is \( G M m \left(\frac{1}{R} - \frac{1}{R + h}\right) \), which is less. Escape requires overcoming all potential energy to infinity.

questions.question_text: What is the primary source of centripetal force for an Earth satellite?
questions.explanation: For a satellite in circular orbit, the centripetal force (\( F = \frac{m v^2}{r} \)) is provided by Earth’s gravitational force (\( F = \frac{G M_E m}{r^2} \)), which keeps it in orbit.

questions.question_text: Three masses of \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) each are at the vertices of an equilateral triangle with side \( 3 \, \text{m} \). What is the net force on one mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Force between two masses: \( F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2} = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \frac{4 \times 4}{3^2} = 1.185 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \). Two forces act at 60°: \( F_R = \sqrt{F^2 + F^2 + 2 F^2 \cos 60^\circ} \). \( F_R = \sqrt{(1.185 \times 10^{-10})^2 (1 + 1 + 1)} = 1.185 \times 10^{-10} \sqrt{3} \). \( F_R \approx 2.05 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the kinetic energy of a \( 500 \, \text{kg} \) satellite at \( 7 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( K = \frac{G M_E m}{2 r} \). \( r = 7 R_E = 4.48 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( K = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 500}{2 \times 4.48 \times 10^7} \). \( K = \frac{2.001 \times 10^{17}}{8.96 \times 10^7} \approx 2.23 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: What is the kinetic energy of a \( 150 \, \text{kg} \) satellite at \( 3 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( K = \frac{G M_E m}{2 r} \). \( r = 3 R_E = 1.92 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \). \( K = \frac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times 150}{2 \times 1.92 \times 10^7} \). \( K = \frac{6.003 \times 10^{16}}{3.84 \times 10^7} \approx 1.56 \times 10^9 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: What does the negative total energy of a bound system indicate?
questions.explanation: Negative total energy (\( E = KE + PE < 0 \)) means the system is bound, requiring external energy to separate the objects to infinity, where \( E = 0 \), typical for orbits.

questions.question_text: What condition must an object’s energy satisfy to remain bound to Earth?
questions.explanation: For an object to remain bound, its total mechanical energy (\( E = KE + PE \)) must be negative, indicating it lacks sufficient energy to reach infinity where \( E = 0 \).

questions.question_text: A satellite near Earth has a period of 86 minutes. What is its period at \( h = 5 R_E \)? (\( R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
What is the escape speed from a planet with mass \( 1.8 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 3.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 1.8 \times 10^{24}}{3.5 \times 10^6}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{6.861 \times 10^7} \approx 8.28 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \approx 8.3 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: A planet moves in an elliptical orbit around the Sun with a semi-major axis of \( 2.25 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \). If its orbital period is 2 years, what is the mass of the Sun? (Take \( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \), \( 1 \, \text{year} = 3.156 \times 10^7 \, \text{s} \))
A planet orbits the Sun with a period of 10 years. If Earth’s orbital radius is \( 1.5 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \), what is its semi-major axis?

A moon orbits a planet with a period of 10 days and radius \( 7 \times 10^8 \, \text{m} \). What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2, 1 \, \text{day} = 86400 \, \text{s} \))
Why is the gravitational force zero at the center of a uniform solid sphere?
options: Mass is zero at the center
Distance to the surface is infinite
questions.explanation: At the center (\( r = 0 \)), the gravitational forces from all mass elements of a uniform sphere cancel out due to symmetry, as the net force from opposite directions balances to zero.

questions.question_text: A body is launched from Earth at \( 12 \, \text{km/s} \). What is its speed at infinity? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s} \))
Why does the work done by gravity in moving an object depend only on the vertical displacement near Earth’s surface?
options: It depends on the path taken
questions.explanation: Near Earth’s surface, gravity is approximately constant (\( F = mg \)), and the force acts vertically. Thus, work (\( W = F \cdot \Delta h \)) depends only on vertical displacement (\( \Delta h \)), as horizontal motion is perpendicular to the force.

questions.question_text: A body is launched from Earth at \( 15.5 \, \text{km/s} \). What is its speed at infinity? (Escape speed = \( 11.2 \, \text{km/s} \))
Which of the following statements is incorrect about gravitational force?
questions.explanation: It’s attractive (option 1 correct), follows inverse-square (option 2 correct), and is conservative (option 4 correct). Option 3 is incorrect as it is not limited to Earth.

questions.question_text: What is the escape speed from a planet with mass \( 9 \times 10^{23} \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 2.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \)? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 9 \times 10^{23}}{2.5 \times 10^6}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{4.801 \times 10^7} \approx 6.93 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \approx 6.9 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: A satellite near Earth has a period of 89 minutes. What is its period at \( h = 7 R_E \)? (\( R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))

What is the kinetic energy of a \( 900 \, \text{kg} \) satellite at \( 11 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( M_E = 6 \times 10^{24} \, \text{kg}, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m}, G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
A satellite orbits a planet at \( 3 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center with a period of 6 hours. What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
A satellite orbits a planet at \( 8 \times 10^7 \, \text{m} \) from its center with a period of 20 hours. What is the planet’s mass? (\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \))
Which of the following statements is incorrect about escape speed?
options: It depends on the planet’s mass
It is independent of launch direction
It is independent of object mass
questions.explanation: Escape speed depends on planet parameters (option 1 correct), is independent of direction (option 3 correct), and mass (option 4 correct). Option 2 is incorrect as it decreases with altitude.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum speed to escape from \( 5 R_E \) from Earth’s center? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2 g R_E^2}{5 R_E}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{5}} \). \( v_e = \sqrt{2.509 \times 10^7} \approx 5.01 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} = 5.0 \, \text{km/s} \).

questions.question_text: A body weighs \( 294 \, \text{N} \) on Earth’s surface. What is its weight at a height \( h = 3 R_E/4 \)? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
At what height above Earth’s surface is \( g \) reduced to \( 5.88 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)? (\( g_0 = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
A body weighs \( 147 \, \text{N} \) on Earth’s surface. What is its weight at a height \( h = R_E/3 \)? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A satellite orbits Earth at \( 2.5 R_E \) from the center. What is its orbital speed? (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, R_E = 6.4 \times 10^6 \, \text{m} \))
questions.explanation: \( v = \sqrt{\frac{g R_E^2}{r}} \). \( r = 2.5 R_E \), \( v = \sqrt{\frac{9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{2.5}} \). \( v = \sqrt{2.509 \times 10^7} \approx 5.01 \times 10^3 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the physical significance of the gravitational constant \( G \) in Newton’s law?
questions.explanation: \( G \) is the universal gravitational constant, determining the strength of the gravitational force between two masses. It is a fundamental constant that scales the force in \( F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2} \).

questions.question_text: What ensures that a planet moves faster at perihelion than at aphelion?
questions.explanation: Angular momentum conservation (\( m r v = \text{constant} \)) implies that at perihelion (smaller \( r \)), the speed \( v \) is greater than at aphelion (larger \( r \)), as derived from Kepler’s second law.

questions.question_text: A planet orbits the Sun with a period of 5 years. If Earth’s orbital radius is \( 1.5 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \), what is its semi-major axis?

A \( 4.8 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 37^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is pulled upward by a \( 6.8 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 6.8 \, \text{kg} \): \( 6.8g - T = 6.8a \Rightarrow 68 - T = 6.8a \). For \( 4.8 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - mg \sin 37^\circ - f_k = 4.8a \). \( N = mg \cos 37^\circ = 4.8 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 38.4 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.2 \times 38.4 = 7.68 \, \text{N} \). \( mg \sin 37^\circ = 48 \times 0.6 = 28.8 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 28.8 - 7.68 = 4.8a \Rightarrow T - 36.48 = 4.8a \). Solve: \( 68 - T = 6.8a \), \( T - 36.48 = 4.8a \). Substitute: \( 68 - (4.8a + 36.48) = 6.8a \Rightarrow 68 - 36.48 - 4.8a = 6.8a \Rightarrow 31.52 = 11.6a \). \( a \approx 2.72 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( T - 36.48 = 4.8 \times 2.72 \Rightarrow T - 36.48 \approx 13.06 \Rightarrow T \approx 49.54 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A force of \( 10 \, \text{N} \) acts on a body of mass \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) initially at rest. What is the velocity of the body after \( 5 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: First, calculate acceleration using Newton’s Second Law: \( a = \frac{F}{m} \). Substitute: \( F = 10 \, \text{N} \), \( m = 2 \, \text{kg} \). So, \( a = \frac{10}{2} = 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use the equation \( v = u + at \), where initial velocity \( u = 0 \), \( t = 5 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 5 \times 5 = 25 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 2000 \, \text{kg} \) truck accelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then a \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) ball is dropped. What is the horizontal distance from the drop point after \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \)? (Neglect air resistance)
questions.explanation: Truck’s speed at \( t = 5 \, \text{s} \): \( v = 0 + 2 \times 5 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \). Ball retains horizontal velocity of \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \). After drop, no horizontal acceleration. Distance = \( v \times t = 10 \times 1.5 = 15 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.6 \, \text{kg} \) stone in a vertical circle of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) has a tension of \( 20 \, \text{N} \) at the bottom. What is the tension at the top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Bottom: \( T_b - mg = m \omega^2 r \Rightarrow 20 - 0.6 \times 10 = 0.6 \times \omega^2 \times 1.5 \). \( 20 - 6 = 0.9 \omega^2 \Rightarrow 14 = 0.9 \omega^2 \Rightarrow \omega^2 = \frac{14}{0.9} \approx 15.56 \). Top: \( T_t + mg = m \omega^2 r \Rightarrow T_t + 0.6 \times 10 = 0.6 \times 15.56 \times 1.5 \). \( T_t + 6 = 14 \Rightarrow T_t = 14 - 6 = 8 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) ball moving at \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to a wall rebounds at \( 30^\circ \) with the same speed. What is the impulse magnitude? (Take \( \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \), \( \cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \), \( \cos 30^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Initial momentum: \( p_{x1} = 0.15 \times 25 \times 0.5 = 1.875 \, \text{kg m/s} \), \( p_{y1} = 0.15 \times 25 \times 0.866 = 3.2475 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Final momentum: \( p_{x2} = -0.15 \times 25 \times 0.866 = -3.2475 \, \text{kg m/s} \), \( p_{y2} = 0.15 \times 25 \times 0.5 = 1.875 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Change: \( \Delta p_x = -3.2475 - 1.875 = -5.1225 \, \text{kg m/s} \), \( \Delta p_y = 1.875 - 3.2475 = -1.3725 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Magnitude: \( |\Delta p| = \sqrt{(-5.1225)^2 + (-1.3725)^2} = \sqrt{26.24 + 1.883} \approx \sqrt{28.123} \approx 5.3 \, \text{N s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 3000 \, \text{kg} \) truck accelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then a \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) ball is dropped. What is the horizontal distance traveled by the ball in \( 2 \, \text{s} \) relative to the ground? (Neglect air resistance)
questions.explanation: The truck’s initial velocity is zero, and it accelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \). Velocity at \( t = 4 \, \text{s} \): \( v = u + at = 0 + 3 \times 4 = 12 \, \text{m/s} \). The ball is dropped with this horizontal velocity relative to the ground. After dropping, no horizontal forces act (air resistance neglected), so the ball’s horizontal velocity remains \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \). Distance traveled in \( 2 \, \text{s} \): \( s = v \times t = 12 \times 2 = 24 \, \text{m} \). Relative to the ground, this is the total horizontal displacement from the drop point.

questions.question_text: A batsman hits a ball of mass \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) coming at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) straight back with the same speed. What is the impulse imparted to the ball?
questions.explanation: Impulse equals the change in momentum of the ball. Initial momentum \( p_i = m \times v = 0.2 \times 15 = 3 \, \text{kg m/s} \) (towards batsman). Final momentum \( p_f = 0.2 \times (-15) = -3 \, \text{kg m/s} \) (opposite direction). Change in momentum \( = p_f - p_i = -3 - 3 = -6 \, \text{N s} \). The magnitude of impulse is \( 6 \, \text{N s} \).

questions.question_text: A book of mass \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) is at rest on a horizontal table. What is the magnitude of the normal force exerted by the table on the book? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: The book is at rest, so the net force on it must be zero by Newton’s First Law. The weight of the book acts downward and is given by \( mg = 2 \times 10 = 20 \, \text{N} \). The normal force \( R \) acts upward and balances the weight. Thus, \( R = mg = 20 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.25 \)) is pulled by a \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 15 \, \text{N} \) force at \( 45^\circ \) upward aids the \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 45^\circ = \cos 45^\circ = 0.707 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 6 \, \text{kg} \): \( 6g - T = 6a \Rightarrow 60 - T = 6a \). For \( 4 \, \text{kg} \): \( T + F \cos 45^\circ - f_k = 4a \), \( N = mg - F \sin 45^\circ \). \( N = 4 \times 10 - 15 \times 0.707 = 40 - 10.605 = 29.395 \, \text{N} \). \( f_k = 0.25 \times 29.395 \approx 7.35 \, \text{N} \), \( F \cos 45^\circ = 15 \times 0.707 \approx 10.605 \, \text{N} \). \( T + 10.605 - 7.35 = 4a \Rightarrow T + 3.255 = 4a \). Solve: \( 60 - T = 6a \), \( T + 3.255 = 4a \Rightarrow 60 - (4a - 3.255) = 6a \Rightarrow 63.255 = 10a \Rightarrow a \approx 6.33 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( T = 60 - 6 \times 6.33 \approx 22 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 37^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_k = 0.3 \)) is pulled up by a \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley with a \( 20 \, \text{N} \) force opposing the \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 5 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - mg \sin\theta - f_k - 20 = 5a \), \( f_k = 0.3 \times 5 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 12 \, \text{N} \). \( T - 5 \times 10 \times 0.6 - 12 - 20 = 5a \Rightarrow T - 30 - 12 - 20 = 5a \Rightarrow T - 62 = 5a \). For \( 7 \, \text{kg} \): \( 7g - T = 7a \Rightarrow 70 - T = 7a \). Solve: \( 70 - T = 7a \), \( T - 62 = 5a \Rightarrow 70 - (5a + 62) = 7a \Rightarrow 8 = 12a \Rightarrow a = 0.67 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) mass in a lift accelerating upward at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) is pushed downward with a force of \( 50 \, \text{N} \) by a spring. What is the normal force on the floor? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Net force on mass: \( N - mg - F_{\text{spring}} = ma \). \( N - 10 \times 10 - 50 = 10 \times 3 \). \( N - 100 - 50 = 30 \). \( N - 150 = 30 \Rightarrow N = 180 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A man of mass \( 60 \, \text{kg} \) stands on a weighing scale in a lift moving upwards with an acceleration of \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is the reading on the scale? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: The scale reads the normal force \( N \), which is the apparent weight. Net force \( F_{\text{net}} = ma \), and \( N - mg = ma \). So, \( N = mg + ma \). Substitute: \( m = 60 \, \text{kg} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( a = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( N = 60 \times 10 + 60 \times 2 = 600 + 120 = 720 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.3 \)) is connected to a \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 12 \, \text{N} \) force opposes the \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: The \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) mass descends, pulling the \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block horizontally. For \( 6 \, \text{kg} \): \( 6g - T = 6a \Rightarrow 60 - T = 6a \). For \( 4 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - f_k - 12 = 4a \). Normal force: \( N = mg = 4 \times 10 = 40 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.3 \times 40 = 12 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 12 - 12 = 4a \Rightarrow T - 24 = 4a \). Solve: \( 60 - T = 6a \), \( T - 24 = 4a \). Substitute: \( 60 - (4a + 24) = 6a \Rightarrow 60 - 24 - 4a = 6a \Rightarrow 36 = 10a \). \( a = \frac{36}{10} = 3.6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 7.4 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 53^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_k = 0.15 \)) is pulled upward by a \( 9.4 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))
A \( 0.32 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) at \( 48 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Angular speed: \( \omega = 48 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{8\pi}{5} \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega^2 = \left(\frac{8\pi}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{64\pi^2}{25} \approx 25.27 \). Tension: \( T = m \omega^2 r = 0.32 \times 25.27 \times 1.5 \). \( T \approx 0.32 \times 25.27 \times 1.5 \approx 12.13 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A body of mass \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) is on a horizontal surface with a coefficient of static friction \( 0.2 \). What is the maximum static frictional force? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum static friction is given by \( f_s = \mu_s N \). The normal force \( N \) equals the weight: \( N = mg = 10 \times 10 = 100 \, \text{N} \). Coefficient of static friction \( \mu_s = 0.2 \). So, \( f_s = 0.2 \times 100 = 20 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.35 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 1.2 \, \text{m} \) at \( 50 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Angular speed: \( \omega = 50 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{5\pi}{3} \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega^2 = \left(\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{25\pi^2}{9} \approx 27.42 \). Tension: \( T = m \omega^2 r = 0.35 \times 27.42 \times 1.2 \). \( T \approx 0.35 \times 27.42 \times 1.2 \approx 11.52 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) ball moving at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \) to a wall rebounds at the same speed and angle. What is the impulse perpendicular to the wall? (Take \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: Perpendicular component (x-axis) reverses upon rebound. Initial: \( p_{x1} = m v \cos 53^\circ = 0.25 \times 18 \times 0.6 = 2.7 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Final: \( p_{x2} = -m v \cos 53^\circ = -0.25 \times 18 \times 0.6 = -2.7 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Impulse: \( \Delta p_x = -2.7 - 2.7 = -5.4 \, \text{N s} \). Magnitude: \( |\Delta p_x| = 5.4 \, \text{N s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) stone in a vertical circle of radius \( 4 \, \text{m} \) has a speed of \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) at the bottom. A tangential force of \( 4 \, \text{N} \) acts downward from bottom to top. What is the tension at the top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At bottom: \( T_b - mg = m v_b^2 / r \Rightarrow T_b - 1 \times 10 = 1 \times (20)^2 / 4 \). \( T_b - 10 = 100 \Rightarrow T_b = 110 \, \text{N} \). Work by tangential force increases KE: Arc length \( \pi r = 4\pi \approx 12.56 \, \text{m} \), \( W = 4 \times 12.56 = 50.24 \, \text{J} \). Initial KE: \( \frac{1}{2} m v_b^2 = 0.5 \times 1 \times 400 = 200 \, \text{J} \). PE gain: \( 2mg = 2 \times 1 \times 10 \times 4 = 40 \, \text{J} \). Final KE: \( 200 + 50.24 - 40 = 210.24 \, \text{J} \). \( \frac{1}{2} m v_t^2 = 210.24 \Rightarrow 0.5 v_t^2 = 210.24 \Rightarrow v_t^2 = 420.48 \Rightarrow v_t \approx 20.5 \, \text{m/s} \). At top: \( T_t + mg = m v_t^2 / r \Rightarrow T_t + 10 = 1 \times 420.48 / 4 \Rightarrow T_t + 10 = 105.12 \). \( T_t = 105.12 - 10 = 95.12 \, \text{N} \approx 95.1 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 2000 \, \text{kg} \) car on a banked road (\( \theta = 25^\circ \), \( \mu_s = 0.4 \)) turns at radius \( 80 \, \text{m} \) while accelerating tangentially at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is the maximum speed before slipping? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 25^\circ \approx 0.466 \))
questions.explanation: The maximum speed depends on radial forces (centripetal), not tangential acceleration, which affects speed change over time. Formula for max speed on a banked road with friction: \( v_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{rg \frac{\mu_s + \tan\theta}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \). Calculate the numerator: \( \mu_s + \tan\theta = 0.4 + 0.466 = 0.866 \). Calculate the denominator: \( 1 - \mu_s \tan\theta = 1 - 0.4 \times 0.466 = 1 - 0.1864 = 0.8136 \). Substitute: \( v_{\text{max}}^2 = 80 \times 10 \times \frac{0.866}{0.8136} \). \( \frac{0.866}{0.8136} \approx 1.0645 \), so \( v_{\text{max}}^2 = 800 \times 1.0645 \approx 851.6 \). \( v_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{851.6} \approx 29.18 \, \text{m/s} \). The tangential acceleration doesn’t alter the radial friction limit, so this is the maximum speed before slipping.

questions.question_text: A \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) stone in a vertical circle of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \) has a tension of \( 20 \, \text{N} \) at the bottom. What is the tension at the top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At bottom: \( T_b - mg = m v_b^2 / r \Rightarrow 20 - 0.4 \times 10 = 0.4 \times v_b^2 / 2 \). \( 20 - 4 = 0.2 v_b^2 \Rightarrow 16 = 0.2 v_b^2 \Rightarrow v_b^2 = 80 \Rightarrow v_b \approx 8.94 \, \text{m/s} \). Energy conservation: \( \frac{1}{2} m v_b^2 = \frac{1}{2} m v_t^2 + 2mg \) (no tangential force). \( 0.5 \times 0.4 \times 80 = 0.5 \times 0.4 \times v_t^2 + 2 \times 0.4 \times 10 \). \( 16 = 0.2 v_t^2 + 8 \Rightarrow 0.2 v_t^2 = 8 \Rightarrow v_t^2 = 40 \Rightarrow v_t \approx 6.32 \, \text{m/s} \). At top: \( T_t + mg = m v_t^2 / r \Rightarrow T_t + 4 = 0.4 \times 40 / 2 \Rightarrow T_t + 4 = 8 \Rightarrow T_t = 4 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1600 \, \text{kg} \) truck accelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \), then a \( 1.5 \, \text{kg} \) stone is dropped. What is the horizontal distance traveled by the stone in \( 2 \, \text{s} \)? (Neglect air resistance)
questions.explanation: Truck’s velocity after \( 3 \, \text{s} \): \( v = u + at = 0 + 3 \times 3 = 9 \, \text{m/s} \). Stone inherits this horizontal velocity upon drop. No horizontal forces act after drop (air resistance neglected). Distance: \( s = v \times t = 9 \times 2 = 18 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) mass is suspended by a rope with a \( 40 \, \text{N} \) horizontal force at its midpoint. What is the angle the rope makes with the vertical? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At midpoint: horizontal \( T \sin\theta = 40 \, \text{N} \), vertical \( T \cos\theta = mg = 10 \times 10 = 100 \, \text{N} \). Divide: \( \tan\theta = \frac{40}{100} = 0.4 \). \( \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.4) \). Using \( \tan 22^\circ \approx 0.404 \), \( \theta \approx 22^\circ \).

questions.question_text: A \( 8.4 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.25 \)) is pulled by a \( 6.4 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 19 \, \text{N} \) force opposes the \( 8.4 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 6.4 \, \text{kg} \): \( 6.4g - T = 6.4a \Rightarrow 64 - T = 6.4a \). For \( 8.4 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - f_k - 19 = 8.4a \). Normal: \( N = mg = 8.4 \times 10 = 84 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.25 \times 84 = 21 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 21 - 19 = 8.4a \Rightarrow T - 40 = 8.4a \). Solve: \( 64 - T = 6.4a \), \( T - 40 = 8.4a \). Substitute: \( 64 - (8.4a + 40) = 6.4a \Rightarrow 64 - 40 - 8.4a = 6.4a \Rightarrow 24 = 14.8a \). \( a \approx 1.62 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( T - 40 = 8.4 \times 1.62 \Rightarrow T - 40 \approx 13.61 \Rightarrow T \approx 53.61 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) stone tied to a string of length \( 1 \, \text{m} \) is whirled at \( 60 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the maximum tension the string can withstand if it breaks at \( 50 \, \text{N} \)?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force \( F = m \omega^2 r \). \( \omega = 60 \, \text{rev/min} = \frac{60 \times 2\pi}{60} = 2\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega^2 = (2\pi)^2 = 4\pi^2 \). \( F = 0.5 \times 4\pi^2 \times 1 \approx 19.74 \, \text{N} \). Since \( 19.74 \, \text{N} < 50 \, \text{N} \), maximum tension possible here is \( 50 \, \text{N} \) (breaking limit).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.38 \, \text{kg} \) stone in a vertical circle of radius \( 1.9 \, \text{m} \) has a tension of \( 28 \, \text{N} \) at the bottom. What is the tension at the top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At bottom: \( T_b - mg = m v_b^2 / r \Rightarrow 28 - 0.38 \times 10 = 0.38 \times v_b^2 / 1.9 \). \( 28 - 3.8 = 0.2 v_b^2 \Rightarrow 24.2 = 0.2 v_b^2 \Rightarrow v_b^2 = 121 \Rightarrow v_b = 11 \, \text{m/s} \). Energy: \( \frac{1}{2} m v_b^2 = \frac{1}{2} m v_t^2 + 2mg \). \( 0.5 \times 0.38 \times 121 = 0.5 \times 0.38 \times v_t^2 + 2 \times 0.38 \times 10 \). \( 22.99 = 0.19 v_t^2 + 7.6 \Rightarrow 0.19 v_t^2 = 15.39 \Rightarrow v_t^2 \approx 81 \Rightarrow v_t \approx 9 \, \text{m/s} \). At top: \( T_t + mg = m v_t^2 / r \Rightarrow T_t + 3.8 = 0.38 \times 81 / 1.9 \Rightarrow T_t + 3.8 \approx 16.2 \Rightarrow T_t \approx 12.4 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 85 \, \text{kg} \) man in a lift accelerating upward at \( 1.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) stands on a scale. What is the reading? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Scale reads normal force. Net force: \( N - mg = ma \). \( N - 85 \times 10 = 85 \times 1.8 \). \( N - 850 = 153 \Rightarrow N = 1003 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 60 \, \text{kg} \) man stands in a lift that accelerates downward at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) and then jumps with an upward acceleration of \( 7 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) relative to the lift. What is the normal force during the jump? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Relative to ground: \( a_{\text{net}} = a_{\text{jump}} + a_{\text{lift}} = 7 + (-3) = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) upward. \( N - mg = ma_{\text{net}} \). \( N - 60 \times 10 = 60 \times 4 \). \( N - 600 = 240 \Rightarrow N = 840 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) ball moving at \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \) to a wall rebounds elastically at \( 37^\circ \) with speed \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the impulse magnitude? (Take \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Initial: \( p_{x1} = 0.2 \times 25 \times 0.6 = 3 \, \text{kg m/s} \), \( p_{y1} = 0.2 \times 25 \times 0.8 = 4 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Final: \( p_{x2} = -0.2 \times 20 \times 0.8 = -3.2 \, \text{kg m/s} \), \( p_{y2} = 0.2 \times 20 \times 0.6 = 2.4 \, \text{kg m/s} \). \( \Delta p_x = -3.2 - 3 = -6.2 \, \text{kg m/s} \), \( \Delta p_y = 2.4 - 4 = -1.6 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Impulse \( |\Delta p| = \sqrt{(-6.2)^2 + (-1.6)^2} = \sqrt{38.44 + 2.56} = \sqrt{41} \approx 6.4 \, \text{N s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.34 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) at \( 42 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Angular speed: \( \omega = 42 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{7\pi}{5} \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega^2 = \left(\frac{7\pi}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{49\pi^2}{25} \approx 19.36 \). Tension: \( T = m \omega^2 r = 0.34 \times 19.36 \times 1.8 \). \( T \approx 0.34 \times 19.36 \times 1.8 \approx 11.85 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A car of mass \( 1200 \, \text{kg} \) takes a turn of radius \( 50 \, \text{m} \) on a banked road at \( 15^\circ \). What is the optimum speed to avoid friction? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 15^\circ \approx 0.268 \))
questions.explanation: Optimum speed \( v_0 = \sqrt{rg \tan\theta} \). Substitute: \( r = 50 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 15^\circ = 0.268 \). \( v_0 = \sqrt{50 \times 10 \times 0.268} \). \( v_0 = \sqrt{134} \approx 11.58 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 65 \, \text{kg} \) man in a lift accelerating upward at \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) stands on a scale. What is the reading? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Scale reads normal force. Net force: \( N - mg = ma \). \( N - 65 \times 10 = 65 \times 2.5 \). \( N - 650 = 162.5 \Rightarrow N = 812.5 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 53^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is pulled down by a \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley with a \( 15 \, \text{N} \) force opposing the \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 6 \, \text{kg} \): \( mg \sin\theta - f_k - T - 15 = 6a \), \( f_k = 0.2 \times 6 \times 10 \times 0.6 = 7.2 \, \text{N} \). \( 6 \times 10 \times 0.8 - 7.2 - T - 15 = 6a \Rightarrow 48 - 7.2 - 15 - T = 6a \Rightarrow 25.8 - T = 6a \). For \( 4 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - 4g = 4a \Rightarrow T - 40 = 4a \). Solve: \( 25.8 - (4a + 40) = 6a \Rightarrow 25.8 - 40 - 4a = 6a \Rightarrow -14.2 = 10a \). \( a = -1.42 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) (up incline), magnitude \( 1.42 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A stone of mass \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) is dropped from a height. What is the net force acting on it during its downward motion? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), ignore air resistance)
questions.explanation: The stone is in free fall, and the only force acting on it is gravity. The weight of the stone is \( F = mg \). Substitute: \( m = 0.2 \, \text{kg} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). So, \( F = 0.2 \times 10 = 2 \, \text{N} \), directed downward. Since air resistance is ignored, this is the net force.

questions.question_text: A \( 6.2 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is pulled by a \( 4.2 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 13 \, \text{N} \) force aids the \( 6.2 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 4.2 \, \text{kg} \): \( 4.2g - T = 4.2a \Rightarrow 42 - T = 4.2a \). For \( 6.2 \, \text{kg} \): \( T + 13 - f_k = 6.2a \). Normal: \( N = mg = 6.2 \times 10 = 62 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.2 \times 62 = 12.4 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T + 13 - 12.4 = 6.2a \Rightarrow T + 0.6 = 6.2a \).
