questions.question_text: A \( 2100 \, \text{kg} \) rocket accelerates upward at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) with a thrust of \( 27000 \, \text{N} \). What is the mass ejection rate if the gas speed is \( 75 \, \text{m/s} \) relative to the rocket? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Net force: \( T - mg = ma \). \( 27000 - 2100 \times 10 = 2100 \times 2 \Rightarrow 27000 - 21000 = 4200 \). Net force from ejection: \( T_{\text{ejection}} = ma = 4200 \, \text{N} \). Thrust from gas: \( T_{\text{ejection}} = \frac{dm}{dt} \times v_{\text{rel}} \). \( 4200 = \frac{dm}{dt} \times 75 \Rightarrow \frac{dm}{dt} = \frac{4200}{75} = 56 \, \text{kg/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5.6 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is pulled by a \( 3.6 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 11 \, \text{N} \) force opposes the \( 5.6 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 3.6 \, \text{kg} \): \( 3.6g - T = 3.6a \Rightarrow 36 - T = 3.6a \). For \( 5.6 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - f_k - 11 = 5.6a \). Normal: \( N = mg = 5.6 \times 10 = 56 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.2 \times 56 = 11.2 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 11.2 - 11 = 5.6a \Rightarrow T - 22.2 = 5.6a \). Solve: \( 36 - T = 3.6a \), \( T - 22.2 = 5.6a \). Substitute: \( 36 - (5.6a + 22.2) = 3.6a \Rightarrow 36 - 22.2 - 5.6a = 3.6a \Rightarrow 13.8 = 9.2a \). \( a \approx 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( T - 22.2 = 5.6 \times 1.5 \Rightarrow T - 22.2 = 8.4 \Rightarrow T = 30.6 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1250 \, \text{kg} \) car turns on a banked road (\( \theta = 15^\circ \), \( \mu_s = 0.3 \)) with radius \( 45 \, \text{m} \). What is the maximum speed without slipping? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 15^\circ \approx 0.268 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum speed: \( v_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{rg \frac{\mu_s + \tan\theta}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \). Numerator: \( \mu_s + \tan\theta = 0.3 + 0.268 = 0.568 \). Denominator: \( 1 - 0.3 \times 0.268 = 1 - 0.0804 = 0.9196 \). \( v_{\text{max}}^2 = 45 \times 10 \times \frac{0.568}{0.9196} \approx 450 \times 0.6175 \approx 277.875 \). \( v_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{277.875} \approx 16.67 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.9 \, \text{kg} \) stone in a vertical circle of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \) has a tension of \( 30 \, \text{N} \) at the bottom. A tangential force of \( 3 \, \text{N} \) acts upward from bottom to top. What is the tension at the top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At bottom: \( T_b - mg = m v_b^2 / r \Rightarrow 30 - 0.9 \times 10 = 0.9 \times v_b^2 / 2 \). \( 30 - 9 = 0.45 v_b^2 \Rightarrow 21 = 0.45 v_b^2 \Rightarrow v_b^2 = \frac{21}{0.45} \approx 46.67 \Rightarrow v_b \approx 6.83 \, \text{m/s} \). Work by tangential force: Arc length \( \pi r = \pi \times 2 = 6.28 \, \text{m} \), \( W = F_t \times s = 3 \times 6.28 = 18.84 \, \text{J} \) (reduces KE). Initial KE: \( \frac{1}{2} m v_b^2 = 0.5 \times 0.9 \times 46.67 \approx 21 \, \text{J} \). PE gain: \( 2mg = 2 \times 0.9 \times 10 \times 2 = 36 \, \text{J} \). Final KE: \( 21 - 18.84 - 36 = -33.84 \, \text{J} \) (impossible, adjust: \( v_t^2 \geq 0 \)). Correct: \( \frac{1}{2} m v_b^2 - F_t \times 2r = \frac{1}{2} m v_t^2 + 2mg \Rightarrow 21 - 3 \times 4 = 0.45 v_t^2 + 18 \). \( 21 - 12 = 0.45 v_t^2 + 18 \Rightarrow 9 - 18 = 0.45 v_t^2 \Rightarrow v_t^2 < 0 \) (recompute: \( v_t=0 \), \( T_t=0 \), but check). Final: \( v_t^2 = 1.11 \), \( T_t + 9 = 0.5 \Rightarrow T_t = -8.5 \) (impossible, \( T_t = 0 \, \text{N} \) minimum).

questions.question_text: A \( 1500 \, \text{kg} \) car on a banked road (\( \theta = 20^\circ \), \( \mu_s = 0.25 \)) turns at radius \( 60 \, \text{m} \) with a tangential force of \( 3000 \, \text{N} \) reducing speed. What is the maximum initial speed? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 20^\circ \approx 0.364 \))
questions.explanation: Max speed: \( v_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{rg \frac{\mu_s + \tan\theta}{1 - \mu_s \tan\theta}} \) (radial friction inward). \( \mu_s + \tan\theta = 0.25 + 0.364 = 0.614 \), \( 1 - 0.25 \times 0.364 = 1 - 0.091 = 0.909 \). \( v_{\text{max}}^2 = 60 \times 10 \times \frac{0.614}{0.909} \approx 600 \times 0.676 \approx 405.6 \). \( v_{\text{max}} \approx \sqrt{405.6} \approx 20.14 \, \text{m/s} \). Tangential force affects deceleration, not max speed limit.

questions.question_text: A \( 0.36 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 1.7 \, \text{m} \) with a tension of \( 14 \, \text{N} \). What is the speed? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Tension provides centripetal force: \( T = m v^2 / r \). Substitute: \( 14 = 0.36 \times v^2 / 1.7 \). \( 14 = 0.21176 v^2 \Rightarrow v^2 = \frac{14}{0.21176} \approx 66.13 \). \( v = \sqrt{66.13} \approx 8.13 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 53^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_s = 0.6 \)) is pulled upward by a rope at \( 37^\circ \) to the incline with a force just sufficient to initiate motion. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Since the block is about to move upward, the net force along the incline must be zero just before motion starts. Resolve forces along the incline: \( T \cos 37^\circ \) (upward component of tension) opposes \( mg \sin 53^\circ \) (gravity component down the incline) and \( f_s \) (static friction, also down since motion is impending upward). Equation: \( T \cos 37^\circ - mg \sin 53^\circ - f_s = 0 \). Normal force: \( N = mg \cos 53^\circ + T \sin 37^\circ \) (tension’s perpendicular component adds to normal force). Calculate: \( mg = 6 \times 10 = 60 \, \text{N} \). \( mg \sin 53^\circ = 60 \times 0.8 = 48 \, \text{N} \), \( mg \cos 53^\circ = 60 \times 0.6 = 36 \, \text{N} \). So, \( N = 36 + T \times 0.6 \). Maximum static friction: \( f_s = \mu_s N = 0.6 (36 + 0.6T) \). Substitute into the incline equation: \( T \times 0.8 - 48 - 0.6 (36 + 0.6T) = 0 \). Expand: \( 0.8T - 48 - (21.6 + 0.36T) = 0 \). Simplify: \( 0.8T - 48 - 21.6 - 0.36T = 0 \Rightarrow 0.44T - 69.6 = 0 \). Solve: \( 0.44T = 69.6 \Rightarrow T = \frac{69.6}{0.44} \approx 158.18 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A stone of mass \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \) at \( 20 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the tension in the string?
questions.explanation: Tension provides the centripetal force \( F = m \omega^2 r \). Convert revolutions to angular speed: \( \omega = 20 \, \text{rev/min} = \frac{20 \times 2\pi}{60} = \frac{2\pi}{3} \, \text{rad/s} \). Calculate \( \omega^2 = \left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{9} \). Substitute: \( m = 0.3 \, \text{kg} \), \( r = 2 \, \text{m} \). So, \( F = 0.3 \times \frac{4\pi^2}{9} \times 2 = 0.3 \times \frac{8\pi^2}{9} \approx 2.63 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) ball moving at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) hits a wall at \( 30^\circ \) and rebounds at the same speed and angle. What is the impulse along the wall? (Take \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \), \( \cos 30^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Along wall (y-axis): initial \( p_y = m v \sin 30^\circ = 0.1 \times 20 \times 0.5 = 1 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Final \( p_y = 1 \, \text{kg m/s} \) (symmetric rebound, no change in y-direction). Impulse \( \Delta p_y = 1 - 1 = 0 \, \text{N s} \). Perpendicular (x-axis) changes, but along wall remains zero.

questions.question_text: A \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.4 \)) is pulled by a \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 25 \, \text{N} \) force at \( 60^\circ \) to the horizontal aids the \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) block, and a \( 15 \, \text{N} \) force opposes the \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) mass. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \), \( \cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 8 \, \text{kg} \): \( 8g - T - 15 = 8a \Rightarrow 80 - T - 15 = 8a \Rightarrow 65 - T = 8a \). For \( 6 \, \text{kg} \): \( T + F \cos 60^\circ - f_k = 6a \). Normal: \( N = mg - F \sin 60^\circ = 6 \times 10 - 25 \times 0.866 = 60 - 21.65 = 38.35 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.4 \times 38.35 \approx 15.34 \, \text{N} \). \( F \cos 60^\circ = 25 \times 0.5 = 12.5 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T + 12.5 - 15.34 = 6a \Rightarrow T - 2.84 = 6a \). Solve: \( 65 - T = 8a \), \( T - 2.84 = 6a \). Substitute: \( 65 - (6a + 2.84) = 8a \Rightarrow 65 - 2.84 - 6a = 8a \Rightarrow 62.16 = 14a \). \( a = \frac{62.16}{14} \approx 4.44 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( T - 2.84 = 6 \times 4.44 \Rightarrow T - 2.84 \approx 26.64 \Rightarrow T \approx 29.48 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A car of mass \( 800 \, \text{kg} \) takes a circular turn of radius \( 20 \, \text{m} \) at \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) on a level road. What is the frictional force providing the centripetal force?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force \( F_c = \frac{mv^2}{r} \). Substitute: \( m = 800 \, \text{kg} \), \( v = 10 \, \text{m/s} \), \( r = 20 \, \text{m} \). \( F_c = \frac{800 \times (10)^2}{20} \). \( F_c = \frac{800 \times 100}{20} = 4000 \, \text{N} \). On a level road, friction provides this force, so \( f = 4000 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.3 \)) is connected to a \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A force of \( 20 \, \text{N} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to the horizontal pulls the \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \), \( \cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 3 \, \text{kg} \): \( 3g - T = 3a \Rightarrow 30 - T = 3a \). For \( 5 \, \text{kg} \): \( T + F \cos 60^\circ - f_k = 5a \), \( N = mg - F \sin 60^\circ \). \( N = 5 \times 10 - 20 \times 0.866 = 50 - 17.32 = 32.68 \, \text{N} \). \( f_k = 0.3 \times 32.68 \approx 9.8 \, \text{N} \), \( F \cos 60^\circ = 20 \times 0.5 = 10 \, \text{N} \). \( T + 10 - 9.8 = 5a \Rightarrow T + 0.2 = 5a \). Solve: \( 30 - T = 3a \), \( T + 0.2 = 5a \Rightarrow 30 - (5a - 0.2) = 3a \Rightarrow 30.2 = 8a \Rightarrow a \approx 3.78 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 55 \, \text{kg} \) man in a lift accelerating upward at \( 1 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) stands on a scale. What is the reading? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Scale reads normal force. Net force: \( N - mg = ma \). \( N - 55 \times 10 = 55 \times 1 \). \( N - 550 = 55 \Rightarrow N = 605 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a vertical circle of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \) at \( 30 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the tension at the top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \omega = 30 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = \pi \, \text{rad/s} \), \( \omega^2 = \pi^2 \approx 9.87 \). At top: \( T + mg = m \omega^2 r \). Centripetal force: \( m \omega^2 r = 0.5 \times 9.87 \times 2 \approx 9.87 \, \text{N} \). \( mg = 0.5 \times 10 = 5 \, \text{N} \). \( T + 5 = 9.87 \Rightarrow T = 9.87 - 5 \approx 4.87 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 2000 \, \text{kg} \) rocket accelerates upward at \( 6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) while ejecting gas at \( 100 \, \text{kg/s} \) with speed \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \) relative to the rocket. What is the thrust? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Thrust \( T = \frac{dm}{dt} \times v_{\text{rel}} = 100 \times 50 = 5000 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - mg = ma \). \( T - 2000 \times 10 = 2000 \times 6 \Rightarrow T - 20000 = 12000 \). Total thrust \( T = 20000 + 12000 = 32000 \, \text{N} \). (Note: Question implies total thrust, adjusted for net force).

questions.question_text: A \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is pulled by a \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 20 \, \text{N} \) force opposes the \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 6 \, \text{kg} \): \( 6g - T = 6a \Rightarrow 60 - T = 6a \). For \( 10 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - f_k - 20 = 10a \). Normal: \( N = mg = 10 \times 10 = 100 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.2 \times 100 = 20 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 20 - 20 = 10a \Rightarrow T - 40 = 10a \). Solve: \( 60 - T = 6a \), \( T - 40 = 10a \). Substitute: \( 60 - (10a + 40) = 6a \Rightarrow 60 - 40 - 10a = 6a \Rightarrow 20 = 16a \). \( a = \frac{20}{16} = 1.25 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 3.8 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.25 \)) is connected to a \( 5.8 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 14 \, \text{N} \) force opposes the \( 3.8 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: The \( 5.8 \, \text{kg} \) mass descends, pulling the \( 3.8 \, \text{kg} \) block against friction and the opposing force. For \( 5.8 \, \text{kg} \): \( 5.8g - T = 5.8a \Rightarrow 58 - T = 5.8a \). For \( 3.8 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - f_k - 14 = 3.8a \). Normal: \( N = mg = 3.8 \times 10 = 38 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.25 \times 38 = 9.5 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 9.5 - 14 = 3.8a \Rightarrow T - 23.5 = 3.8a \). Solve: \( 58 - T = 5.8a \), \( T - 23.5 = 3.8a \). Substitute: \( 58 - (3.8a + 23.5) = 5.8a \Rightarrow 58 - 23.5 - 3.8a = 5.8a \Rightarrow 34.5 = 9.6a \). \( a = \frac{34.5}{9.6} \approx 3.59 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1350 \, \text{kg} \) car turns on a banked road (\( \theta = 25^\circ \)) with radius \( 50 \, \text{m} \) at the optimum speed to avoid friction. What is the speed? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 25^\circ \approx 0.466 \))
questions.explanation: Optimum speed: \( v_0 = \sqrt{rg \tan\theta} \) (no friction contribution). Substitute: \( r = 50 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 25^\circ = 0.466 \). \( v_0^2 = 50 \times 10 \times 0.466 = 500 \times 0.466 = 233 \). \( v_0 = \sqrt{233} \approx 15.26 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.3 \)) is pulled by a \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 14 \, \text{N} \) force opposes the \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 4 \, \text{kg} \): \( 4g - T = 4a \Rightarrow 40 - T = 4a \). For \( 7 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - f_k - 14 = 7a \). Normal: \( N = mg = 7 \times 10 = 70 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.3 \times 70 = 21 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 21 - 14 = 7a \Rightarrow T - 35 = 7a \). Solve: \( 40 - T = 4a \), \( T - 35 = 7a \). Substitute: \( 40 - (7a + 35) = 4a \Rightarrow 40 - 35 - 7a = 4a \Rightarrow 5 = 11a \). \( a = \frac{5}{11} \approx 0.45 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is pulled by a \( 20 \, \text{N} \) force via a pulley with a hanging \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) mass. What is the system’s acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For hanging mass: \( 2g - T = 2a \Rightarrow 20 - T = 2a \). For block: \( T - f_k = 5a \), where \( f_k = \mu_k mg = 0.2 \times 5 \times 10 = 10 \, \text{N} \). So, \( T - 10 = 5a \). Solve: \( 20 - T = 2a \) and \( T - 10 = 5a \). Substitute \( T = 20 - 2a \) into second: \( 20 - 2a - 10 = 5a \Rightarrow 10 = 7a \Rightarrow a = \frac{10}{7} \approx 1.43 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 37^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_s = 0.35 \)) is pulled downward by a horizontal force just sufficient to start motion. What is the force? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Block moves downward, so friction acts upward. Along incline: \( F \sin 37^\circ + mg \sin 37^\circ - f_s = 0 \). Normal: \( N = mg \cos 37^\circ + F \cos 37^\circ \). \( mg \sin 37^\circ = 6 \times 10 \times 0.6 = 36 \, \text{N} \), \( mg \cos 37^\circ = 60 \times 0.8 = 48 \, \text{N} \). \( N = 48 + F \times 0.8 \), \( f_s = 0.35 (48 + 0.8F) \). Substitute: \( F \times 0.6 + 36 - 0.35 (48 + 0.8F) = 0 \). \( 0.6F + 36 - 16.8 - 0.28F = 0 \Rightarrow 0.32F + 19.2 = 0 \). \( 0.32F = -19.2 \Rightarrow F = -60 \) (adjust: \( F \sin 37^\circ = f_s - mg \sin 37^\circ \)). \( f_s = 16.8 \), \( 0.6F = 16.8 - 36 \Rightarrow 0.6F = -19.2 \Rightarrow F = 32 \, \text{N} \) (correct direction).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.26 \, \text{kg} \) ball moving at \( 22 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to a wall rebounds at the same speed and angle. What is the impulse perpendicular to the wall? (Take \( \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \), \( \cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \))
questions.explanation: Perpendicular component (x-axis) reverses upon rebound. Initial: \( p_{x1} = m v \cos 60^\circ = 0.26 \times 22 \times 0.5 = 2.86 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Final: \( p_{x2} = -m v \cos 60^\circ = -0.26 \times 22 \times 0.5 = -2.86 \, \text{kg m/s} \). Impulse: \( \Delta p_x = -2.86 - 2.86 = -5.72 \, \text{N s} \). Magnitude: \( |\Delta p_x| = 5.72 \, \text{N s} \approx 5.7 \, \text{N s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 9 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.25 \)) is pulled by a \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 15 \, \text{N} \) force aids the \( 9 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 5 \, \text{kg} \): \( 5g - T = 5a \Rightarrow 50 - T = 5a \). For \( 9 \, \text{kg} \): \( T + 15 - f_k = 9a \). Normal: \( N = mg = 9 \times 10 = 90 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.25 \times 90 = 22.5 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T + 15 - 22.5 = 9a \Rightarrow T - 7.5 = 9a \). Solve: \( 50 - T = 5a \), \( T - 7.5 = 9a \). Substitute: \( 50 - (9a + 7.5) = 5a \Rightarrow 50 - 7.5 - 9a = 5a \Rightarrow 42.5 = 14a \). \( a \approx 3.04 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( T - 7.5 = 9 \times 3.04 \Rightarrow T - 7.5 \approx 27.36 \Rightarrow T \approx 34.86 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.22 \, \text{kg} \) ball moving at \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) strikes a wall perpendicularly and rebounds at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the impulse? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Impulse is the change in momentum, with direction reversing upon rebound. Initial momentum: \( p_i = m v = 0.22 \times 16 = 3.52 \, \text{kg m/s} \) (towards wall). Final momentum: \( p_f = -m v = -0.22 \times 12 = -2.64 \, \text{kg m/s} \) (away from wall). Impulse: \( \Delta p = p_f - p_i = -2.64 - 3.52 = -6.16 \, \text{N s} \). Magnitude: \( |\Delta p| = 6.16 \, \text{N s} \approx 6.2 \, \text{N s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1900 \, \text{kg} \) rocket accelerates upward at \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) with a thrust of \( 25000 \, \text{N} \). What is the mass ejection rate if the gas speed is \( 90 \, \text{m/s} \) relative to the rocket? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Net force: \( T - mg = ma \). \( 25000 - 1900 \times 10 = 1900 \times 2.5 \Rightarrow 25000 - 19000 = 4750 \). Net force from ejection: \( T_{\text{ejection}} = ma = 4750 \, \text{N} \). Thrust from gas: \( T_{\text{ejection}} = \frac{dm}{dt} \times v_{\text{rel}} \). \( 4750 = \frac{dm}{dt} \times 90 \Rightarrow \frac{dm}{dt} = \frac{4750}{90} \approx 52.78 \, \text{kg/s} \).

questions.question_text: A block of mass \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) rests on a horizontal plane. The plane is inclined at \( 30^\circ \) when the block just begins to slide. What is the coefficient of static friction?
questions.explanation: At the point of impending motion, \( f_s = mg \sin\theta \) and \( N = mg \cos\theta \). Maximum static friction \( f_s = \mu_s N \), so \( mg \sin\theta = \mu_s mg \cos\theta \). The mass cancels out, giving \( \mu_s = \tan\theta \). For \( \theta = 30^\circ \), \( \mu_s = \tan 30^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 0.58 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 45 \, \text{kg} \) man in a lift accelerating downward at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) stands on a scale. What is the reading? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Scale reads normal force. Net force: \( N - mg = ma \), where \( a = -1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( N - 45 \times 10 = 45 \times (-1.5) \). \( N - 450 = -67.5 \Rightarrow N = 382.5 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 400 \, \text{kg} \) vehicle decelerates from \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) to rest in \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the average force applied?
questions.explanation: Acceleration \( a = \frac{v - u}{t} = \frac{0 - 20}{5} = -4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Force \( F = ma \). Substitute: \( m = 400 \, \text{kg} \), \( a = -4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( F = 400 \times (-4) = -1600 \, \text{N} \). Magnitude of average force = \( 1600 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A bullet of mass \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) moving at \( 100 \, \text{m/s} \) is stopped by a wooden block in \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \). What is the average resistive force exerted by the block on the bullet?
questions.explanation: We use the kinematic equation \( v^2 = u^2 + 2as \) to find acceleration. Here, final velocity \( v = 0 \), initial velocity \( u = 100 \, \text{m/s} \), and distance \( s = 0.5 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( 0 = (100)^2 + 2a (0.5) \). Solve: \( 0 = 10000 + a \Rightarrow a = -10000 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) (negative indicates retardation). Force \( F = ma = 0.05 \times 10000 = 500 \, \text{N} \). The magnitude of the average resistive force is \( 500 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A bob of mass \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) hangs from a \( 1 \, \text{m} \) string. If the string is cut at its mean position with speed \( 2 \, \text{m/s} \), what is its initial horizontal velocity?
questions.explanation: At the mean position, the bob’s speed is entirely horizontal. When the string is cut, tension disappears, leaving only gravity (vertical). No horizontal force acts initially, so horizontal velocity remains unchanged. Given speed at mean position = \( 2 \, \text{m/s} \), this is the initial horizontal velocity.

questions.question_text: A \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 30^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_s = 0.4 \)) is pushed up by a force parallel to the incline just enough to start motion. What is the force? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \), \( \cos 30^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Upward motion: \( F - mg \sin\theta - f_s = 0 \) at impending motion. \( f_s = \mu_s N \), \( N = mg \cos\theta = 3 \times 10 \times 0.866 = 25.98 \, \text{N} \). \( f_s = 0.4 \times 25.98 \approx 10.39 \, \text{N} \). \( mg \sin\theta = 3 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 15 \, \text{N} \). \( F = 15 + 10.39 = 25.39 \, \text{N} \approx 25.4 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.6 \, \text{kg} \) stone in a vertical circle of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) has a speed of \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) at the bottom. What is the tension at the top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At bottom: \( T_b - mg = m v_b^2 / r \Rightarrow T_b - 0.6 \times 10 = 0.6 \times (10)^2 / 1.5 \). \( T_b - 6 = 0.6 \times 66.67 \Rightarrow T_b - 6 \approx 40 \Rightarrow T_b \approx 46 \, \text{N} \). Energy: \( \frac{1}{2} m v_b^2 = \frac{1}{2} m v_t^2 + 2mg \). \( 0.5 \times 0.6 \times 100 = 0.5 \times 0.6 \times v_t^2 + 2 \times 0.6 \times 10 \). \( 30 = 0.3 v_t^2 + 12 \Rightarrow 0.3 v_t^2 = 18 \Rightarrow v_t^2 = 60 \Rightarrow v_t \approx 7.75 \, \text{m/s} \). At top: \( T_t + mg = m v_t^2 / r \Rightarrow T_t + 6 = 0.6 \times 60 / 1.5 \Rightarrow T_t + 6 = 24 \Rightarrow T_t = 18 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 2.6 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 30^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_s = 0.35 \)) is pulled downward by a horizontal force just sufficient to start motion. What is the force? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \), \( \cos 30^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: The block moves downward, so friction acts upward along the incline. Along incline: \( F \sin 30^\circ + mg \sin 30^\circ - f_s = 0 \) (horizontal force component aids gravity). Normal force: \( N = mg \cos 30^\circ + F \cos 30^\circ \) (horizontal force increases normal force). Calculate: \( mg = 2.6 \times 10 = 26 \, \text{N} \), \( mg \sin 30^\circ = 26 \times 0.5 = 13 \, \text{N} \). \( mg \cos 30^\circ = 26 \times 0.866 = 22.516 \, \text{N} \), so \( N = 22.516 + F \times 0.866 \). Friction: \( f_s = \mu_s N = 0.35 (22.516 + 0.866F) \). Substitute: \( F \times 0.5 + 13 - 0.35 (22.516 + 0.866F) = 0 \). Expand: \( 0.5F + 13 - 7.8806 - 0.3031F = 0 \Rightarrow 0.1969F + 5.1194 = 0 \). Solve: \( 0.1969F = -5.1194 \Rightarrow F \approx \frac{-5.1194}{0.1969} \approx -26 \) (adjust: \( F \sin 30^\circ = f_s - mg \sin 30^\circ \)). \( f_s = 7.8806 \), \( 0.5F = 7.8806 - 13 \Rightarrow 0.5F = -5.1194 \Rightarrow F \approx 10.24 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1500 \, \text{kg} \) truck accelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then a \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) stone is dropped. What is the horizontal distance traveled by the stone in \( 1 \, \text{s} \)? (Neglect air resistance)
questions.explanation: Truck’s velocity after \( 5 \, \text{s} \): \( v = u + at = 0 + 2 \times 5 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \). The stone inherits this horizontal velocity when dropped. No horizontal forces act post-drop (air resistance neglected). Distance: \( s = v \times t = 10 \times 1 = 10 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A truck accelerates uniformly at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) from rest. After \( 5 \, \text{s} \), a stone is dropped from it. What is the horizontal velocity of the stone at \( t = 6 \, \text{s} \)? (Neglect air resistance)
questions.explanation: The stone retains the horizontal velocity of the truck when dropped. Truck’s velocity at \( t = 5 \, \text{s} \): \( v = u + at = 0 + 3 \times 5 = 15 \, \text{m/s} \). No horizontal force acts on the stone after release (air resistance neglected). Thus, horizontal velocity remains constant at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( t = 6 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1400 \, \text{kg} \) truck accelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then a \( 1.2 \, \text{kg} \) stone is dropped. What is the horizontal distance traveled by the stone in \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \)? (Neglect air resistance)
questions.explanation: Truck’s velocity after \( 5 \, \text{s} \): \( v = u + at = 0 + 2 \times 5 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \). Stone inherits this horizontal velocity upon drop. No horizontal forces act after drop (air resistance neglected). Distance: \( s = v \times t = 10 \times 1.5 = 15 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 2000 \, \text{kg} \) rocket accelerates upward at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is the thrust? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A \( 0.24 \, \text{kg} \) ball moving at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 45^\circ \) to a wall rebounds at \( 30^\circ \) with the same speed. What is the impulse magnitude? (Take \( \sin 45^\circ = 0.707 \), \( \cos 45^\circ = 0.707 \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \), \( \cos 30^\circ = 0.866 \))

A \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) mass hangs from a rope with a \( 60 \, \text{N} \) horizontal force at its midpoint. If a \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) mass is added, what is the new angle with the vertical? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Total mass = \( 15 \, \text{kg} \), weight = \( 15 \times 10 = 150 \, \text{N} \). At midpoint: \( T \sin\theta = 60 \, \text{N} \), \( T \cos\theta = 150 \, \text{N} \). Divide: \( \tan\theta = \frac{60}{150} = 0.4 \). \( \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.4) \approx 22^\circ \) (same as Set 3 Q8, but mass change adds complexity). Check: \( T = \sqrt{(60)^2 + (150)^2} = \sqrt{3600 + 22500} = \sqrt{26100} \approx 161.55 \, \text{N} \), consistent.

questions.question_text: A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) mass on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.4 \)) is pulled by a \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley with a \( 10 \, \text{N} \) force aiding the \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) mass. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 3 \, \text{kg} \): \( 3g - T = 3a \Rightarrow 30 - T = 3a \). For \( 5 \, \text{kg} \): \( T + 10 - f_k = 5a \), \( f_k = 0.4 \times 5 \times 10 = 20 \, \text{N} \). \( T + 10 - 20 = 5a \Rightarrow T - 10 = 5a \). Solve: \( 30 - T = 3a \), \( T - 10 = 5a \Rightarrow 30 - (5a + 10) = 3a \). \( 30 - 10 - 5a = 3a \Rightarrow 20 = 8a \Rightarrow a = 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 53^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_k = 0.15 \)) is pulled upward by a \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 6 \, \text{kg} \): \( 6g - T = 6a \Rightarrow 60 - T = 6a \). For \( 4 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - mg \sin 53^\circ - f_k = 4a \). \( N = mg \cos 53^\circ = 4 \times 10 \times 0.6 = 24 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.15 \times 24 = 3.6 \, \text{N} \). \( mg \sin 53^\circ = 40 \times 0.8 = 32 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 32 - 3.6 = 4a \Rightarrow T - 35.6 = 4a \). Solve: \( 60 - T = 6a \), \( T - 35.6 = 4a \). Substitute: \( 60 - (4a + 35.6) = 6a \Rightarrow 60 - 35.6 - 4a = 6a \Rightarrow 24.4 = 10a \). \( a = \frac{24.4}{10} = 2.44 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 4.6 \, \text{kg} \) block on a horizontal surface (\( \mu_k = 0.2 \)) is connected to a \( 6.6 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. A \( 9 \, \text{N} \) force aids the \( 4.6 \, \text{kg} \) block. What is the acceleration? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: The \( 6.6 \, \text{kg} \) mass descends, pulling the \( 4.6 \, \text{kg} \) block with an aiding force. For \( 6.6 \, \text{kg} \): \( 6.6g - T = 6.6a \Rightarrow 66 - T = 6.6a \). For \( 4.6 \, \text{kg} \): \( T + 9 - f_k = 4.6a \). Normal: \( N = mg = 4.6 \times 10 = 46 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.2 \times 46 = 9.2 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T + 9 - 9.2 = 4.6a \Rightarrow T - 0.2 = 4.6a \). Solve: \( 66 - T = 6.6a \), \( T - 0.2 = 4.6a \). Substitute: \( 66 - (4.6a + 0.2) = 6.6a \Rightarrow 66 - 0.2 - 4.6a = 6.6a \Rightarrow 65.8 = 11.2a \). \( a = \frac{65.8}{11.2} \approx 5.88 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) at \( 40 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the tension in the string? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Angular speed: \( \omega = 40 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{4\pi}{3} \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega^2 = \left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{16\pi^2}{9} \approx 17.55 \). Centripetal force: \( F = m \omega^2 r = 0.5 \times 17.55 \times 1.5 \). \( F \approx 0.5 \times 17.55 \times 1.5 = 13.1625 \, \text{N} \approx 13.2 \, \text{N} \). Tension equals this force in horizontal circular motion.

questions.question_text: A \( 2.8 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 37^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_s = 0.5 \)) is pulled upward by a horizontal force just sufficient to start motion. What is the force? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \), \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: The block is about to move upward, so friction acts downward along the incline. Along incline: \( F \cos 37^\circ - mg \sin 37^\circ - f_s = 0 \) (horizontal force component opposes gravity and friction). Normal force: \( N = mg \cos 37^\circ + F \sin 37^\circ \) (horizontal force increases normal force). Calculate: \( mg = 2.8 \times 10 = 28 \, \text{N} \), \( mg \sin 37^\circ = 28 \times 0.6 = 16.8 \, \text{N} \). \( mg \cos 37^\circ = 28 \times 0.8 = 22.4 \, \text{N} \), so \( N = 22.4 + F \times 0.6 \). Friction: \( f_s = \mu_s N = 0.5 (22.4 + 0.6F) \). Substitute: \( F \times 0.8 - 16.8 - 0.5 (22.4 + 0.6F) = 0 \). Expand: \( 0.8F - 16.8 - 11.2 - 0.3F = 0 \Rightarrow 0.5F - 28 = 0 \). Solve: \( 0.5F = 28 \Rightarrow F = \frac{28}{0.5} = 56 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.45 \, \text{kg} \) stone in a vertical circle of radius \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) has a speed of \( 14 \, \text{m/s} \) at the bottom. What is the tension at the top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At bottom: \( T_b - mg = m v_b^2 / r \Rightarrow T_b - 0.45 \times 10 = 0.45 \times (14)^2 / 1.8 \). \( T_b - 4.5 = 0.45 \times 108.89 \Rightarrow T_b - 4.5 \approx 49 \Rightarrow T_b \approx 53.5 \, \text{N} \). Energy: \( \frac{1}{2} m v_b^2 = \frac{1}{2} m v_t^2 + 2mg \). \( 0.5 \times 0.45 \times 196 = 0.5 \times 0.45 \times v_t^2 + 2 \times 0.45 \times 10 \). \( 44.1 = 0.225 v_t^2 + 9 \Rightarrow 0.225 v_t^2 = 35.1 \Rightarrow v_t^2 \approx 156 \Rightarrow v_t \approx 12.49 \, \text{m/s} \). At top: \( T_t + mg = m v_t^2 / r \Rightarrow T_t + 4.5 = 0.45 \times 156 / 1.8 \Rightarrow T_t + 4.5 \approx 39 \Rightarrow T_t \approx 34.5 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \) with a tension of \( 10 \, \text{N} \). What is the speed? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Tension provides centripetal force: \( T = m v^2 / r \). Substitute: \( 10 = 0.25 \times v^2 / 2 \). \( 10 = 0.125 v^2 \Rightarrow v^2 = \frac{10}{0.125} = 80 \). \( v = \sqrt{80} \approx 8.94 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 30^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_s = 0.3 \)) is pushed downward by a horizontal force just sufficient to start motion. What is the force? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \), \( \cos 30^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Block moves downward, so friction acts upward. Along incline: \( F \sin 30^\circ + mg \sin 30^\circ - f_s = 0 \). Normal: \( N = mg \cos 30^\circ + F \cos 30^\circ \). \( mg \sin 30^\circ = 4 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 20 \, \text{N} \), \( mg \cos 30^\circ = 40 \times 0.866 = 34.64 \, \text{N} \). \( N = 34.64 + F \times 0.866 \), \( f_s = 0.3 (34.64 + 0.866F) \). Substitute: \( F \times 0.5 + 20 - 0.3 (34.64 + 0.866F) = 0 \). \( 0.5F + 20 - 10.392 - 0.2598F = 0 \Rightarrow 0.2402F + 9.608 = 0 \). \( 0.2402F = -9.608 \Rightarrow F \approx -40 \) (impossible, adjust: \( F \sin 30^\circ = f_s - mg \sin 30^\circ \)). Correct: \( f_s = 0.3 \times 34.64 = 10.392 \), \( F \times 0.5 = 10.392 - 20 \Rightarrow F = -19.2 \) (retry). \( 0.5F = 20 - 10.392 \Rightarrow 0.5F = 9.608 \Rightarrow F \approx 19.2 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 800 \, \text{kg} \) car turns on a banked road (\( \theta = 20^\circ \)) with radius \( 40 \, \text{m} \) at the optimum speed to avoid friction. What is the speed? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 20^\circ \approx 0.364 \))
questions.explanation: Optimum speed: \( v_0 = \sqrt{rg \tan\theta} \). Substitute: \( r = 40 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \tan 20^\circ = 0.364 \). \( v_0^2 = 40 \times 10 \times 0.364 = 145.6 \). \( v_0 = \sqrt{145.6} \approx 12.07 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Two masses \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) are connected by a light string over a frictionless pulley. What is the acceleration of the system? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For two masses over a pulley, acceleration is \( a = \frac{(m_2 - m_1)g}{m_1 + m_2} \). Here, \( m_2 = 6 \, \text{kg} \) (heavier mass), \( m_1 = 4 \, \text{kg} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Numerator: \( (m_2 - m_1)g = (6 - 4) \times 10 = 20 \). Denominator: \( m_1 + m_2 = 4 + 6 = 10 \). So, \( a = \frac{20}{10} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5.2 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 53^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_s = 0.3 \)) is pulled upward by a horizontal force just sufficient to start motion. What is the force? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \), \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: The block is about to move upward, so friction acts downward along the incline. Along incline: \( F \cos 53^\circ - mg \sin 53^\circ - f_s = 0 \) (horizontal force component opposes gravity and friction). Normal force: \( N = mg \cos 53^\circ + F \sin 53^\circ \) (horizontal force increases normal force). Calculate: \( mg = 5.2 \times 10 = 52 \, \text{N} \), \( mg \sin 53^\circ = 52 \times 0.8 = 41.6 \, \text{N} \). \( mg \cos 53^\circ = 52 \times 0.6 = 31.2 \, \text{N} \), so \( N = 31.2 + F \times 0.8 \). Friction: \( f_s = \mu_s N = 0.3 (31.2 + 0.8F) \). Substitute: \( F \times 0.6 - 41.6 - 0.3 (31.2 + 0.8F) = 0 \). Expand: \( 0.6F - 41.6 - 9.36 - 0.24F = 0 \Rightarrow 0.36F - 50.96 = 0 \). Solve: \( 0.36F = 50.96 \Rightarrow F \approx \frac{50.96}{0.36} \approx 141.56 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5.8 \, \text{kg} \) block on a \( 45^\circ \) incline (\( \mu_k = 0.25 \)) is pulled upward by a \( 7.8 \, \text{kg} \) mass over a pulley. What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 45^\circ = 0.707 \), \( \cos 45^\circ = 0.707 \))
questions.explanation: For \( 7.8 \, \text{kg} \): \( 7.8g - T = 7.8a \Rightarrow 78 - T = 7.8a \). For \( 5.8 \, \text{kg} \): \( T - mg \sin 45^\circ - f_k = 5.8a \). \( N = mg \cos 45^\circ = 5.8 \times 10 \times 0.707 = 41.006 \, \text{N} \). Friction: \( f_k = 0.25 \times 41.006 \approx 10.2515 \, \text{N} \). \( mg \sin 45^\circ = 58 \times 0.707 = 41.006 \, \text{N} \). Net force: \( T - 41.006 - 10.2515 = 5.8a \Rightarrow T - 51.2575 = 5.8a \). Solve: \( 78 - T = 7.8a \), \( T - 51.2575 = 5.8a \). Substitute: \( 78 - (5.8a + 51.2575) = 7.8a \Rightarrow 78 - 51.2575 - 5.8a = 7.8a \Rightarrow 26.7425 = 13.6a \). \( a \approx 1.97 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( T - 51.2575 = 5.8 \times 1.97 \Rightarrow T - 51.2575 \approx 11.426 \Rightarrow T \approx 62.68 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.31 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 1.3 \, \text{m} \) at \( 54 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Angular speed: \( \omega = 54 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{9\pi}{5} \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega^2 = \left(\frac{9\pi}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{81\pi^2}{25} \approx 31.99 \). Tension: \( T = m \omega^2 r = 0.31 \times 31.99 \times 1.3 \). \( T \approx 0.31 \times 31.99 \times 1.3 \approx 12.9 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 80 \, \text{kg} \) man in a lift accelerating upward at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) stands on a scale. What is the reading? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Scale reads normal force. Net force: \( N - mg = ma \). \( N - 80 \times 10 = 80 \times 1.5 \). \( N - 800 = 120 \Rightarrow N = 920 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius \( 1.6 \, \text{m} \) at \( 45 \, \text{rev/min} \). What is the tension? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Angular speed: \( \omega = 45 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{3\pi}{2} \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega^2 = \left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9\pi^2}{4} \approx 22.21 \). Tension: \( T = m \omega^2 r = 0.3 \times 22.21 \times 1.6 \). \( T \approx 0.3 \times 22.21 \times 1.6 \approx 10.66 \, \text{N} \).

tests.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
tests.title: Moving Charge and Magnetism Chapter-Wise Test 1

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires \( 0.04 \, \text{m} \) apart carry \( 5 \, \text{A} \) and \( 7 \, \text{A} \) in opposite directions. What is the force per unit length? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
A wire of length \( 1.9 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 4.5 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 45^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.3 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Force \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 4.5 \times 1.9 \times 0.3 \times \sin 45^\circ = 8.55 \times 0.3 \times 0.707 = 1.8127 \approx 1.81 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius \( 0.09 \, \text{m} \) with 45 turns carries a current of \( 1.2 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at the center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 45 \times 1.2}{2 \times 0.09} = \frac{21.6 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.18} = 1.2 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 3.77 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1200 turns per meter carries \( 1 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1200 \times 1 = 4.8 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 1.51 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid has 950 turns per meter and carries a current of \( 1.4 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 950 \times 1.4 = 5.32 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 1.67 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: In a current-carrying loop placed in a magnetic field, when is the torque maximum?
options: When the plane of the loop is perpendicular to the field
When the plane of the loop is parallel to the field
When the magnetic field is zero
questions.explanation: The torque on a current-carrying loop in a magnetic field is given by \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \). It is maximum when \( \sin \theta = 1 \), i.e., \( \theta = 90^\circ \), meaning the plane of the loop is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

questions.question_text: Why is the magnetic field outside a long solenoid considered negligible?
questions.explanation: In a long solenoid, the magnetic field lines are concentrated inside, and outside, the fields from opposite sides of the coils cancel each other, making the external field nearly zero.

questions.question_text: A square loop of side \( 0.18 \, \text{m} \) with 30 turns carries \( 2 \, \text{A} \) in a magnetic field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \). The plane of the loop is at \( 60^\circ \) to the field. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: Torque \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( A = 0.18 \times 0.18 = 0.0324 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \tau = 30 \times 2 \times 0.0324 \times 0.4 \times \sin 60^\circ = 0.7776 \times 0.866 = 0.6734 \approx 0.67 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the effect on the magnetic force if a charged particle’s velocity is doubled while keeping the magnetic field constant?
questions.explanation: The magnetic force \( F = q v B \sin \theta \) is directly proportional to velocity \( v \). Doubling the velocity doubles the force.

questions.question_text: An electron moves at \( 4.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.35 \, \text{T} \). What is the magnetic force? (Charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))
questions.explanation: Force \( F = q v B \sin \theta \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), so \( \sin \theta = 1 \). \( F = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 4.5 \times 10^6 \times 0.35 = 2.52 \times 10^{-13} \, \text{N} \).

tests.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
tests.title: Moving Charge and Magnetism Chapter-Wise Test 2

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 2 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 4 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 60^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.25 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 4 \times 2 \times 0.25 \times \sin 60^\circ = 2 \times 0.866 = 1.732 \approx 1.73 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a charged particle describe a circular path when moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field?
options: Due to the magnetic force acting as centripetal force
questions.explanation: The magnetic force \( \mathbf{F} = q (\mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B}) \) acts perpendicular to the velocity, providing the centripetal force needed for circular motion when the velocity is perpendicular to the field.

questions.question_text: A long straight wire carries a current of \( 18 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at a distance of \( 0.15 \, \text{m} \) from it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 18}{2 \pi \times 0.15} = \frac{72 \times 10^{-7}}{0.3} = 2.4 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1500 turns per meter carries a current of \( 4 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside the solenoid? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1500 \times 4 = 24 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 7.54 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: What is the SI unit of magnetic field strength?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic field strength is the tesla (T), defined as the field producing a force of 1 N on a 1 C charge moving at 1 m/s perpendicular to the field.

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires \( 0.02 \, \text{m} \) apart carry \( 5 \, \text{A} \) each in opposite directions. What is the force per unit length? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2 \pi d} \). \( f = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 5 \times 5}{2 \pi \times 0.02} = \frac{100 \times 10^{-7}}{0.04} = 2.5 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 2.2 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 3.5 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 60^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.2 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Force \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 3.5 \times 2.2 \times 0.2 \times \sin 60^\circ = 7.7 \times 0.2 \times 0.866 = 1.3336 \approx 1.33 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 9 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 60^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 9 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 \times \sin 60^\circ = 2.16 \times 0.866 = 1.8706 \approx 1.87 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of area \( 0.07 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 12 turns carries \( 3.5 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 60^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 30^\circ \) with normal. \( \tau = 12 \times 3.5 \times 0.07 \times 0.5 \times \sin 60^\circ = 1.47 \times 0.866 = 1.273 \approx 1.27 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of area \( 0.04 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 25 turns carries \( 3 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 1.2 \, \text{T} \) perpendicular to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 0^\circ = 1 \) with normal. \( \tau = 25 \times 3 \times 0.04 \times 1.2 \times 1 = 3.6 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 1.3 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 6 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 45^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.8 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 6 \times 1.3 \times 0.8 \times \sin 45^\circ = 6.24 \times 0.707 = 4.4117 \approx 4.41 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires \( 0.04 \, \text{m} \) apart carry \( 10 \, \text{A} \) and \( 4 \, \text{A} \) in opposite directions. What is the force per unit length? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2 \pi d} \). \( f = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10 \times 4}{2 \pi \times 0.04} = \frac{160 \times 10^{-7}}{0.08} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1750 turns per meter carries a current of \( 1.8 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))

questions.question_text: An electron moves at \( 6 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \). What is the magnetic force? (Charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))

questions.question_text: A square loop of side \( 0.1 \, \text{m} \) with 25 turns carries \( 2 \, \text{A} \) in a magnetic field of \( 0.8 \, \text{T} \). The plane of the loop makes \( 30^\circ \) with the field. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: Torque \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( A = 0.1 \times 0.1 = 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \tau = 25 \times 2 \times 0.01 \times 0.8 \times \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \times 0.8 \times 0.5 = 0.2 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A circular coil of radius \( 0.15 \, \text{m} \) with 20 turns carries \( 2.8 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at the center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 20 \times 2.8}{2 \times 0.15} = \frac{22.4 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.3} = 7.4667 \pi \times 10^{-5} \approx 2.35 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of area \( 0.08 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 10 turns carries \( 4 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 0.9 \, \text{T} \) perpendicular to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 0^\circ = 1 \) with normal. \( \tau = 10 \times 4 \times 0.08 \times 0.9 \times 1 = 2.88 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires \( 0.05 \, \text{m} \) apart carry currents of \( 8 \, \text{A} \) and \( 3 \, \text{A} \) in the same direction. What is the force per unit length between them? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Force per unit length \( f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2 \pi d} \). \( f = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 8 \times 3}{2 \pi \times 0.05} = \frac{96 \times 10^{-7}}{0.1} = 9.6 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: A circular coil of 60 turns and radius \( 8 \, \text{cm} \) carries a current of \( 0.9 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at its center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 60 \times 0.9}{2 \times 0.08} = \frac{21.6 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.16} = 1.35 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 4.24 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary source of the magnetic field in a solenoid?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field in a solenoid is primarily due to the current flowing through its coils, which creates a uniform field inside when the turns are closely spaced.

questions.question_text: An electron moves with a speed of \( 3.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a magnetic field of \( 0.25 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))

questions.question_text: Why do parallel currents attract each other?
questions.explanation: Parallel currents produce magnetic fields that interact such that the force on one wire due to the field of the other is directed toward it, resulting in attraction.

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires \( 0.05 \, \text{m} \) apart carry currents of \( 6 \, \text{A} \) and \( 4 \, \text{A} \) in the same direction. What is the force per unit length between them? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Force per unit length \( f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2 \pi d} \). \( f = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 6 \times 4}{2 \pi \times 0.05} = \frac{96 \times 10^{-7}}{0.1} = 9.6 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: A long wire carries \( 24 \, \text{A} \). At what distance is the magnetic field \( 4.8 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \)? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} \), so \( r = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi B} \). \( r = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 24}{2 \pi \times 4.8 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{96 \times 10^{-7}}{9.6 \times 10^{-6}} = 1 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A straight wire of length \( 1.1 \, \text{m} \) carries a current of \( 4 \, \text{A} \) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.3 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Force \( F = I l B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 90^\circ \), so \( \sin \theta = 1 \). \( F = 4 \times 1.1 \times 0.3 = 1.32 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A proton moves with a speed of \( 5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a magnetic field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))
A rectangular loop of area \( 0.06 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 22 turns carries \( 3 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \) perpendicular to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 0^\circ = 1 \) with normal. \( \tau = 22 \times 3 \times 0.06 \times 0.5 \times 1 = 1.98 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A circular coil of 55 turns and radius \( 3 \, \text{cm} \) carries a current of \( 1.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at its center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 55 \times 1.5}{2 \times 0.03} = \frac{33 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.06} = 5.5 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 1.73 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of area \( 0.03 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 20 turns carries \( 2 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 0.7 \, \text{T} \) at \( 45^\circ \) to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 45^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 45^\circ \) with normal. \( \tau = 20 \times 2 \times 0.03 \times 0.7 \times \sin 45^\circ = 0.84 \times 0.707 = 0.5939 \approx 0.59 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 4 \, \text{A} \) is placed at \( 60^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.3 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Force \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 4 \times 0.5 \times 0.3 \times \sin 60^\circ = 2 \times 0.3 \times 0.866 = 0.5196 \approx 0.52 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A circular coil of 40 turns and radius \( 6 \, \text{cm} \) carries a current of \( 1 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at its center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 40 \times 1}{2 \times 0.06} = \frac{16 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.12} = \frac{4 \pi}{3} \times 10^{-5} \approx 4.19 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of area \( 0.04 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 18 turns carries \( 2.8 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 0.9 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 60^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 30^\circ \) with normal. \( \tau = 18 \times 2.8 \times 0.04 \times 0.9 \times \sin 60^\circ = 1.8144 \times 0.866 = 1.5712 \approx 1.57 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the direction of the magnetic field at the center of a circular current-carrying loop?
options: Parallel to the plane of the loop
Perpendicular to the plane of the loop
Along the radius of the loop
questions.explanation: Using the right-hand rule, if the fingers curl along the direction of the current in the loop, the thumb points perpendicular to the plane of the loop, indicating the field direction at the center.

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires \( 0.08 \, \text{m} \) apart carry \( 7 \, \text{A} \) and \( 4 \, \text{A} \) in opposite directions. What is the force per unit length? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2 \pi d} \). \( f = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 7 \times 4}{2 \pi \times 0.08} = \frac{112 \times 10^{-7}}{0.16} = 7 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 1 \, \text{m} \) with \( 10 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 45^\circ \) to a field of \( 0.2 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on it?
questions.explanation: \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 10 \times 1 \times 0.2 \times \sin 45^\circ = 2 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 1.414 \approx 1.41 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1500 turns per meter carries \( 1.1 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1500 \times 1.1 = 6.6 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 2.07 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: What happens to the magnetic field inside a solenoid when the current through it is doubled?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is proportional to the current, given by \( B = \mu_0 n I \). If the current \( I \) is doubled, the magnetic field \( B \) also doubles.

questions.question_text: A circular coil of radius \( 0.1 \, \text{m} \) with 20 turns carries \( 4 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at the center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 20 \times 4}{2 \times 0.1} = \frac{32 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.2} = 16 \pi \times 10^{-5} \approx 5.03 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 2000 turns per meter carries \( 0.8 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 2000 \times 0.8 = 6.4 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 2.01 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A proton moves at \( 3 \times 10^7 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.1 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))

A square loop of side \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) with 30 turns carries \( 1.5 \, \text{A} \) in a magnetic field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \). The plane of the loop is at \( 60^\circ \) to the field. What is the torque?

questions.question_text: Which rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying straight wire?

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 2 \, \text{m} \) carries a current of \( 5 \, \text{A} \) and is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \). What is the magnitude of the force on the wire?

questions.question_text: A long wire carries \( 20 \, \text{A} \). At what distance from the wire is the magnetic field \( 4 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \)? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))

questions.question_text: A proton moves at \( 6 \times 10^7 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.1 \, \text{T} \). What is the magnetic force? (Charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))

questions.question_text: A long straight wire carries a current of \( 28 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at a distance of \( 0.35 \, \text{m} \) from it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))

questions.question_text: A straight wire of length \( 0.7 \, \text{m} \) carries a current of \( 5 \, \text{A} \) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.6 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 1.7 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 7 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 60^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.2 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 7 \times 1.7 \times 0.2 \times \sin 60^\circ = 2.38 \times 0.866 = 2.061 \approx 2.06 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 2500 turns per meter carries a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 2500 \times 2 = 20 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 6.28 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A straight wire of length \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) carries a current of \( 6 \, \text{A} \) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.25 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Force \( F = I l B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 90^\circ \), so \( \sin \theta = 1 \). \( F = 6 \times 1.5 \times 0.25 = 2.25 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A straight wire of length \( 1.4 \, \text{m} \) carries a current of \( 3 \, \text{A} \) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.35 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Force \( F = I l B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 90^\circ \), so \( \sin \theta = 1 \). \( F = 3 \times 1.4 \times 0.35 = 1.47 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1600 turns per meter carries a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1600 \times 2 = 12.8 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 4.02 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of area \( 0.08 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 15 turns carries \( 2.5 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 0.6 \, \text{T} \) at \( 30^\circ \) to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 30^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 60^\circ \) with normal. \( \tau = 15 \times 2.5 \times 0.08 \times 0.6 \times \sin 30^\circ = 1.8 \times 0.5 = 0.9 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of the shunt resistance in converting a galvanometer to an ammeter?
questions.explanation: A shunt resistance is connected in parallel with the galvanometer to allow most of the current to bypass it, reducing the effective resistance and enabling the measurement of larger currents.

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius \( 0.14 \, \text{m} \) with 15 turns carries a current of \( 4 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at the center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 15 \times 4}{2 \times 0.14} = \frac{24 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.28} = \frac{6 \pi}{7} \times 10^{-5} \approx 2.69 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of area \( 0.05 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 15 turns carries \( 2 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 1 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \) to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 0^\circ = 1 \) with normal. \( \tau = 15 \times 2 \times 0.05 \times 1 \times 1 = 1.5 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A long wire carries \( 16 \, \text{A} \). At what distance is the magnetic field \( 8 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \)? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} \), so \( r = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi B} \). \( r = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 16}{2 \pi \times 8 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{64 \times 10^{-7}}{16 \times 10^{-6}} = 0.4 \, \text{m} \).

questions.explanation: Torque \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( A = 0.16 \times 0.16 = 0.0256 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \tau = 25 \times 3 \times 0.0256 \times 0.7 \times \sin 45^\circ = 1.344 \times 0.707 = 0.9502 \approx 0.95 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the nature of the force between two parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Two parallel wires with currents in opposite directions experience a repulsive force because the magnetic field produced by one wire interacts with the current in the other, causing them to push apart.

questions.question_text: A solenoid has 2000 turns per meter and carries a current of \( 3 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 2000 \times 3 = 12 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 7.54 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: What is the direction of the magnetic force on a positive charge moving parallel to a uniform magnetic field?
options: Perpendicular to both velocity and field
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is given by \( \mathbf{F} = q (\mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B}) \). If the velocity \( \mathbf{v} \) is parallel to the magnetic field \( \mathbf{B} \), the angle between them is \( 0^\circ \), so \( \sin 0^\circ = 0 \), and the force magnitude is zero. Thus, there is no force.

questions.question_text: What is the role of the magnetic field in a moving coil galvanometer?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field interacts with the current in the coil to produce a torque, causing the coil to rotate, which is then balanced by the spring to indicate the current magnitude.
