questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 850 \times 1.6 = 5.44 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 1.71 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A square loop of side \( 0.12 \, \text{m} \) with 35 turns carries \( 1.8 \, \text{A} \) in a magnetic field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \). The plane of the loop is at \( 30^\circ \) to the field. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: Torque \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( A = 0.12 \times 0.12 = 0.0144 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \tau = 35 \times 1.8 \times 0.0144 \times 0.5 \times \sin 30^\circ = 0.9072 \times 0.5 = 0.4536 \approx 0.45 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the condition for zero torque on a current-carrying loop in a magnetic field?
options: Field is perpendicular to the loop
Plane of the loop is parallel to the field
Area of the loop is zero
questions.explanation: Torque \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \) is zero when \( \sin \theta = 0 \), i.e., \( \theta = 0^\circ \) or \( 180^\circ \), meaning the plane of the loop is parallel to the magnetic field.

questions.question_text: A square loop of side \( 0.25 \, \text{m} \) with 20 turns carries \( 2.5 \, \text{A} \) in a magnetic field of \( 0.3 \, \text{T} \). The plane of the loop is at \( 45^\circ \) to the field. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: Torque \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( A = 0.25 \times 0.25 = 0.0625 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \tau = 20 \times 2.5 \times 0.0625 \times 0.3 \times \sin 45^\circ = 0.9375 \times 0.707 = 0.6633 \approx 0.66 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A proton moves at \( 4 \times 10^7 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.05 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))

An electron moves at \( 5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a magnetic field of \( 0.2 \, \text{T} \). What is the magnetic force on it? (Charge of electron = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))
questions.explanation: Force \( F = q v B \sin \theta \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), so \( \sin \theta = 1 \). \( F = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 5 \times 10^6 \times 0.2 = 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular loop of area \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 10 turns carries \( 3 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 60^\circ \) to the plane means \( \sin 30^\circ \) with the normal. \( \tau = 10 \times 3 \times 0.02 \times 0.5 \times \sin 60^\circ = 0.3 \times 0.866 = 0.2598 \approx 0.26 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A straight wire of length \( 1.2 \, \text{m} \) carries a current of \( 6 \, \text{A} \) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.25 \, \text{T} \). What is the force acting on the wire?
questions.explanation: Force \( F = I l B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 90^\circ \), so \( \sin \theta = 1 \). \( F = 6 \times 1.2 \times 0.25 = 1.8 \, \text{N} \).

tests.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
tests.title: Moving Charge and Magnetism Chapter-Wise Test 13

questions.question_text: What happens to the torque on a rectangular current loop if the magnetic field direction is reversed?
questions.explanation: Torque is given by \( \boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{m} \times \mathbf{B} \). Reversing the magnetic field \( \mathbf{B} \) reverses the direction of the torque vector, but its magnitude remains the same.

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius \( 0.15 \, \text{m} \) with 15 turns carries a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at the center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 15 \times 2}{2 \times 0.15} = \frac{12 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.3} = 4 \pi \times 10^{-5} \approx 1.26 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A proton moves with a speed of \( 2 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its circular path? (Mass of proton = \( 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))
questions.explanation: Radius \( r = \frac{mv}{qB} \). Substitute: \( r = \frac{1.67 \times 10^{-27} \times 2 \times 10^6}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 0.5} = \frac{3.34 \times 10^{-21}}{8 \times 10^{-20}} = 4.175 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{m} = 4.18 \, \text{cm} \).

questions.question_text: A long wire carries \( 12 \, \text{A} \). At what distance is the magnetic field \( 2.4 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \)? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} \), so \( r = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi B} \). \( r = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 12}{2 \pi \times 2.4 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{48 \times 10^{-7}}{4.8 \times 10^{-6}} = 1 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: Which factor does not affect the magnetic field produced by a current element according to the Biot-Savart law?
options: Angle between current and position vector
questions.explanation: The Biot-Savart law states \( d\mathbf{B} \propto \frac{I d\mathbf{l} \times \mathbf{r}}{r^3} \). The field depends on current, length of the element, distance, and angle, but not on the mass of the conductor.

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius \( 0.13 \, \text{m} \) with 20 turns carries a current of \( 3.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at the center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 20 \times 3.5}{2 \times 0.13} = \frac{28 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.26} = 1.0769 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 3.38 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 8 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 60^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 8 \times 1.5 \times 0.5 \times \sin 60^\circ = 12 \times 0.5 \times 0.866 = 5.196 \approx 5.2 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A circular coil of 70 turns and radius \( 7 \, \text{cm} \) carries a current of \( 0.8 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at its center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 70 \times 0.8}{2 \times 0.07} = \frac{22.4 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.14} = 1.6 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 5.03 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: An electron moves with a speed of \( 2 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a magnetic field of \( 0.7 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))
A circular coil of radius \( 0.12 \, \text{m} \) with 35 turns carries \( 1.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at the center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 35 \times 1.5}{2 \times 0.12} = \frac{21 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.24} = 8.75 \pi \times 10^{-5} \approx 2.75 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

tests.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
tests.title: Moving Charge and Magnetism Chapter-Wise Test 14

questions.question_text: A long straight wire carries a current of \( 10 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at a point \( 0.1 \, \text{m} \) from the wire? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10}{2 \pi \times 0.1} = \frac{4 \times 10^{-6}}{0.2} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A long straight wire carries a current of \( 40 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at a distance of \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) from it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 40}{2 \pi \times 0.5} = \frac{160 \times 10^{-7}}{1} = 1.6 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid has 600 turns per meter and carries a current of \( 3 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 600 \times 3 = 7.2 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 2.26 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid has 1250 turns per meter and carries a current of \( 1.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1250 \times 1.5 = 7.5 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 2.36 × 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1100 turns per meter carries \( 1.8 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1100 \times 1.8 = 7.92 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 2.49 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires \( 0.12 \, \text{m} \) apart carry currents of \( 4 \, \text{A} \) and \( 7 \, \text{A} \) in the same direction. What is the force per unit length between them? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Force per unit length \( f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2 \pi d} \). \( f = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 4 \times 7}{2 \pi \times 0.12} = \frac{112 \times 10^{-7}}{0.24} = 4.67 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the shape of the magnetic field lines produced by a straight current-carrying wire?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire form concentric circles centered on the wire, as derived from the Biot-Savart law or Ampere’s law.

questions.question_text: An electron moves at \( 2.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))

An electron moves at \( 6.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.2 \, \text{T} \). What is the radius of its path? (Mass = \( 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} \), charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))
A rectangular loop of area \( 0.06 \, \text{m}^2 \) with 15 turns carries \( 2.5 \, \text{A} \) in a field of \( 0.8 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to the plane. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( \theta = 60^\circ \) to plane means \( \sin 30^\circ \) with normal. \( \tau = 15 \times 2.5 \times 0.06 \times 0.8 \times \sin 60^\circ = 1.8 \times 0.866 = 1.5588 \approx 1.56 \, \text{N m} \).

tests.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
tests.title: Moving Charge and Magnetism Chapter-Wise Test 15

questions.question_text: A long wire carries \( 14 \, \text{A} \). At what distance is the magnetic field \( 7 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \)? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} \), so \( r = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi B} \). \( r = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 14}{2 \pi \times 7 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{56 \times 10^{-7}}{14 \times 10^{-6}} = 0.4 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1400 turns per meter carries a current of \( 2.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field inside it? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \mu_0 n I \). \( B = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1400 \times 2.5 = 14 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 4.40 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A wire of length \( 0.8 \, \text{m} \) carrying \( 5 \, \text{A} \) is at \( 30^\circ \) to a magnetic field of \( 0.8 \, \text{T} \). What is the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Force \( F = I l B \sin \theta \). \( F = 5 \times 0.8 \times 0.8 \times \sin 30^\circ = 4 \times 0.8 \times 0.5 = 1.6 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A circular coil of 45 turns and radius \( 6 \, \text{cm} \) carries a current of \( 1.2 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at its center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 45 \times 1.2}{2 \times 0.06} = \frac{21.6 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.12} = 1.8 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 5.65 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A circular loop of radius \( 0.08 \, \text{m} \) with 60 turns carries a current of \( 0.75 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic field at the center? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Magnetic field \( B = \frac{\mu_0 N I}{2 R} \). \( B = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 60 \times 0.75}{2 \times 0.08} = \frac{18 \pi \times 10^{-6}}{0.16} = 1.125 \pi \times 10^{-4} \approx 3.53 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A long wire carries \( 15 \, \text{A} \). At what distance is the magnetic field \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \)? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: \( B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} \), so \( r = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi B} \). \( r = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 15}{2 \pi \times 3 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{60 \times 10^{-7}}{6 \times 10^{-6}} = 1 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: Which property of magnetic field lines distinguishes them from electric field lines?
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines form closed loops because there are no magnetic monopoles, unlike electric field lines, which originate from positive charges and terminate at negative charges or extend to infinity.

questions.question_text: A square loop of side \( 0.15 \, \text{m} \) with 50 turns carries \( 1 \, \text{A} \) in a magnetic field of \( 0.6 \, \text{T} \). The plane of the loop is at \( 30^\circ \) to the field. What is the torque?
questions.explanation: Torque \( \tau = N I A B \sin \theta \), where \( A = 0.15 \times 0.15 = 0.0225 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \tau = 50 \times 1 \times 0.0225 \times 0.6 \times \sin 30^\circ = 0.675 \times 0.5 = 0.3375 \approx 0.34 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires \( 0.08 \, \text{m} \) apart carry currents of \( 5 \, \text{A} \) and \( 3 \, \text{A} \) in the same direction. What is the force per unit length between them? (\( \mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m/A} \))
questions.explanation: Force per unit length \( f = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2 \pi d} \). \( f = \frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 5 \times 3}{2 \pi \times 0.08} = \frac{60 \times 10^{-7}}{0.16} = 3.75 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: An electron moves at \( 7 \times 10^6 \, \text{m/s} \) perpendicular to a field of \( 0.2 \, \text{T} \). What is the magnetic force? (Charge = \( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \))
questions.explanation: Force \( F = q v B \sin \theta \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), so \( \sin \theta = 1 \). \( F = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 7 \times 10^6 \times 0.2 = 2.24 \times 10^{-13} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A material’s ability to retain strong magnetism after an external field is removed is a property of:
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials, especially hard ones, retain strong magnetism after the external field is removed due to the persistence of aligned domains, making them suitable for permanent magnets. This distinguishes them from soft ferromagnetic or other materials.

questions.question_text: A solenoid produces \( B = 1.2 \, \text{T} \) with a core of \( \mu_r = 400 \) and \( n = 2000 \, \text{m}^{-1} \). What is the current \( I \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A dipole with \( m = 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \) has torque:
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), \( \sin 90^\circ = 1 \). \( \tau = 0.9 \times 0.5 \times 1 = 0.45 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet produces a field of \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \) at \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A bar magnet with \( m = 1.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \) produces a field at \( 0.25 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A bar magnet with \( m = 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \) produces a field at \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
Why do magnetic field lines never intersect, unlike some electric field lines in complex charge distributions?
options: The field direction would be ambiguous at the intersection
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines represent the direction of the magnetic field at each point. If they intersected, it would imply two different directions for the field at the same point, which is physically impossible. This uniqueness stems from the vector nature of the magnetic field and the absence of magnetic monopoles.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet produces a field of \( 6 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \) at \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The reason a soft ferromagnetic material loses its magnetism when the external field is removed is:
options: Its domains randomize without the field
questions.explanation: Soft ferromagnetic materials have low coercivity and do not retain significant magnetization after the external field is removed. Their domains, which align strongly in the presence of a field, return to a random orientation due to minimal internal resistance, unlike hard ferromagnets.

questions.question_text: A superconductor has a susceptibility \( \chi \) of:
questions.explanation: Superconductors exhibit perfect diamagnetism with \( \chi = -1 \), as the magnetic field is completely expelled (Meissner effect).

questions.question_text: Which material has a negative \( \chi \) and is weakly repelled by a magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have a small negative \( \chi \) and are weakly repelled from stronger to weaker field regions.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet produces a field of \( 5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \) at \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
Which of the following materials has \( \chi \) negative and tends to move from stronger to weaker magnetic field regions?
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have negative \( \chi \) and are repelled from stronger to weaker field regions.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1100 turns per meter and current \( 1.5 \, \text{A} \) has a core with \( \mu_r = 200 \). What is \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A bar magnet produces a magnetic field of \( 2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \) at a point \( 0.1 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material has \( B = 0.54 \, \text{T} \) and \( M = 4.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material that conducts electricity perfectly while expelling magnetic fields relies on:
questions.explanation: Superconductors achieve perfect conductivity and expel magnetic fields (Meissner effect) below their critical temperature, where induced surface currents counteract the external field, a phenomenon tied to zero resistance and perfect diamagnetism.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 2.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 2.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.2 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 2.0}{(0.2)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{4.0}{0.008} = 5.0 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A material that conducts electricity perfectly and repels magnetic fields is likely operating as:
questions.explanation: Superconductors, when below their critical temperature, exhibit zero electrical resistance (perfect conductivity) and perfect diamagnetism (repelling magnetic fields via the Meissner effect), a unique combination not seen in other materials.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet’s field resembles that of a solenoid because:
options: It can be modeled as circulating currents
It has a uniform field throughout
Its field lines are straight and parallel
questions.explanation: A bar magnet’s magnetic field mimics that of a solenoid due to the analogy that its magnetization can be modeled as arising from circulating currents within the material, similar to the current loops in a solenoid, producing comparable field patterns with north and south poles.

questions.question_text: The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 3 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: \( B_m = \mu_0 M \). Given: \( M = 3 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \), \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \). \( B_m = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 3 \times 10^5 = 0.3768 \, \text{T} \approx 0.38 \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A material that exhibits strong magnetism due to the growth and alignment of microscopic domains when placed in an external field is:
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials have microscopic domains that align and grow in the presence of an external magnetic field, leading to strong magnetization. This cooperative behavior amplifies the field inside the material significantly.

questions.question_text: The net magnetic flux through a closed surface surrounding a bar magnet is:
questions.explanation: Gauss’s law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, as magnetic field lines form closed loops with no monopoles.

questions.question_text: A material with \( \mu_r = 600 \) and \( H = 300 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with \( m = 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \) is:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 60^\circ \), \( \cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \). Substitute: \( U_m = -0.6 \times 0.3 \times 0.5 = -0.09 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 400 turns per meter carries a current of \( 6 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \). Given: \( n = 400 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 6 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 400 \times 6 = 2400 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 700 turns per meter carries a current of \( 3 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \). Given: \( n = 700 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 3 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 700 \times 3 = 2100 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A ferromagnetic material has \( \mu_r = 1000 \) and \( H = 500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is the magnetic field \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: \( B = \mu_0 \mu_r H \). Given: \( \mu_r = 1000 \), \( H = 500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \), \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1000 \times 500 = 0.628 \, \text{T} \approx 0.63 \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with \( m = 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \) is:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), \( \cos 90^\circ = 0 \). Substitute: \( U_m = -0.9 \times 0.4 \times 0 = 0 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: The reason a magnetic field does not exert a force along its own direction on a moving charge is:
options: The force is perpendicular to the field
The field cancels the charge’s motion
The force aligns with the field lines
The charge moves parallel to the field
questions.explanation: The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by \( F = q (\mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B}) \), which is always perpendicular to both the velocity \( \mathbf{v} \) and the magnetic field \( \mathbf{B} \). Thus, the force has no component along the field direction, as the cross product ensures orthogonality.

questions.question_text: The reason a superconductor can levitate a magnet is:
questions.explanation: Superconductors exhibit perfect diamagnetism (Meissner effect), expelling all magnetic field lines from their interior by inducing surface currents that create an opposing field. This repulsion allows them to levitate a magnet, a phenomenon unique to their zero permeability state.

questions.question_text: A solenoid produces \( B = 0.6 \, \text{T} \) with a core of \( \mu_r = 200 \) and \( n = 1000 \, \text{m}^{-1} \). What is the current \( I \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material with susceptibility \( \chi = -6 \times 10^{-5} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
The magnetic flux through a closed surface is always zero. This statement is a consequence of:
options: The presence of magnetic dipoles only
questions.explanation: The absence of magnetic monopoles means that magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops. As a result, the number of field lines entering a closed surface equals the number leaving it, leading to a net magnetic flux of zero, as per Gauss’s law for magnetism.

questions.question_text: A material with \( \mu_r = 600 \) and \( H = 400 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material with \( \mu_r = 250 \) and \( H = 700 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 2.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A magnetic dipole experiences a torque of \( 0.02 \, \text{N m} \) in a field of \( 0.4 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \). What is its magnetic moment?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \), so \( m = \frac{\tau}{B \sin\theta} \). Given: \( \tau = 0.02 \, \text{N m} \), \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), \( \sin 90^\circ = 1 \). \( m = \frac{0.02}{0.4 \times 1} = 0.05 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: The magnetic field lines of a solenoid resemble those of a bar magnet because:
options: It acts as a magnetic dipole
questions.explanation: A solenoid’s field lines emerge from one end (acting as a north pole) and enter the other (acting as a south pole), mirroring a bar magnet’s dipole field pattern due to the cumulative effect of current loops behaving like a magnetic dipole.

questions.question_text: The magnetic field lines of a bar magnet are closest together:
options: At the center of the magnet
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines are closest together near the poles of a bar magnet, where the field strength is greatest, as the density of lines reflects the magnitude of the magnetic field.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 800 turns per meter and current \( 1.5 \, \text{A} \) has a core with \( \mu_r = 300 \). What is \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A magnetic dipole of moment \( 0.3 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is in a uniform field of \( 0.7 \, \text{T} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is the torque on it?
questions.explanation: Torque is \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.3 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.7 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 30^\circ \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \). Substitute: \( \tau = 0.3 \times 0.7 \times 0.5 = 0.105 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with original \( m = 3.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is cut along its length into two equal parts. What is \( m \) of each part?
questions.explanation: When cut along its length, each part typically has half the original magnetic moment in standard problems. Given: \( m = 3.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \). Each part: \( m' = \frac{3.0}{2} = 1.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: Which material exhibits perfect diamagnetism with \( \chi = -1 \) and is used in levitating trains?
questions.explanation: Superconductors exhibit perfect diamagnetism with \( \chi = -1 \) due to the Meissner effect and are used in applications like magnetically levitated trains.

questions.question_text: A material placed in a magnetic field reduces the field inside it slightly due to:
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials reduce the magnetic field inside them slightly because an external field induces weak currents that create an opposing magnetic moment, resulting in a small negative susceptibility and a minor field reduction.

questions.question_text: The magnetic field outside a long solenoid is nearly zero because:
options: The field lines are confined within the solenoid
questions.explanation: In a long solenoid, the magnetic field lines are confined within the core, forming closed loops that exit and re-enter at the ends. Outside, the field lines spread widely and cancel out, resulting in a negligible field due to the solenoid’s symmetry and length.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with original \( m = 2.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is cut transversely into two equal parts. What is \( m \) of each part?
questions.explanation: When cut transversely, each part has half the original magnetic moment. Given: \( m = 2.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \). Each part: \( m' = \frac{2.4}{2} = 1.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet produces a field of \( 4 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \) at \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A bar magnet produces a field of \( 7 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \) at \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 1.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 1.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.4 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 1.2}{(0.4)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2.4}{0.064} = 3.75 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: The fact that magnetic field lines do not start or end at any point is a direct result of:
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines form closed loops because there are no magnetic monopoles; every field line exiting a region must re-enter, ensuring continuity, as dictated by the absence of isolated magnetic charges in nature.

questions.question_text: A material that completely expels magnetic field lines from its interior when cooled to a very low temperature is likely to be:
questions.explanation: Superconductors exhibit perfect diamagnetism (Meissner effect) when cooled below their critical temperature, expelling all magnetic field lines from their interior. This is due to induced surface currents that cancel the internal field, a property unique to superconductors.

questions.question_text: A material has \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \) and \( M = 2 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A bar magnet is cut transversely into two equal parts. If the original magnetic moment was \( 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \), what is the magnetic moment of each part?
questions.explanation: When a bar magnet is cut transversely, each half becomes a magnet with half the original magnetic moment. Given: \( m = 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \). Each part: \( m' = \frac{0.6}{2} = 0.3 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A material that weakly repels magnetic field lines and has a susceptibility slightly less than zero is classified as:
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have a small negative susceptibility (\( \chi < 0 \)), causing them to weakly repel magnetic field lines. This occurs because an applied magnetic field induces an opposing magnetic moment in the material, reducing the field inside it.

questions.question_text: A paramagnetic material with \( \chi = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \) in \( H = 600 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has magnetization \( M \):
A material’s weak attraction to a magnetic field is due to:
options: Partial alignment of atomic magnetic moments
questions.explanation: Paramagnetic materials exhibit weak attraction to a magnetic field because their atomic or molecular magnetic moments, which are randomly oriented in the absence of a field, partially align with an external field, producing a small positive magnetization.

questions.question_text: A paramagnetic material with \( \chi = 7 \times 10^{-4} \) in \( H = 3000 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has magnetization \( M \):
The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is uniform because:
options: The field lines are parallel and evenly spaced
The field lines diverge at the ends
The current varies along its length
The field cancels outside the solenoid
questions.explanation: In a long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform inside due to the symmetrical arrangement of current-carrying loops, which produce overlapping field lines that are parallel and evenly spaced along the solenoid’s axis, minimizing edge effects in the central region.

questions.question_text: The magnetic field inside a material increases significantly when placed in an external field due to:
options: Alignment and growth of magnetic domains
questions.explanation: In ferromagnetic materials, the magnetic field inside increases significantly because the external field aligns and expands pre-existing magnetic domains, enhancing the overall magnetization and field strength far beyond the applied field.

questions.question_text: The reason a bar magnet cannot exert a torque on itself is:
options: It lacks an external field to act on it
questions.explanation: A bar magnet cannot exert a torque on itself because torque requires an external field acting on the dipole. The field produced by the magnet itself does not generate a net rotational effect on its own structure, as internal forces cancel out.

questions.question_text: A material has \( B = 0.65 \, \text{T} \) and \( M = 4.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A magnetic dipole of moment \( 0.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed in a uniform field of \( 0.3 \, \text{T} \) at \( 45^\circ \). What is the torque on the dipole?
questions.explanation: Torque is \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 45^\circ \), \( \sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 \). Substitute: \( \tau = 0.2 \times 0.3 \times 0.707 = 0.04242 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.042 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the magnetic field at a point on the equatorial line of a bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 2 \, \text{A m}^2 \) at a distance of \( 10 \, \text{cm} \) from its center? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field on the equatorial line is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 2 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.1 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2}{(0.1)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2}{0.001} = 2 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A material with susceptibility \( \chi = 4 \times 10^{-3} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
questions.explanation: \( \mu_r = 1 + \chi \). Given: \( \chi = 4 \times 10^{-3} \). Substitute: \( \mu_r = 1 + 4 \times 10^{-3} = 1.004 \).

questions.question_text: A material with susceptibility \( \chi = -3 \times 10^{-5} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
A solenoid with 700 turns per meter carries a current of \( 2 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \). Given: \( n = 700 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 2 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 700 \times 2 = 1400 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A material with susceptibility \( \chi = -8 \times 10^{-5} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
A dipole with \( m = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \) at \( 45^\circ \) has potential energy:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 45^\circ \), \( \cos 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 \). \( U_m = -0.8 \times 0.5 \times 0.707 \approx -0.2828 \, \text{J} \approx -0.28 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: The net magnetic flux through a closed surface surrounding a toroid with current is:
questions.explanation: Gauss’s law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, as magnetic field lines form closed loops with no monopoles.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with original \( m = 1.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is cut along its length into two equal parts. What is \( m \) of each part?
questions.explanation: When cut along its length, each part typically has half the original magnetic moment in standard problems. Given: \( m = 1.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \). Each part: \( m' = \frac{1.4}{2} = 0.7 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 2.8 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A bar magnet of magnetic moment \( 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 20 \, \text{cm} \) from its center along its axis. Calculate the magnetic field \( B \) at that point. (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis of a bar magnet is given by \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 20 \, \text{cm} = 0.2 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 0.5}{(0.2)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{1}{0.008} = 10^{-7} \times 125 = 1.25 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 1.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is at \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A bar magnet produces a field of \( 8 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \) at \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material with \( \mu_r = 150 \) and \( H = 800 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
If a bar magnet is broken into two pieces, each piece retains both a north and a south pole. This observation supports the idea that:
options: Magnetic fields can be shielded completely
The magnet loses its magnetism upon breaking
questions.explanation: Unlike electric charges, magnetic poles cannot be isolated. Breaking a magnet creates two smaller magnets, each with its own north and south pole, indicating that magnetic monopoles do not exist in nature, a key principle in magnetism.

questions.question_text: A material placed in a magnetic field increases the field inside it slightly and moves toward stronger field regions. This behavior is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Paramagnetic materials have a small positive susceptibility (\( \chi > 0 \)), causing a slight enhancement of the magnetic field inside them due to the weak alignment of atomic magnetic moments with the external field. They are attracted to regions of stronger field strength.

questions.question_text: Which property of magnetic field lines distinguishes them from electric field lines in the context of a dipole?
options: They originate and terminate on charges
They intersect at points of high field strength
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops because there are no magnetic monopoles; they emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole, looping back internally. In contrast, electric field lines of a dipole start at the positive charge and end at the negative charge, or extend to infinity if unterminated.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 1.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 1.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.5 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 1.8}{(0.5)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{3.6}{0.125} = 2.88 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A material has \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \) and \( M = 1.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material with \( \mu_r = 400 \) and \( H = 500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A bar magnet with \( m = 1.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) produces a field at \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The reason magnetic field lines are denser near the poles of a magnet is:
options: The field strength is greatest there
The magnet is weaker at the center
questions.explanation: The density of magnetic field lines indicates the field strength. Near the poles, the field is strongest because the lines converge or diverge there, reflecting the concentration of magnetic influence at these points.

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.25 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 1500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( M \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A dipole with \( m = 0.7 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \) at \( 45^\circ \) has torque:
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.7 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 45^\circ \), \( \sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 \). \( \tau = 0.7 \times 0.2 \times 0.707 = 0.09898 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.1 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A material has a magnetic susceptibility \( \chi = 0.001 \). What is its relative magnetic permeability \( \mu_r \)?
questions.explanation: Relative magnetic permeability \( \mu_r = 1 + \chi \). Given: \( \chi = 0.001 \). Substitute: \( \mu_r = 1 + 0.001 = 1.001 \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid produces \( B = 0.96 \, \text{T} \) with a core of \( \mu_r = 300 \) and \( n = 1000 \, \text{m}^{-1} \). What is the current \( I \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A magnetic dipole in a uniform field is in unstable equilibrium when:
options: It is perpendicular to the field
It is parallel to the field
It is anti-parallel to the field
questions.explanation: The potential energy \( U = -m B \cos\theta \) is maximized when \( \theta = 180^\circ \) (anti-parallel), making it an unstable equilibrium position. Any small perturbation causes the dipole to rotate toward the stable position (\( \theta = 0^\circ \)), as the energy decreases in that direction.

questions.question_text: A material with susceptibility \( \chi = -4 \times 10^{-5} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
A material’s susceptibility becomes large and positive when its microscopic regions align spontaneously. This is a feature of:
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials exhibit large, positive susceptibility due to the spontaneous alignment of magnetic domains, which amplifies the magnetization far beyond that of paramagnetic or diamagnetic materials.

questions.question_text: Which material has a large positive \( \chi \) and forms domains?
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials have large positive \( \chi \) and exhibit domain formation due to spontaneous alignment of magnetic moments.

questions.question_text: A magnetic dipole oscillates in a uniform field when displaced from its equilibrium position because:
options: The torque acts as a restoring force
The field exerts a constant force
The dipole’s poles repel each other
questions.explanation: The torque on a magnetic dipole (\( \tau = m B \sin\theta \)) acts as a restoring force when displaced from its equilibrium position (aligned with the field). This torque causes oscillatory motion, similar to a pendulum, as it seeks to return to the stable alignment.

questions.question_text: The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 3.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A dipole with \( m = 0.25 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \) has potential energy:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.25 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), \( \cos 90^\circ = 0 \). \( U_m = -0.25 \times 0.4 \times 0 = 0 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: The alignment of a magnetic dipole in a uniform field results in:
options: A net force toward the field source
questions.explanation: In a uniform field, a magnetic dipole experiences a torque that aligns it with the field to minimize potential energy (\( U = -m B \cos\theta \)), reaching a stable equilibrium when parallel (\( \theta = 0^\circ \)), with no net force due to field uniformity.

questions.question_text: When a magnetic dipole is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field, the torque acting on it is maximum because:
options: The angle between the dipole moment and field is 90°
The dipole moment cancels the field
The dipole aligns with the field lines
questions.explanation: The torque on a magnetic dipole is given by \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). It reaches its maximum value when \( \sin\theta = 1 \), which occurs at \( \theta = 90^\circ \) (perpendicular orientation), as the cross product \( m \times B \) is greatest when the angle between the dipole moment and field is 90 degrees.

questions.question_text: A magnetic dipole with \( m = 0.3 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \) has potential energy:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.3 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), \( \cos 90^\circ = 0 \). \( U_m = -0.3 \times 0.4 \times 0 = 0 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A magnetic dipole of moment \( 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is in a uniform field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \) at \( 45^\circ \). What is the torque on it?
questions.explanation: Torque is \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 45^\circ \), \( \sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 \). Substitute: \( \tau = 0.8 \times 0.5 \times 0.707 \approx 0.2828 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.28 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \) at \( 0^\circ \) has potential energy:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 0^\circ \), \( \cos 0^\circ = 1 \). \( U_m = -0.4 \times 0.3 \times 1 = -0.12 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A material loses its magnetic properties when heated beyond a certain temperature because:
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials lose their magnetism above the Curie temperature, where thermal energy disrupts the aligned domains, transitioning the material to a paramagnetic state with random moment orientations.

questions.question_text: The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with \( m = 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \) is:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), \( \cos 90^\circ = 0 \). Substitute: \( U_m = -0.9 \times 0.2 \times 0 = 0 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A material with \( \chi = -1 \) and \( \mu_r = 0 \) is classified as:
questions.explanation: A material with \( \chi = -1 \) and \( \mu_r = 0 \) exhibits perfect diamagnetism, characteristic of a superconductor due to the Meissner effect.

questions.question_text: A material with \( \mu_r = 300 \) and \( H = 600 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic field lines inside a bar magnet run from:
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines form closed loops, exiting the north pole and entering the south pole externally. Inside a bar magnet, they run from the south pole to the north pole to complete the loop, consistent with the convention of field direction from north to south outside.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 3.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is at \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A solenoid produces \( B = 0.9 \, \text{T} \) with a core of \( \mu_r = 300 \) and \( n = 1500 \, \text{m}^{-1} \). What is the current \( I \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material that enhances the magnetic field inside it significantly when placed in an external field is likely:
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials greatly enhance the magnetic field inside them due to the strong alignment and growth of magnetic domains, resulting in a high susceptibility and permeability, far exceeding that of paramagnetic or diamagnetic materials.

questions.question_text: A material that repels a magnet and is repelled by it in return is likely:
questions.explanation: Superconductors, exhibiting perfect diamagnetism (Meissner effect), expel magnetic fields completely, causing mutual repulsion with a magnet. This is distinct from weak diamagnetic repulsion and stronger than other material responses.

questions.question_text: Which material has a small positive \( \chi \) and aligns weakly with an external magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Paramagnetic materials have a small positive \( \chi \) and align weakly with an external magnetic field due to the alignment of atomic dipoles.

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.45 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 3000 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( M \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A magnetic dipole of moment \( 0.25 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is in a uniform field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is the torque on it?
questions.explanation: Torque is \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.25 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 30^\circ \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \). Substitute: \( \tau = 0.25 \times 0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.0625 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 300 turns per meter carries a current of \( 6 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \). Given: \( n = 300 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 6 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 300 \times 6 = 1800 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.35 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in \( B = 0.9 \, \text{T} \) at \( 30^\circ \) has torque:
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.35 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.9 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 30^\circ \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \). \( \tau = 0.35 \times 0.9 \times 0.5 = 0.1575 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 2.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is at \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
Which material has a large positive \( \chi \) and exhibits spontaneous domain alignment?
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials have a large positive \( \chi \) and exhibit spontaneous alignment of magnetic moments into domains.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1200 turns per meter and current \( 2.5 \, \text{A} \) has a core with \( \mu_r = 150 \). What is \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A solenoid with 1200 turns per meter and current \( 2.5 \, \text{A} \) has a core with \( \mu_r = 200 \). What is \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material with susceptibility \( \chi = 2 \times 10^{-3} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
questions.explanation: \( \mu_r = 1 + \chi \). Given: \( \chi = 2 \times 10^{-3} \). Substitute: \( \mu_r = 1 + 2 \times 10^{-3} = 1.002 \).

questions.question_text: The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with \( m = 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \) at \( 0^\circ \) is:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 0^\circ \), \( \cos 0^\circ = 1 \). Substitute: \( U_m = -0.6 \times 0.2 \times 1 = -0.12 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.36 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 2500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( M \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
Which material has \( \chi \) slightly positive and moves from weaker to stronger field regions?
questions.explanation: Paramagnetic materials have a small positive \( \chi \) and are weakly attracted from weaker to stronger magnetic field regions.

questions.question_text: A solenoid produces \( B = 1.2 \, \text{T} \) with a core of \( \mu_r = 400 \) and \( n = 1500 \, \text{m}^{-1} \). What is the current \( I \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A bar magnet with original \( m = 1.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is cut transversely into two equal parts. What is \( m \) of each part?
questions.explanation: When cut transversely, each part has half the original magnetic moment. Given: \( m = 1.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \). Each part: \( m' = \frac{1.6}{2} = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 400 turns per meter carries a current of \( 5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \). Given: \( n = 400 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 5 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 400 \times 5 = 2000 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 3.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is at \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A bar magnet with \( m = 1.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \) produces a field at \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic field inside a material becomes zero when:
options: It is heated above a critical temperature
questions.explanation: In a superconductor below its critical temperature, the magnetic field inside becomes zero due to the Meissner effect, where induced currents completely cancel the external field, a hallmark of perfect diamagnetism.

questions.question_text: The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 1.2 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A magnetic dipole in a non-uniform field experiences a net force because:
options: The dipole aligns with the field
The field is constant across the dipole
questions.explanation: In a non-uniform field, the field strength varies across the dipole, causing the forces on its poles to differ in magnitude. This imbalance results in a net force, unlike in a uniform field where the forces cancel out.

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \) has torque:
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), \( \sin 90^\circ = 1 \). \( \tau = 0.2 \times 0.5 \times 1 = 0.1 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.66 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 4500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( M \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with \( m = 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \) at \( 0^\circ \) is:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 0^\circ \), \( \cos 0^\circ = 1 \). Substitute: \( U_m = -0.5 \times 0.3 \times 1 = -0.15 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A material has \( B = 0.28 \, \text{T} \) and \( M = 2.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A magnetic field line pattern that forms closed loops entirely within a material is most likely observed in:
questions.explanation: In a toroid, magnetic field lines are confined within the core, forming closed loops due to the circular symmetry and the current in the windings. This contrasts with bar magnets or solenoids, where field lines extend externally.

questions.question_text: A material with \( \mu_r = 500 \) and \( H = 300 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A solenoid with 500 turns per meter carries a current of \( 4.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \). Given: \( n = 500 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 4.5 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 500 \times 4.5 = 2250 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 2.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \) produces a field at \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material has \( B = 0.25 \, \text{T} \) and \( M = 1.8 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
In a material where magnetic domains spontaneously align over large regions, the susceptibility is:
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials have magnetic domains that spontaneously align, resulting in a large positive susceptibility (\( \chi \gg 1 \)). This strong magnetization occurs due to cooperative interactions among atomic magnetic moments, distinguishing them from other materials.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with original \( m = 2.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is cut transversely into two equal parts. What is \( m \) of each part?
questions.explanation: When cut transversely, each part has half the original magnetic moment. Given: \( m = 2.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \). Each part: \( m' = \frac{2.8}{2} = 1.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \) at \( 0^\circ \) has potential energy:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 0^\circ \), \( \cos 0^\circ = 1 \). \( U_m = -0.6 \times 0.8 \times 1 = -0.48 \, \text{J} \).
