The net magnetic flux through a closed surface surrounding a current-carrying solenoid is:
questions.explanation: Gauss’s law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, as magnetic field lines form closed loops.

questions.question_text: A material’s weak repulsion from a magnetic field is due to:
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials exhibit weak repulsion from a magnetic field because an external field induces small currents in their atoms that generate an opposing magnetic moment, per Lenz’s law, resulting in a slight reduction of the field inside the material.

questions.question_text: A magnetic dipole of moment \( 0.15 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is in a uniform field of \( 0.8 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is the torque on it?
questions.explanation: Torque is \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.15 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 60^\circ \), \( \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866 \). Substitute: \( \tau = 0.15 \times 0.8 \times 0.866 \approx 0.1039 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.104 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid with magnetic field \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \) inside has a core with \( \mu_r = 400 \) and \( n = 800 \, \text{m}^{-1} \). What is the current \( I \) in the solenoid? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: \( B = \mu_0 \mu_r n I \), so \( I = \frac{B}{\mu_0 \mu_r n} \). Given: \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \), \( \mu_r = 400 \), \( n = 800 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( I = \frac{0.8}{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 400 \times 800} = \frac{0.8}{4\pi \times 3.2 \times 10^{-2}} \approx 1.989 \, \text{A} \approx 2 \, \text{A} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with original \( m = 2.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is cut transversely into two equal parts. What is \( m \) of each part?
questions.explanation: When cut transversely, each part has half the original magnetic moment. Given: \( m = 2.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \). Each part: \( m' = \frac{2.0}{2} = 1.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A material’s weak enhancement of the magnetic field inside it is due to:
questions.explanation: Paramagnetic materials weakly enhance the magnetic field inside them because their atomic magnetic moments partially align with the external field, producing a small positive magnetization that adds to the applied field.

questions.question_text: A magnetic dipole placed in a uniform magnetic field experiences no net force but a torque. This is because:
options: Forces on the poles cancel out but produce a couple
The field exerts a net force in one direction
The dipole is inherently unstable in uniform fields
The field strength varies across the dipole
questions.explanation: In a uniform magnetic field, the forces on the north and south poles of a dipole are equal and opposite, canceling out to produce no net force. However, these forces act at different points, creating a torque that tends to align the dipole with the field.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 600 turns per meter carries a current of \( 3.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \). Given: \( n = 600 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 3.5 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 600 \times 3.5 = 2100 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 2000 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( M \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
What is the magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with magnetization \( M = 4 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: \( B_m = \mu_0 M \). Given: \( M = 4 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \), \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B_m = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 4 \times 10^5 = 1.6\pi \times 10^{-1} \approx 0.5 \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.35 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 1800 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( M \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 1.8 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A material with \( \mu_r = 0 \) completely expels magnetic fields and is classified as:
questions.explanation: A material with \( \mu_r = 0 \) (and \( \chi = -1 \)) exhibits perfect diamagnetism, characteristic of a superconductor due to the Meissner effect.

questions.question_text: A material has \( B = 0.42 \, \text{T} \) and \( M = 3.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The potential energy of a magnetic dipole in a uniform field is highest when:
options: It is perpendicular to the field
It is anti-parallel to the field
It is parallel to the field
questions.explanation: The potential energy \( U = -m B \cos\theta \) is highest when \( \cos\theta = -1 \), i.e., \( \theta = 180^\circ \), when the dipole is anti-parallel to the field. This is the least stable position, as energy is maximized.

questions.question_text: The absence of a net force on a magnetic dipole in a uniform field implies:
options: The field varies across the dipole
questions.explanation: In a uniform magnetic field, the forces on the dipole’s poles are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, resulting in no net translational force. This occurs because the field strength does not vary, unlike in a non-uniform field where a gradient would produce a net force.

questions.question_text: A material’s magnetic susceptibility becomes zero when:
options: It is heated beyond its melting point
It is placed in a vacuum
questions.explanation: For a superconductor below its critical temperature, the susceptibility \( \chi = -1 \) and relative permeability \( \mu_r = 0 \), but in a broader context, susceptibility can approach zero for non-magnetic materials or when magnetization is negligible compared to the applied field. However, the question implies a specific state, and superconductors achieve this uniquely with perfect diamagnetism.

questions.question_text: A material with susceptibility \( \chi = -5 \times 10^{-5} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
The net magnetic flux through a closed surface around a toroid is:
questions.explanation: Gauss’s law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, even for a toroid, as magnetic field lines form closed loops.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 800 turns per meter carries a current of \( 2.5 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \). Given: \( n = 800 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 2.5 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 800 \times 2.5 = 2000 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is at \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A magnetic dipole of moment \( 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is in a uniform field of \( 0.3 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is the torque on it?
questions.explanation: Torque is \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 60^\circ \), \( \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866 \). Substitute: \( \tau = 0.5 \times 0.3 \times 0.866 \approx 0.1299 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.13 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: The net magnetic flux through a closed surface surrounding a solenoid is:
questions.explanation: Gauss’s law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, as magnetic field lines form closed loops with no monopoles.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet’s field strength decreases with distance because:
questions.explanation: The magnetic field strength of a bar magnet decreases with distance as the field lines spread out, reducing their density and thus the field intensity, following an inverse cube relationship (\( B \propto 1/r^3 \)) for a dipole at large distances.

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.7 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.4 \, \text{T} \) at \( 180^\circ \) has potential energy:
The net magnetic flux through a closed surface surrounding a bar magnet is:
questions.explanation: Gauss’s law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero, as magnetic field lines form closed loops with no monopoles.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 900 turns per meter and current \( 3 \, \text{A} \) has a core with \( \mu_r = 250 \). What is \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A paramagnetic material has \( \chi = 5 \times 10^{-4} \) and \( H = 2 \times 10^3 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is its magnetization \( M \)?
questions.explanation: \( M = \chi H \). Given: \( \chi = 5 \times 10^{-4} \), \( H = 2 \times 10^3 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). Substitute: \( M = 5 \times 10^{-4} \times 2 \times 10^3 = 1 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 2.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is at \( 0.7 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with \( m = 0.7 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \) at \( 0^\circ \) is:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.7 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 0^\circ \), \( \cos 0^\circ = 1 \). Substitute: \( U_m = -0.7 \times 0.2 \times 1 = -0.14 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A solenoid has 500 turns per meter and carries a current of \( 3 \, \text{A} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \) inside the solenoid?
questions.explanation: Magnetic intensity \( H = n I \), where \( n \) is turns per unit length and \( I \) is current. Given: \( n = 500 \, \text{m}^{-1} \), \( I = 3 \, \text{A} \). Substitute: \( H = 500 \times 3 = 1500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \).

questions.question_text: The reason a paramagnetic material’s magnetization increases with a stronger external field is:
questions.explanation: In paramagnetic materials, magnetization increases with a stronger external field because more atomic magnetic moments align with the field, overcoming random thermal motion, though the alignment remains partial compared to ferromagnetic materials.

questions.question_text: Unlike a bar magnet, an iron nail near a magnet experiences both a net force and a torque. This is primarily due to:
options: The uniform nature of the magnet’s field
The non-uniform field inducing a magnetic moment
The cancellation of forces on the nail
questions.explanation: An iron nail, being a ferromagnetic material, becomes magnetized in the non-uniform field of a bar magnet, developing an induced magnetic moment. The field's gradient causes a net force toward the stronger region (typically the pole), while the misalignment of the induced moment with the field produces a torque.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 1.6 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is at \( 0.8 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 3.2 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A diamagnetic material has a susceptibility \( \chi = -2 \times 10^{-5} \). What is its magnetic permeability \( \mu \) in terms of \( \mu_0 \)?
questions.explanation: Magnetic permeability \( \mu = \mu_0 (1 + \chi) \). Given: \( \chi = -2 \times 10^{-5} \). Substitute: \( \mu = \mu_0 (1 - 2 \times 10^{-5}) = \mu_0 \times 0.99998 \).

questions.question_text: A material with \( \mu_r = 350 \) and \( H = 400 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 1.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 1.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.6 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 1.5}{(0.6)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{3.0}{0.216} \approx 1.389 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \approx 1.39 × 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \) at \( 0^\circ \) has potential energy:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 0^\circ \), \( \cos 0^\circ = 1 \). \( U_m = -0.4 \times 0.8 \times 1 = -0.32 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 2 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: \( B_m = \mu_0 M \). Given: \( M = 2 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \), \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \). \( B_m = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 2 \times 10^5 = 0.2512 \, \text{T} \approx 0.25 \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in \( B = 0.1 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \) has torque:
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.1 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 60^\circ \), \( \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866 \). \( \tau = 0.5 \times 0.1 \times 0.866 = 0.0433 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.043 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: The magnetization \( M \) of a sample is \( 5 \times 10^4 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) in a magnetic field \( B = 0.1 \, \text{T} \). What is the magnetic intensity \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A bar magnet with \( m = 1.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) produces a field at \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A solenoid with 900 turns per meter and current \( 3.5 \, \text{A} \) has a core with \( \mu_r = 150 \). What is \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 1.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 1.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.3 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 1.5}{(0.3)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{3}{0.027} = 1.11 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A material has \( B = 0.15 \, \text{T} \) and \( M = 8 \times 10^4 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \). What is \( H \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic field inside a bar magnet is directed from:
questions.explanation: Inside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines run from the south pole to the north pole to form closed loops with the external field (north to south), maintaining continuity as there are no magnetic monopoles.

questions.question_text: The strongest magnetic field of a bar magnet is observed:
questions.explanation: The magnetic field of a bar magnet is strongest at its poles, where field lines are most concentrated, as opposed to the central region where the field is weaker and less dense.

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.48 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 3200 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( M \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The torque on a magnetic dipole in a uniform magnetic field is zero when:
options: The dipole is parallel or anti-parallel to the field
The dipole is perpendicular to the field
questions.explanation: The torque on a magnetic dipole is given by \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). It becomes zero when \( \sin\theta = 0 \), which occurs when the dipole is aligned with the field (\( \theta = 0^\circ \)) or anti-aligned (\( \theta = 180^\circ \)), as the cross product \( m \times B \) vanishes.

questions.question_text: A material with \( \mu_r = 800 \) and \( H = 250 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( B \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A bar magnet with \( m = 0.75 \, \text{A m}^2 \) produces a field at \( 0.15 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 0.9 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.3 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 0.9}{(0.3)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{1.8}{0.027} \approx 6.67 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \) at \( 90^\circ \) has potential energy:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.3 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 90^\circ \), \( \cos 90^\circ = 0 \). \( U_m = -0.8 \times 0.3 \times 0 = 0 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: The magnetic field contribution \( B_m \) due to a material with \( M = 1.6 \times 10^5 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) is: (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with moment \( 0.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.5 \, \text{T} \) when aligned at \( 30^\circ \) to the field is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic potential energy is \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.5 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 30^\circ \), \( \cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866 \). Substitute: \( U_m = -0.4 \times 0.5 \times 0.866 = -0.1732 \, \text{J} \approx -0.17 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.4 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 0.8}{(0.4)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{1.6}{0.064} = 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A paramagnetic material with \( \chi = 8 \times 10^{-4} \) in \( H = 2500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has magnetization \( M \):

A bar magnet produces a field of \( 5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \) at \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) on its equatorial line. What is its magnetic moment? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A solenoid with 1100 turns per meter and current \( 2 \, \text{A} \) has a core with \( \mu_r = 250 \). What is \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A dipole with \( m = 0.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \) at \( 60^\circ \) has torque:
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.4 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 60^\circ \), \( \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866 \). \( \tau = 0.4 \times 0.8 \times 0.866 \approx 0.277 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.28 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with \( m = 2.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is at \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is \( B \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
The magnetic field lines inside a solenoid are nearly parallel because:
options: The current loops produce a uniform field
questions.explanation: Inside a solenoid, the magnetic field lines are nearly parallel due to the uniform distribution of current loops along its length, creating a consistent field direction and magnitude, especially in a long solenoid where end effects are minimal.

questions.question_text: The primary reason a diamagnetic material develops a weak opposing magnetic moment in an external field is:
questions.explanation: In diamagnetic materials, an external magnetic field induces orbital currents in atoms that oppose the applied field, per Lenz’s law. This results in a weak, negative magnetization, as all electrons contribute to this effect in materials with no net magnetic moment.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 1300 turns per meter and current \( 2 \, \text{A} \) has a core with \( \mu_r = 100 \). What is \( B \) inside? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
A dipole with \( m = 0.7 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in \( B = 0.6 \, \text{T} \) at \( 30^\circ \) has torque:
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.7 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.6 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 30^\circ \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \). \( \tau = 0.7 \times 0.6 \times 0.5 = 0.21 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.5 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.6 \, \text{T} \) at \( 180^\circ \) has potential energy:
Which material has \( \chi = -1 \) and completely expels magnetic field lines?
questions.explanation: Superconductors have \( \chi = -1 \) and exhibit perfect diamagnetism, expelling all magnetic field lines (Meissner effect).

questions.question_text: A paramagnetic material with \( \chi = 4 \times 10^{-4} \) in \( H = 2000 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has magnetization \( M \):
A magnetic dipole of moment \( 0.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is in a uniform field of \( 0.9 \, \text{T} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is the torque on it?
questions.explanation: Torque is \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.9 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 30^\circ \), \( \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \). Substitute: \( \tau = 0.2 \times 0.9 \times 0.5 = 0.09 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: The magnetic potential energy of a dipole with \( m = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in a field \( B = 0.25 \, \text{T} \) at \( 180^\circ \) is:
questions.explanation: \( U_m = -m B \cos\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.8 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.25 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 180^\circ \), \( \cos 180^\circ = -1 \). Substitute: \( U_m = -0.8 \times 0.25 \times (-1) = 0.2 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A material with susceptibility \( \chi = 5 \times 10^{-3} \) has a relative permeability \( \mu_r \) of:
questions.explanation: \( \mu_r = 1 + \chi \). Given: \( \chi = 5 \times 10^{-3} \). Substitute: \( \mu_r = 1 + 5 \times 10^{-3} = 1.005 \).

questions.question_text: A dipole with \( m = 0.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \) in \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \) at \( 45^\circ \) has torque:
questions.explanation: \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.2 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.8 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 45^\circ \), \( \sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 \). \( \tau = 0.2 \times 0.8 \times 0.707 \approx 0.11312 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.11 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A material’s susceptibility becomes negative and large when:
options: It is heated above a critical point
It aligns weakly with the field
questions.explanation: A superconductor has a susceptibility of \( \chi = -1 \) (large and negative) when it transitions to the superconducting state below its critical temperature, expelling all magnetic fields via the Meissner effect, a unique property among materials.

questions.question_text: A paramagnetic material with \( \chi = 3 \times 10^{-3} \) in \( H = 400 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has magnetization \( M \):
Which material retains magnetization after the external field is removed and is used in permanent magnets?
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials, particularly hard ferromagnets, retain magnetization after the external field is removed and are used in permanent magnets.

questions.question_text: A bar magnet with magnetic moment \( 1.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed at a distance of \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) along its axis. What is the magnetic field \( B \) at that point? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).
questions.explanation: The magnetic field along the axis is \( B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \frac{2m}{r^3} \). Given: \( m = 1.0 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( r = 0.5 \, \text{m} \), \( \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7} \). Substitute: \( B = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2 \times 1.0}{(0.5)^3} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{2.0}{0.125} = 1.6 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{T} \).

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 1000 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has magnetization \( M \). What is \( M \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A magnetic needle with magnetic moment \( 0.1 \, \text{A m}^2 \) is placed in a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.2 \, \text{T} \) at an angle of \( 60^\circ \) with the field. What is the torque acting on it?
questions.explanation: Torque on a magnetic dipole is \( \tau = m B \sin\theta \). Given: \( m = 0.1 \, \text{A m}^2 \), \( B = 0.2 \, \text{T} \), \( \theta = 60^\circ \), \( \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866 \). Substitute: \( \tau = 0.1 \times 0.2 \times 0.866 = 0.01732 \, \text{N m} \approx 0.017 \, \text{N m} \).

questions.question_text: A material with \( B = 0.55 \, \text{T} \) and \( H = 3500 \, \text{A m}^{-1} \) has \( M \): (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

A solenoid produces \( B = 1.5 \, \text{T} \) with a core of \( \mu_r = 500 \) and \( n = 2000 \, \text{m}^{-1} \). What is the current \( I \)? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T m A}^{-1} \)).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 1

questions.question_text: What is the total pressure at a depth of \( 2.8 \, \text{m} \) in whole blood (\( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with atmospheric pressure \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A horizontal pipe carries water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) at \( 2 \, \text{m/s} \) and \( 1.4 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed becomes \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the pressure?
What is the fundamental difference between gauge pressure and absolute pressure?
questions.explanation: Absolute pressure is the total pressure, including atmospheric pressure (\( P = P_a + \rho g h \)), while gauge pressure is the excess pressure above atmospheric pressure (\( P_g = \rho g h \)), as defined in the chapter.

questions.question_text: Water flows at \( 2.0 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) height with pressure \( 1.65 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the pressure at \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) height with speed \( 3.0 \, \text{m/s} \)? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

Water flows at \( 3 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 2 \, \text{m} \) height with pressure \( 1.3 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the pressure at \( 0 \, \text{m} \) height with speed \( 4 \, \text{m/s} \)? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
What prevents a fluid from flowing when the pressure gradient is zero?
questions.explanation: A pressure gradient drives fluid flow by creating a net force. When the gradient is zero (uniform pressure), no net force exists to initiate motion, keeping the fluid at rest unless acted upon by other forces.

questions.question_text: A hydraulic lift raises a \( 1900 \, \text{kg} \) load using a small piston of radius \( 4.5 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 18 \, \text{cm} \). What force is applied on the small piston? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
An aircraft (\( m = 2.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 500 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies level. What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \). \( mg = 2.5 \times 10^5 \times 9.8 = 2.45 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \), \( A = 500 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2.45 \times 10^6}{500} = 4900 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A soap bubble of radius \( 4 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.025 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside the bubble?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.025 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 4 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.025}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = 25 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A sphere of radius \( 0.07 \, \text{m} \) moves at \( 0.14 \, \text{m/s} \) through honey (\( \eta = 0.2 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What is the viscous drag force?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 0.2 \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.07 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.14 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 0.2 \times 0.07 \times 0.14 = 0.0369 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary reason gases are more compressible than liquids?
questions.explanation: Gases have weaker intermolecular forces and larger intermolecular spaces compared to liquids, allowing them to compress significantly under pressure, while liquids’ strong forces resist volume changes.

questions.question_text: A soap bubble of radius \( 12 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.024 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.024 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 12 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.024}{12 \times 10^{-3}} = 8 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A soap bubble of radius \( 9 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.026 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.026 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 9 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.026}{9 \times 10^{-3}} = 11.56 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Why does the velocity of a fluid layer in contact with a stationary surface become zero?
questions.explanation: In viscous flow, the no-slip condition states that the fluid layer in contact with a stationary surface adheres to it due to frictional forces, resulting in zero velocity relative to the surface.

questions.question_text: A hydraulic press applies \( 200 \, \text{N} \) on a small piston of area \( 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \). What force is exerted by a large piston of area \( 0.04 \, \text{m}^2 \)?

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 2

questions.question_text: Water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) flows horizontally at \( 2.8 \, \text{m/s} \) with pressure \( 1.9 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed increases to \( 5.2 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure?
What is the excess pressure inside an ethanol drop of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.0227 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.0227 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.0227}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 30.27 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A soap film supports \( 3.6 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 60 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?
Which statement is incorrect about hydraulic systems?
options: Force is amplified by area ratio
questions.explanation: Hydraulic systems rely on incompressible fluids to transmit pressure effectively (Pascal’s law). The incorrect statement is that they use highly compressible fluids, which would reduce efficiency.

questions.question_text: Water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) flows horizontally at \( 4.5 \, \text{m/s} \) with pressure \( 2.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed increases to \( 7.0 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure?
Which of the following statements is correct about the equation of continuity?
options: It applies only to viscous fluids
questions.explanation: The equation of continuity (\( A v = \text{constant} \)) assumes an incompressible fluid, ensuring mass flow rate conservation, not requiring viscosity or turbulence considerations.

questions.question_text: What is the gauge pressure at a depth of \( 4.5 \, \text{m} \) in ethyl alcohol (\( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 4.5 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 806 \times 10 \times 4.5 = 36270 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A plate of area \( 0.06 \, \text{m}^2 \) moves at \( 0.6 \, \text{m/s} \) over a \( 0.4 \, \text{mm} \) thick glycerine film (\( \eta = 0.83 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What force is required?
A soap bubble of radius \( 15 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.023 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.023 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 15 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.023}{15 \times 10^{-3}} = 6.13 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A hydraulic system applies \( 150 \, \text{N} \) on a small piston of area \( 0.015 \, \text{m}^2 \). What force is exerted by a large piston of area \( 0.075 \, \text{m}^2 \)?
What property of a fluid does the coefficient of viscosity measure?
questions.explanation: The coefficient of viscosity (\( \eta \)) measures a fluid’s internal resistance to flow, defined as the ratio of shear stress to the strain rate (\( \eta = F l / v A \)), reflecting its “thickness” or friction between layers.

questions.question_text: A manometer with seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 0.19 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 0.19 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = 1.03 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 0.19 = 1957 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: An aircraft (\( m = 3.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 450 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies level. What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \). \( mg = 3.0 \times 10^5 \times 10 = 3.0 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \), \( A = 450 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{3.0 \times 10^6}{450} = 6666.67 \, \text{Pa} \approx 6667 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A capillary tube of radius \( 0.55 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in water (\( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \)). What is the capillary rise? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
What is the excess pressure inside an oxygen drop of radius \( 0.5 \, \text{mm} \) at \( -183^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.0132 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.0132 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 0.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.0132}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 52.8 \, \text{Pa} \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 3

questions.question_text: A soap bubble of radius \( 7 \, \text{mm} \) has an excess pressure of \( 20 \, \text{Pa} \) inside. What is its surface tension?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( \Delta P = 20 \, \text{Pa} \), \( r = 7 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( S = \frac{\Delta P \cdot r}{4} = \frac{20 \times 7 \times 10^{-3}}{4} = 0.035 \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: A soap bubble of radius \( 8 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.026 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.026 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 8 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.026}{8 \times 10^{-3}} = 13 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A capillary tube of radius \( 0.45 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in water (\( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \)). What is the capillary rise? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A bubble of radius \( 4.0 \, \text{mm} \) is blown at \( 60 \, \text{cm} \) depth in a soap solution (\( \rho = 1.2 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( S = 0.025 \, \text{N/m} \)). What is the total pressure inside? (Take \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A capillary tube of radius \( 0.35 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in ethanol (\( S = 0.0227 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \)). What is the capillary rise? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A \( 60 \, \text{kg} \) person stands on two cylindrical bones, each of cross-sectional area \( 15 \, \text{cm}^2 \). What is the average pressure on the bones? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( P_{av} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( F = mg = 60 \times 10 = 600 \, \text{N} \). Total area \( A = 2 \times 15 \times 10^{-4} = 3 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^2 \). \( P_{av} = \frac{600}{3 \times 10^{-3}} = 2 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) flows horizontally at \( 3.8 \, \text{m/s} \) with pressure \( 1.8 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed increases to \( 6.2 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure?
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Pascal’s law?
options: It applies only to moving fluids
questions.explanation: Pascal’s law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to all parts, making it the basis for hydraulic systems, not dependent on fluid velocity or viscosity.

questions.question_text: A hydraulic lift raises a \( 1400 \, \text{kg} \) load using a small piston of radius \( 2.5 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 10 \, \text{cm} \). What force is applied on the small piston? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
What is the gauge pressure at a depth of \( 0.9 \, \text{m} \) in whole blood (\( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 0.9 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 1.06 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 0.9 = 9540 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: What causes a liquid to form a concave meniscus in a glass tube?
questions.explanation: A concave meniscus forms when adhesive forces between the liquid (e.g., water) and glass exceed cohesive forces within the liquid, pulling the edges upward and creating a curved surface.

questions.question_text: A spray tube (\( 6 \, \text{cm}^2 \)) has 30 holes of diameter \( 1.1 \, \text{mm} \). If the flow speed is \( 3.6 \, \text{m/min} \), what is the ejection speed?

A capillary tube of radius \( 0.1 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in water (\( S = 0.073 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)). What is the height of capillary rise? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \))
questions.explanation: Capillary rise: \( h = \frac{2 S \cos \theta}{\rho g a} \). \( S = 0.073 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( a = 0.1 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \). \( h = \frac{2 \times 0.073}{1000 \times 10 \times 0.1 \times 10^{-3}} = 0.146 \, \text{m} = 14.6 \, \text{cm} \).

questions.question_text: A hydraulic system applies \( 300 \, \text{N} \) on a small piston of area \( 0.015 \, \text{m}^2 \). What force is exerted by a large piston of area \( 0.045 \, \text{m}^2 \)?
A soap bubble of radius \( 10 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.025 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.025 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 10 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.025}{10 \times 10^{-3}} = 10 \, \text{Pa} \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 4

questions.question_text: What is the absolute pressure at \( 450 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A hydraulic lift raises a \( 1700 \, \text{kg} \) load using a small piston of radius \( 3.5 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 14 \, \text{cm} \). What force is applied on the small piston? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A sphere of radius \( 0.05 \, \text{m} \) moves at \( 0.11 \, \text{m/s} \) through blood (\( \eta = 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Pa s} \)). What is the viscous drag force?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.05 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.11 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.05 \times 0.11 = 0.0028 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: Water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) flows horizontally at \( 4.2 \, \text{m/s} \) with pressure \( 1.95 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed increases to \( 6.5 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure?
Which statement is incorrect about Stokes’ law?
options: Velocity is constant at terminal speed
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law (\( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \)) applies to small spherical objects in viscous, streamline flow, not turbulent flow, where inertial forces dominate. The incorrect statement is that it applies to turbulent flow.

questions.question_text: What is the reason a small insect can walk on water?
questions.explanation: Surface tension creates a “skin-like” effect at the water’s surface, supporting the insect’s weight if the force per unit length (\( S \)) exceeds the downward force distributed over its contact area, due to its small size and light weight.

questions.question_text: What is the excess pressure inside a water drop of radius \( 2.5 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 2.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.0727}{2.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 58.16 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: What is the total pressure at a depth of \( 2.2 \, \text{m} \) in hydrogen liquid (\( \rho = 9.0 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with atmospheric pressure \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A tank has a hole \( 1.4 \, \text{m} \) below the water surface, open to the atmosphere. What is the efflux speed? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law: \( v = \sqrt{2 g h} \). \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 1.4 \, \text{m} \). \( v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 1.4} = \sqrt{27.44} \approx 5.24 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A bubble of radius \( 5.5 \, \text{mm} \) is blown at \( 45 \, \text{cm} \) depth in water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \)). What is the total pressure inside? (Take \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A manometer with water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 0.15 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Why does the pressure inside a liquid drop exceed the external pressure?
questions.explanation: Surface tension creates a contractile force at the drop’s surface, requiring higher internal pressure (\( \Delta P = 2S/r \)) to balance this inward force, as the curved surface tends to reduce its area.

questions.question_text: A soap film supports \( 2.2 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 44 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?
Why does a fluid at rest exert the same pressure at all points at the same horizontal level?
questions.explanation: Pascal’s law states that pressure in a fluid at rest is transmitted equally in all directions. At the same horizontal level, the depth (\( h \)) is constant, so \( P = P_a + \rho g h \) is uniform, assuming no horizontal flow.

questions.question_text: A soap film supports \( 1.8 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 35 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 5

questions.question_text: A soap film supports \( 4.8 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 48 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?
What ensures that a submarine can withstand high pressure at great depths?
questions.explanation: The submarine’s rigid structure resists the external hydrostatic pressure (\( P = \rho g h \)), which increases with depth, preventing collapse by balancing the inward force with structural strength.

questions.question_text: A capillary tube of radius \( 0.05 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in water (\( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \)). What is the capillary rise? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
What is the excess pressure inside a helium drop of radius \( 1 \, \text{mm} \) at \( -270^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.000239 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.000239 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 1 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.000239}{1 \times 10^{-3}} = 0.478 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: What happens to an object falling through a viscous fluid when the viscous force equals the gravitational force?
questions.explanation: When the viscous force (from Stokes’ law) plus buoyant force equals the gravitational force, the net force becomes zero, and the object reaches terminal velocity, moving at a constant speed, as explained in the chapter.

questions.question_text: A pipe’s cross-sectional area decreases from \( 0.15 \, \text{m}^2 \) to \( 0.05 \, \text{m}^2 \). If water flows at \( 1.8 \, \text{m/s} \) in the larger section, what is the speed in the smaller section?

A bubble of radius \( 6 \, \text{mm} \) is blown at \( 25 \, \text{cm} \) depth in water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \)). What is the total pressure inside? (Take \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A hydraulic lift raises a \( 2000 \, \text{kg} \) load using a small piston of radius \( 5 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 20 \, \text{cm} \). What force is applied on the small piston? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

What is the absolute pressure at \( 250 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Water flows through a pipe of area \( 0.05 \, \text{m}^2 \) at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the speed in a section of area \( 0.015 \, \text{m}^2 \)?
A hydraulic system applies \( 180 \, \text{N} \) on a small piston of area \( 0.012 \, \text{m}^2 \). What force is exerted by a large piston of area \( 0.06 \, \text{m}^2 \)?
Why does a fluid’s density remain nearly constant in streamline flow through a narrowing pipe?
questions.explanation: The equation of continuity assumes the fluid is incompressible, meaning its density (\( \rho \)) remains constant, even as velocity increases in a narrowing pipe, ensuring mass conservation (\( A v = \text{constant} \)).

questions.question_text: What is the absolute pressure \( 800 \, \text{m} \) deep in an ocean (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A swimmer is at a depth of \( 5 \, \text{m} \) in a lake (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)). What is the gauge pressure experienced by the swimmer? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure is \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 5 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 1000 \times 10 \times 5 = 5 \times 10^4 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a barometer reading increase when taken to a lower altitude?
questions.explanation: At lower altitudes, the air column above is taller and heavier, increasing atmospheric pressure (\( P_a = \rho g h \)), which raises the height of the mercury column in the barometer to balance the greater external pressure.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 6

questions.question_text: What is the reason a liquid’s terminal velocity depends on its radius when falling through a viscous medium?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law (\( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \)) shows that viscous force is proportional to radius (\( a \)), while weight (\( \frac{4}{3} \pi a^3 \rho g \)) depends on \( a^3 \). At terminal velocity, these balance, making \( v \propto a^2 \).

questions.question_text: In streamline flow, why do streamlines never cross each other?
options: Because each streamline has a unique velocity
questions.explanation: In streamline flow, each streamline represents the path of a fluid particle with a unique velocity at each point. If streamlines crossed, a particle at the intersection would have two different velocities simultaneously, which is impossible in steady flow.

questions.question_text: What is the excess pressure inside an ethanol drop of radius \( 2.2 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.0227 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.0227 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 2.2 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.0227}{2.2 \times 10^{-3}} = 20.64 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: What is the excess pressure inside a water drop of radius \( 1.8 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 1.8 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.0727}{1.8 \times 10^{-3}} = 80.78 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A soap film supports \( 4.0 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 40 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?
What is the primary source of resistance to motion in a viscous fluid?
questions.explanation: Viscosity, the internal friction between fluid layers moving at different velocities, resists relative motion, causing a shear stress proportional to the velocity gradient, as seen in Stokes’ law.

questions.question_text: A pipe narrows from \( 0.12 \, \text{m}^2 \) to \( 0.04 \, \text{m}^2 \). If water flows at \( 1.6 \, \text{m/s} \) in the wider section, what is the speed in the narrower section?
A plate of area \( 0.08 \, \text{m}^2 \) moves at \( 0.4 \, \text{m/s} \) over a \( 0.25 \, \text{mm} \) thick oil film (\( \eta = 0.034 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What force is required?
A tank has a hole \( 1.1 \, \text{m} \) below the water surface, open to the atmosphere. What is the efflux speed? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law: \( v = \sqrt{2 g h} \). \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 1.1 \, \text{m} \). \( v = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 1.1} = \sqrt{22} \approx 4.69 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: An aircraft (\( m = 3.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 550 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies level. What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \). \( mg = 3.5 \times 10^5 \times 10 = 3.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \), \( A = 550 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{3.5 \times 10^6}{550} = 6363.64 \, \text{Pa} \approx 6364 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Water flows at \( 2.6 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 4.0 \, \text{m} \) height with pressure \( 1.7 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the pressure at \( 2.0 \, \text{m} \) height with speed \( 3.8 \, \text{m/s} \)? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A sphere of radius \( 0.06 \, \text{m} \) moves at \( 0.13 \, \text{m/s} \) through glycerine (\( \eta = 0.83 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What is the viscous drag force?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 0.83 \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.06 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.13 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 0.83 \times 0.06 \times 0.13 = 0.1222 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary reason mercury does not wet glass?
questions.explanation: Mercury has an obtuse angle of contact with glass because its cohesive forces (between mercury molecules) are stronger than its adhesive forces with glass, causing it to form droplets rather than spread.

questions.question_text: A sphere of radius \( 0.02 \, \text{m} \) falls through glycerine (\( \eta = 0.83 \, \text{Pa s} \)) at a terminal velocity of \( 0.1 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the viscous drag force?
questions.explanation: Using Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 0.83 \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.02 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.1 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 0.83 \times 0.02 \times 0.1 \approx 0.0313 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What causes the speed of efflux from a hole in a tank to equal the speed of a freely falling body from the same height?
options: Conversion of potential energy to kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law (\( v = \sqrt{2gh} \)) equates the kinetic energy of the efflux (\( \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \)) to the potential energy lost (\( mgh \)) as fluid falls from the surface to the hole, mirroring the free fall equation (\( v = \sqrt{2gh} \)), assuming no energy losses.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 7

questions.question_text: A cylindrical vessel is filled with water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) to a height of \( 2 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure at the bottom of the vessel if the atmospheric pressure is \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Using the pressure variation with depth: \( P = P_a + \rho g h \). Given: \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 2 \, \text{m} \). \( P = 1.01 \times 10^5 + 1000 \times 10 \times 2 \). \( P = 1.01 \times 10^5 + 20000 = 1.21 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: What is the key assumption behind the equation of continuity for fluid flow?
questions.explanation: The equation of continuity (\( A v = \text{constant} \)) assumes the fluid is incompressible, meaning its density remains constant, ensuring mass conservation in steady flow through varying cross-sections.

questions.question_text: What is the primary condition for streamline flow to occur in a fluid?
questions.explanation: Streamline flow occurs when viscous forces dominate inertial forces, keeping fluid motion steady and layered. This requires a low velocity, below the critical speed where turbulence begins.

questions.question_text: What is the force on a submarine window (\( 0.07 \, \text{m}^2 \)) at \( 350 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)), interior at atmospheric pressure? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h = 1.03 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 350 = 3.605 \times 10^6 \, \text{Pa} \). \( F = P_g A = 3.605 \times 10^6 \times 0.07 = 2.5235 \times 10^5 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the total pressure at a depth of \( 1.6 \, \text{m} \) in air (\( \rho = 1.29 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with atmospheric pressure \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A tank has a hole \( 0.7 \, \text{m} \) below the water surface, open to the atmosphere. What is the efflux speed? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law: \( v = \sqrt{2 g h} \). \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 0.7 \, \text{m} \). \( v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 0.7} = \sqrt{13.72} \approx 3.7 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the main reason a plane’s wings generate lift during flight?
options: Pressure difference due to airflow speed
questions.explanation: The aerofoil shape causes air to move faster over the top than underneath, reducing pressure above (Bernoulli’s principle) and creating a pressure difference that lifts the plane, known as dynamic lift.

questions.question_text: A soap film supports \( 2.4 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 48 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?

An aircraft (\( m = 2.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 400 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies at \( 900 \, \text{km/h} \). What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \rho_{\text{air}} = 1.2 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \), \( mg = 2.5 \times 10^5 \times 10 = 2.5 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \). \( A = 400 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2.5 \times 10^6}{400} = 6250 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A manometer with ethyl alcohol (\( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 0.3 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = 806 \times 10 \times 0.3 = 2418 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A capillary tube of radius \( 0.65 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in water (\( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \)). What is the capillary rise? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A sphere of radius \( 0.045 \, \text{m} \) moves at \( 0.15 \, \text{m/s} \) through machine oil (\( \eta = 0.034 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What is the viscous drag force?

Water flows at \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 3 \, \text{m} \) height with pressure \( 1.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the pressure at \( 1 \, \text{m} \) height with speed \( 3.5 \, \text{m/s} \)? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A hydraulic lift has a small piston of area \( 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \) and a large piston of area \( 0.09 \, \text{m}^2 \). If a force of \( 100 \, \text{N} \) is applied on the small piston, what is the force exerted by the large piston?
questions.explanation: By Pascal’s law, pressure is transmitted equally: \( P = \frac{F_1}{A_1} = \frac{F_2}{A_2} \). \( F_2 = F_1 \times \frac{A_2}{A_1} \). \( F_1 = 100 \, \text{N} \), \( A_1 = 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( A_2 = 0.09 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( F_2 = 100 \times \frac{0.09}{0.01} = 100 \times 9 = 900 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A sphere of radius \( 0.035 \, \text{m} \) moves at \( 0.09 \, \text{m/s} \) through glycerine (\( \eta = 0.83 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What is the viscous drag force?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 0.83 \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.035 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.09 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 0.83 \times 0.035 \times 0.09 = 0.0493 \, \text{N} \).
