tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 9

questions.question_text: Why does Bernoulli’s principle not apply to fluids with high viscosity?
options: It applies only to turbulent flow
Viscosity causes energy loss due to friction
questions.explanation: Bernoulli’s principle assumes no energy loss due to friction, which is valid for non-viscous fluids. High viscosity causes frictional losses between fluid layers, converting kinetic energy into heat, thus violating the energy conservation assumption.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about a liquid drop?
options: It is flat due to pressure
It is spherical due to surface tension
It forms a cube due to viscosity
questions.explanation: Surface tension minimizes surface area, making a sphere (with the least surface area for a given volume) the natural shape of a liquid drop in the absence of external forces like gravity.

questions.question_text: A hydraulic lift raises a \( 1800 \, \text{kg} \) load using a small piston of radius \( 3 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 15 \, \text{cm} \). What force is applied on the small piston? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Why does a spinning ball deviate from a straight path in air, as explained by the Magnus effect?
options: Due to pressure difference from spinning
questions.explanation: The Magnus effect occurs due to Bernoulli’s principle: a spinning ball drags air, creating a velocity difference (faster on one side, slower on the other), resulting in a pressure difference that generates a net force perpendicular to its path.

questions.question_text: A pipe’s cross-sectional area changes from \( 0.1 \, \text{m}^2 \) to \( 0.025 \, \text{m}^2 \). If water flows at \( 2.2 \, \text{m/s} \) in the larger section, what is the speed in the smaller section?
A manometer with mercury (\( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 0.28 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 0.28 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = 13.6 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 0.28 = 38080 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A pipe narrows from \( 0.06 \, \text{m}^2 \) to \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^2 \). If water flows at \( 1.8 \, \text{m/s} \) in the wider section, what is the speed in the narrower section?
Why does water rise in a capillary tube against gravity?
questions.explanation: Capillary rise occurs due to surface tension, where the adhesive forces between water and the tube wall exceed cohesive forces within water, creating an upward force balanced by the pressure difference across the curved meniscus.

questions.question_text: What is the total pressure at a depth of \( 3.6 \, \text{m} \) in mercury (\( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with atmospheric pressure \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
What is the significance of the term \( \rho g h \) in the pressure equation for a fluid at rest?
questions.explanation: \( \rho g h \) represents the hydrostatic pressure due to the weight of the fluid column above a point, increasing with depth, as it accounts for gravitational potential energy per unit volume.

questions.question_text: What is the gauge pressure at a depth of \( 3.5 \, \text{m} \) in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 3.5 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 1.03 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 3.5 = 3.605 \times 10^4 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease with altitude?
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column above a point. As altitude increases, the height and mass of the air column decrease, reducing the pressure exerted at higher elevations.

questions.question_text: A manometer with seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 0.22 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A plate of area \( 0.07 \, \text{m}^2 \) moves at \( 0.6 \, \text{m/s} \) over a \( 0.9 \, \text{mm} \) thick machine oil film (\( \eta = 0.113 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What force is required?
Which of the following statements is correct about viscosity?
options: It increases with temperature in liquids
It is independent of shear stress
questions.explanation: Viscosity measures a fluid’s resistance to flow due to internal friction between layers, decreasing with temperature in liquids as cohesive forces weaken, not increasing.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 10

questions.question_text: A \( 40 \, \text{kg} \) wooden plank is placed on a performer’s chest. If each femur has an area of \( 12 \, \text{cm}^2 \), what is the pressure on the femurs? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( P = \frac{F}{A} \), \( F = 40 \times 10 = 400 \, \text{N} \). Total area \( A = 2 \times 12 \times 10^{-4} = 2.4 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^2 \). \( P = \frac{400}{2.4 \times 10^{-3}} \approx 1.67 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A manometer with ethyl alcohol (\( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 0.26 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A sphere of radius \( 0.03 \, \text{m} \) falls through machine oil (\( \eta = 0.113 \, \text{Pa s} \)) at \( 0.15 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the viscous drag force?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 0.113 \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.03 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.15 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 0.113 \times 0.03 \times 0.15 = 0.0958 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the absolute pressure at \( 300 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A capillary tube of radius \( 0.3 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in water (\( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \)). What is the capillary rise? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A pipe’s cross-sectional area changes from \( 0.08 \, \text{m}^2 \) to \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^2 \). If the speed at the larger end is \( 1.2 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the speed at the smaller end?
What is the primary reason a heavy object falls faster than a lighter one through a viscous fluid?
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity (\( v \propto (m g - F_b) / 6 \pi \eta a \)) depends on weight minus buoyant force. A heavier object has a greater net downward force, increasing its terminal velocity compared to a lighter object of the same size.

questions.question_text: A hydraulic lift raises a \( 2300 \, \text{kg} \) load using a small piston of radius \( 5.0 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 20 \, \text{cm} \). What force is applied on the small piston? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
An aircraft (\( m = 2.2 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 440 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies level. What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \). \( mg = 2.2 \times 10^5 \times 10 = 2.2 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \), \( A = 440 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2.2 \times 10^6}{440} = 5000 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A spray pump tube (\( 10 \, \text{cm}^2 \)) has 50 holes, each of diameter \( 0.8 \, \text{mm} \). If the flow speed inside is \( 1.2 \, \text{m/min} \), what is the ejection speed?
Why does a bubble collapse when the external pressure exceeds its internal pressure?
questions.explanation: The excess pressure inside a bubble (\( 4S/r \)) balances the external pressure. If external pressure exceeds this, the net inward force overcomes surface tension’s resistance, causing the bubble to collapse.

questions.question_text: A soap bubble of radius \( 11 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.027 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.027 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 11 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.027}{11 \times 10^{-3}} = 9.82 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: What does the equation of continuity imply about fluid flow in a pipe of varying cross-section?
questions.explanation: The equation of continuity (\( A v = \text{constant} \)) states that the product of cross-sectional area and velocity remains constant for an incompressible fluid in steady flow. As the area decreases, velocity increases to conserve mass flow rate.

questions.question_text: Water flows at \( 3.5 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 4.5 \, \text{m} \) height with pressure \( 1.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the pressure at \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) height with speed \( 4.5 \, \text{m/s} \)? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
According to Pascal’s law, what happens to the pressure in a fluid when an external force is applied?
options: It increases only at the point of application
It is transmitted undiminished to all points
questions.explanation: Pascal’s law states that a change in pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every point within the fluid and to the walls of the container, ensuring uniform pressure distribution.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 11

questions.question_text: Why is the pressure of the atmosphere measured as the weight of a column of air?
options: It’s the weight of air per unit area
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column per unit area above a point, extending to the top of the atmosphere, as it results from the gravitational force acting on the air mass, as described in the chapter.

questions.question_text: What assumption does Bernoulli’s principle make about fluid flow that limits its application to real fluids?
questions.explanation: Bernoulli’s principle assumes zero viscosity (non-viscous flow), ignoring frictional losses that occur in real fluids, where viscosity converts kinetic energy into heat, reducing its applicability.

questions.question_text: A hydraulic system has a small piston (\( 0.005 \, \text{m}^2 \)) and a large piston (\( 0.025 \, \text{m}^2 \)). If \( 80 \, \text{N} \) is applied on the small piston, what force does the large piston exert?
A \( 75 \, \text{kg} \) person stands on two bones, each with area \( 24 \, \text{cm}^2 \). What is the average pressure on the bones? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A pipe has a cross-sectional area of \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^2 \) at one end and \( 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \) at the other. If water flows at \( 2 \, \text{m/s} \) through the wider end, what is the speed at the narrower end?
questions.explanation: Using the equation of continuity: \( A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2 \). \( A_1 = 0.02 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( v_1 = 2 \, \text{m/s} \), \( A_2 = 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( v_2 = \frac{A_1 v_1}{A_2} = \frac{0.02 \times 2}{0.01} = 4 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What ensures that the braking effort is equal on all wheels in a hydraulic brake system?
questions.explanation: Pascal’s law ensures that pressure applied to the brake fluid is transmitted undiminished to all brake cylinders, providing equal force to each wheel, as the system relies on uniform pressure distribution.

questions.question_text: A spray tube (\( 4 \, \text{cm}^2 \)) has 20 holes of diameter \( 1.4 \, \text{mm} \). If the flow speed is \( 1.8 \, \text{m/min} \), what is the ejection speed?
Which statement is incorrect about the Magnus effect?
options: It is due to gravitational force
questions.explanation: The Magnus effect causes a spinning object to deviate due to a pressure difference from varying air speeds (Bernoulli’s principle), not viscosity or gravity alone. The incorrect statement is that it’s due to gravitational force.

questions.question_text: A \( 55 \, \text{kg} \) person stands on two bones, each with area \( 14 \, \text{cm}^2 \). What is the average pressure on the bones? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Which of the following statements is correct about a barometer?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure by balancing it with the weight of a liquid column (\( P_a = \rho g h \)), typically mercury due to its high density, which shortens the column height.

questions.question_text: Why do liquid drops tend to be spherical in the absence of external forces?
questions.explanation: Surface tension minimizes surface energy by reducing surface area. For a given volume, a sphere has the smallest surface area, making it the preferred shape for liquid drops when gravity or other forces are negligible.

questions.question_text: A capillary tube of radius \( 0.25 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in ethanol (\( S = 0.0227 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( \cos \theta = 1 \)). What is the capillary rise? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A tank has a hole \( 1.7 \, \text{m} \) below the water surface, open to the atmosphere. What is the efflux speed? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law: \( v = \sqrt{2 g h} \). \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 1.7 \, \text{m} \). \( v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 1.7} = \sqrt{33.32} \approx 5.77 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A bubble of radius \( 4.5 \, \text{mm} \) is blown at \( 35 \, \text{cm} \) depth in a soap solution (\( \rho = 1.2 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( S = 0.025 \, \text{N/m} \)). What is the total pressure inside? (Take \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Why is pressure considered a scalar quantity despite being defined as force per unit area?
options: It acts equally in all directions
questions.explanation: Pressure is a scalar because it acts equally in all directions in a fluid at rest and lacks directional properties, even though force (a vector) is involved. Only the normal component of force is considered in its definition (\( P = F/A \)).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 12

questions.question_text: What is the excess pressure inside a mercury drop of radius \( 2 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension of mercury = \( 0.465 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a drop: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.465 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 2 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.465}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = 465 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Which statement is incorrect about surface tension?
options: It acts like a stretched membrane
questions.explanation: Surface tension arises from cohesive forces at the liquid’s surface, decreasing with temperature due to weaker molecular interactions, not increasing. The incorrect statement is that it increases with temperature.

questions.question_text: Why does adding a wetting agent like soap reduce the angle of contact of water on a surface?
questions.explanation: Wetting agents reduce surface tension and increase adhesion between the liquid and solid, lowering the angle of contact (\( \theta \)), as the liquid spreads more easily, enhancing wetting, as explained in the chapter.

questions.question_text: A tank has a hole \( 1.3 \, \text{m} \) below the water surface, open to the atmosphere. What is the efflux speed? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law: \( v = \sqrt{2 g h} \). \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 1.3 \, \text{m} \). \( v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 1.3} = \sqrt{25.48} \approx 5.05 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the total pressure at a depth of \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) in oxygen liquid (\( \rho = 1.43 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with atmospheric pressure \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
What is the gauge pressure at \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) depth in a tank of mercury (\( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 2.5 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 13.6 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 2.5 = 3.4 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: An aircraft (\( m = 2.8 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 480 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies level. What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \). \( mg = 2.8 \times 10^5 \times 9.8 = 2.744 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \), \( A = 480 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2.744 \times 10^6}{480} = 5716.67 \, \text{Pa} \approx 5717 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A plate of area \( 0.05 \, \text{m}^2 \) moves at \( 0.7 \, \text{m/s} \) over a \( 0.8 \, \text{mm} \) thick water film (\( \eta = 1.0 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Pa s} \)). What force is required?
Which of the following statements is correct about the angle of contact?
options: It depends on adhesive and cohesive forces
It is independent of the liquid
questions.explanation: The angle of contact depends on the relative strength of adhesive (liquid-solid) and cohesive (liquid-liquid) forces, determining wetting behavior (acute for wetting, obtuse for non-wetting).

questions.question_text: What is the gauge pressure at a depth of \( 2.4 \, \text{m} \) in whole blood (\( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 2.4 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 1.06 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 2.4 = 25440 \, \text{Pa} \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 13

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about terminal velocity?
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity occurs when the viscous force (proportional to velocity) equals the net gravitational force, resulting in zero acceleration and constant speed, as per Stokes’ law.

questions.question_text: A soap bubble of radius \( 7 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.028 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.028 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 7 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.028}{7 \times 10^{-3}} = 16 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: An aircraft (\( m = 2.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 400 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies level. What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \). \( mg = 2.0 \times 10^5 \times 9.8 = 1.96 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \), \( A = 400 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{1.96 \times 10^6}{400} = 4900 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A plate of area \( 0.08 \, \text{m}^2 \) moves at \( 0.8 \, \text{m/s} \) over a \( 0.7 \, \text{mm} \) thick glycerine film (\( \eta = 0.83 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What force is required?
A sphere of radius \( 0.04 \, \text{m} \) moves at \( 0.12 \, \text{m/s} \) through honey (\( \eta = 0.2 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What is the viscous drag force?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 0.2 \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.04 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.12 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 0.2 \times 0.04 \times 0.12 = 0.1809 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What ensures that a fluid at rest cannot sustain a shear stress?
questions.explanation: Fluids lack rigidity and cannot resist shear stress without flowing. Any attempt to apply shear stress causes deformation (flow), as fluids have no fixed shape, unlike solids, which resist shear due to strong intermolecular forces.

questions.question_text: Water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) flows horizontally at \( 4 \, \text{m/s} \) with pressure \( 1.6 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed increases to \( 7 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure?

A hydraulic lift raises a \( 1600 \, \text{kg} \) load using a small piston of radius \( 4 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 16 \, \text{cm} \). What force is applied on the small piston? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Why does the pressure at the bottom of three differently shaped vessels connected at the base remain the same when filled with water to the same height?
options: Due to varying volumes of water
Because pressure depends only on depth
questions.explanation: The hydrostatic paradox demonstrates that pressure in a fluid at rest depends only on depth (\( \rho g h \)) and not on the shape or volume of the container. At the same depth, the pressure is identical regardless of the vessel’s shape.

questions.question_text: A manometer with mercury (\( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 0.25 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 14

questions.question_text: A tank has a hole \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) below the water surface, open to the atmosphere. What is the efflux speed? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law: \( v = \sqrt{2 g h} \). \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 1.5 \, \text{m} \). \( v = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 1.5} = \sqrt{30} \approx 5.48 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the gauge pressure at a depth of \( 1.9 \, \text{m} \) in ethyl alcohol (\( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 1.9 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 806 \times 10 \times 1.9 = 15314 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) flows horizontally at \( 5.0 \, \text{m/s} \) with pressure \( 2.1 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed increases to \( 7.5 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure?
Why does the pressure exerted by a fluid increase with depth?
options: Due to the weight of the fluid above
questions.explanation: Pressure increases with depth due to the weight of the fluid column above, as given by \( P = \rho g h \). The greater the depth, the more fluid mass contributes to the pressure at that point.

questions.question_text: A bubble of radius \( 2.5 \, \text{mm} \) is blown at \( 20 \, \text{cm} \) depth in water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \)). What is the total pressure inside? (Take \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Why does a mercury barometer use mercury instead of water?
questions.explanation: Mercury’s high density (\( 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) results in a shorter column height (\( h = P_a / \rho g \)) to balance atmospheric pressure, making it more practical than water, which requires a much taller column due to lower density.

questions.question_text: What is the excess pressure inside a mercury drop of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.4355 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.4355 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.4355}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 580.67 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a liquid’s surface behave like a stretched membrane?
options: Due to cohesive forces at the surface
questions.explanation: Surface tension arises from cohesive forces between liquid molecules, creating a contractile force at the surface, resembling a stretched membrane that resists expansion, as molecules at the surface have higher energy than those inside.

questions.question_text: Water flows at \( 2.3 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 3.5 \, \text{m} \) height with pressure \( 1.6 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the pressure at \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) height with speed \( 3.2 \, \text{m/s} \)? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

What is the total pressure at a depth of \( 4 \, \text{m} \) in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) if atmospheric pressure is \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 15

questions.question_text: A soap film on a wire supports \( 1.2 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 25 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?
A soap bubble of radius \( 8 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.027 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.027 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 8 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.027}{8 \times 10^{-3}} = 13.5 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A bubble of radius \( 3.5 \, \text{mm} \) is blown at \( 15 \, \text{cm} \) depth in water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \)). What is the total pressure inside? (Take \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

The pressure at a depth of \( 3 \, \text{m} \) in ethyl alcohol (\( \rho = 806 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) is measured with atmospheric pressure as \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the total pressure? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A pipe’s cross-sectional area decreases from \( 0.04 \, \text{m}^2 \) to \( 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \). If the speed at the larger end is \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the speed at the smaller end?
A metal plate of area \( 0.05 \, \text{m}^2 \) moves over a liquid film (\( \eta = 0.02 \, \text{Pa s} \)) of thickness \( 0.2 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 0.5 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the force required?
An aircraft (\( m = 4.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 600 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies level. What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \). \( mg = 4.0 \times 10^5 \times 9.8 = 3.92 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \), \( A = 600 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{3.92 \times 10^6}{600} = 6533.33 \, \text{Pa} \approx 6533 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Water flows at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) height with pressure \( 1.8 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the pressure at \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) height with speed \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s} \)? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Which statement is incorrect about hydrostatic pressure?
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure (\( P = \rho g h \)) depends on depth, not the container’s shape or fluid velocity (which applies to dynamic flow). The incorrect statement is that it depends on container shape.

questions.question_text: A \( 70 \, \text{kg} \) person stands on two bones, each with area \( 16 \, \text{cm}^2 \). What is the average pressure on the bones? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 16

questions.question_text: A spray tube (\( 9 \, \text{cm}^2 \)) has 45 holes of diameter \( 0.6 \, \text{mm} \). If the flow speed is \( 2.0 \, \text{m/min} \), what is the ejection speed?
Which of the following statements is correct about pressure in a fluid at rest?
options: It depends on the shape of the container
It acts equally in all directions
questions.explanation: Pressure in a fluid at rest acts equally in all directions (Pascal’s law) and increases with depth (\( P = P_a + \rho g h \)), not influenced by the container’s shape, ruling out options involving directionality or shape dependence.

questions.question_text: A plate of area \( 0.09 \, \text{m}^2 \) moves at \( 0.5 \, \text{m/s} \) over a \( 0.6 \, \text{mm} \) thick machine oil film (\( \eta = 0.113 \, \text{Pa s} \)). What force is required?
A spray tube (\( 5 \, \text{cm}^2 \)) has 25 holes of diameter \( 1.3 \, \text{mm} \). If the flow speed is \( 2.7 \, \text{m/min} \), what is the ejection speed?
What is the gauge pressure at a depth of \( 2.7 \, \text{m} \) in mercury (\( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 2.7 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 13.6 \times 10^3 \times 9.8 \times 2.7 = 359856 \, \text{Pa} = 3.59856 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: What is the excess pressure inside a water drop of radius \( 2.5 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.3 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.3 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 2.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.3 \times 10^{-3}}{2.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 0.24 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 45 \, \text{kg} \) person stands on two bones, each with area \( 18 \, \text{cm}^2 \). What is the average pressure on the bones? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A hydraulic lift raises a \( 2100 \, \text{kg} \) load using a small piston of radius \( 3.0 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 12 \, \text{cm} \). What force is applied on the small piston? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

What is the total pressure at a depth of \( 3.2 \, \text{m} \) in water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with atmospheric pressure \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A soap film supports \( 2.8 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{N} \) over a \( 56 \, \text{cm} \) slider. What is the surface tension?

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 17

questions.question_text: A hydraulic press applies \( 250 \, \text{N} \) on a small piston of area \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^2 \). What force is exerted by a large piston of area \( 0.08 \, \text{m}^2 \)?

Water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) flows horizontally at \( 3.2 \, \text{m/s} \) with pressure \( 1.85 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed increases to \( 5.8 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure?
Which statement is incorrect about fluids?
options: They resist shear stress like solids
questions.explanation: Fluids cannot resist shear stress without flowing due to their lack of rigidity; solids, not fluids, resist shear stress with a fixed shape. The incorrect statement is that fluids resist shear stress like solids.

questions.question_text: A hydraulic press applies \( 350 \, \text{N} \) on a small piston of area \( 0.025 \, \text{m}^2 \). What force is exerted by a large piston of area \( 0.1 \, \text{m}^2 \)?
What happens if the pressure applied to a hydraulic system exceeds the fluid’s ability to transmit it?
options: The system fails or fluid compresses
questions.explanation: Pascal’s law assumes an incompressible fluid. If pressure exceeds the fluid’s incompressibility limit, the fluid compresses or the system fails (e.g., leaks or bursts), as the assumption of uniform pressure transmission breaks down.

questions.question_text: What property distinguishes liquids and gases from solids in terms of shape?
options: They can flow and lack a definite shape
questions.explanation: Liquids and gases are fluids that can flow and take the shape of their container due to their inability to maintain a fixed shape, unlike solids, which have a definite shape due to strong intermolecular forces resisting deformation.

questions.question_text: A capillary tube of radius \( 0.2 \, \text{mm} \) is dipped in mercury (\( S = 0.4355 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( \cos \theta = -0.5 \)). What is the depression? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Capillary rise: \( h = \frac{2 S \cos \theta}{\rho g a} \). \( S = 0.4355 \, \text{N/m} \), \( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( a = 0.2 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \), \( \cos \theta = -0.5 \). \( h = \frac{2 \times 0.4355 \times (-0.5)}{13.6 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 0.2 \times 10^{-3}} = -0.016 \, \text{m} = -1.6 \, \text{cm} \).

questions.question_text: What is the force on a submarine window (\( 0.09 \, \text{m}^2 \)) at \( 200 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)), interior at atmospheric pressure? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h = 1.03 \times 10^3 \times 9.8 \times 200 = 2.0194 \times 10^6 \, \text{Pa} \). \( F = P_g A = 2.0194 \times 10^6 \times 0.09 = 1.81746 \times 10^5 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: Which statement is incorrect about capillary action?
questions.explanation: Capillary rise (\( h = 2S \cos \theta / \rho g r \)) is inversely proportional to radius, not directly proportional. The incorrect statement is that height increases with tube radius.

questions.question_text: Why does the height of a mercury column in a barometer decrease during a storm?
questions.explanation: The barometer measures atmospheric pressure (\( P_a = \rho g h \)). During a storm, atmospheric pressure drops, reducing the force supporting the mercury column, causing its height to decrease, as noted in the chapter.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 18

questions.question_text: An aircraft (\( m = 4.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{kg} \), wing area \( 600 \, \text{m}^2 \)) flies level. What is the pressure difference across the wings? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P \cdot A = mg \). \( mg = 4.5 \times 10^5 \times 9.8 = 4.41 \times 10^6 \, \text{N} \), \( A = 600 \, \text{m}^2 \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4.41 \times 10^6}{600} = 7350 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A tank has a hole \( 0.9 \, \text{m} \) below the water surface, open to the atmosphere. What is the efflux speed? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law: \( v = \sqrt{2 g h} \). \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 0.9 \, \text{m} \). \( v = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.9} = \sqrt{18} \approx 4.24 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A sphere of radius \( 0.025 \, \text{m} \) moves at \( 0.08 \, \text{m/s} \) through blood (\( \eta = 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Pa s} \)). What is the viscous drag force?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.025 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.08 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.025 \times 0.08 = 1.017 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A fluid flows through a pipe with speeds \( v_1 = 2 \, \text{m/s} \) at height \( h_1 = 1 \, \text{m} \) and \( v_2 = 4 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( h_2 = 0 \, \text{m} \). If \( P_1 = 1.2 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), find \( P_2 \). (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Which of the following statements is correct about streamline flow?
questions.explanation: In streamline flow, fluid particles follow fixed paths (streamlines) with constant velocity at each point, occurring at low speeds where viscous forces dominate, not requiring high speed or turbulence.

questions.question_text: Why does a liquid jet emerging from a small hole maintain a constant range until near the hole?
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law (\( v = \sqrt{2gh} \)) shows that the efflux speed depends only on depth, remaining constant near the hole until external factors (e.g., air resistance or gravity’s vertical effect) alter its trajectory.

questions.question_text: What is the force on a submarine window (\( 0.05 \, \text{m}^2 \)) at \( 600 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)), interior at atmospheric pressure? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h = 1.03 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 600 = 6.18 \times 10^6 \, \text{Pa} \). \( F = P_g A = 6.18 \times 10^6 \times 0.05 = 3.09 \times 10^5 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A hydraulic press applies \( 50 \, \text{N} \) on a piston of area \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^2 \). What force is exerted by a piston of area \( 0.1 \, \text{m}^2 \)?
What determines whether a liquid wets a solid surface or forms droplets on it?
questions.explanation: The angle of contact (\( \theta \)) determines wetting behavior: an acute angle (strong attraction to the solid) causes spreading (wetting), while an obtuse angle (weak attraction) leads to droplet formation, as explained in the surface tension section.

questions.question_text: Which statement is incorrect about Bernoulli’s principle?
options: It applies to highly viscous fluids
It conserves energy along a streamline
questions.explanation: Bernoulli’s principle assumes non-viscous flow, not high viscosity, as viscosity causes energy loss, violating the energy conservation assumption. The incorrect statement is that it applies to highly viscous fluids.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 19

questions.question_text: A bubble of radius \( 3 \, \text{mm} \) is blown at \( 30 \, \text{cm} \) depth in water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( S = 0.0727 \, \text{N/m} \)). What is the total pressure inside? (Take \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Why does blowing over a piece of paper lift it upwards?
options: Due to lower pressure above from faster airflow
questions.explanation: Bernoulli’s principle states that faster airflow above the paper reduces pressure, while slower air below maintains higher pressure, creating an upward lift due to the pressure difference.

questions.question_text: Why does a fluid’s flow rate remain constant in a pipe of varying diameter?
questions.explanation: The equation of continuity (\( A v = \text{constant} \)) ensures that the mass flow rate (volume flow rate for an incompressible fluid) remains constant, as the product of area and velocity adjusts inversely with diameter changes.

questions.question_text: A pipe narrows from \( 0.07 \, \text{m}^2 \) to \( 0.035 \, \text{m}^2 \). If water flows at \( 2.4 \, \text{m/s} \) in the wider section, what is the speed in the narrower section?
Why does a fluid’s flow transition from streamline to turbulent beyond a critical speed?
options: Because inertial forces exceed viscous forces
questions.explanation: Beyond a critical speed, inertial forces dominate over viscous forces, disrupting the orderly motion of streamline flow, leading to chaotic, turbulent flow with eddies and mixing, as noted in the chapter.

questions.question_text: Which statement is incorrect regarding Torricelli’s law?
options: It equates to free fall speed
questions.explanation: Torricelli’s law (\( v = \sqrt{2gh} \)) assumes non-viscous flow and neglects losses, not depending on viscosity or requiring turbulence. The incorrect statement is that it depends on fluid viscosity.

questions.question_text: Why does a liquid’s surface tension decrease with increasing temperature?
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature weakens cohesive forces between liquid molecules by increasing their kinetic energy, reducing the contractile force at the surface, thus lowering surface tension, as noted in the chapter.

questions.question_text: Why does a fluid’s viscosity contribute to energy loss in real flow systems?
options: It converts kinetic energy to heat
questions.explanation: Viscosity causes internal friction between fluid layers, converting kinetic energy into heat through shear stress, leading to energy dissipation, which Bernoulli’s ideal flow neglects.

questions.question_text: What causes the height of capillary rise to be inversely proportional to the tube’s radius?
options: Pressure difference varies inversely with radius
questions.explanation: The capillary rise formula (\( h = 2S \cos \theta / \rho g r \)) shows that \( h \) is inversely proportional to radius (\( r \)) because the pressure difference due to surface tension (\( 2S/r \)) must balance the weight of the liquid column, which depends on \( h \).

questions.question_text: Why do fluids exert pressure only normal to a surface at rest?
options: Because fluids cannot resist shear stress
questions.explanation: In a fluid at rest, any tangential (shear) force would cause the fluid to flow due to its inability to resist shear stress. According to Newton’s third law, if a tangential force existed, the fluid would exert an equal and opposite force, leading to motion. Since the fluid is at rest, no such motion occurs, and the force must be normal to the surface.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 20

questions.question_text: A sphere of radius \( 0.015 \, \text{m} \) moves at \( 0.2 \, \text{m/s} \) through water (\( \eta = 1.0 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Pa s} \)). What is the viscous force?
questions.explanation: Stokes’ law: \( F = 6 \pi \eta a v \). \( \eta = 1.0 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Pa s} \), \( a = 0.015 \, \text{m} \), \( v = 0.2 \, \text{m/s} \). \( F = 6 \times 3.14 \times 1.0 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.015 \times 0.2 = 5.652 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the excess pressure inside a mercury drop of radius \( 4 \, \text{mm} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \)? (Surface tension = \( 0.4355 \, \text{N/m} \))
questions.explanation: Excess pressure: \( \Delta P = \frac{2 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.4355 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 4 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{2 \times 0.4355}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = 217.75 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 1500 \, \text{kg} \) car is lifted by a hydraulic system with a small piston of radius \( 6 \, \text{cm} \) and a large piston of radius \( 18 \, \text{cm} \). What force is needed on the small piston? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
What is the primary reason a sharp needle pierces the skin more easily than a blunt object with the same force?
options: The needle has a smaller area, increasing pressure
questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as force per unit area (\( P = F/A \)). A sharp needle has a smaller contact area, resulting in higher pressure for the same force, making it easier to penetrate the skin compared to a blunt object with a larger area.

questions.question_text: What is the force on a submarine window (\( 0.06 \, \text{m}^2 \)) at \( 400 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)), interior at atmospheric pressure? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h = 1.03 \times 10^3 \times 9.8 \times 400 = 4.0376 \times 10^6 \, \text{Pa} \). \( F = P_g A = 4.0376 \times 10^6 \times 0.06 = 2.42256 \times 10^5 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: Why does the viscosity of liquids generally decrease with increasing temperature?
questions.explanation: Higher temperatures increase molecular kinetic energy in liquids, weakening intermolecular forces, reducing resistance to flow, and thus lowering viscosity, as noted in the chapter.

questions.question_text: A bubble of radius \( 4 \, \text{mm} \) is formed at \( 50 \, \text{cm} \) depth in a soap solution (\( \rho = 1.2 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( S = 0.025 \, \text{N/m} \)). What is the total pressure inside? (Take \( P_a = 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Which statement is incorrect about dynamic lift?
questions.explanation: Dynamic lift (e.g., on airplane wings) results from a pressure difference due to faster airflow above (Bernoulli’s principle), not viscosity or gravitational force alone. The incorrect statement is that it’s due to viscosity.

questions.question_text: A spray tube (\( 7 \, \text{cm}^2 \)) has 35 holes of diameter \( 0.8 \, \text{mm} \). If the flow speed is \( 3.0 \, \text{m/min} \), what is the ejection speed?
A hydraulic press uses a small piston of area \( 0.008 \, \text{m}^2 \) to exert \( 120 \, \text{N} \). What force is produced by a large piston of area \( 0.032 \, \text{m}^2 \)?

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 21

questions.question_text: Why does the pressure in a fluid decrease when its speed increases in a horizontal pipe?
questions.explanation: Bernoulli’s principle states that in steady flow, an increase in kinetic energy (\( \frac{1}{2} \rho v^2 \)) corresponds to a decrease in pressure energy, as total energy is conserved along a horizontal streamline.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude as the weight of the air column above reduces, a fundamental concept in the chapter’s discussion of pressure variation.

questions.question_text: A container has whole blood (\( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) up to \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \). What is the gauge pressure at the bottom? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 1.5 \, \text{m} \). \( P_g = 1.06 \times 10^3 \times 9.8 \times 1.5 = 15582 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 60 \, \text{kg} \) person stands on two bones, each with area \( 25 \, \text{cm}^2 \). What is the average pressure on the bones? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A spray tube (\( 10 \, \text{cm}^2 \)) has 50 holes of diameter \( 0.9 \, \text{mm} \). If the flow speed is \( 2.5 \, \text{m/min} \), what is the ejection speed?
What happens to the fluid velocity when a pipe narrows, assuming steady flow?
questions.explanation: The equation of continuity (\( A v = \text{constant} \)) for an incompressible fluid in steady flow implies that as the cross-sectional area decreases, the velocity must increase to maintain a constant mass flow rate.

questions.question_text: A mercury barometer shows a height of \( 75 \, \text{cm} \) at sea level. What is the atmospheric pressure? (\( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

Water flows through a horizontal pipe at a speed of \( 3 \, \text{m/s} \) with a pressure of \( 1.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed increases to \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \))

What is the total pressure at a depth of \( 3.4 \, \text{m} \) in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) with atmospheric pressure \( 1.01 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A person stands on two bones, each with area \( 22 \, \text{cm}^2 \), exerting a total force of \( 588 \, \text{N} \). What is the average pressure on the bones?

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids Chapter-Wise Test 22

questions.question_text: A soap bubble of radius \( 6 \, \text{mm} \) has a surface tension of \( 0.03 \, \text{N/m} \). What is the excess pressure inside?
questions.explanation: Excess pressure in a bubble: \( \Delta P = \frac{4 S}{r} \). \( S = 0.03 \, \text{N/m} \), \( r = 6 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = \frac{4 \times 0.03}{6 \times 10^{-3}} = 20 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: Water (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) flows horizontally at \( 3.5 \, \text{m/s} \) with pressure \( 1.7 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). If the speed rises to \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \), what is the new pressure?
A manometer with mercury (\( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 20 \, \text{cm} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 13.6 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 0.2 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = 13.6 \times 10^3 \times 9.8 \times 0.2 = 26656 \, \text{Pa} \).

questions.question_text: What is the force on a submarine window (\( 0.08 \, \text{m}^2 \)) at \( 300 \, \text{m} \) depth in seawater (\( \rho = 1.03 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)), interior at atmospheric pressure? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure: \( P_g = \rho g h = 1.03 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 300 = 3.09 \times 10^6 \, \text{Pa} \). \( F = P_g A = 3.09 \times 10^6 \times 0.08 = 2.472 \times 10^5 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What is the physical significance of the term \( \frac{1}{2} \rho v^2 \) in Bernoulli’s equation?
questions.explanation: In Bernoulli’s equation, \( \frac{1}{2} \rho v^2 \) represents the kinetic energy per unit volume of the fluid, reflecting the energy associated with its motion, balanced against pressure and potential energy terms.

questions.question_text: Water flows at \( 2.9 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 3.2 \, \text{m} \) height with pressure \( 1.9 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa} \). What is the pressure at \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) height with speed \( 4.0 \, \text{m/s} \)? (\( \rho = 1000 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
Why does a hydraulic lift amplify force when lifting a heavy load?
questions.explanation: Pascal’s law ensures pressure is transmitted equally. A smaller piston area (\( A_1 \)) with force \( F_1 \) creates pressure (\( P = F_1/A_1 \)), which, applied to a larger area (\( A_2 \)), results in a larger force (\( F_2 = P \cdot A_2 \)), amplifying the input force.

questions.question_text: A plate of area \( 0.07 \, \text{m}^2 \) moves at \( 0.3 \, \text{m/s} \) over a \( 0.5 \, \text{mm} \) thick water film (\( \eta = 1.0 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Pa s} \)). What force is required?
A spray tube (\( 7 \, \text{cm}^2 \)) has 35 holes of diameter \( 1.2 \, \text{mm} \). If the flow speed is \( 3.0 \, \text{m/min} \), what is the ejection speed?
A manometer with whole blood (\( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \)) shows a height difference of \( 0.18 \, \text{m} \). What is the pressure difference? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: \( \Delta P = \rho g h \). \( \rho = 1.06 \times 10^3 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( h = 0.18 \, \text{m} \). \( \Delta P = 1.06 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 0.18 = 1908 \, \text{Pa} \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 1

questions.question_text: A copper block of dimensions \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \times 0.05 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 1.5 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of copper is \( 4.2 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \). Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.4 \times 0.2 = 0.08 \, \text{m}^2 \). Shear stress: \( \frac{1.5 \times 10^4}{0.08} = 1.875 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{1.875 \times 10^5}{4.2 \times 10^{10}} \approx 4.46 \times 10^{-6} \).

questions.question_text: What does the term "elastic limit" refer to in the context of a material’s stress-strain behavior?
options: The point where the material fractures
The maximum stress before plastic deformation begins
The maximum stress beyond which the material does not return to its original shape
The minimum stress required for permanent deformation
questions.explanation: The elastic limit is the maximum stress a material can withstand while still returning to its original shape upon removal of the load; beyond this, permanent deformation occurs.

questions.question_text: Which type of stress leads to a change in length of a body without changing its shape?
questions.explanation: Longitudinal stress (tensile or compressive) causes a change in length along the direction of the applied force without altering the shape of the body.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best defines stress in the context of mechanical properties of solids?
options: Change in length per unit area
Change in volume per unit force
questions.explanation: Stress is defined as the restoring force per unit area developed in a body due to an external deforming force, given by \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} \).

questions.question_text: What does the steepness of the linear portion of a stress-strain curve typically indicate about a material?
questions.explanation: The steepness of the linear portion of the stress-strain curve indicates a higher Young’s modulus, meaning the material is stiffer and requires more stress to produce a given strain.

questions.question_text: An aluminium rod of length \( 1.6 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is compressed by a force of \( 600 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of aluminium is \( 7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the compression?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{600 \times 1.6}{2 \times 10^{-6} \times 7 \times 10^{10}} = \frac{960}{1.4 \times 10^5} \approx 6.86 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 6.86 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A water sample of volume 1 litre is compressed by 0.05%. If the bulk modulus of water is 2.2 × 10 9 N/m 2 , what is the pressure applied?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: B = -p / (ΔV / V). Rearrange: p = -B × (ΔV / V). Given: ΔV / V = -0.05% = -0.0005. Substitute: p = 2.2 × 10 9 × 0.0005 = 1.1 × 10 6 N/m 2 .

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length 4 m and cross-sectional area 2 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by 0.4 mm. If the force applied is 200 N, what is the Young's modulus of the steel?
A steel wire of length 3 m and cross-sectional area 4 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by 0.3 mm. If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = (F L) / (A ΔL). Rearrange: F = (Y A ΔL) / L. Substitute: ΔL = 0.3 × 10 -3 m, so F = (2 × 10 11 × 4 × 10 -6 × 0.3 × 10 -3 ) / 3 = 80 N.

questions.question_text: Why is steel often chosen over materials like copper for heavy-duty structural applications?
questions.explanation: Steel has a higher Young’s modulus (\( \approx 200 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \)) compared to copper (\( \approx 110 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \)), requiring a larger force to produce the same deformation, making it more suitable for resisting bending and stretching.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 2

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 3 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 2 \times 10^{11} \times 3 \times 10^{-4} = 6 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Force: \( F = \text{Stress} \times A = 6 \times 10^7 \times 2 \times 10^{-6} = 120 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A copper rod of radius \( 0.02 \, \text{m} \) and length \( 1.0 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a tensile force producing a stress of \( 2 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). What is the force applied? (Take \( \pi \approx 3.14 \))
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} \). Area: \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.02)^2 = 3.14 \times 4 \times 10^{-4} = 1.256 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^2 \). Force: \( F = \text{Stress} \times A = 2 \times 10^7 \times 1.256 \times 10^{-3} = 2.512 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length 2.5 m and cross-sectional area 3 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by a force producing a strain of 2 × 10 -4 . If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = Stress / Strain. Stress: Stress = Y × Strain = 2 × 10 11 × 2 × 10 -4 = 4 × 10 7 N/m 2 . Force: F = Stress × A = 4 × 10 7 × 3 × 10 -6 = 120 N.

questions.question_text: What does the steepness of the initial linear portion of a stress-strain curve indicate?
questions.explanation: The steepness of the initial linear portion indicates a higher Young’s modulus, meaning the material is stiffer and requires more stress to produce a given strain.

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length 1 m and cross-sectional area 1 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by a force of 50 N. If the Young's modulus of copper is 1.1 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = (F L) / (A ΔL). Rearrange: ΔL = (F L) / (A Y). Substitute: ΔL = (50 × 1) / (1 × 10 -6 × 1.1 × 10 11 ) = 50 / (1.1 × 10 5 ) ≈ 4.55 × 10 -4 m = 0.455 mm.

questions.question_text: Which type of stress leads to a change in length of a body without changing its shape?
questions.explanation: Longitudinal stress (tensile or compressive) causes a change in length along the direction of the applied force without altering the shape of the body.

questions.question_text: In the stress-strain behavior of a material, what occurs after the maximum stress point when the material is ductile?
options: The material returns to its original shape
The stress decreases leading to fracture
questions.explanation: For a ductile material, after the maximum stress point (ultimate tensile strength), the stress decreases with increasing strain as the material necks, leading to fracture.

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 3 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{3 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -8.11 \times 10^{-5} \). Magnitude: \( 8.11 \times 10^{-5} \).

questions.question_text: Why are I-shaped beams commonly used in construction for load-bearing applications?
options: They have a higher shear modulus
They provide a large load-bearing surface with reduced bending
questions.explanation: I-shaped beams provide a large load-bearing surface and sufficient depth to reduce bending, minimizing buckling while reducing weight compared to solid beams.

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 1.6 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 1.8 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 180 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{180 \times 1.6}{1.8 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.1 \times 10^{11}} = \frac{288}{1.98 \times 10^5} \approx 1.45 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 1.45 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A brass wire of length \( 2.0 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 300 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of brass is \( 9 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain produced?
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{300}{2 \times 10^{-6}} = 1.5 \times 10^8 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{1.5 \times 10^8}{9 \times 10^{10}} \approx 1.67 \times 10^{-3} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 2 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by a force of 200 N. If the elongation is 0.727 mm, what is the Young's modulus of copper?

A water sample of volume \( 2.5 \, \text{litres} \) is compressed by a pressure of \( 2 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of water is \( 2.2 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{2 \times 10^6}{2.2 \times 10^9} \approx -9.09 \times 10^{-4} \). Magnitude: \( 9.09 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 4 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{4 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -1.08 \times 10^{-4} \). Magnitude: \( 1.08 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: An aluminium wire of length \( 2.3 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 1.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a stress of \( 2 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the Young's modulus of aluminium is \( 7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{2 \times 10^7}{7 \times 10^{10}} \approx 2.86 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A glass block of volume 0.01 m 3 is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of 4 × 10 6 N/m 2 . If the bulk modulus of glass is 3.7 × 10 10 N/m 2 , what is the change in volume?
A copper cube of edge length 0.1 m is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of 5 × 10 6 N/m 2 . If the bulk modulus of copper is 1.4 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: B = -p / (ΔV / V). Volume: V = (0.1) 3 = 0.001 m 3 . Fractional change: ΔV / V = -p / B = -(5 × 10 6 ) / (1.4 × 10 11 ) ≈ -3.57 × 10 -5 . Change in volume: ΔV = (ΔV / V) × V = -3.57 × 10 -5 × 0.001 ≈ -3.57 × 10 -8 m 3 .

questions.question_text: What is the primary reason solids are far less compressible than gases?
questions.explanation: The tight coupling between neighboring atoms in solids results in a much higher resistance to volume change compared to gases, where molecules are weakly coupled.

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 1 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 100 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{100 \times 1.5}{1 \times 10^{-6} \times 2 \times 10^{11}} = \frac{150}{2 \times 10^5} = 7.5 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m} = 0.75 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{150 \times 2.0}{1.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 7 \times 10^{10}} = \frac{300}{1.05 \times 10^5} \approx 2.86 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 2.86 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: Why do materials like steel require a significantly larger force to produce small deformations compared to materials like rubber?
questions.explanation: Steel has a much larger Young’s modulus compared to rubber, meaning it has greater stiffness and requires more force to produce the same strain.

questions.question_text: What property of a material primarily determines its resistance to uniform compression?
questions.explanation: The bulk modulus determines a material’s resistance to uniform compression by measuring how much it resists volume change under pressure applied in all directions.

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.03 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 6 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?

questions.question_text: A copper rod of length \( 2.0 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is subjected to a tensile force of \( 500 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain produced?
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{500}{2.5 \times 10^{-6}} = 2 \times 10^8 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{2 \times 10^8}{1.1 \times 10^{11}} \approx 1.82 \times 10^{-3} \).

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.05 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 8 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{8 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -2.16 \times 10^{-4} \). Magnitude: \( 2.16 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A copper block of dimensions \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \times 0.05 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 3 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of copper is \( 4.2 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \). Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.3 \times 0.2 = 0.06 \, \text{m}^2 \). Shear stress: \( \frac{3 \times 10^4}{0.06} = 5 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{5 \times 10^5}{4.2 \times 10^{10}} \approx 1.19 \times 10^{-5} \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 6

questions.question_text: A brass block of dimensions \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \times 0.3 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 6 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of brass is \( 3.6 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the displacement of the top face?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{F / A}{\Delta x / L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta x = \frac{F L}{A G} \). Area: \( A = 0.5 \times 0.3 = 0.15 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( L = 0.2 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( \Delta x = \frac{6 \times 10^4 \times 0.2}{0.15 \times 3.6 \times 10^{10}} = \frac{12000}{5.4 \times 10^9} \approx 2.22 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 2.7 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 450 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain?
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{450}{3 \times 10^{-6}} = 1.5 \times 10^8 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{1.5 \times 10^8}{2 \times 10^{11}} = 7.5 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length 5 m and cross-sectional area 4 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by 0.5 mm. If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the stress?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = (Stress) / (Strain). Strain: Strain = ΔL / L = (0.5 × 10 -3 ) / 5 = 1 × 10 -4 . Stress: Stress = Y × Strain = 2 × 10 11 × 1 × 10 -4 = 2 × 10 7 N/m 2 .

questions.question_text: A copper block of dimensions \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \times 0.4 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 7 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of copper is \( 4.2 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \). Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.24 \, \text{m}^2 \). Shear stress: \( \frac{7 \times 10^4}{0.24} \approx 2.92 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{2.92 \times 10^5}{4.2 \times 10^{10}} \approx 6.95 \times 10^{-6} \).

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between elastic and plastic deformation in a material?
options: Elastic deformation occurs only in solids
Plastic deformation occurs at lower stress
Elastic deformation is reversible, plastic is not
questions.explanation: Elastic deformation is reversible, meaning the material returns to its original shape after the load is removed, while plastic deformation results in permanent changes.

questions.question_text: An aluminium rod of length \( 1.4 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is compressed by a force producing a stress of \( 3 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the Young's modulus of aluminium is \( 7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the compression?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{3 \times 10^7}{7 \times 10^{10}} \approx 4.29 \times 10^{-4} \). Compression: \( \Delta L = \text{Strain} \times L = 4.29 \times 10^{-4} \times 1.4 \approx 6 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m} = 0.6 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A glass slab experiences a hydraulic pressure of 8 × 10 6 N/m 2 . If the bulk modulus of glass is 3.7 × 10 10 N/m 2 , what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: B = -p / (ΔV / V). Rearrange: ΔV / V = -p / B. Substitute: ΔV / V = -(8 × 10 6 ) / (3.7 × 10 10 ) ≈ -2.16 × 10 -4 . Magnitude: 2.16 × 10 -4 .

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 2 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by a force of 200 N. If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the elongation of the wire?
questions.explanation: Using Young's modulus formula: Y = (F L) / (A ΔL). Rearrange for elongation: ΔL = (F L) / (A Y). Substitute values: ΔL = (200 × 2) / (2 × 10 -6 × 2 × 10 11 ). Calculate: ΔL = 400 / (4 × 10 5 ) = 10 -3 m = 1 mm.

questions.question_text: Which modulus describes a material’s resistance to volume change under uniform pressure in all directions?
questions.explanation: The bulk modulus measures a material’s resistance to volume change when subjected to uniform pressure (hydraulic stress) in all directions, affecting volume but not shape.

questions.question_text: A steel cable of radius 0.02 m is used to lift a load. If the maximum stress it can withstand is 1 × 10 8 N/m 2 , what is the maximum load it can support? (Take π ≈ 3.14)

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 7

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 2.0 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 250 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{250 \times 2.0}{2.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.1 \times 10^{11}} = \frac{500}{2.75 \times 10^5} \approx 1.82 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 1.82 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 2.3 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 200 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain?
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{200}{2 \times 10^{-6}} = 1 \times 10^8 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{1 \times 10^8}{1.1 \times 10^{11}} \approx 9.09 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 2.4 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 1.5 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the stress?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 1.1 \times 10^{11} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-4} = 1.65 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: What does the steepness of the linear portion of a stress-strain curve typically indicate about a material?
questions.explanation: The steepness of the linear portion of the stress-strain curve indicates a higher Young’s modulus, meaning the material is stiffer and requires more stress to produce a given strain.

questions.question_text: A water sample of volume \( 1 \, \text{litre} \) is compressed by a pressure of \( 1 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of water is \( 2.2 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{1 \times 10^6}{2.2 \times 10^9} \approx -4.55 \times 10^{-4} \). Magnitude: \( 4.55 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A steel cable of radius 0.015 m is used to support a load. If the maximum stress it can withstand is 2 × 10 8 N/m 2 , what is the maximum load it can support? (Take π ≈ 3.14)

A steel wire of length \( 2.7 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by \( 0.54 \, \text{mm} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the stress?
questions.explanation: Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\Delta L}{L} = \frac{0.54 \times 10^{-3}}{2.7} = 2 \times 10^{-4} \). Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 2 \times 10^{11} \times 2 \times 10^{-4} = 4 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A brass block of dimensions \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \times 0.4 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 9 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of brass is \( 3.6 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \). Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.24 \, \text{m}^2 \). Shear stress: \( \frac{9 \times 10^4}{0.24} = 3.75 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{3.75 \times 10^5}{3.6 \times 10^{10}} \approx 1.04 \times 10^{-5} \).

questions.question_text: A rectangular slab of length 0.4 m, width 0.2 m, and thickness 0.1 m is subjected to a shearing force of 8 × 10 4 N. If the shear modulus is 4 × 10 9 N/m 2 , what is the displacement of the upper face relative to the lower face?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: G = (Shear stress) / (Shear strain) = (F / A) / (Δx / L). Rearrange: Δx = (F L) / (A G). Area A = 0.4 × 0.2 = 0.08 m 2 , L = 0.1 m. Substitute: Δx = (8 × 10 4 × 0.1) / (0.08 × 4 × 10 9 ) = 8000 / (3.2 × 10 8 ) = 2.5 × 10 -5 m.

questions.question_text: An aluminium block of dimensions \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \times 0.4 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 8 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of aluminium is \( 2.5 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the displacement of the top face?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{F / A}{\Delta x / L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta x = \frac{F L}{A G} \). Area: \( A = 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.24 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( L = 0.2 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( \Delta x = \frac{8 \times 10^4 \times 0.2}{0.24 \times 2.5 \times 10^{10}} = \frac{16000}{6 \times 10^9} \approx 2.67 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m} \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 8

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.01 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 2 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{2 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -5.41 \times 10^{-5} \). Change in volume: \( \Delta V = \frac{\Delta V}{V} \times V = -5.41 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.01 \approx -5.41 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}^3 \).

questions.question_text: A brass wire of length \( 1.6 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a stress of \( 4 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the Young's modulus of brass is \( 9 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{4 \times 10^7}{9 \times 10^{10}} \approx 4.44 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A brass wire of length \( 2.4 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a stress of \( 5 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the Young's modulus of brass is \( 9 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{5 \times 10^7}{9 \times 10^{10}} \approx 5.56 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 2.6 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 400 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{400 \times 2.6}{2 \times 10^{-6} \times 2 \times 10^{11}} = \frac{1040}{4 \times 10^5} = 2.6 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 2.6 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A brass rod of radius \( 0.008 \, \text{m} \) and length \( 1.0 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a tensile force producing a stress of \( 5 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). What is the force applied? (Take \( \pi \approx 3.14 \))
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} \). Area: \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.008)^2 = 3.14 \times 6.4 \times 10^{-5} \approx 2.01 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m}^2 \). Force: \( F = \text{Stress} \times A = 5 \times 10^7 \times 2.01 \times 10^{-4} \approx 1.005 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A steel rod of radius \( 0.01 \, \text{m} \) and length \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a tensile force producing a stress of \( 4 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). What is the force applied? (Take \( \pi \approx 3.14 \))
