questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} \). Area: \( A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times (0.01)^2 = 3.14 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m}^2 \). Force: \( F = \text{Stress} \times A = 4 \times 10^7 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-4} = 1.256 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What property of a material primarily determines its resistance to uniform compression?
questions.explanation: The bulk modulus determines a material’s resistance to uniform compression by measuring how much it resists volume change under pressure applied in all directions.

questions.question_text: A copper rod of length 1 m and diameter 2 mm is subjected to a tensile force. If the stress is 4 × 10 7 N/m 2 , what is the force applied? (Take π ≈ 3.14)
A copper block of dimensions 0.4 m × 0.3 m × 0.1 m is subjected to a shearing force of 3 × 10 4 N. If the shear modulus of copper is 4.2 × 10 10 N/m 2 , what is the displacement of the top face?

A brass wire of length \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 2 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of brass is \( 9 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the stress?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 9 \times 10^{10} \times 2 \times 10^{-4} = 1.8 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 9

questions.question_text: Why are I-shaped beams commonly used in construction for load-bearing applications?
options: They have a higher shear modulus
They provide a large load-bearing surface with reduced bending
questions.explanation: I-shaped beams provide a large load-bearing surface and sufficient depth to reduce bending, minimizing buckling while reducing weight compared to solid beams.

questions.question_text: Why do engineers prefer materials with a large Young’s modulus for designing columns and beams?
questions.explanation: Materials with a large Young’s modulus are stiffer, requiring greater force to produce small deformations, which ensures better resistance to bending and stretching.

questions.question_text: In designing bridges, why is it critical to understand the elastic properties of materials?
options: To increase the weight of the bridge
To reduce the cost of materials
questions.explanation: Understanding elastic properties ensures that materials can withstand various loads (traffic, wind, weight) without undergoing permanent deformation, maintaining structural integrity.

questions.question_text: An aluminium block of dimensions \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \times 0.05 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 1.5 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of aluminium is \( 2.5 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \). Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.3 \times 0.2 = 0.06 \, \text{m}^2 \). Shear stress: \( \frac{1.5 \times 10^4}{0.06} = 2.5 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{2.5 \times 10^5}{2.5 \times 10^{10}} = 1 \times 10^{-5} \).

questions.question_text: A steel rod of length 0.8 m and cross-sectional area 2 × 10 -5 m 2 is compressed by a force of 800 N. If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the compression?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = (F L) / (A ΔL). Rearrange: ΔL = (F L) / (A Y). Substitute: ΔL = (800 × 0.8) / (2 × 10 -5 × 2 × 10 11 ) = 640 / (4 × 10 6 ) = 1.6 × 10 -4 m = 0.16 mm.

questions.question_text: A cylindrical rod of length 0.5 m and radius 0.01 m is compressed by a force of 5000 N. If the compressive stress is 5 × 10 6 N/m 2 , what is the cross-sectional area of the rod?
questions.explanation: Stress: Stress = F / A. Rearrange: A = F / Stress. Substitute: A = 5000 / (5 × 10 6 ) = 10 -3 m 2 .

questions.question_text: Why do engineers prefer materials with a large Young’s modulus for designing columns and beams?
questions.explanation: Materials with a large Young’s modulus are stiffer, requiring greater force to produce small deformations, which ensures better resistance to bending and stretching.

questions.question_text: An aluminium wire of length \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 1.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 150 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of aluminium is \( 7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the stress?
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{150}{1.5 \times 10^{-6}} = 1 \times 10^8 \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume 0.005 m 3 is compressed by a pressure of 3 × 10 6 N/m 2 . If the bulk modulus of glass is 3.7 × 10 10 N/m 2 , what is the change in volume?

A steel wire of length \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 350 \, \text{N} \). If the elongation is \( 0.2 \, \text{mm} \), what is the Young's modulus of steel?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = 0.2 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( Y = \frac{350 \times 2.5}{3.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.2 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{875}{7 \times 10^{-10}} \approx 1.25 \times 10^{12} \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 10

questions.question_text: Which type of stress causes a change in the shape of a body without altering its volume?
questions.explanation: Shearing stress causes a change in the shape of a body by producing relative displacement of opposite faces (pure shear) without changing its volume.

questions.question_text: A copper block of dimensions \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \times 0.3 \, \text{m} \times 0.1 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 6 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of copper is \( 4.2 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the displacement of the top face?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{F / A}{\Delta x / L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta x = \frac{F L}{A G} \). Area: \( A = 0.5 \times 0.3 = 0.15 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( L = 0.1 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( \Delta x = \frac{6 \times 10^4 \times 0.1}{0.15 \times 4.2 \times 10^{10}} = \frac{6000}{6.3 \times 10^9} \approx 9.52 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 3.2 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by \( 0.8 \, \text{mm} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( F = \frac{Y A \Delta L}{L} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = 0.8 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( F = \frac{2 \times 10^{11} \times 5 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.8 \times 10^{-3}}{3.2} = \frac{800}{3.2} = 250 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: Why is steel often chosen over materials like copper for heavy-duty structural applications?
questions.explanation: Steel has a higher Young’s modulus (\( \approx 200 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \)) compared to copper (\( \approx 110 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \)), requiring a larger force to produce the same deformation, making it more suitable for resisting bending and stretching.

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.015 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 2 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{2 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -5.41 \times 10^{-5} \). Change in volume: \( \Delta V = \frac{\Delta V}{V} \times V = -5.41 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.015 \approx -8.11 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}^3 \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 2.2 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 1.8 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 180 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain?
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{180}{1.8 \times 10^{-6}} = 1 \times 10^8 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{1 \times 10^8}{1.1 \times 10^{11}} \approx 9.09 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A water sample of volume \( 1.5 \, \text{litres} \) is compressed by a pressure of \( 3 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of water is \( 2.2 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{3 \times 10^6}{2.2 \times 10^9} \approx -1.36 \times 10^{-3} \). Magnitude: \( 1.36 \times 10^{-3} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 3 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by a force of 150 N. If the strain produced is 1 × 10 -3 , what is the Young's modulus of copper?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = Stress / Strain. Stress: Stress = F / A = 150 / (3 × 10 -6 ) = 5 × 10 7 N/m 2 . Strain: 1 × 10 -3 . So, Y = (5 × 10 7 ) / (1 × 10 -3 ) = 5 × 10 10 N/m 2 .

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 3.0 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 200 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{200 \times 3.0}{2 \times 10^{-6} \times 2 \times 10^{11}} = \frac{600}{4 \times 10^5} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 1.5 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.025 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 4 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{4 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -1.08 \times 10^{-4} \). Change in volume: \( \Delta V = \frac{\Delta V}{V} \times V = -1.08 \times 10^{-4} \times 0.025 \approx -2.7 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^3 \).

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 11

questions.question_text: An aluminium wire of length \( 1.7 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by \( 0.34 \, \text{mm} \). If the Young's modulus of aluminium is \( 7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( F = \frac{Y A \Delta L}{L} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = 0.34 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( F = \frac{7 \times 10^{10} \times 2 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.34 \times 10^{-3}}{1.7} = \frac{47.6}{1.7} \approx 28 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.04 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 7 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{7 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -1.89 \times 10^{-4} \). Magnitude: \( 1.89 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: An aluminium wire of length \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 140 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of aluminium is \( 7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{140 \times 1.5}{2 \times 10^{-6} \times 7 \times 10^{10}} = \frac{210}{1.4 \times 10^5} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 1.5 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A steel rod of length 0.6 m and cross-sectional area 5 × 10 -6 m 2 is compressed by a force producing a strain of 3 × 10 -4 . If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = Stress / Strain. Stress: Stress = Y × Strain = 2 × 10 11 × 3 × 10 -4 = 6 × 10 7 N/m 2 . Force: F = Stress × A = 6 × 10 7 × 5 × 10 -6 = 300 N.

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length 1.2 m and cross-sectional area 1.5 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by a force producing a stress of 2 × 10 7 N/m 2 . If the Young's modulus of copper is 1.1 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the strain?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = Stress / Strain. Strain: Strain = Stress / Y = (2 × 10 7 ) / (1.1 × 10 11 ) ≈ 1.82 × 10 -4 .

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 2.0 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 1 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 1.1 \times 10^{11} \times 1 \times 10^{-4} = 1.1 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Force: \( F = \text{Stress} \times A = 1.1 \times 10^7 \times 2 \times 10^{-6} = 22 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A brass wire of length \( 2.0 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 5 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of brass is \( 9 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 9 \times 10^{10} \times 5 \times 10^{-4} = 4.5 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Force: \( F = \text{Stress} \times A = 4.5 \times 10^7 \times 3 \times 10^{-6} = 135 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What characterizes the stress-strain behavior of a material in the region where plastic deformation begins?
options: The material undergoes purely elastic deformation
questions.explanation: When plastic deformation begins, the material experiences permanent deformation, meaning it does not return to its original shape even after the load is removed.

questions.question_text: Which modulus is not applicable for describing the elastic behavior of liquids and gases under shear stress?
questions.explanation: The shear modulus is not applicable for liquids and gases because they do not sustain shear stress and instead flow; only solids have a defined shear modulus.

questions.question_text: In the stress-strain behavior of a ductile material, what happens after the maximum stress the material can endure?
options: The material returns to its original shape
The proportionality between stress and strain holds
The material undergoes elastic deformation only
questions.explanation: After the maximum stress (ultimate tensile strength), a ductile material experiences a decrease in stress with additional strain, leading to eventual fracture.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 12

questions.question_text: Which modulus is not applicable for describing the elastic behavior of liquids and gases under shear stress?
questions.explanation: The shear modulus is not applicable for liquids and gases because they do not sustain shear stress and instead flow; only solids have a defined shear modulus.

questions.question_text: A brass wire of length 3 m and cross-sectional area 2 × 10 -6 m 2 is stretched by a force of 400 N. If the Young's modulus of brass is 9 × 10 10 N/m 2 , what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: Y = (F L) / (A ΔL). Rearrange: ΔL = (F L) / (A Y). Substitute: ΔL = (400 × 3) / (2 × 10 -6 × 9 × 10 10 ) = 1200 / (1.8 × 10 5 ) = 6.67 × 10 -3 m ≈ 6.67 mm.

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 200 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the stress?
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{200}{2 \times 10^{-6}} = 1 \times 10^8 \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A brass wire of length \( 1.9 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 2 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of brass is \( 9 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 9 \times 10^{10} \times 2 \times 10^{-4} = 1.8 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Force: \( F = \text{Stress} \times A = 1.8 \times 10^7 \times 2 \times 10^{-6} = 36 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A steel block of dimensions \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \times 0.3 \, \text{m} \times 0.1 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 5 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of steel is \( 8.4 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \). Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.5 \times 0.3 = 0.15 \, \text{m}^2 \). Shear stress: \( \frac{5 \times 10^4}{0.15} \approx 3.33 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{3.33 \times 10^5}{8.4 \times 10^{10}} \approx 3.96 \times 10^{-6} \).

questions.question_text: A brass wire of length \( 1.7 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 4 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of brass is \( 9 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the stress?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 9 \times 10^{10} \times 4 \times 10^{-4} = 3.6 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A brass plate experiences a shearing force of 4 × 10 4 N across an area of 0.05 m 2 . If the shear strain is 2 × 10 -5 , what is the shear modulus of brass?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: G = (Shear stress) / (Shear strain). Shear stress: Shear stress = F / A = (4 × 10 4 ) / 0.05 = 8 × 10 5 N/m 2 . Shear strain: 2 × 10 -5 . Substitute: G = (8 × 10 5 ) / (2 × 10 -5 ) = 4 × 10 10 N/m 2 .

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 2.8 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by \( 0.7 \, \text{mm} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain?
questions.explanation: Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\Delta L}{L} = \frac{0.7 \times 10^{-3}}{2.8} = 2.5 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: What distinguishes a ductile material from a brittle material in terms of stress-strain behavior?
options: Ductile materials have a larger shear modulus
Ductile materials undergo significant plastic deformation before fracture
Ductile materials break at a lower stress
Ductile materials have a lower bulk modulus
questions.explanation: A ductile material undergoes significant plastic deformation before fracture, allowing it to withstand larger strains, while a brittle material fractures with minimal plastic deformation.

questions.question_text: A brass rod of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 5 × 10 -6 m 2 is compressed by a force of 1000 N. If the Young's modulus of brass is 9 × 10 10 N/m 2 , what is the longitudinal strain?
questions.explanation: Stress: Stress = F / A = 1000 / (5 × 10 -6 ) = 2 × 10 8 N/m 2 . Young's modulus: Y = Stress / Strain. Strain: Strain = Stress / Y = (2 × 10 8 ) / (9 × 10 10 ) ≈ 2.22 × 10 -3 .

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 13

questions.question_text: Why do materials like steel require a significantly larger force to produce small deformations compared to materials like rubber?
questions.explanation: Steel has a much larger Young’s modulus compared to rubber, meaning it has greater stiffness and requires more force to produce the same strain.

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.03 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 5 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{5 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -1.35 \times 10^{-4} \). Change in volume: \( \Delta V = \frac{\Delta V}{V} \times V = -1.35 \times 10^{-4} \times 0.03 \approx -4.05 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^3 \).

questions.question_text: A steel rod of length 1 m and cross-sectional area 1 × 10 -5 m 2 is subjected to a tensile force of 1000 N. If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the strain produced?
questions.explanation: Stress: Stress = F / A = 1000 / (1 × 10 -5 ) = 1 × 10 8 N/m 2 . Young's modulus: Y = Stress / Strain. Strain: Strain = Stress / Y = (1 × 10 8 ) / (2 × 10 11 ) = 5 × 10 -4 .

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 2.0 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by \( 0.4 \, \text{mm} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( F = \frac{Y A \Delta L}{L} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = 0.4 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( F = \frac{2 \times 10^{11} \times 3 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.4 \times 10^{-3}}{2} = \frac{240}{2} = 120 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A glass slab of volume \( 0.02 \, \text{m}^3 \) is subjected to a hydraulic pressure of \( 5 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of glass is \( 3.7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{5 \times 10^6}{3.7 \times 10^{10}} \approx -1.35 \times 10^{-4} \). Magnitude: \( 1.35 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 2.8 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 4 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 1.5 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\Delta L}{L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \text{Strain} \times L = 1.5 \times 10^{-4} \times 2.8 = 4.2 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m} = 0.42 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 3 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 3 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the stress?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 1.1 \times 10^{11} \times 3 \times 10^{-4} = 3.3 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A water sample of volume 2 litres is compressed by a pressure of 2 × 10 6 N/m 2 . If the bulk modulus of water is 2.2 × 10 9 N/m 2 , what is the fractional change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: B = -p / (ΔV / V). Rearrange: ΔV / V = -p / B = -(2 × 10 6 ) / (2.2 × 10 9 ) ≈ -9.09 × 10 -4 . Magnitude: 9.09 × 10 -4 .

questions.question_text: A water sample of volume \( 1.5 \, \text{litres} \) is compressed by a pressure of \( 3 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of water is \( 2.2 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{3 \times 10^6}{2.2 \times 10^9} \approx -1.36 \times 10^{-3} \). Volume: \( V = 1.5 \, \text{litres} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3 \). Change in volume: \( \Delta V = \frac{\Delta V}{V} \times V = -1.36 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \approx -2.04 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^3 \).

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between elastic and plastic deformation in a material?
options: Elastic deformation occurs only in solids
Plastic deformation occurs at lower stress
Elastic deformation is reversible, plastic is not
questions.explanation: Elastic deformation is reversible, meaning the material returns to its original shape after the load is removed, while plastic deformation results in permanent changes.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 14

questions.question_text: A steel wire and a copper wire have the same length and cross-sectional area. Both are stretched by the same force. If Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 and that of copper is 1.1 × 10 11 N/m 2 , what is the ratio of elongation of the steel wire to the copper wire?
questions.explanation: Elongation: ΔL = (F L) / (A Y). Ratio: (ΔL steel )/(ΔL copper ) = Y copper / Y steel = (1.1 × 10 11 ) / (2 × 10 11 ) = 11/20 = 0.55.

questions.question_text: A steel rod of length 1 m and diameter 2 mm is subjected to a tensile force producing a stress of 5 × 10 7 N/m 2 . What is the force applied? (Take π ≈ 3.14)
Which of the following best defines stress in the context of mechanical properties of solids?
options: Change in length per unit area
Change in volume per unit force
questions.explanation: Stress is defined as the restoring force per unit area developed in a body due to an external deforming force, given by \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} \).

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 2.0 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 250 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the strain produced?
questions.explanation: Stress: \( \text{Stress} = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{250}{2.5 \times 10^{-6}} = 1 \times 10^8 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Strain: \( \text{Strain} = \frac{\text{Stress}}{Y} = \frac{1 \times 10^8}{2 \times 10^{11}} = 5 \times 10^{-4} \).

questions.question_text: A copper wire of length \( 2.8 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force of \( 160 \, \text{N} \). If the Young's modulus of copper is \( 1.1 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the elongation?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = \frac{160 \times 2.8}{2 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.1 \times 10^{11}} = \frac{448}{2.2 \times 10^5} \approx 2.04 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 2.04 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: In designing bridges, why is it critical to understand the elastic properties of materials?
options: To increase the weight of the bridge
To reduce the cost of materials
questions.explanation: Understanding elastic properties ensures that materials can withstand various loads (traffic, wind, weight) without undergoing permanent deformation, maintaining structural integrity.

questions.question_text: A brass block of dimensions \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \times 0.1 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 5 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of brass is \( 3.6 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \). Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.5 \times 0.2 = 0.1 \, \text{m}^2 \). Shear stress: \( \frac{5 \times 10^4}{0.1} = 5 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{5 \times 10^5}{3.6 \times 10^{10}} \approx 1.39 \times 10^{-5} \).

questions.question_text: What characterizes the stress-strain behavior of a material in the region where plastic deformation begins?
options: The material undergoes purely elastic deformation
questions.explanation: When plastic deformation begins, the material experiences permanent deformation, meaning it does not return to its original shape even after the load is removed.

questions.question_text: A steel wire of length \( 2.6 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by \( 0.52 \, \text{mm} \). If the Young's modulus of steel is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L} \). Rearrange: \( F = \frac{Y A \Delta L}{L} \). Substitute: \( \Delta L = 0.52 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). \( F = \frac{2 \times 10^{11} \times 2 \times 10^{-6} \times 0.52 \times 10^{-3}}{2.6} = \frac{208}{2.6} = 80 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: What does the steepness of the initial linear portion of a stress-strain curve indicate?
questions.explanation: The steepness of the initial linear portion indicates a higher Young’s modulus, meaning the material is stiffer and requires more stress to produce a given strain.

tests.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids Chapter-Wise Test 15

questions.question_text: A rectangular block of aluminium with dimensions 0.5 m × 0.2 m × 0.1 m is subjected to a shearing force of 6 × 10 4 N. If the shear modulus of aluminium is 2.5 × 10 10 N/m 2 , what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: G = (Shear stress) / (Shear strain). Shear stress: Shear stress = F / A, A = 0.5 × 0.2 = 0.1 m 2 . So, Shear stress = (6 × 10 4 ) / 0.1 = 6 × 10 5 N/m 2 . Shear strain: Shear strain = Shear stress / G = (6 × 10 5 ) / (2.5 × 10 10 ) = 2.4 × 10 -5 .

questions.question_text: In the stress-strain behavior of a ductile material, what happens after the maximum stress the material can endure?
options: The material returns to its original shape
The proportionality between stress and strain holds
The material undergoes elastic deformation only
questions.explanation: After the maximum stress (ultimate tensile strength), a ductile material experiences a decrease in stress with additional strain, leading to eventual fracture.

questions.question_text: In the stress-strain behavior of a material, what occurs after the maximum stress point when the material is ductile?
options: The material returns to its original shape
The stress decreases leading to fracture
questions.explanation: For a ductile material, after the maximum stress point (ultimate tensile strength), the stress decreases with increasing strain as the material necks, leading to fracture.

questions.question_text: An aluminium wire of length \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) and cross-sectional area \( 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^2 \) is stretched by a force producing a strain of \( 2 \times 10^{-4} \). If the Young's modulus of aluminium is \( 7 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the force applied?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus: \( Y = \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} \). Stress: \( \text{Stress} = Y \times \text{Strain} = 7 \times 10^{10} \times 2 \times 10^{-4} = 1.4 \times 10^7 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Force: \( F = \text{Stress} \times A = 1.4 \times 10^7 \times 2 \times 10^{-6} = 28 \, \text{N} \).

questions.question_text: A brass block of dimensions \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \times 0.2 \, \text{m} \times 0.05 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 2 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of brass is \( 3.6 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{\text{Shear strain}} \). Shear stress: \( \text{Shear stress} = \frac{F}{A} \), \( A = 0.5 \times 0.2 = 0.1 \, \text{m}^2 \). Shear stress: \( \frac{2 \times 10^4}{0.1} = 2 \times 10^5 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). Shear strain: \( \text{Shear strain} = \frac{\text{Shear stress}}{G} = \frac{2 \times 10^5}{3.6 \times 10^{10}} \approx 5.56 \times 10^{-6} \).

questions.question_text: A water sample of volume \( 3 \, \text{litres} \) is compressed by a pressure of \( 4 \times 10^6 \, \text{N/m}^2 \). If the bulk modulus of water is \( 2.2 \times 10^9 \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the change in volume?
questions.explanation: Bulk modulus: \( B = -\frac{p}{\frac{\Delta V}{V}} \). Rearrange: \( \frac{\Delta V}{V} = -\frac{p}{B} = -\frac{4 \times 10^6}{2.2 \times 10^9} \approx -1.82 \times 10^{-3} \). Volume: \( V = 3 \, \text{litres} = 3 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m}^3 \). Change in volume: \( \Delta V = \frac{\Delta V}{V} \times V = -1.82 \times 10^{-3} \times 3 \times 10^{-3} \approx -5.45 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}^3 \).

questions.question_text: A steel block of dimensions 0.2 m × 0.1 m × 0.05 m is subjected to a shearing force of 1 × 10 4 N. If the shear modulus of steel is 8.4 × 10 10 N/m 2 , what is the shear strain?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: G = (Shear stress) / (Shear strain). Shear stress: Shear stress = F / A, A = 0.2 × 0.1 = 0.02 m 2 . Shear stress = (1 × 10 4 ) / 0.02 = 5 × 10 5 N/m 2 . Shear strain: Shear strain = Shear stress / G = (5 × 10 5 ) / (8.4 × 10 10 ) ≈ 5.95 × 10 -6 .

questions.question_text: What distinguishes a ductile material from a brittle material in terms of stress-strain behavior?
options: Ductile materials have a larger shear modulus
Ductile materials undergo significant plastic deformation before fracture
Ductile materials break at a lower stress
Ductile materials have a lower bulk modulus
questions.explanation: A ductile material undergoes significant plastic deformation before fracture, allowing it to withstand larger strains, while a brittle material fractures with minimal plastic deformation.

questions.question_text: Which type of stress causes a change in the shape of a body without altering its volume?
questions.explanation: Shearing stress causes a change in the shape of a body by producing relative displacement of opposite faces (pure shear) without changing its volume.

questions.question_text: A brass block of dimensions \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \times 0.3 \, \text{m} \times 0.1 \, \text{m} \) is subjected to a shearing force of \( 3 \times 10^4 \, \text{N} \). If the shear modulus of brass is \( 3.6 \times 10^{10} \, \text{N/m}^2 \), what is the displacement of the top face?
questions.explanation: Shear modulus: \( G = \frac{F / A}{\Delta x / L} \). Rearrange: \( \Delta x = \frac{F L}{A G} \). Area: \( A = 0.4 \times 0.3 = 0.12 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( L = 0.1 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( \Delta x = \frac{3 \times 10^4 \times 0.1}{0.12 \times 3.6 \times 10^{10}} = \frac{3000}{4.32 \times 10^9} \approx 6.94 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A bike moving at \( 126 \, \text{km/h} \) decelerates uniformly and stops in \( 7 \, \text{s} \). What is the magnitude of deceleration?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 126 \, \text{km/h} = 126 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 35 \, \text{m/s} \). Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 35 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 7 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( a = \frac{0 - 35}{7} = -5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A vehicle accelerates uniformly from rest at \( 1.2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 10 \, \text{s} \). What is the final velocity?
questions.explanation: Use the equation \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, initial velocity \( v_0 = 0 \), acceleration \( a = 1.2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), time \( t = 10 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 1.2 \cdot 10 = 12 \, \text{m/s} \). The final velocity is \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A train moving at \( 54 \, \text{km/h} \) accelerates at \( 1 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 10 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to rest. What is the total distance covered?
A person walks \( 6 \, \text{m} \) in \( 3 \, \text{s} \) and then walks back \( 2 \, \text{m} \) in \( 1 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time. Total distance = \( 6 \, \text{m} + 2 \, \text{m} = 8 \, \text{m} \), total time = \( 3 \, \text{s} + 1 \, \text{s} = 4 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{8}{4} = 2 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 90 \, \text{km/h} \) decelerates uniformly and stops in \( 12 \, \text{s} \). What is the magnitude of deceleration?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 90 \, \text{km/h} = 90 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 25 \, \text{m/s} \). Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 25 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 12 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( a = \frac{0 - 25}{12} = -2.083 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is approximately \( 2.08 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 28 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 98 \, \text{m} \). What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 28 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 98 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (28)^2 = 0 + 2 a (98) \Rightarrow 784 = 196 a \Rightarrow a = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A train moving at \( 108 \, \text{km/h} \) accelerates at \( 1.2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 10 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to rest. What is the total distance covered?
A truck moves with a constant speed of \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 40 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: For constant speed, distance \( x = v t \). Here, \( v = 15 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 40 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 15 \cdot 40 = 600 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 600 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its velocity after \( 3 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 3 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 20 - 10 \cdot 3 = 20 - 30 = -10 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( -10 \, \text{m/s} \) (downward).

questions.question_text: A rocket accelerates from rest at \( 7 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A train accelerates uniformly from \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 35 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 8 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{35 - 15}{8} = 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 15 \cdot 8 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2.5 \cdot (8)^2 = 120 + 80 = 200 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 200 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls freely from a height of \( 45 \, \text{m} \). How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For free fall, use \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). Here, \( y = 45 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 45 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow 45 = 5 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 9 \Rightarrow t = 3 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 3 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from rest. What is its velocity after falling \( 61.25 \, \text{m} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 61.25 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 61.25 = 1225 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{1225} = 35 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 35 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest in \( 8 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{0 - 40}{8} = -5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 40 \cdot 8 + \frac{1}{2} (-5) (8)^2 = 320 - 160 = 160 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 160 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from rest. What is the distance covered in the 6th second of its fall? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Distance in \( n \)-th second = \( g \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \). For 6th second, \( n = 6 \). Substitute: \( d = 10 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 6 - 1}{2} = 10 \cdot \frac{11}{2} = 55 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 55 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A lift ascends at \( 4 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to stop. If a ball is dropped \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \) after deceleration starts, how far does it fall relative to the ground in \( 1 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Lift stops in \( \frac{4}{2} = 2 \, \text{s} \). At \( t = 1.5 \, \text{s} \): \( v_{\text{lift}} = 4 - 2 \cdot 1.5 = 1 \, \text{m/s} \), \( y_{\text{lift}} = 4 \cdot 1.5 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (1.5)^2 = 6 - 2.25 = 3.75 \, \text{m} \). Ball: \( y_{\text{ball}} = 1 \cdot 1 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (1)^2 = 1 + 5 = 6 \, \text{m} \) from drop point. Lift at \( t = 2.5 \, \text{s} \): \( y = 4 \cdot 2 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (2)^2 = 8 - 4 = 4 \, \text{m} \), then constant. Ball’s position = \( 3.75 + 6 = 9.75 \, \text{m} \), distance = \( 9.75 - 4 = 5.75 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 14 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 49 \, \text{m} \). What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 14 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 49 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (14)^2 = 0 + 2 a (49) \Rightarrow 196 = 98 a \Rightarrow a = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 8 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{16 - 0}{8} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 0 \cdot 8 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (8)^2 = 0 + 1 \cdot 64 = 64 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 64 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 45 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the time to reach the maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At max height, \( v = 0 \). Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 45 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = 45 - 10 t \Rightarrow 10 t = 45 \Rightarrow t = 4.5 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 4.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from a height of \( 31.25 \, \text{m} \). What is its velocity just before hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 31.25 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 31.25 = 625 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{625} = 25 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 22 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its velocity after \( 1 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 22 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 22 - 10 \cdot 1 = 12 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A balloon descends at \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) and releases a stone. If the stone hits the ground after \( 5 \, \text{s} \), what was the height of the balloon? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Initial velocity = \( -8 \, \text{m/s} \) (upward positive). \( y = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), \( y = -8 \cdot 5 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (5)^2 = -40 + 125 = 85 \, \text{m} \). Height = \( 85 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from a balloon ascending at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \). If it hits the ground after \( 6 \, \text{s} \), what was the height of the balloon at the moment of release? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Initial velocity of stone = \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) upward. \( y = v_0 t - \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). Ground level \( y = -h \): \( -h = 12 \cdot 6 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (6)^2 = 72 - 180 = -108 \). Height \( h = 108 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 55 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the time to reach the maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At max height, \( v = 0 \). Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 55 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = 55 - 10 t \Rightarrow 10 t = 55 \Rightarrow t = 5.5 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 5.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A lift descends at \( 3 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to stop. If a ball is dropped \( 1 \, \text{s} \) after deceleration begins, how far does it fall relative to the ground in \( 2 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At drop: \( v_{\text{lift}} = 3 - 2 \cdot 1 = 1 \, \text{m/s} \) downward. Ball: \( y_{\text{ball}} = 1 \cdot 2 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (2)^2 = 2 + 20 = 22 \, \text{m} \). Lift stops in \( \frac{3}{2} = 1.5 \, \text{s} \), distance = \( 3 \cdot 1.5 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (1.5)^2 = 4.5 - 2.25 = 2.25 \, \text{m} \), then stationary. After 2 s, lift at \( 2.25 \, \text{m} \), ball at \( 22 \, \text{m} \), distance = \( 22 - 2.25 = 19.75 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from a height of \( 100 \, \text{m} \) on a planet where \( g = 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is the ratio of the distance covered in the 2nd second to the 1st second?
questions.explanation: Distance in \( n \)-th second: \( d_n = g \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \). 1st second: \( d_1 = 5 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 1 - 1}{2} = 2.5 \, \text{m} \). 2nd second: \( d_2 = 5 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 2 - 1}{2} = 7.5 \, \text{m} \). Ratio: \( \frac{d_2}{d_1} = \frac{7.5}{2.5} = 3 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from a tower. After \( 2 \, \text{s} \), its velocity is \( 19.6 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the acceleration due to gravity?
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 19.6 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( 19.6 = 0 + a \cdot 2 \Rightarrow a = \frac{19.6}{2} = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{15 - 5}{5} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 5 \cdot 5 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (5)^2 = 25 + 25 = 50 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 50 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from rest. What is the distance covered in the 4th second of its fall? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Distance in \( n \)-th second = \( g \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \). For 4th second, \( n = 4 \). Substitute: \( d = 10 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 4 - 1}{2} = 10 \cdot \frac{7}{2} = 35 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 35 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A balloon ascends at \( 7 \, \text{m/s} \) and releases a stone after \( 4 \, \text{s} \). If the stone hits the ground \( 5 \, \text{s} \) later, what was the initial height of the balloon? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Height at release: \( h_1 = 7 \cdot 4 = 28 \, \text{m} \). Stone: \( h_{\text{total}} = h_0 + 28 \), \( -h_{\text{total}} = 7 \cdot 5 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (5)^2 = 35 - 125 = -90 \). \( h_{\text{total}} = 90 \, \text{m} \), \( h_0 = 90 - 28 = 62 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A train accelerates from rest at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 10 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 1 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to rest. What is the total distance covered?
A car accelerates uniformly from \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 80 \, \text{m} \). What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v = 30 \, \text{m/s} \), \( v_0 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 80 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (30)^2 = (10)^2 + 2 a (80) \Rightarrow 900 = 100 + 160 a \Rightarrow 160 a = 800 \Rightarrow a = 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates from rest at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 6 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed is \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A body moving with an initial velocity of \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) comes to rest after traveling \( 40 \, \text{m} \) under uniform retardation. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 40 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( 0 = (20)^2 + 2 a (40) \Rightarrow 0 = 400 + 80 a \Rightarrow 80 a = -400 \Rightarrow a = -5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of acceleration is \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 36 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the maximum height reached? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a h \). At max height, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 36 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = (36)^2 + 2 (-10) h \Rightarrow 0 = 1296 - 20 h \Rightarrow h = \frac{1296}{20} = 64.8 \, \text{m} \). The maximum height is \( 64.8 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist accelerates from \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed is \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A person walks \( 10 \, \text{m} \) in \( 4 \, \text{s} \) and then walks back \( 2 \, \text{m} \) in \( 1 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time. Total distance = \( 10 \, \text{m} + 2 \, \text{m} = 12 \, \text{m} \), total time = \( 4 \, \text{s} + 1 \, \text{s} = 5 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{12}{5} = 2.4 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A train accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 25 \, \text{m} \). What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 10 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 25 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (10)^2 = 0 + 2 a (25) \Rightarrow 100 = 50 a \Rightarrow a = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: An object falls freely from rest. What is its velocity after traveling \( 4.9 \, \text{m} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 4.9 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 9.8 \cdot 4.9 = 96.04 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{96.04} \approx 9.8 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 9.8 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Two balls are dropped from a height of \( 180 \, \text{m} \), with a \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \) interval. What is their separation when the first ball hits the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: First ball: \( 180 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 36 \Rightarrow t = 6 \, \text{s} \). Second ball (after 4.5 s): \( y_2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (4.5)^2 = 101.25 \, \text{m} \). Separation = \( 180 - 101.25 = 78.75 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls from a height of \( 80 \, \text{m} \) on a planet and takes \( 4 \, \text{s} \) to reach the ground. What is the gravitational acceleration on this planet?
questions.explanation: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), \( 80 = \frac{1}{2} g (4)^2 \Rightarrow 80 = 8 g \Rightarrow g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \) from a cliff. It returns to the cliff’s height after \( 12 \, \text{s} \). What is the height of the cliff? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to max height: \( t = \frac{50}{10} = 5 \, \text{s} \). Max height: \( h_{\text{max}} = 50 \cdot 5 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (5)^2 = 250 - 125 = 125 \, \text{m} \). Time down to cliff = \( 12 - 5 = 7 \, \text{s} \). Distance fallen: \( h = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (7)^2 = 245 \, \text{m} \). Cliff height = \( 245 - 125 = 120 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist moves at a constant speed of \( 15 \, \text{km/h} \) for \( 12 \, \text{minutes} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 15 \, \text{km/h} = 15 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = \frac{25}{6} \, \text{m/s} \). Time = \( 12 \, \text{min} = 12 \cdot 60 = 720 \, \text{s} \). Distance \( x = v t = \frac{25}{6} \cdot 720 = 3000 \, \text{m} = 3 \, \text{km} \). The distance covered is \( 3 \, \text{km} \).

questions.question_text: A balloon descends at \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) from \( 150 \, \text{m} \) and releases a stone after \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is the time taken by the stone to hit the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Height at release: \( h = 150 - 5 \cdot 3 = 135 \, \text{m} \). Stone’s initial velocity = \( -5 \, \text{m/s} \). \( -135 = -5 t + 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 5 t - 135 = 0 \Rightarrow t^2 - t - 27 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 108}}{2} = \frac{1 \pm 10.44}{2} \), \( t = 5.72 \, \text{s} \) (positive root).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from a height of \( 125 \, \text{m} \). What is its velocity just before hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 125 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 125 = 2500 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{2500} = 50 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 32 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the maximum height reached? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a h \). At max height, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 32 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = (32)^2 + 2 (-10) h \Rightarrow 0 = 1024 - 20 h \Rightarrow h = \frac{1024}{20} = 51.2 \, \text{m} \). The maximum height is \( 51.2 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the maximum height reached? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a h \). At max height, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 16 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = (16)^2 + 2 (-10) h \Rightarrow 0 = 256 - 20 h \Rightarrow h = \frac{256}{20} = 12.8 \, \text{m} \). The maximum height is \( 12.8 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A runner moves at a constant speed of \( 4 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 75 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: For constant speed, distance \( x = v t \). Here, \( v = 4 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 75 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 4 \cdot 75 = 300 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 300 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A truck traveling at \( 36 \, \text{km/h} \) stops in \( 5 \, \text{s} \) with uniform deceleration. What is the distance covered before stopping?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 36 \, \text{km/h} = 36 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 10 \, \text{m/s} \). Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{0 - 10}{5} = -2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 10 \cdot 5 + \frac{1}{2} (-2) (5)^2 = 50 - 25 = 25 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 25 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from a height of \( 20 \, \text{m} \). What is its velocity just before hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 20 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 20 = 400 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{400} = 20 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A car decelerates uniformly from \( 45 \, \text{m/s} \) to rest over a distance of \( 112.5 \, \text{m} \). What is the deceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 45 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 112.5 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( 0 = (45)^2 + 2 a (112.5) \Rightarrow 0 = 2026 + 225 a \Rightarrow a = -9 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 9 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 60 \, \text{m} \) cliff. What is its speed when it hits the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A truck travels at a constant speed of \( 60 \, \text{km/h} \) for \( 15 \, \text{minutes} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 60 \, \text{km/h} = 60 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = \frac{50}{3} \, \text{m/s} \). Time = \( 15 \, \text{min} = 15 \cdot 60 = 900 \, \text{s} \). Distance \( x = v t = \frac{50}{3} \cdot 900 = 15000 \, \text{m} = 15 \, \text{km} \). The distance covered is \( 15 \, \text{km} \).

questions.question_text: A car decelerates uniformly from \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) to rest in \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{0 - 18}{6} = -3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Distance \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 18 \cdot 6 + \frac{1}{2} (-3) (6)^2 = 108 - 54 = 54 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 54 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car moves at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 1 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until it reaches \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) again. What is the total distance covered?
A cyclist moves at a constant speed of \( 7 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 60 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: For constant speed, distance \( x = v t \). Here, \( v = 7 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 60 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 7 \cdot 60 = 420 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 420 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest in \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{0 - 30}{6} = -5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 30 \cdot 6 + \frac{1}{2} (-5) (6)^2 = 180 - 90 = 90 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 90 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls from a height \( h \) and covers \( 78.4 \, \text{m} \) in the last \( 2 \, \text{s} \) of its fall. What is the total time of fall? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Total time = \( t \), last 2 s: \( h = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot t^2 \), \( h - 78.4 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot (t - 2)^2 \). Distance in last 2 s: \( 78.4 = 4.9 [t^2 - (t - 2)^2] \Rightarrow 16 = t^2 - (t^2 - 4t + 4) \Rightarrow 16 = 4t - 4 \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 42 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the time to reach the maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At max height, \( v = 0 \). Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 42 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = 42 - 10 t \Rightarrow 10 t = 42 \Rightarrow t = 4.2 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 4.2 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 60 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the time to reach the maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At max height, \( v = 0 \). Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 60 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = 60 - 10 t \Rightarrow 10 t = 60 \Rightarrow t = 6 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 6 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 45 \, \text{m} \) tower. What is its speed when it passes \( 15 \, \text{m} \) below the tower’s top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 52 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the time to reach the maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At max height, \( v = 0 \). Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 52 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = 52 - 10 t \Rightarrow 10 t = 52 \Rightarrow t = 5.2 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 5.2 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 72 \, \text{km/h} \) decelerates uniformly and stops in \( 8 \, \text{s} \). What is the magnitude of deceleration?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 72 \, \text{km/h} = 72 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 20 \, \text{m/s} \). Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 8 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( a = \frac{0 - 20}{8} = -2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist moves at a constant speed of \( 9 \, \text{km/h} \) for \( 20 \, \text{minutes} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 9 \, \text{km/h} = 9 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 2.5 \, \text{m/s} \). Time = \( 20 \, \text{min} = 20 \cdot 60 = 1200 \, \text{s} \). Distance \( x = v t = 2.5 \cdot 1200 = 3000 \, \text{m} = 3 \, \text{km} \). The distance covered is \( 3 \, \text{km} \).

questions.question_text: A truck moves at a constant speed of \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 20 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: For constant speed, distance \( x = v t \). Here, \( v = 25 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 20 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 25 \cdot 20 = 500 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 500 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: Two stones are dropped from a height of \( 245 \, \text{m} \), with a \( 3 \, \text{s} \) interval. What is their separation when the second stone has fallen for \( 4 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: First stone (after 7 s): \( y_1 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (7)^2 = 245 \, \text{m} \) (hits ground). Second stone (after 4 s): \( y_2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (4)^2 = 80 \, \text{m} \). Separation = \( 245 - 80 = 165 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 32 \, \text{m} \) tower. What is its speed when it passes the tower’s base on the way down? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A particle moves with a uniform acceleration of \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) starting from rest. What is its velocity after traveling \( 18 \, \text{m} \)?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( a = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( x = 18 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 18 = 72 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2} \approx 8.48 \, \text{m/s} \). Approximate value is \( 8.5 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: An object is dropped from a height of \( 19.6 \, \text{m} \) above the ground. How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For free fall, use \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). Here, \( y = 19.6 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 19.6 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow 19.6 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 4 \Rightarrow t = 2 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 2 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the maximum height it reaches? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a h \). At max height, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 40 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = (40)^2 + 2 (-10) h \Rightarrow 0 = 1600 - 20 h \Rightarrow h = \frac{1600}{20} = 80 \, \text{m} \). The maximum height is \( 80 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 9 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{18 - 0}{9} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 0 \cdot 9 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (9)^2 = 0 + 1 \cdot 81 = 81 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 81 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the maximum height reached? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a h \). At max height, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 12 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = (12)^2 + 2 (-10) h \Rightarrow 0 = 144 - 20 h \Rightarrow h = \frac{144}{20} = 7.2 \, \text{m} \). The maximum height is \( 7.2 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from a cliff and takes \( 5 \, \text{s} \) to hit the ground. What is the height of the cliff? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For free fall, distance is given by \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). Here, \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 5 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( y = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (5)^2 = 5 \cdot 25 = 125 \, \text{m} \). The height of the cliff is \( 125 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls freely from a height and reaches the ground with a velocity of \( 19.6 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the height? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 19.6 \, \text{m/s} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( (19.6)^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 9.8 \cdot y \Rightarrow 384.16 = 19.6 y \Rightarrow y = 19.6 \, \text{m} \). The height is \( 19.6 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car moves at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the net displacement?
A ball is dropped from a height \( h \) and hits the ground with a speed of \( 29.4 \, \text{m/s} \) after \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \) of fall. What is the value of \( g \) at that location?
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + g t \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 29.4 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 1.5 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( 29.4 = 0 + g \cdot 1.5 \Rightarrow g = \frac{29.4}{1.5} = 19.6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The value of \( g \) is \( 19.6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A bike moving at \( 108 \, \text{km/h} \) comes to rest in \( 9 \, \text{s} \) with uniform deceleration. What is the magnitude of deceleration?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 108 \, \text{km/h} = 108 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 30 \, \text{m/s} \). Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 30 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 9 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( a = \frac{0 - 30}{9} = -3.33 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is approximately \( 3.33 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A car moves at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \). What is the net displacement?

A rocket accelerates uniformly from rest at \( 8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until it reaches a speed of \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \), then maintains that speed for \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the total distance covered?
questions.explanation: Phase 1 (acceleration): \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 40 = 0 + 8 t \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \). Distance: \( x_1 = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 0 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 8 \cdot (5)^2 = 100 \, \text{m} \). Phase 2 (constant speed): \( x_2 = v t = 40 \cdot 5 = 200 \, \text{m} \). Total distance = \( x_1 + x_2 = 100 + 200 = 300 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist accelerates from \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed is \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?

A car accelerates from \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed over the entire motion?

A particle moves at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed halves, then accelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to its original speed. What is the total time taken?
questions.explanation: Phase 1: \( 9 = 18 - 3 t \Rightarrow t_1 = 3 \, \text{s} \). Phase 2: \( 18 = 9 + 2 t \Rightarrow t_2 = 4.5 \, \text{s} \). Total time = \( 3 + 4.5 = 7.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist moves with a constant speed of \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 20 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: For constant speed, distance \( x = v t \). Here, \( v = 5 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 20 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 5 \cdot 20 = 100 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 100 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car traveling at \( 54 \, \text{km/h} \) comes to rest in \( 10 \, \text{s} \) with uniform deceleration. What is the magnitude of the deceleration?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 54 \, \text{km/h} = 54 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 15 \, \text{m/s} \). Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 15 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 10 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( a = \frac{0 - 15}{10} = -1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls from a height and covers \( 58.8 \, \text{m} \) in the last \( 1.2 \, \text{s} \) of its fall. What is the total height? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A train moving at \( 72 \, \text{km/h} \) passes a pole in \( 9 \, \text{s} \). If it decelerates uniformly to rest in \( 30 \, \text{s} \) after passing the pole, what is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: Speed: \( 72 \, \text{km/h} = 20 \, \text{m/s} \). Length = distance to pass pole = \( 20 \cdot 9 = 180 \, \text{m} \). Check: Deceleration \( a = \frac{0 - 20}{30} = -\frac{2}{3} \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Distance to stop = \( 20 \cdot 30 + \frac{1}{2} (-\frac{2}{3}) (30)^2 = 600 - 300 = 300 \, \text{m} \). Length = \( 180 \, \text{m} \) (initial pass distance).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from a height of \( 45 \, \text{m} \) on a planet where it takes \( 3 \, \text{s} \) to reach the ground. What is the acceleration due to gravity on this planet?
questions.explanation: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), \( 45 = \frac{1}{2} g (3)^2 \Rightarrow 45 = 4.5 g \Rightarrow g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A bike accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 40 \, \text{m} \). What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 20 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 40 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (20)^2 = 0 + 2 a (40) \Rightarrow 400 = 80 a \Rightarrow a = 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls freely from rest and reaches a velocity of \( 14.7 \, \text{m/s} \). How long did it fall? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + g t \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 14.7 \, \text{m/s} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 14.7 = 0 + 9.8 t \Rightarrow t = \frac{14.7}{9.8} = 1.5 \, \text{s} \). The time of fall is \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: Two stones are dropped from a height of \( 125 \, \text{m} \), with a \( 2 \, \text{s} \) interval between them. How far apart are they when the second stone has fallen for \( 3 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Stone 1 (after 5 s): \( y_1 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (5)^2 = 125 \, \text{m} \) (hits ground). Stone 2 (after 3 s): \( y_2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (3)^2 = 45 \, \text{m} \). Distance apart = \( 125 - 45 = 80 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 38 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its velocity after \( 3 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 38 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 3 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 38 - 10 \cdot 3 = 38 - 30 = 8 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A rocket ascends with an acceleration of \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 6 \, \text{s} \), then its engines shut off. How long does it take to reach its maximum height from the start? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: After 6 s: \( v = 4 \cdot 6 = 24 \, \text{m/s} \). Deceleration phase: \( v = 24 - 10 t \), \( 0 = 24 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 2.4 \, \text{s} \). Total time = \( 6 + 2.4 = 8.4 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: Two stones are dropped from a height of \( 80 \, \text{m} \), \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \) apart. How long after the second stone is released do they meet if the first rebounds at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) upon hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: First stone: \( 80 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow t = 4 \, \text{s} \). Second stone released at \( t = 2.5 \, \text{s} \), meets after \( t' \) s. First stone after rebound: \( y_1 = 15 (t' + 1.5) \), second stone: \( y_2 = 5 t'^2 \). \( 80 - y_1 = y_2 \Rightarrow 80 - 15 (t' + 1.5) = 5 t'^2 \Rightarrow 80 - 15 t' - 22.5 = 5 t'^2 \Rightarrow 5 t'^2 + 15 t' - 57.5 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{-15 \pm \sqrt{225 + 1150}}{10} = \frac{-15 \pm 37.08}{10} \), \( t = 2.21 \, \text{s} \) (positive root).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown upwards at \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 55 \, \text{m} \) tower. How far below the tower’s top is it after \( 7 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Displacement: \( y = 30 \cdot 7 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (7)^2 = 210 - 245 = -35 \, \text{m} \). Distance below top = \( 35 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from rest. What is the distance covered in the 3rd second of its fall? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Distance in \( n \)-th second = \( g \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \). For 3rd second, \( n = 3 \). Substitute: \( d = 10 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 3 - 1}{2} = 10 \cdot \frac{5}{2} = 25 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 25 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A runner moves at a constant speed of \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 25 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered by the runner?
questions.explanation: For constant speed, distance \( x = v t \). Here, \( v = 8 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 25 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 8 \cdot 25 = 200 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 200 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest over \( 62.5 \, \text{m} \). What is the time taken to stop?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \) to find \( a \): \( 0 = (25)^2 + 2 a (62.5) \Rightarrow 0 = 625 + 125 a \Rightarrow a = -5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Then, \( v = v_0 + a t \): \( 0 = 25 - 5 t \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed is \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A body starts from rest and accelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \). What is its final velocity?
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( a = 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 4 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 3 \cdot 4 = 12 \, \text{m/s} \). The final velocity is \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its velocity after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 18 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 18 - 10 \cdot 2 = 18 - 20 = -2 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( -2 \, \text{m/s} \) (downward).

questions.question_text: A train accelerates uniformly from \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} \). Here, \( v = 30 \, \text{m/s} \), \( v_0 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 5 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( a = \frac{30 - 10}{5} = \frac{20}{5} = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown upwards from a \( 60 \, \text{m} \) cliff at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the time taken to reach a point \( 20 \, \text{m} \) below the cliff’s edge? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Displacement \( y = -80 \, \text{m} \) (downward positive). Use \( y = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), \( v_0 = -20 \, \text{m/s} \). \( 80 = -20 t + 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 20 t - 80 = 0 \Rightarrow t^2 - 4 t - 16 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 + 64}}{2} = \frac{4 \pm 8.94}{2} \), \( t = 6.47 \, \text{s} \) (positive root).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from a height of \( 44.1 \, \text{m} \). What is its velocity just before hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 44.1 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 9.8 \cdot 44.1 = 864.36 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{864.36} \approx 29.4 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 29.4 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from a height \( h \) and falls \( 44.1 \, \text{m} \) in the last \( 1 \, \text{s} \) before hitting the ground. What is the height \( h \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
