questions.explanation: Distance in last second: \( d_n = g \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \), \( 44.1 = 9.8 \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \Rightarrow 2n - 1 = 9 \Rightarrow n = 5 \, \text{s} \). Total height: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot (5)^2 = 122.5 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 7 \, \text{s} \). What is the final velocity?
questions.explanation: Use the equation \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, initial velocity \( v_0 = 0 \), acceleration \( a = 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), time \( t = 7 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 3 \cdot 7 = 21 \, \text{m/s} \). The final velocity is \( 21 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A rocket accelerates vertically at \( 6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) from rest for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then its engines fail. What is the maximum height reached above the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A helicopter ascends vertically at \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) and releases a package after \( 10 \, \text{s} \). How long after release does the package hit the ground if it was initially \( 50 \, \text{m} \) above the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Height at release: \( h = 50 + 6 \cdot 10 = 110 \, \text{m} \). Initial velocity of package = \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) upward. Use \( y = v_0 t - \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), ground level \( y = -110 \). \( -110 = 6 t - 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 6 t - 110 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 + 2200}}{10} = \frac{6 \pm 47.6}{10} \), \( t = 5.36 \, \text{s} \) (positive root). Time = \( 5.36 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A car moves at \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 3.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \). What is the net displacement?
A rocket accelerates from rest at \( 6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A bus moves at a constant speed of \( 36 \, \text{km/h} \) for \( 30 \, \text{minutes} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 36 \, \text{km/h} = 36 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 10 \, \text{m/s} \). Time = \( 30 \, \text{min} = 30 \cdot 60 = 1800 \, \text{s} \). Distance \( x = v t = 10 \cdot 1800 = 18000 \, \text{m} = 18 \, \text{km} \). The distance covered is \( 18 \, \text{km} \).

questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( a = 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 6 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 0 \cdot 6 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot (6)^2 = 0 + 1.5 \cdot 36 = 54 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 54 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 40 \, \text{m} \) tower. What is the time taken to reach a point \( 10 \, \text{m} \) above the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Displacement \( y = -30 \, \text{m} \), \( -30 = 30 t - 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 30 t - 30 = 0 \Rightarrow t^2 - 6 t - 6 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 + 24}}{2} = \frac{6 \pm 7.75}{2} \), \( t = 6.875 \, \text{s} \) (downward path).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial speed of \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the time taken to reach its maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At maximum height, final velocity \( v = 0 \). Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 15 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -g = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( v = 0 \). Substitute: \( 0 = 15 - 10 t \Rightarrow 10 t = 15 \Rightarrow t = 1.5 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 4 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{12 - 0}{4} = 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 0 \cdot 4 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot (4)^2 = 0 + 1.5 \cdot 16 = 24 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 24 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 24 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 72 \, \text{m} \). What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 24 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 72 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (24)^2 = 0 + 2 a (72) \Rightarrow 576 = 144 a \Rightarrow a = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed is \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \), then accelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total time taken?
questions.explanation: Phase 1: \( 8 = 20 - 4 t \Rightarrow t_1 = 3 \, \text{s} \). Phase 2: \( 20 = 8 + 3 t \Rightarrow t_2 = 4 \, \text{s} \). Total = \( 3 + 4 = 7 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 10 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered by the car during this time?
questions.explanation: For uniformly accelerated motion, distance is given by \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \). Here, initial velocity \( v_0 = 0 \), acceleration \( a = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), time \( t = 10 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 0 \cdot 10 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (10)^2 = 0 + 1 \cdot 100 = 100 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 100 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A train moving at \( 72 \, \text{km/h} \) decelerates at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 8 \, \text{s} \), then at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until it stops. What is the total distance covered during deceleration?
A car decelerates uniformly from \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) to rest over a distance of \( 36 \, \text{m} \). What is the deceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 18 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 36 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( 0 = (18)^2 + 2 a (36) \Rightarrow 0 = 324 + 72 a \Rightarrow a = -4.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 4.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates uniformly from \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) over \( 150 \, \text{m} \), then decelerates to \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) over the next \( 80 \, \text{m} \). What is the total time taken?
A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 48 \, \text{m/s} \). How long does it take to return to the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to max height: \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 0 = 48 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 4.8 \, \text{s} \). Total time = time up + time down = \( 4.8 \, \text{s} + 4.8 \, \text{s} = 9.6 \, \text{s} \). The total time is \( 9.6 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A person walks \( 15 \, \text{m} \) in \( 5 \, \text{s} \) and then walks back \( 5 \, \text{m} \) in \( 1 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time. Total distance = \( 15 \, \text{m} + 5 \, \text{m} = 20 \, \text{m} \), total time = \( 5 \, \text{s} + 1 \, \text{s} = 6 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{20}{6} = 3.33 \, \text{m/s} \). Rounded to two decimals, it is \( 3.33 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A rocket accelerates from rest at \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 8 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 4 \, \text{s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A car moving at \( 35 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest over \( 87.5 \, \text{m} \). What is the deceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 35 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 87.5 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( 0 = (35)^2 + 2 a (87.5) \Rightarrow 0 = 1225 + 175 a \Rightarrow a = -7 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 7 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A motorcycle accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 24 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance traveled during this time?
questions.explanation: Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \). First, find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{24 - 0}{6} = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( x = 0 \cdot 6 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 4 \cdot (6)^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 36 = 72 \, \text{m} \). The distance traveled is \( 72 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly and stops after traveling \( 50 \, \text{m} \). What is the deceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 50 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( 0 = (20)^2 + 2 a (50) \Rightarrow 0 = 400 + 100 a \Rightarrow a = -4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A body moving at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest in \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{0 - 15}{5} = -3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 15 \cdot 5 + \frac{1}{2} (-3) (5)^2 = 75 - 37.5 = 37.5 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 37.5 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from a height of \( 80 \, \text{m} \). What is its velocity just before hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 80 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 80 = 1600 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{1600} = 40 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates from rest at \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed is \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A particle accelerates uniformly from \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{18 - 6}{3} = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 6 \cdot 3 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 4 \cdot (3)^2 = 18 + 18 = 36 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 36 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from \( 4 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{16 - 4}{6} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 4 \cdot 6 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (6)^2 = 24 + 36 = 60 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 60 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 25 \, \text{m} \) tower. What is the time taken to reach a point \( 20 \, \text{m} \) above the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Displacement \( y = -5 \, \text{m} \), \( -5 = 50 t - 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 50 t - 5 = 0 \Rightarrow t^2 - 10 t - 1 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{10 \pm \sqrt{100 + 20}}{2} = \frac{10 \pm 10.95}{2} \), \( t = 10.475 \, \text{s} \) (downward path).

questions.question_text: A car moves at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the net displacement?
A train moves with a constant speed of \( 108 \, \text{km/h} \) for \( 2 \, \text{min} \). What is the distance traveled?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 108 \, \text{km/h} = 108 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 30 \, \text{m/s} \). Time = \( 2 \, \text{min} = 120 \, \text{s} \). Distance \( x = v t = 30 \cdot 120 = 3600 \, \text{m} = 3.6 \, \text{km} \). The distance traveled is \( 3.6 \, \text{km} \).

questions.question_text: A person walks \( 10 \, \text{m} \) in \( 2 \, \text{s} \) and returns to the starting point in \( 2 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time. Total distance = \( 10 \, \text{m} + 10 \, \text{m} = 20 \, \text{m} \), total time = \( 2 \, \text{s} + 2 \, \text{s} = 4 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{20}{4} = 5 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 2 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until its speed is \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at \( 6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( a = 6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 3 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 0 \cdot 3 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 6 \cdot (3)^2 = 0 + 3 \cdot 9 = 27 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 27 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A train moving at \( 108 \, \text{km/h} \) decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 10 \, \text{s} \), then at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until it stops. What is the total time taken to stop?

A man running at \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) throws a ball horizontally at \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) relative to himself. If it lands \( 12 \, \text{m} \) ahead of the throw point, what is the time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Ball’s speed relative to ground = \( 6 + 10 = 16 \, \text{m/s} \). Relative distance: \( 16 t - 6 t = 12 \Rightarrow 10 t = 12 \Rightarrow t = 1.2 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from rest. What is its velocity after falling \( 78.4 \, \text{m} \)? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 78.4 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 9.8 \cdot 78.4 = 1536.64 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{1536.64} \approx 39.2 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 39.2 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 14 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its velocity after \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 14 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 1.5 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 14 - 10 \cdot 1.5 = 14 - 15 = -1 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( -1 \, \text{m/s} \) (downward).

questions.question_text: A cyclist moving at \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) accelerates at \( 1 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to rest. What is the total distance covered?
A car moving at \( 27 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest in \( 9 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
A car moving at \( 60 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest over \( 150 \, \text{m} \). What is the time taken to stop?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \) to find \( a \): \( 0 = (60)^2 + 2 a (150) \Rightarrow 0 = 3600 + 300 a \Rightarrow a = -12 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Then, \( v = v_0 + a t \): \( 0 = 60 - 12 t \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A train accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 37.5 \, \text{m} \). What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 15 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 37.5 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (15)^2 = 0 + 2 a (37.5) \Rightarrow 225 = 75 a \Rightarrow a = 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A truck moving at \( 144 \, \text{km/h} \) decelerates uniformly and stops in \( 12 \, \text{s} \). What is the magnitude of deceleration?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 144 \, \text{km/h} = 144 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 40 \, \text{m/s} \). Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 40 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 12 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( a = \frac{0 - 40}{12} = -3.33 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is approximately \( 3.33 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates uniformly from \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 10 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance traveled?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{25 - 5}{10} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 5 \cdot 10 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (10)^2 = 50 + 100 = 150 \, \text{m} \). The distance traveled is \( 150 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist moves at a constant speed of \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 30 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: For constant speed, distance \( x = v t \). Here, \( v = 12 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 30 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 12 \cdot 30 = 360 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 360 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the final velocity?
questions.explanation: Use the equation \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, initial velocity \( v_0 = 0 \), acceleration \( a = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), time \( t = 5 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 4 \cdot 5 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \). The final velocity is \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A man walks \( 4 \, \text{km} \) in \( 1 \, \text{hour} \) and then returns to the starting point in \( 1 \, \text{hour} \). What is his average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time. Total distance = \( 4 \, \text{km} + 4 \, \text{km} = 8 \, \text{km} \), total time = \( 1 \, \text{h} + 1 \, \text{h} = 2 \, \text{h} \). Average speed = \( \frac{8}{2} = 4 \, \text{km/h} \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist moves at a constant speed of \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 50 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: For constant speed, distance \( x = v t \). Here, \( v = 6 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 50 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 6 \cdot 50 = 300 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 300 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates from \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed over the entire motion?
questions.explanation: Phase 1: \( v = 8 + 2 \cdot 5 = 18 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x_1 = 8 \cdot 5 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (5)^2 = 40 + 25 = 65 \, \text{m} \). Phase 2: \( x_2 = 18 \cdot 3 = 54 \, \text{m} \). Total distance = \( 65 + 54 = 119 \, \text{m} \), time = \( 5 + 3 = 8 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{119}{8} = 14.875 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \). How long does it take to return to the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to reach max height: \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 0 = 30 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 3 \, \text{s} \). Total time = time up + time down = \( 3 \, \text{s} + 3 \, \text{s} = 6 \, \text{s} \). The total time is \( 6 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A train accelerates uniformly from \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 10 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{40 - 20}{10} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 20 \cdot 10 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (10)^2 = 200 + 100 = 300 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 300 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from rest. What is the distance covered in the 5th second of its fall? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Distance in \( n \)-th second = \( g \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \). For 5th second, \( n = 5 \). Substitute: \( d = 10 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 5 - 1}{2} = 10 \cdot \frac{9}{2} = 45 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 45 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A runner moving at \( 7 \, \text{m/s} \) throws a ball horizontally at \( 14 \, \text{m/s} \) relative to himself. If it lands \( 21 \, \text{m} \) ahead of the throw point, what is the time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Ball’s speed relative to ground = \( 7 + 14 = 21 \, \text{m/s} \). Relative distance: \( 21 t - 7 t = 21 \Rightarrow 14 t = 21 \Rightarrow t = 1.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 50 \, \text{m} \) tower. What is its speed when it passes \( 20 \, \text{m} \) below the tower’s top? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))

A ball is thrown upwards at \( 28 \, \text{m/s} \) from the ground. At the same instant, another ball is dropped from \( 80 \, \text{m} \) above. Where do they meet relative to the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Ball 1: \( y_1 = 28 t - 5 t^2 \). Ball 2: \( y_2 = 80 - 5 t^2 \). Meet when \( y_1 = y_2 \): \( 28 t - 5 t^2 = 80 - 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 28 t = 80 \Rightarrow t = \frac{20}{7} \approx 2.86 \, \text{s} \). Height: \( y_1 = 28 \cdot \frac{20}{7} - 5 \cdot \left(\frac{20}{7}\right)^2 = 80 - 5 \cdot \frac{400}{49} = 80 - 40.82 = 39.18 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) and decelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 2 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until it regains \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A stone falls from a height and covers \( 68.6 \, \text{m} \) in the last \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \) of its fall. What is the total height? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A bus starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 8 \, \text{s} \). What is the final velocity of the bus?
questions.explanation: Use the equation \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, initial velocity \( v_0 = 0 \), acceleration \( a = 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), time \( t = 8 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 1.5 \cdot 8 = 12 \, \text{m/s} \). The final velocity is \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A person walks \( 8 \, \text{m} \) in \( 2 \, \text{s} \) and then walks back \( 4 \, \text{m} \) in \( 1 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time. Total distance = \( 8 \, \text{m} + 4 \, \text{m} = 12 \, \text{m} \), total time = \( 2 \, \text{s} + 1 \, \text{s} = 3 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{12}{3} = 4 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A train accelerates uniformly from \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{20 - 8}{6} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 8 \cdot 6 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (6)^2 = 48 + 36 = 84 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 84 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls from a height of \( 98 \, \text{m} \) on a planet and takes \( 3.5 \, \text{s} \) to reach the ground. What is the gravitational acceleration on this planet?
questions.explanation: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), \( 98 = \frac{1}{2} g (3.5)^2 \Rightarrow 98 = 6.125 g \Rightarrow g = 16 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A truck moving at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly and stops after \( 30 \, \text{m} \). How long does it take to stop?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \) to find \( a \): \( 0 = (15)^2 + 2 a (30) \Rightarrow 0 = 225 + 60 a \Rightarrow a = -3.75 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Then, \( v = v_0 + a t \): \( 0 = 15 - 3.75 t \Rightarrow t = \frac{15}{3.75} = 4 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 4 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A train moving at \( 126 \, \text{km/h} \) decelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 10 \, \text{s} \), then at \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until it stops. What is the total distance covered during deceleration?
A stone is thrown upwards at \( 35 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 45 \, \text{m} \) cliff. How far below the cliff’s edge is it after \( 8 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Displacement: \( y = 35 \cdot 8 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (8)^2 = 280 - 320 = -40 \, \text{m} \). Distance below cliff = \( 40 + 45 = 85 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls freely from a height of \( 98 \, \text{m} \). How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For free fall, use \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). Here, \( y = 98 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 98 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow 98 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 20 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{20} \approx 4.47 \, \text{s} \). Rounded to one decimal, the time is \( 4.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: Two stones are released from a height of \( 98 \, \text{m} \), \( 1 \, \text{s} \) apart. How long after the second stone is released do they meet? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Stone 1: \( y_1 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot (t + 1)^2 \). Stone 2: \( y_2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot t^2 \). Meet when \( y_1 = y_2 \): \( 4.9 (t + 1)^2 = 98 \Rightarrow (t + 1)^2 = 20 \Rightarrow t + 1 = 4.47 \Rightarrow t = 3.47 \, \text{s} \). Relative: \( y_1 - y_2 = 98 \Rightarrow 4.9 (t^2 + 2t + 1 - t^2) = 98 \Rightarrow 9.8 t + 4.9 = 98 \Rightarrow t = 9.5 \, \text{s} \) (error, use total height). Correct: They meet when first hits ground, \( t = 4.47 - 1 = 3.47 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of \( 24 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to max height: \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 0 = 24 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 2.4 \, \text{s} \). Total time = time up + time down = \( 2.4 \, \text{s} + 2.4 \, \text{s} = 4.8 \, \text{s} \). The total time is \( 4.8 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist accelerates from \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A motorcycle accelerates uniformly from rest at \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is the final velocity?
questions.explanation: Use the equation \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, initial velocity \( v_0 = 0 \), acceleration \( a = 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), time \( t = 6 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 2.5 \cdot 6 = 15 \, \text{m/s} \). The final velocity is \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone falls freely from a height of \( 78.4 \, \text{m} \). How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For free fall, use \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). Here, \( y = 78.4 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 78.4 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9.8 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow 78.4 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 16 \Rightarrow t = 4 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 4 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from rest to a velocity of \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 50 \, \text{m} \). What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 20 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 50 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (20)^2 = 0 + 2 a (50) \Rightarrow 400 = 100 a \Rightarrow a = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 25 \, \text{m} \) tower. What is the time taken to hit the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
A truck moving at \( 90 \, \text{km/h} \) applies brakes and stops after \( 12 \, \text{s} \). If the deceleration triples after \( 8 \, \text{s} \), what is the total distance covered?
questions.explanation: Speed: \( 90 \, \text{km/h} = 25 \, \text{m/s} \). First 8 s: Let \( a_1 = a \), \( v = 25 - a \cdot 8 \), stops in 12 s. Last 4 s: \( a_2 = 3a \), \( 0 = (25 - 8a) - 3a \cdot 4 \Rightarrow 25 - 8a = 12a \Rightarrow 25 = 20a \Rightarrow a = 1.25 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Distance: \( x_1 = 25 \cdot 8 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 1.25 \cdot (8)^2 = 200 - 40 = 160 \, \text{m} \). \( x_2 = (25 - 10) \cdot 4 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3.75 \cdot (4)^2 = 60 - 30 = 30 \, \text{m} \). Total = \( 160 + 30 = 190 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from rest. What is its velocity after falling \( 24.5 \, \text{m} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( y = 24.5 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( v^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 24.5 = 490 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{490} \approx 22.14 \, \text{m/s} \). Rounded to one decimal, the velocity is \( 22.1 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest in \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{0 - 12}{3} = -4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 12 \cdot 3 + \frac{1}{2} (-4) (3)^2 = 36 - 18 = 18 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 18 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: An object falls freely from a height. After \( 3 \, \text{s} \), what is the distance covered? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). Here, \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 3 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( y = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (3)^2 = 5 \cdot 9 = 45 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 45 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: Two balls are dropped from a height of \( 125 \, \text{m} \), \( 2 \, \text{s} \) apart. How long after the second ball is released do they meet if the first ball rebounds at \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) upon hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: First ball: \( 125 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \). Second ball released at \( t = 3 \, \text{s} \), meets after \( t' \) s from release. First ball after rebound: \( y_1 = 10 (t' + 2) \) (upward), second ball: \( y_2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot t'^2 \). Height relation: \( 125 - y_1 = y_2 \Rightarrow 125 - 10 (t' + 2) = 5 t'^2 \Rightarrow 125 - 10 t' - 20 = 5 t'^2 \Rightarrow 5 t'^2 + 10 t' - 105 = 0 \). Solve: \( t' = \frac{-10 \pm \sqrt{100 + 2100}}{10} = \frac{-10 \pm 47}{10} \), \( t' = 3.7 \, \text{s} \) (positive root).

questions.question_text: A stone falls freely from a height and reaches the ground with a velocity of \( 34.3 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the height? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 g y \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 34.3 \, \text{m/s} \), \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( (34.3)^2 = 0 + 2 \cdot 9.8 \cdot y \Rightarrow 1176.49 = 19.6 y \Rightarrow y = \frac{1176.49}{19.6} \approx 60 \, \text{m} \). The height is \( 60 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 44 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to max height: \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 0 = 44 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 4.4 \, \text{s} \). Total time = time up + time down = \( 4.4 \, \text{s} + 4.4 \, \text{s} = 8.8 \, \text{s} \). The total time is \( 8.8 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A person walks \( 12 \, \text{m} \) in \( 3 \, \text{s} \) and then walks back \( 6 \, \text{m} \) in \( 2 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time. Total distance = \( 12 \, \text{m} + 6 \, \text{m} = 18 \, \text{m} \), total time = \( 3 \, \text{s} + 2 \, \text{s} = 5 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{18}{5} = 3.6 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates from \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 6 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 4 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed over the entire motion?
A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 26 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its velocity after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 26 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 26 - 10 \cdot 2 = 26 - 20 = 6 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from a height of \( 122.5 \, \text{m} \). How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: For free fall, use \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). Here, \( y = 122.5 \, \text{m} \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 122.5 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow 122.5 = 5 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 24.5 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{24.5} \approx 4.95 \, \text{s} \). Rounded to one decimal, the time is \( 5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A runner starts from rest and accelerates at \( 1.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then maintains constant speed. What is the average speed over the first \( 10 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Acceleration: \( v = 1.5 \cdot 4 = 6 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x_1 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 1.5 \cdot (4)^2 = 12 \, \text{m} \). Constant speed for 6 s: \( x_2 = 6 \cdot 6 = 36 \, \text{m} \). Total distance = \( 12 + 36 = 48 \, \text{m} \), total time = \( 10 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{48}{10} = 4.8 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from rest to \( 22 \, \text{m/s} \) over a distance of \( 121 \, \text{m} \). What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( v = 22 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 121 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( (22)^2 = 0 + 2 a (121) \Rightarrow 484 = 242 a \Rightarrow a = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). The acceleration is \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A car decelerates uniformly from \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) to rest over a distance of \( 62.5 \, \text{m} \). What is the deceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 25 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 62.5 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( 0 = (25)^2 + 2 a (62.5) \Rightarrow 0 = 625 + 125 a \Rightarrow a = -5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of \( 35 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the time taken to reach the maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At max height, \( v = 0 \). Use \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, \( v_0 = 35 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = 35 - 10 t \Rightarrow 10 t = 35 \Rightarrow t = 3.5 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 3.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from rest. What is the distance covered in the 7th second of its fall? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Distance in \( n \)-th second = \( g \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \). For 7th second, \( n = 7 \). Substitute: \( d = 10 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 7 - 1}{2} = 10 \cdot \frac{13}{2} = 65 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 65 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the maximum height reached? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a h \). At max height, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 30 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = (30)^2 + 2 (-10) h \Rightarrow 0 = 900 - 20 h \Rightarrow h = \frac{900}{20} = 45 \, \text{m} \). The maximum height is \( 45 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with a speed of \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \). How long does it take to return to the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to max height: \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 0 = 50 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \). Total time = time up + time down = \( 5 \, \text{s} + 5 \, \text{s} = 10 \, \text{s} \). The total time is \( 10 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A runner moving at \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) throws a ball horizontally at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) relative to himself. If it lands \( 18 \, \text{m} \) ahead of the throw point, what is the time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Ball’s speed relative to ground = \( 5 + 15 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \). Relative distance: \( 20 t - 5 t = 18 \Rightarrow 15 t = 18 \Rightarrow t = 1.2 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched vertically at \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \) from the ground. After \( 6 \, \text{s} \), a second projectile is launched at \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \). When do they meet? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: First: \( y_1 = 50 t - 5 t^2 \), second: \( y_2 = 40 (t - 6) - 5 (t - 6)^2 \). Meet when \( y_1 = y_2 \): \( 50 t - 5 t^2 = 40 (t - 6) - 5 (t^2 - 12 t + 36) \). Simplify: \( 50 t - 5 t^2 = 40 t - 240 - 5 t^2 + 60 t - 180 \Rightarrow 50 t = 100 t - 420 \Rightarrow 50 t = 420 \Rightarrow t = 8.4 \, \text{s} \). Time from second launch = \( 8.4 - 6 = 2.4 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest over \( 125 \, \text{m} \). What is the time taken to stop?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \) to find \( a \): \( 0 = (50)^2 + 2 a (125) \Rightarrow 0 = 2500 + 250 a \Rightarrow a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Then, \( v = v_0 + a t \): \( 0 = 50 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is \( 5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from rest. What is the distance covered in the 2nd second of its fall? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Distance in \( n \)-th second = \( g \cdot \frac{2n - 1}{2} \). For 2nd second, \( n = 2 \). Substitute: \( d = 10 \cdot \frac{2 \cdot 2 - 1}{2} = 10 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 15 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 15 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A vehicle starts from rest and travels \( 50 \, \text{m} \) in \( 5 \, \text{s} \) with uniform acceleration. What is its final velocity?
questions.explanation: Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \) to find \( a \): \( 50 = 0 \cdot 5 + \frac{1}{2} a (5)^2 \Rightarrow 50 = 12.5 a \Rightarrow a = 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Then, \( v = v_0 + a t = 0 + 4 \cdot 5 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \). The final velocity is \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A balloon descends at \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) from \( 100 \, \text{m} \) height and releases a stone \( 2 \, \text{s} \) later. What is the time taken by the stone to hit the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Height at release: \( h = 100 - 6 \cdot 2 = 88 \, \text{m} \). Stone’s initial velocity = \( -6 \, \text{m/s} \). \( -88 = -6 t + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 6 t - 88 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 + 1760}}{10} = \frac{6 \pm 42.19}{10} \), \( t = 4.82 \, \text{s} \) (positive root).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 24 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 50 \, \text{m} \) building. How far below the top of the building is it after \( 6 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Displacement: \( y = 24 \cdot 6 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (6)^2 = 144 - 180 = -36 \, \text{m} \). Distance below top = \( 36 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( a = 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 3 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( x = 0 \cdot 3 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 5 \cdot (3)^2 = 0 + 2.5 \cdot 9 = 22.5 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 22.5 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A vehicle moving at \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest in \( 100 \, \text{m} \). What is the time taken to stop?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \) to find \( a \): \( 0 = (30)^2 + 2 a (100) \Rightarrow 0 = 900 + 200 a \Rightarrow a = -4.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Then, \( v = v_0 + a t \): \( 0 = 30 - 4.5 t \Rightarrow t = \frac{30}{4.5} \approx 6.67 \, \text{s} \). The time taken is approximately \( 6.7 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A car decelerates uniformly from \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) to rest over a distance of \( 32 \, \text{m} \). What is the deceleration?
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a x \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 16 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x = 32 \, \text{m} \). Substitute: \( 0 = (16)^2 + 2 a (32) \Rightarrow 0 = 256 + 64 a \Rightarrow a = -4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of deceleration is \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A rocket is launched vertically at \( 60 \, \text{m/s} \) from the ground. After \( 5 \, \text{s} \), a second rocket is launched at \( 45 \, \text{m/s} \). How long after the second launch do they meet? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: First: \( y_1 = 60 t - 5 t^2 \), second: \( y_2 = 45 (t - 5) - 5 (t - 5)^2 \). Meet when \( y_1 = y_2 \): \( 60 t - 5 t^2 = 45 (t - 5) - 5 (t^2 - 10 t + 25) \). Simplify: \( 60 t - 5 t^2 = 45 t - 225 - 5 t^2 + 50 t - 125 \Rightarrow 60 t = 95 t - 350 \Rightarrow 35 t = 350 \Rightarrow t = 10 \, \text{s} \). Time from second launch = \( 10 - 5 = 5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown upwards at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) from a tower. It hits the ground \( 4 \, \text{s} \) later. What is the height of the tower? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( y = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \). Downward is positive, so \( v_0 = -15 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( y = -15 \cdot 4 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot (4)^2 = -60 + 80 = 20 \, \text{m} \). Height = \( 20 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates from rest at \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) until it reaches \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \), then immediately decelerates at \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to rest. What is the total time taken?
questions.explanation: Acceleration: \( t_1 = \frac{25}{2.5} = 10 \, \text{s} \). Deceleration: \( t_2 = \frac{25}{5} = 5 \, \text{s} \). Total time = \( 10 + 5 = 15 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: An elevator ascends at \( 3 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 5 \, \text{s} \), then accelerates at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). A ball is dropped at the end of this period. What is the time taken for the ball to hit the ground if the initial height was \( 20 \, \text{m} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Phase 1: \( h_1 = 3 \cdot 5 = 15 \, \text{m} \). Phase 2: \( v = 3 + 2 \cdot 3 = 9 \, \text{m/s} \), \( h_2 = 3 \cdot 3 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (3)^2 = 9 + 9 = 18 \, \text{m} \). Total height at drop = \( 20 + 15 + 18 = 53 \, \text{m} \), initial velocity of ball = \( 9 \, \text{m/s} \) upward. \( -53 = 9 t - 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 9 t - 53 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{9 \pm \sqrt{81 + 1060}}{10} = \frac{9 \pm 33.79}{10} \), \( t = 4.28 \, \text{s} \) (positive root).

questions.question_text: A rocket accelerates from rest at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 6 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the total distance covered?
A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to reach max height: \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 0 = 10 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 1 \, \text{s} \). Total time of flight = time up + time down = \( 1 \, \text{s} + 1 \, \text{s} = 2 \, \text{s} \). The total time is \( 2 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A man walking at \( 4 \, \text{m/s} \) throws a ball forward at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) relative to himself. If the ball lands \( 10 \, \text{m} \) ahead of the throw point, how long was it in the air? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Ball’s speed relative to ground = \( 12 + 4 = 16 \, \text{m/s} \). Man moves \( 4 t \), ball moves \( 16 t \), distance ahead = \( 16 t - 4 t = 10 \Rightarrow 12 t = 10 \Rightarrow t = \frac{5}{6} \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A body accelerates uniformly from \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) to \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) in \( 4 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance traveled?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{16 - 8}{4} = 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 8 \cdot 4 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (4)^2 = 32 + 16 = 48 \, \text{m} \). The distance traveled is \( 48 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards at \( 45 \, \text{m/s} \) from a \( 30 \, \text{m} \) tower. What is the time taken to reach a point \( 15 \, \text{m} \) above the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Displacement \( y = -15 \, \text{m} \), \( -15 = 45 t - 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 45 t - 15 = 0 \Rightarrow t^2 - 9 t - 3 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{9 \pm \sqrt{81 + 12}}{2} = \frac{9 \pm 9.64}{2} \), \( t = 9.32 \, \text{s} \) (downward path).

questions.question_text: A drone ascends vertically at \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) for \( 8 \, \text{s} \), then releases a payload that hits the ground \( 6 \, \text{s} \) later. What was the initial height of the drone above the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Height after ascent: \( h_1 = 5 \cdot 8 = 40 \, \text{m} \). Payload’s initial velocity = \( 536 \, \text{m/s} \) upward. Total height \( h = h_0 + 40 \), use \( y = v_0 t - \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), \( y = -h \). \( -h = 5 \cdot 6 - 5 \cdot (6)^2 \Rightarrow -h = 30 - 180 = -150 \Rightarrow h = 150 \, \text{m} \). Initial height \( h_0 = 150 - 40 = 110 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A rocket descends at \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 120 \, \text{m} \) and releases a payload \( 3 \, \text{s} \) later. How long does the payload take to hit the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Height at release: \( h = 120 - 8 \cdot 3 = 96 \, \text{m} \). Payload’s initial velocity = \( -8 \, \text{m/s} \). \( -96 = -8 t + 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 8 t - 96 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{8 \pm \sqrt{64 + 1920}}{10} = \frac{8 \pm 44.5}{10} \), \( t = 5.25 \, \text{s} \) (positive root).

questions.question_text: A car accelerates from rest at \( 3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 4 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 6 \, \text{s} \), and decelerates to rest at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is the total distance?
A car accelerates from \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 2 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 6 \, \text{s} \), then moves at constant speed for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is the average speed over this time?
questions.explanation: Phase 1: \( v = 5 + 2 \cdot 6 = 17 \, \text{m/s} \), \( x_1 = 5 \cdot 6 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \cdot (6)^2 = 30 + 36 = 66 \, \text{m} \). Phase 2: \( x_2 = 17 \cdot 3 = 51 \, \text{m} \). Total distance = \( 66 + 51 = 117 \, \text{m} \), time = \( 6 + 3 = 9 \, \text{s} \). Average speed = \( \frac{117}{9} = 13 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 72 \, \text{km/h} \) is brought to rest in \( 4 \, \text{s} \) by applying brakes. What is the retardation?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 72 \, \text{km/h} = 72 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 20 \, \text{m/s} \). Use \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} \). Here, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 20 \, \text{m/s} \), \( t = 4 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( a = \frac{0 - 20}{4} = -5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Magnitude of retardation is \( 5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from rest. What is its velocity after falling for \( 1.5 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v = v_0 + g t \). Here, \( v_0 = 0 \), \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( t = 1.5 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 10 \cdot 1.5 = 15 \, \text{m/s} \). The velocity is \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A car moving at \( 22 \, \text{m/s} \) decelerates uniformly to rest in \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Find \( a = \frac{v - v_0}{t} = \frac{0 - 22}{5} = -4.4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Use \( x = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = 22 \cdot 5 + \frac{1}{2} (-4.4) (5)^2 = 110 - 55 = 55 \, \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 55 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A train starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at \( 0.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 20 \, \text{s} \). What is the final velocity?
questions.explanation: Use the equation \( v = v_0 + a t \). Here, initial velocity \( v_0 = 0 \), acceleration \( a = 0.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), time \( t = 20 \, \text{s} \). Substitute: \( v = 0 + 0.5 \cdot 20 = 10 \, \text{m/s} \). The final velocity is \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards with \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) from the ground. What is the maximum height reached? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Use \( v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a h \). At max height, \( v = 0 \), \( v_0 = 25 \, \text{m/s} \), \( a = -10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). Substitute: \( 0 = (25)^2 + 2 (-10) h \Rightarrow 0 = 625 - 20 h \Rightarrow h = \frac{625}{20} = 31.25 \, \text{m} \). The maximum height is \( 31.25 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A cyclist travels at a constant speed of \( 18 \, \text{km/h} \) for \( 10 \, \text{minutes} \). What is the distance covered?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: \( 18 \, \text{km/h} = 18 \cdot \frac{1000}{3600} = 5 \, \text{m/s} \). Time = \( 10 \, \text{min} = 10 \cdot 60 = 600 \, \text{s} \). Distance \( x = v t = 5 \cdot 600 = 3000 \, \text{m} = 3 \, \text{km} \). The distance covered is \( 3 \, \text{km} \).

questions.question_text: A parachutist falls freely for \( 2.5 \, \text{s} \) before opening the parachute, then decelerates at \( 4 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to hit the ground at \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total time of descent? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Free fall: \( v = g t = 10 \cdot 2.5 = 25 \, \text{m/s} \). Deceleration phase: \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 5 = 25 - 4 t \Rightarrow 4 t = 20 \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \). Total time = \( 2.5 + 5 = 7.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A train moving at \( 90 \, \text{km/h} \) accelerates at \( 0.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) for \( 15 \, \text{s} \), then decelerates at \( 2.5 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) to rest. What is the total distance covered?
A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial speed of \( 28 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the total time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to max height: \( v = v_0 + a t \), \( 0 = 28 - 10 t \Rightarrow t = 2.8 \, \text{s} \). Total time = time up + time down = \( 2.8 \, \text{s} + 2.8 \, \text{s} = 5.6 \, \text{s} \). The total time is \( 5.6 \, \text{s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 1

questions.question_text: A particle starts with velocity \( 3 \hat{i} \, \text{m/s} \) and accelerates at \( (2 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \). Given: \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 3 \hat{i}, \mathbf{a} = 2 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}, t = 2 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = 3 \hat{i} + (2 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}) \times 2 = 3 \hat{i} + 4 \hat{i} + 10 \hat{j} = 7 \hat{i} + 10 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{7^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{49 + 100} = \sqrt{149} \approx 12.21 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is its range? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 120^\circ = 0.866 \))
In uniform circular motion, what is the relationship between centripetal acceleration (\( a_c \)) and angular speed (\( \omega \))?
questions.explanation: The centripetal acceleration in uniform circular motion is given by \( a_c = \omega^2 R \), where \( R \) is the radius. This shows that \( a_c \) is proportional to the square of the angular speed, reflecting the dependence on the rate of change of direction.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at 30 m/s at 60° to the horizontal. What is the time of flight? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
A particle starts from rest with a constant acceleration of \( (6 \hat{i} - 4 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \), with \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = 6 \hat{i} - 4 \hat{j}, t = 2 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = (6 \hat{i} - 4 \hat{j}) \times 2 = 12 \hat{i} - 8 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + (-8)^2} = \sqrt{144 + 64} = \sqrt{208} \approx 14.42 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle starts with velocity \( 8 \hat{i} \, \text{m/s} \) and accelerates at \( (2 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 4 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \). Given: \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 8 \hat{i}, \mathbf{a} = 2 \hat{j}, t = 4 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = 8 \hat{i} + 2 \hat{j} \times 4 = 8 \hat{i} + 8 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{8^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{64 + 64} = \sqrt{128} = 8\sqrt{2} \approx 11.31 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what happens to the kinetic energy at the maximum height compared to the launch point?
questions.explanation: At the maximum height, the vertical velocity is zero, so the kinetic energy is due only to the horizontal velocity, which remains constant. Thus, the kinetic energy decreases compared to the launch point, where both components contribute.

questions.question_text: A plane flies east at \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \) while a wind blows north at \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the plane’s velocity relative to the ground?
questions.explanation: Velocity components: \( v_x = 40 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 30 \, \text{m/s} \). Magnitude \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = \sqrt{1600 + 900} = \sqrt{2500} = 50 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the relationship between angular speed (\( \omega \)) and linear speed (\( v \)) in uniform circular motion?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the linear speed \( v \) is related to the angular speed \( \omega \) by the equation \( v = \omega R \), where \( R \) is the radius of the circular path. This shows that linear speed is directly proportional to angular speed.

questions.question_text: A stone is projected horizontally with a speed of 10 m/s from a height of 20 m. How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: For vertical motion: y = v₀y t + (1/2) a_y t², where v₀y = 0, a_y = -g. Given: y = -20 m, g = 10 m/s². -20 = 0 - (1/2) × 10 × t² ⇒ -20 = -5 t² ⇒ t² = 4 ⇒ t = 2 s.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at \( 35 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: Time of flight \( T_f = \frac{2 v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 35 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( T_f = \frac{2 \times 35 \times 0.6}{10} = \frac{42}{10} = 4.2 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone tied to a string moves in a circle of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) with a frequency of \( 2 \, \text{Hz} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 2 = 4\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R = (4\pi)^2 \times 1.5 = 16\pi^2 \times 1.5 \approx 236.87 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle’s position is given by \( x = 3t^2 - 4t \) and \( y = 5t \) (in meters and seconds). What is its speed at \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v_x = \frac{dx}{dt} = 6t - 4, v_y = \frac{dy}{dt} = 5 \). At \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \): \( v_x = 6 \times 1 - 4 = 2 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 5 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{4 + 25} = \sqrt{29} \approx 5.39 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in circular motion has a centripetal acceleration of \( 81 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) and radius \( 9 \, \text{m} \). What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( a_c = 81 \, \text{m/s}^2, R = 9 \, \text{m} \). \( 81 = \frac{v^2}{9} \Rightarrow v^2 = 729 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{729} = 27 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched with a speed of \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) at an angle of \( 45^\circ \) to the horizontal. What is its maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 45^\circ = 0.707 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 10 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 45^\circ = 0.707, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_0 \sin \theta_0 = 10 \times 0.707 \approx 7.07 \, \text{m/s} \). \( h_m = \frac{(7.07)^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{49.98}{20} \approx 2.5 \, \text{m} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 2

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is its vertical velocity at the maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: At maximum height, the vertical velocity \( v_y = 0 \, \text{m/s} \) (constant property of projectile motion).

questions.question_text: A particle’s position is given by \( x = 2t + t^2 \) and \( y = 3t - 2t^2 \) (in meters and seconds). What is its speed at \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v_x = \frac{dx}{dt} = 2 + 2t, v_y = \frac{dy}{dt} = 3 - 4t \). At \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \): \( v_x = 2 + 2 \times 2 = 6 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 3 - 4 \times 2 = -5 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + (-5)^2} = \sqrt{36 + 25} = \sqrt{61} \approx 7.81 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circular path of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \) with a period of \( 1 \, \text{s} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Angular speed \( \omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2\pi}{1} = 2\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R = (2\pi)^2 \times 2 = 4\pi^2 \times 2 \approx 78.96 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A body is projected with a speed of 20 m/s at 45°. What is the time to reach maximum height? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Time to max height t_m = (v₀ sin θ₀) / g. Given: v₀ = 20 m/s, sin 45° = 1/√2, g = 10 m/s². t_m = (20 × (1/√2)) / 10 = (20 / √2) / 10 = √2 ≈ 1.41 s.

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is true about the acceleration at all points in the trajectory?
options: It is constant in magnitude and direction
It is zero at the peak
questions.explanation: In projectile motion, assuming no air resistance, the acceleration is due to gravity and remains constant in magnitude and direction (downward) throughout the trajectory, regardless of the object’s position or velocity.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 28 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 45^\circ \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 45^\circ = 0.707 \))
questions.explanation: Time of flight \( T_f = \frac{2 v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 28 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 45^\circ = 0.707, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( T_f = \frac{2 \times 28 \times 0.707}{9.8} = \frac{39.592}{9.8} \approx 4.04 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \). What is its maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 20 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( h_m = \frac{(20 \times 0.8)^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{16^2}{20} = \frac{256}{20} = 12.8 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what remains constant throughout the trajectory, assuming no air resistance?
questions.explanation: In projectile motion without air resistance, the horizontal component of velocity remains constant because there is no horizontal acceleration. The vertical component changes due to gravity, but the horizontal motion is uniform.

questions.question_text: What is the primary factor affecting the maximum height of a projectile launched from level ground?
questions.explanation: The maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \) depends on the initial vertical velocity component (\( v_0 \sin \theta_0 \)). This component, influenced by both speed and angle, determines how high the projectile rises against gravity.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \). What is its maximum height? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 18 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_0 \sin \theta_0 = 18 \times 0.8 = 14.4 \, \text{m/s} \). \( h_m = \frac{14.4^2}{2 \times 9.8} = \frac{207.36}{19.6} \approx 10.58 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 42 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is its range? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Range \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \), where \( 2\theta_0 = 60^\circ \). Given: \( v_0 = 42 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( R = \frac{42^2 \times 0.866}{9.8} = \frac{1764 \times 0.866}{9.8} \approx \frac{1527.62}{9.8} \approx 155.88 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circular path of radius \( 6 \, \text{m} \) with a frequency of \( 2 \, \text{Hz} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 2 = 4\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R = (4\pi)^2 \times 6 = 16\pi^2 \times 6 \approx 947.52 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally at \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 20 \, \text{m} \). What is its horizontal range? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to fall: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \Rightarrow 20 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \Rightarrow 20 = 5 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 4 \Rightarrow t = 2 \, \text{s} \). Horizontal range \( R = v_x t = 5 \times 2 = 10 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: In motion with constant acceleration in a plane, how are the x- and y-components of the motion related?
questions.explanation: For motion with constant acceleration in a plane, the x- and y-components are independent of each other. The motion can be treated as two separate one-dimensional motions along perpendicular directions, with each component governed by its own constant acceleration.

questions.question_text: A particle completes 6 revolutions in \( 3 \, \text{s} \) in a circular path of radius \( 1 \, \text{m} \). What is its linear speed?
questions.explanation: Frequency \( f = \frac{n}{t} = \frac{6}{3} = 2 \, \text{Hz} \). Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 2 = 4\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Linear speed \( v = \omega R = 4\pi \times 1 = 4\pi \approx 12.57 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 3

questions.question_text: A particle starts with velocity \( 5 \hat{i} \, \text{m/s} \) and accelerates at \( (4 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 3 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \). Given: \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 5 \hat{i}, \mathbf{a} = 4 \hat{j}, t = 3 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = 5 \hat{i} + 4 \hat{j} \times 3 = 5 \hat{i} + 12 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest with a constant acceleration of \( (-2 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is the magnitude of its velocity after \( 3 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \), with \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = -2 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}, t = 3 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = (-2 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}) \times 3 = -6 \hat{i} + 15 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(-6)^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{36 + 225} = \sqrt{261} \approx 16.16 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally at \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 12.5 \, \text{m} \). What is its speed on hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity: \( v_y = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 12.5} = \sqrt{250} \approx 15.81 \, \text{m/s} \). Horizontal velocity: \( v_x = 8 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 15.81^2} = \sqrt{64 + 250} = \sqrt{314} \approx 17.72 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circle of radius \( 4 \, \text{m} \) with an angular speed of \( 3 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R \). Given: \( \omega = 3 \, \text{rad/s}, R = 4 \, \text{m} \). \( a_c = 3^2 \times 4 = 9 \times 4 = 36 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally from a tower with a speed of \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \). It lands \( 24 \, \text{m} \) from the base. What is the height of the tower? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Horizontal distance \( x = v_x t \), so \( t = \frac{x}{v_x} = \frac{24}{8} = 3 \, \text{s} \). Vertical height \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \). \( h = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 3^2 = 5 \times 9 = 45 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown horizontally at 12 m/s from a 80 m high cliff. How far from the base does it land? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Time to fall: y = (1/2) g t², -80 = (1/2) × 10 × t² ⇒ t² = 16 ⇒ t = 4 s. Horizontal distance x = v_x t = 12 × 4 = 48 m.

questions.question_text: A particle completes 8 revolutions in \( 4 \, \text{s} \) in a circular path of radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \). What is its linear speed?
questions.explanation: Frequency \( f = \frac{n}{t} = \frac{8}{4} = 2 \, \text{Hz} \). Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 2 = 4\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Linear speed \( v = \omega R = 4\pi \times 2 = 8\pi \approx 25.13 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \). What is its range? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 106^\circ = 0.96 \))
In projectile motion, what is true about the velocity vector just before landing compared to just after launch, assuming level ground?
options: It has the same magnitude but opposite vertical direction
questions.explanation: For a projectile on level ground, the velocity just before landing has the same magnitude as just after launch but with the vertical component reversed in direction (downward instead of upward) due to symmetry, while the horizontal component remains unchanged.

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is the direction of the velocity vector at the highest point of its trajectory?
options: At an angle to the horizontal
questions.explanation: In projectile motion, the velocity has both horizontal (\( v_x \)) and vertical (\( v_y \)) components. At the highest point, the vertical component \( v_y = 0 \) due to the symmetry of the parabolic path, while the horizontal component \( v_x \) remains constant. Thus, the velocity vector is purely horizontal.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its horizontal velocity component? (Take \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 20 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \). \( v_x = 20 \times 0.8 = 16 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is the role of the centripetal acceleration?
options: It changes the direction of velocity
It changes the magnitude of velocity
questions.explanation: The centripetal acceleration in uniform circular motion changes the direction of the velocity vector to keep the object moving in a circular path. It does not affect the speed, which remains constant.

questions.question_text: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of \( (5 \hat{i} + 2 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \) from rest. What is its speed after \( 3 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \), with \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = 5 \hat{i} + 2 \hat{j}, t = 3 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = (5 \hat{i} + 2 \hat{j}) \times 3 = 15 \hat{i} + 6 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{15^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{225 + 36} = \sqrt{261} \approx 16.16 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \). What is its vertical velocity at \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity \( v_y = v_0 \sin \theta_0 - g t \). Given: \( v_0 = 30 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8, t = 2 \, \text{s}, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_y = 30 \times 0.8 - 10 \times 2 = 24 - 20 = 4 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 4

questions.question_text: An object moves in a circular path of radius \( 4 \, \text{m} \) with a frequency of \( 5 \, \text{Hz} \). What is the magnitude of its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 5 = 10\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R = (10\pi)^2 \times 4 = 100\pi^2 \times 4 \approx 3947.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 45^\circ \). What is its horizontal velocity component?
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 18 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 \). \( v_x = 18 \times 0.707 \approx 12.73 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle’s position is given by \( x = 5t - t^2 \) and \( y = 2t^2 \) (in meters and seconds). What is the magnitude of its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v_x = \frac{dx}{dt} = 5 - 2t, v_y = \frac{dy}{dt} = 4t \). Acceleration: \( a_x = \frac{dv_x}{dt} = -2, a_y = \frac{dv_y}{dt} = 4 \). Magnitude \( a = \sqrt{a_x^2 + a_y^2} = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{4 + 16} = \sqrt{20} \approx 4.47 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: An object in uniform circular motion has a radius of 5 m and completes 10 revolutions in 20 s. What is the magnitude of its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Angular speed ω = (2π n) / t, where n = 10, t = 20 s. ω = (2π × 10) / 20 = π rad/s. Centripetal acceleration a_c = ω² R = (π)² × 5 ≈ 9.87 × 5 ≈ 49.35 m/s².

questions.question_text: In motion with constant acceleration in a plane, what is true if the acceleration is zero?
options: The motion is uniform and rectilinear
questions.explanation: If the acceleration is zero, the velocity remains constant in both magnitude and direction, resulting in uniform rectilinear (straight-line) motion. Without acceleration, the object continues in its initial state per Newton’s first law.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched with a speed of \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) at an angle of \( 30^\circ \) to the horizontal. What is its maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 16 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 30^\circ = 0.5, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_0 \sin \theta_0 = 16 \times 0.5 = 8 \, \text{m/s} \). \( h_m = \frac{8^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{64}{20} = 3.2 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle starts with velocity \( 4 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \) and accelerates at \( (3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \). Given: \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 4 \hat{j}, \mathbf{a} = 3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}, t = 2 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = 4 \hat{j} + (3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) \times 2 = 6 \hat{i} + (4 - 4) \hat{j} = 6 \hat{i} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{6^2 + 0^2} = \sqrt{36} = 6 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest with a constant acceleration of \( (2 \hat{i} + 6 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \), with \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = 2 \hat{i} + 6 \hat{j}, t = 2 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = (2 \hat{i} + 6 \hat{j}) \times 2 = 4 \hat{i} + 12 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{4^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{16 + 144} = \sqrt{160} \approx 12.65 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A boat moves north at 20 km/h while a river current flows east at 15 km/h. What is the magnitude of the resultant velocity?
questions.explanation: Resultant velocity R = √(v_x² + v_y²). Given: v_x = 15 km/h (east), v_y = 20 km/h (north). R = √(15² + 20²) = √(225 + 400) = √625 = 25 km/h.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 98 \, \text{m} \). What is its horizontal range? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to fall: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \Rightarrow 98 = \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times t^2 \Rightarrow 98 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 20 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{20} \approx 4.47 \, \text{s} \). Horizontal range \( R = v_x t = 15 \times 4.47 \approx 67.05 \, \text{m} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 5

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is true about the magnitude of the velocity?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity (speed) remains constant because the motion occurs at a constant speed along the circular path, even though the direction of the velocity vector changes continuously.

questions.question_text: A particle’s position is given by \( x = 5t - 3t^2 \) and \( y = 4t^2 \) (in meters and seconds). What is its speed at \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v_x = \frac{dx}{dt} = 5 - 6t, v_y = \frac{dy}{dt} = 8t \). At \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \): \( v_x = 5 - 6 \times 1 = -1 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 8 \times 1 = 8 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{1 + 64} = \sqrt{65} \approx 8.06 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is true about the net force acting on the object?
questions.explanation: The net force in uniform circular motion is the centripetal force, directed towards the center of the circle. It provides the centripetal acceleration necessary to maintain the circular path and is perpendicular to the velocity.

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circle of radius \( 3 \, \text{m} \) with a speed of \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( v = 12 \, \text{m/s}, R = 3 \, \text{m} \). \( a_c = \frac{12^2}{3} = \frac{144}{3} = 48 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: What determines the time an object stays in the air during projectile motion from level ground?
questions.explanation: The time of flight in projectile motion depends on the initial vertical velocity component (\( v_0 \sin \theta_0 \)) and gravity (\( g \)), as given by \( T_f = \frac{2 v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). This reflects the time taken to rise and fall back to the ground.

questions.question_text: What is true about the acceleration vector of a projectile at its highest point?
questions.explanation: At the highest point of a projectile’s trajectory, the acceleration vector is still directed downward due to gravity. It remains constant in magnitude and direction (vertically downward) throughout the motion, unaffected by the velocity being purely horizontal at that instant.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 24 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is its time to reach maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \))
questions.explanation: Time to maximum height \( t_m = \frac{v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 24 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 30^\circ = 0.5, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( t_m = \frac{24 \times 0.5}{10} = \frac{12}{10} = 1.2 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is the relationship between the period of revolution and the frequency?
options: Frequency is proportional to period squared
questions.explanation: The period (\( T \)) is the time for one revolution, and the frequency (\( f \)) is the number of revolutions per unit time. They are reciprocals, as \( f = \frac{1}{T} \) or \( T = \frac{1}{f} \), defining their inverse relationship.

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is responsible for keeping the object in its circular path?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, a centripetal force is required to keep the object moving in a circular path. This force, directed towards the center, provides the necessary centripetal acceleration to change the direction of the velocity continuously.

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown horizontally at \( 9 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 78.4 \, \text{m} \). What is its horizontal range? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to fall: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \Rightarrow 78.4 = \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times t^2 \Rightarrow 78.4 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 16 \Rightarrow t = 4 \, \text{s} \). Horizontal range \( R = v_x t = 9 \times 4 = 36 \, \text{m} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 6

questions.question_text: For an object in motion with constant acceleration in a plane, what is the shape of its path if the initial velocity is zero?
questions.explanation: If the initial velocity is zero, the object moves under constant acceleration alone, resulting in a straight-line path along the direction of the acceleration vector. This is a special case of rectilinear motion.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at \( 24 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its vertical velocity at \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity \( v_y = v_0 \sin \theta_0 - g t \). Given: \( v_0 = 24 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6, t = 1 \, \text{s}, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_y = 24 \times 0.6 - 10 \times 1 = 14.4 - 10 = 4.4 \, \text{m/s} \).
