questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circular path of radius \( 1 \, \text{m} \) completing 3 revolutions in \( 6 \, \text{s} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Frequency \( f = \frac{n}{t} = \frac{3}{6} = 0.5 \, \text{Hz} \). Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 0.5 = \pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R = (\pi)^2 \times 1 \approx 9.87 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: For an object in motion with constant acceleration in a plane, what is true when the acceleration is parallel to the initial velocity?
options: The path is a straight line
questions.explanation: When the constant acceleration is parallel to the initial velocity, the motion occurs in a straight line along the direction of the initial velocity, as the acceleration only changes the magnitude of the velocity, not its direction.

questions.question_text: A projectile launched at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \) reaches a horizontal distance of \( 18 \, \text{m} \). What is the value of \( g \)? (Take \( \sin 53^\circ = 0.8, \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: Range \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \), where \( 2\theta_0 = 106^\circ, \sin 106^\circ = \sin (180^\circ - 106^\circ) = \sin 74^\circ \approx 0.96 \). Given: \( R = 18 \, \text{m}, v_0 = 15 \, \text{m/s} \). \( 18 = \frac{15^2 \times 0.96}{g} = \frac{225 \times 0.96}{g} = \frac{216}{g} \). \( g = \frac{216}{18} = 12 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circle of radius \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) with a speed of \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( v = 10 \, \text{m/s}, R = 2.5 \, \text{m} \). \( a_c = \frac{10^2}{2.5} = \frac{100}{2.5} = 40 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle’s position is given by \( x = 4t^2 - t \) and \( y = 2t + t^2 \) (in meters and seconds). What is its speed at \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v_x = \frac{dx}{dt} = 8t - 1, v_y = \frac{dy}{dt} = 2 + 2t \). At \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \): \( v_x = 8 \times 1 - 1 = 7 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 2 + 2 \times 1 = 4 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{7^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{49 + 16} = \sqrt{65} \approx 8.06 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: For a projectile launched from the ground, what is true about its time of ascent and time of descent?
questions.explanation: For a projectile launched from and returning to the ground, the time of ascent equals the time of descent due to the symmetry of the parabolic path. The time to reach maximum height (\( t_m = \frac{v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \)) is half the total time of flight, and the descent mirrors the ascent.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its horizontal velocity component? (Take \( \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 16 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \). \( v_x = 16 \times 0.8 = 12.8 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle starts with velocity \( 6 \hat{i} \, \text{m/s} \) and accelerates at \( (2 \hat{i} + 4 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 3 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \). Given: \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 6 \hat{i}, \mathbf{a} = 2 \hat{i} + 4 \hat{j}, t = 3 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = 6 \hat{i} + (2 \hat{i} + 4 \hat{j}) \times 3 = 6 \hat{i} + 6 \hat{i} + 12 \hat{j} = 12 \hat{i} + 12 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{12^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{144 + 144} = \sqrt{288} = 12\sqrt{2} \approx 16.97 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 7

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is true about the total mechanical energy, assuming no air resistance?
options: It becomes zero at the peak
questions.explanation: Assuming no air resistance, the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) of a projectile remains conserved throughout its trajectory. Energy transforms between kinetic and potential forms, but the sum stays constant as no external non-conservative forces act.

questions.question_text: What is the significance of the horizontal component of velocity in determining the range of a projectile?
options: It has no effect on range
questions.explanation: The horizontal component of velocity (\( v_0 \cos \theta_0 \)) determines how far the projectile travels horizontally during its time of flight. It remains constant and, combined with the time of flight (influenced by the vertical component), defines the range.

questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest with an acceleration of \( (3 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its displacement magnitude after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Displacement \( \mathbf{r} = \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{a} t^2 \) (since \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \)). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = 3 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}, t = 2 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{r} = \frac{1}{2} (3 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}) \times 2^2 = 2 (3 \hat{i} + 5 \hat{j}) = 6 \hat{i} + 10 \hat{j} \, \text{m} \). Magnitude \( |\mathbf{r}| = \sqrt{6^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{36 + 100} = \sqrt{136} \approx 11.66 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A swimmer moves north at \( 3 \, \text{m/s} \) in a river flowing west at \( 4 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the swimmer’s velocity relative to the ground?
questions.explanation: Velocity components: \( v_x = -4 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 3 \, \text{m/s} \). Magnitude \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25} = 5 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 24.5 \, \text{m} \). What is its horizontal range? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to fall: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \Rightarrow 24.5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times t^2 \Rightarrow 24.5 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 5 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.24 \, \text{s} \). Horizontal range \( R = v_x t = 12 \times 2.24 \approx 26.88 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched with a speed of \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) at an angle of \( 60^\circ \) to the horizontal. What is its maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 15 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_0 \sin \theta_0 = 15 \times 0.866 \approx 12.99 \, \text{m/s} \). \( h_m = \frac{(12.99)^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{168.74}{20} \approx 8.44 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: For an object moving in a plane with constant acceleration, what is true about its velocity vector?
options: It changes in magnitude and/or direction
questions.explanation: In motion with constant acceleration in a plane, the velocity vector changes in magnitude and/or direction over time because the acceleration continuously alters it. Unlike uniform motion, the velocity is not constant unless the acceleration is zero.

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is the condition for achieving maximum horizontal range on level ground?
questions.explanation: The horizontal range \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \) is maximized when \( \sin 2\theta_0 = 1 \), which occurs at \( 2\theta_0 = 90^\circ \) or \( \theta_0 = 45^\circ \). This angle balances the horizontal and vertical components for the greatest distance.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \))
questions.explanation: Time of flight \( T_f = \frac{2 v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 15 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 30^\circ = 0.5, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( T_f = \frac{2 \times 15 \times 0.5}{10} = \frac{15}{10} = 1.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown horizontally at \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 80 \, \text{m} \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical motion: \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), where \( y = -80 \, \text{m} \). \( -80 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \Rightarrow -80 = 5 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 16 \Rightarrow t = 4 \, \text{s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 8

questions.question_text: An object moves in a circle of radius 2 m with a constant speed of 4 m/s. What is its angular speed?
questions.explanation: Angular speed ω = v / R. Given: v = 4 m/s, R = 2 m. ω = 4 / 2 = 2 rad/s.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 45^\circ \) from a height of \( 5 \, \text{m} \). What is its range? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time of flight: \( y = v_{0y} t - \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), where \( y = -5 \, \text{m}, v_{0y} = 20 \sin 45^\circ = 10\sqrt{2} \). \( -5 = 10\sqrt{2} t - 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 10\sqrt{2} t - 5 = 0 \Rightarrow t^2 - 2\sqrt{2} t - 1 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{2\sqrt{2} \pm \sqrt{8 + 4}}{2} = \frac{2\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{12}}{2} = \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3} \approx 3.146 \, \text{s} \). Range \( R = v_{0x} t = 20 \cos 45^\circ \times 3.146 = 10\sqrt{2} \times 3.146 \approx 44.41 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle starts with velocity \( 5 \hat{i} \, \text{m/s} \) and accelerates at \( (-3 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its displacement magnitude after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Displacement \( \mathbf{r} = \mathbf{v}_0 t + \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{a} t^2 \). \( x = v_{0x} t = 5 \times 2 = 10 \, \text{m} \). \( y = \frac{1}{2} a_y t^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times (-3) \times 2^2 = -6 \, \text{m} \). Magnitude \( |\mathbf{r}| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{100 + 36} = \sqrt{136} \approx 11.66 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: An object in uniform circular motion has a centripetal acceleration of 16 m/s² and a radius of 4 m. What is its linear speed?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a_c = v² / R. Given: a_c = 16 m/s², R = 4 m. 16 = v² / 4 ⇒ v² = 64 ⇒ v = √64 = 8 m/s.

questions.question_text: A car moves north at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) while a wind blows east at \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the car’s velocity relative to the ground?
questions.explanation: Velocity components: \( v_x = 5 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 12 \, \text{m/s} \). Magnitude \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circle of radius \( 5 \, \text{m} \) with an angular speed of \( 2 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R \). Given: \( \omega = 2 \, \text{rad/s}, R = 5 \, \text{m} \). \( a_c = 2^2 \times 5 = 4 \times 5 = 20 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from a height of \( 44.1 \, \text{m} \) with a horizontal speed of \( 7 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its speed on hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity: \( v_y = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 44.1} = \sqrt{863.28} \approx 29.38 \, \text{m/s} \). Horizontal velocity: \( v_x = 7 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{7^2 + 29.38^2} = \sqrt{49 + 863.28} = \sqrt{912.28} \approx 30.2 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in circular motion has a centripetal acceleration of \( 36 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) and radius \( 2 \, \text{m} \). What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( a_c = 36 \, \text{m/s}^2, R = 2 \, \text{m} \). \( 36 = \frac{v^2}{2} \Rightarrow v^2 = 72 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2} \approx 8.49 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the effect on the range of a projectile if the launch angle is increased beyond 45° on level ground?
questions.explanation: The range \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \) is maximized at \( \theta_0 = 45^\circ \) (when \( 2\theta_0 = 90^\circ \)). Beyond 45°, \( \sin 2\theta_0 \) decreases (e.g., at 60°, \( 2\theta_0 = 120^\circ \), \( \sin 120^\circ < 1 \)), reducing the range.

questions.question_text: A cyclist moves east at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) while the wind blows south at \( 24 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the relative velocity of the wind with respect to the cyclist?
questions.explanation: Relative velocity \( \mathbf{v}_{wc} = \mathbf{v}_w - \mathbf{v}_c \), where \( \mathbf{v}_c = 18 \hat{i}, \mathbf{v}_w = -24 \hat{j} \). \( \mathbf{v}_{wc} = -24 \hat{j} - 18 \hat{i} = -18 \hat{i} - 24 \hat{j} \). Magnitude \( |\mathbf{v}_{wc}| = \sqrt{(-18)^2 + (-24)^2} = \sqrt{324 + 576} = \sqrt{900} = 30 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 9

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is its range? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \))

A projectile is launched with a speed of \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) at an angle of \( 37^\circ \) to the horizontal. What is the time taken to reach its maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \), \( \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: Time to maximum height is given by \( t_m = \frac{v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 25 \, \text{m/s}, \theta_0 = 37^\circ, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( t_m = \frac{25 \times 0.6}{10} = \frac{15}{10} = 1.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary reason a projectile follows a curved path?
questions.explanation: The curved (parabolic) path of a projectile results from the constant acceleration due to gravity acting vertically, while the horizontal motion remains uniform. This combination of uniform horizontal motion and accelerated vertical motion produces the curve.

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is the relationship between centripetal force and the object’s mass?
options: It is proportional to mass squared
questions.explanation: The centripetal force is given by \( F_c = m \frac{v^2}{R} = m a_c \), where \( m \) is the mass. Thus, the centripetal force is directly proportional to the mass of the object, meaning a greater mass requires a larger force to maintain the same motion.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 35 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is its range? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 120^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Range \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \), where \( 2\theta_0 = 120^\circ \). Given: \( v_0 = 35 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 120^\circ = 0.866, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( R = \frac{35^2 \times 0.866}{10} = \frac{1225 \times 0.866}{10} \approx \frac{1060.85}{10} \approx 106.09 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the nature of the acceleration in uniform circular motion?
options: Constant in magnitude but not direction
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal, meaning it is directed towards the center of the circle. It changes direction continuously to remain radial but maintains a constant magnitude, as the speed is constant.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally at \( 9 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 44.1 \, \text{m} \). What is its speed on hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity: \( v_y = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 44.1} = \sqrt{863.28} \approx 29.38 \, \text{m/s} \). Horizontal velocity: \( v_x = 9 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{9^2 + 29.38^2} = \sqrt{81 + 863.28} = \sqrt{944.28} \approx 30.73 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, at what point is the speed of the projectile minimum?
questions.explanation: The speed of a projectile is minimum at its maximum height because the vertical component of velocity (\( v_y \)) is zero, leaving only the horizontal component (\( v_x \)), which is constant. At all other points, the speed includes both components.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 45 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is its speed at the maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \))
questions.explanation: At maximum height, \( v_y = 0 \), speed = \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 45 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \). \( v_x = 45 \times 0.5 = 22.5 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its speed at maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: At maximum height, speed = \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 50 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \). \( v_x = 50 \times 0.8 = 40 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 10

questions.question_text: A particle in circular motion has a centripetal acceleration of \( 100 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) and speed of \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its radius?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( a_c = 100 \, \text{m/s}^2, v = 20 \, \text{m/s} \). \( 100 = \frac{20^2}{R} \Rightarrow 100 = \frac{400}{R} \Rightarrow R = \frac{400}{100} = 4 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 26 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 45^\circ \). What is its time to reach maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to maximum height \( t_m = \frac{v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 26 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( t_m = \frac{26 \times 0.707}{10} \approx \frac{18.382}{10} \approx 1.84 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown horizontally at \( 7 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 31.25 \, \text{m} \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical motion: \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), where \( y = -31.25 \, \text{m} \). \( -31.25 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \Rightarrow -31.25 = 5 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 6.25 \Rightarrow t = 2.5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in circular motion has a centripetal acceleration of \( 25 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) and radius \( 5 \, \text{m} \). What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( a_c = 25 \, \text{m/s}^2, R = 5 \, \text{m} \). \( 25 = \frac{v^2}{5} \Rightarrow v^2 = 125 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{125} \approx 11.18 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from a height of \( 20 \, \text{m} \) with a horizontal speed of \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its horizontal distance from the drop point when it lands? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to fall: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \Rightarrow 20 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 4 \Rightarrow t = 2 \, \text{s} \). Horizontal distance \( x = v_x t = 10 \times 2 = 20 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: In motion with constant acceleration in a plane, what determines the path of the object?
questions.explanation: The path of an object in motion with constant acceleration in a plane depends on its initial velocity and the direction and magnitude of the constant acceleration. For example, zero initial velocity with constant acceleration results in a straight line, while non-zero initial velocity can produce a parabolic path (e.g., projectile motion).

questions.question_text: For an object in projectile motion, which component of acceleration is zero?
questions.explanation: In projectile motion, neglecting air resistance, the only acceleration is due to gravity, acting vertically downward. The horizontal component of acceleration is zero because there is no force acting horizontally to change the horizontal velocity.

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is the angle between the velocity and acceleration vectors at the highest point?
questions.explanation: At the highest point, the velocity is purely horizontal (\( v_y = 0 \)), while the acceleration (gravity) is vertical downward. Thus, the angle between them is 90°, as they are perpendicular.

questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest with a constant acceleration of (4 î + 2 ĵ) m/s². What is its speed after 5 s?
questions.explanation: Velocity v = v₀ + at, where v₀ = 0. Given: a = 4 î + 2 ĵ, t = 5 s. v = (4 î + 2 ĵ) × 5 = 20 î + 10 ĵ m/s. Speed v = √(v_x² + v_y²) = √(20² + 10²) = √(400 + 100) = √500 ≈ 22.36 m/s.

questions.question_text: A particle completes 5 revolutions in \( 2 \, \text{s} \) in a circular path of radius \( 0.8 \, \text{m} \). What is its linear speed?
questions.explanation: Frequency \( f = \frac{n}{t} = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5 \, \text{Hz} \). Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 2.5 = 5\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Linear speed \( v = \omega R = 5\pi \times 0.8 = 4\pi \approx 12.57 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 11

questions.question_text: A boat travels west at \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) while a current flows south at \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the boat’s velocity relative to the ground?
questions.explanation: Velocity components: \( v_x = -6 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = -8 \, \text{m/s} \). Magnitude \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(-6)^2 + (-8)^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is true about the direction of the net force relative to the velocity?
questions.explanation: The net force (centripetal force) in uniform circular motion is perpendicular to the velocity vector, as it acts towards the center of the circle, while the velocity is tangential, ensuring the object follows a circular path.

questions.question_text: A particle moves in the x-y plane with a constant acceleration of (2 î + 3 ĵ) m/s². If it starts from rest at the origin, what is its speed after 2 s?
questions.explanation: Velocity is given by v = v₀ + at, where v₀ = 0 (starts from rest). Given: a = 2 î + 3 ĵ, t = 2 s. v = 0 + (2 î + 3 ĵ) × 2 = 4 î + 6 ĵ m/s. Speed v = √(v_x² + v_y²) = √(4² + 6²) = √(16 + 36) = √52 ≈ 7.21 m/s.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched with a speed of \( 32 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to the horizontal. What is its maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 32 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_0 \sin \theta_0 = 32 \times 0.866 \approx 27.712 \, \text{m/s} \). \( h_m = \frac{(27.712)^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{767.95}{20} \approx 38.4 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A boy throws a ball with a speed of 20 m/s at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. What is the maximum height reached by the ball? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Maximum height is given by h_m = (v₀ sin θ₀)² / (2g). Given: v₀ = 20 m/s, θ₀ = 30°, g = 10 m/s². sin 30° = 0.5, so v₀ sin θ₀ = 20 × 0.5 = 10 m/s. h_m = (10)² / (2 × 10) = 100 / 20 = 5 m.

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is the effect of launching at complementary angles (e.g., 30° and 60°) on the range?
questions.explanation: For complementary angles (\( \theta \) and \( 90^\circ - \theta \)), \( \sin 2\theta = \sin (180^\circ - 2\theta) \), so \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta}{g} \) is the same (e.g., \( \sin 60^\circ = \sin 120^\circ \)). Thus, the range remains the same for complementary angles.

questions.question_text: For an object in uniform circular motion, what is the direction of the velocity vector relative to the acceleration vector?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the velocity vector is tangential to the circular path, while the centripetal acceleration is directed towards the center. Thus, the velocity and acceleration vectors are perpendicular to each other at every point.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 45^\circ \). What is its time to reach maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 45^\circ = 0.707 \))
questions.explanation: Time to maximum height \( t_m = \frac{v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 30 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 45^\circ = 0.707, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( t_m = \frac{30 \times 0.707}{10} \approx \frac{21.21}{10} \approx 2.12 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched with a speed of 50 m/s at 45°. What is its horizontal range? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Range R = (v₀² sin 2θ₀) / g. Given: v₀ = 50 m/s, θ₀ = 45°, sin 90° = 1, g = 10 m/s². R = (50² × 1) / 10 = 2500 / 10 = 250 m.

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is true about the horizontal component of velocity throughout the trajectory?
options: It becomes zero at the peak
questions.explanation: In projectile motion, assuming no air resistance, the horizontal component of velocity remains constant because there is no horizontal acceleration. Gravity acts only vertically, leaving the horizontal motion unaffected.

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 12

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 18 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is its range? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Range \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \), where \( 2\theta_0 = 60^\circ, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \). Given: \( v_0 = 18 \, \text{m/s}, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( R = \frac{18^2 \times 0.866}{9.8} = \frac{324 \times 0.866}{9.8} \approx 28.63 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle completes 10 revolutions in \( 5 \, \text{s} \) in a circular path of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \). What is its linear speed?
questions.explanation: Frequency \( f = \frac{n}{t} = \frac{10}{5} = 2 \, \text{Hz} \). Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 2 = 4\pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Linear speed \( v = \omega R = 4\pi \times 1.5 = 6\pi \approx 18.85 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the shape of the path followed by a projectile under the influence of gravity alone?
questions.explanation: The path of a projectile under gravity alone is a parabola. This results from the horizontal motion being uniform (constant velocity) and the vertical motion being uniformly accelerated due to gravity, combining to form a parabolic trajectory.

questions.question_text: What is true about the angular speed in uniform circular motion if the period of revolution increases?
questions.explanation: Angular speed is \( \omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} \), where \( T \) is the period. If the period increases, \( \omega \) decreases because they are inversely proportional; a longer period means fewer revolutions per unit time.

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what causes the acceleration of the object?
questions.explanation: The acceleration in uniform circular motion is centripetal, caused by a force (e.g., tension, gravity, friction) directed towards the center of the circle. This force continuously changes the direction of the velocity, maintaining circular motion.

questions.question_text: In motion with constant acceleration in a plane, what happens if the acceleration is opposite to the initial velocity?
options: The object moves in a circle
The object slows, reverses, and accelerates
questions.explanation: If the acceleration is opposite to the initial velocity, the object slows down, reverses direction, and then accelerates in the direction of the acceleration along a straight line. The path remains linear but with a change in direction.

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what happens to the object’s motion if its speed doubles while the radius remains constant?
questions.explanation: If the speed doubles (\( v' = 2v \)) and the radius remains constant, the centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \) increases by a factor of four (\( a_c' = \frac{(2v)^2}{R} = 4 \frac{v^2}{R} \)), as it is proportional to the square of the speed.

questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest with a constant acceleration of \( (4 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 5 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \), with \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = 4 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j}, t = 5 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = (4 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j}) \times 5 = 20 \hat{i} - 15 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{20^2 + (-15)^2} = \sqrt{400 + 225} = \sqrt{625} = 25 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between the velocity and acceleration vectors in uniform circular motion?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the velocity vector is tangential to the path, while the acceleration vector (centripetal) is directed towards the center. This perpendicular relationship ensures the object maintains a circular path with constant speed.

questions.question_text: A particle starts with velocity \( 7 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \) and accelerates at \( (3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \). Given: \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 7 \hat{j}, \mathbf{a} = 3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}, t = 2 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = 7 \hat{j} + (3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) \times 2 = 6 \hat{i} + (7 - 4) \hat{j} = 6 \hat{i} + 3 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{6^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{36 + 9} = \sqrt{45} \approx 6.71 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 13

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 24 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \) to the horizontal. What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 9.6 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Time of flight \( T_f = \frac{2 v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 24 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866, g = 9.6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( T_f = \frac{2 \times 24 \times 0.866}{9.6} = \frac{41.568}{9.6} \approx 4.33 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is the direction of acceleration throughout the trajectory?
questions.explanation: The acceleration in projectile motion, due to gravity, is always directed downward towards the Earth. It remains constant in magnitude and direction, acting vertically regardless of the projectile’s position or velocity.

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown horizontally at \( 14 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 39.2 \, \text{m} \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical motion: \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), where \( y = -39.2 \, \text{m} \). \( -39.2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times t^2 \Rightarrow -39.2 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 8 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally at \( 11 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 19.6 \, \text{m} \). What is its speed on hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity: \( v_y = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 19.6} = \sqrt{384.16} \approx 19.6 \, \text{m/s} \). Horizontal velocity: \( v_x = 11 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{11^2 + 19.6^2} = \sqrt{121 + 384.16} = \sqrt{505.16} \approx 22.47 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its speed at maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: At maximum height, speed = \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 40 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 37^\circ = 0.8 \). \( v_x = 40 \times 0.8 = 32 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: For an object in uniform circular motion, what is the direction of its acceleration?
options: Towards the center of the circle
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal, always directed towards the center of the circular path. This is because the velocity vector changes direction continuously, and the acceleration is perpendicular to the velocity, pointing inward.

questions.question_text: What is the primary factor determining the range of a projectile launched from level ground?
questions.explanation: The range of a projectile depends on the launch angle and initial speed, as given by \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \). The angle \( \theta_0 \) maximizes the range when \( 2\theta_0 = 90^\circ \) (i.e., \( \theta_0 = 45^\circ \)), making it a critical factor alongside speed.

questions.question_text: A particle in circular motion has a centripetal acceleration of \( 64 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) and radius \( 4 \, \text{m} \). What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( a_c = 64 \, \text{m/s}^2, R = 4 \, \text{m} \). \( 64 = \frac{v^2}{4} \Rightarrow v^2 = 256 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{256} = 16 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary reason an object in uniform circular motion does not move towards the center?
options: Tangential velocity keeps it in orbit
questions.explanation: The object does not move towards the center because its tangential velocity provides the inertia to maintain the circular path. The centripetal force only changes the direction of this velocity, not its magnitude, balancing the tendency to move outward.

questions.question_text: An object completes 5 revolutions in 10 s in a circular path of radius 3 m. What is its linear speed?
questions.explanation: Angular speed ω = (2π n) / t = (2π × 5) / 10 = π rad/s. Linear speed v = ω R = π × 3 ≈ 3.14 × 3 ≈ 9.42 m/s.

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 14

questions.question_text: A car moves at 72 km/h in a circular path of radius 50 m. What is its centripetal acceleration? (Take 72 km/h = 20 m/s)
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a_c = v² / R. Given: v = 20 m/s, R = 50 m. a_c = (20)² / 50 = 400 / 50 = 8 m/s².

questions.question_text: A car moves in a circle of radius \( 10 \, \text{m} \) with a speed of \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its angular speed?
questions.explanation: Angular speed \( \omega = \frac{v}{R} \). Given: \( v = 5 \, \text{m/s}, R = 10 \, \text{m} \). \( \omega = \frac{5}{10} = 0.5 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of \( (3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \) from rest. What is the magnitude of its velocity after \( 4 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \), with \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = 3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}, t = 4 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = (3 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) \times 4 = 12 \hat{i} - 8 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + (-8)^2} = \sqrt{144 + 64} = \sqrt{208} \approx 14.42 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: An object in uniform circular motion has a period of \( 2 \, \text{s} \) and a radius of \( 8 \, \text{m} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Angular speed \( \omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R = (\pi)^2 \times 8 \approx 9.87 \times 8 \approx 78.96 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves with an initial velocity of \( 4 \hat{i} \, \text{m/s} \) and an acceleration of \( (2 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its speed after \( 3 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a} t \). Given: \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 4 \hat{i}, \mathbf{a} = 2 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j}, t = 3 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{v} = 4 \hat{i} + (2 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j}) \times 3 = 4 \hat{i} + 6 \hat{i} - 9 \hat{j} = 10 \hat{i} - 9 \hat{j} \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{10^2 + (-9)^2} = \sqrt{100 + 81} = \sqrt{181} \approx 13.45 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at \( 15 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is its vertical velocity after \( 1 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity \( v_y = v_0 \sin \theta_0 - g t \). Given: \( v_0 = 15 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866, t = 1 \, \text{s}, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_y = 15 \times 0.866 - 10 \times 1 = 12.99 - 10 \approx 2.99 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is true about the potential energy of a projectile at its maximum height?
questions.explanation: At the maximum height, the potential energy of a projectile is at its maximum because the height is greatest, and the vertical kinetic energy is zero (\( v_y = 0 \)). This maximizes the gravitational potential energy (\( mgh \)).

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is the effect of increasing the radius while keeping the speed constant?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is given by \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). If speed (\( v \)) remains constant and radius (\( R \)) increases, \( a_c \) decreases because it is inversely proportional to the radius, requiring less force to maintain the motion.

questions.question_text: A ball is projected horizontally at \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 125 \, \text{m} \). What is the time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical motion: \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), where \( y = -125 \, \text{m} \). \( -125 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \Rightarrow -125 = 5 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 25 \Rightarrow t = 5 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 40 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 45^\circ \) from a height of \( 10 \, \text{m} \). What is its range? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 45^\circ = 0.707 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical motion: \( y = v_{0y} t - \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), where \( y = -10, v_{0y} = 40 \times 0.707 \approx 28.28 \). \( -10 = 28.28 t - 5 t^2 \Rightarrow 5 t^2 - 28.28 t - 10 = 0 \). Solve: \( t = \frac{28.28 \pm \sqrt{799.76 + 200}}{10} = \frac{28.28 \pm 31.62}{10} \), \( t \approx 5.99 \, \text{s} \) (positive root). Range \( R = v_{0x} t = 28.28 \times 5.99 \approx 169.39 \, \text{m} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 15

questions.question_text: A particle in circular motion has a centripetal acceleration of \( 25 \, \text{m/s}^2 \) and a speed of \( 10 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the radius of the path?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( a_c = 25 \, \text{m/s}^2, v = 10 \, \text{m/s} \). \( 25 = \frac{10^2}{R} \Rightarrow 25 = \frac{100}{R} \Rightarrow R = \frac{100}{25} = 4 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched with a speed of 40 m/s at an angle of 30°. What is its velocity at the highest point? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: At the highest point, v_y = 0, v_x = v₀ cos θ₀. Given: v₀ = 40 m/s, cos 30° = √3/2. v_x = 40 × (√3/2) = 20 √3 ≈ 34.64 m/s.

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circular path with a period of \( 4 \, \text{s} \) and radius \( 6 \, \text{m} \). What is its linear speed?
questions.explanation: Angular speed \( \omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2} \, \text{rad/s} \). Linear speed \( v = \omega R = \frac{\pi}{2} \times 6 = 3\pi \approx 9.42 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 19.6 \, \text{m} \). What is its speed on hitting the ground? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity: \( v_y = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 19.6} = \sqrt{384.16} \approx 19.6 \, \text{m/s} \). Horizontal velocity: \( v_x = 12 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + 19.6^2} = \sqrt{144 + 384.16} = \sqrt{528.16} \approx 22.98 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is the relationship between the velocity vector and the path of the object?
options: It is tangential to the path
It is radial towards the center
It is radial away from the center
It is perpendicular to the plane of motion
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the velocity vector is always tangential to the circular path, directed along the instantaneous direction of motion, perpendicular to the radius at every point.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 25 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its vertical velocity at \( t = 1 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity \( v_y = v_0 \sin \theta_0 - g t \). Given: \( v_0 = 25 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6, t = 1 \, \text{s}, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_y = 25 \times 0.6 - 10 \times 1 = 15 - 10 = 5 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In motion with constant acceleration in a plane, what is true about the acceleration vector?
options: It is constant in magnitude and direction
questions.explanation: The acceleration vector in motion with constant acceleration remains constant in both magnitude and direction. This allows the motion to be analyzed as two independent one-dimensional motions along perpendicular axes.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 34 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is its horizontal range? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 120^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Range \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \), where \( 2\theta_0 = 120^\circ \). Given: \( v_0 = 34 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 120^\circ = 0.866, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( R = \frac{34^2 \times 0.866}{9.8} = \frac{1156 \times 0.866}{9.8} \approx \frac{1001.096}{9.8} \approx 102.15 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle has an initial velocity of 3 î m/s and a constant acceleration of 2 ĵ m/s². What is the magnitude of its displacement after 3 s?
questions.explanation: Displacement r = v₀ t + (1/2) a t². x = v₀x t = 3 × 3 = 9 m. y = (1/2) a_y t² = (1/2) × 2 × 3² = 9 m. Magnitude |r| = √(x² + y²) = √(9² + 9²) = √162 ≈ 12.73 m.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 26 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \). What is its horizontal velocity component? (Take \( \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 26 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \). \( v_x = 26 \times 0.6 = 15.6 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 16

questions.question_text: A particle in uniform circular motion has a radius of \( 10 \, \text{m} \) and completes 4 revolutions in \( 8 \, \text{s} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Frequency \( f = \frac{n}{t} = \frac{4}{8} = 0.5 \, \text{Hz} \). Angular speed \( \omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 0.5 = \pi \, \text{rad/s} \). Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \omega^2 R = (\pi)^2 \times 10 \approx 9.87 \times 10 \approx 98.7 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: For an object in uniform circular motion, what happens if the centripetal force suddenly disappears?
options: It moves in a straight line tangentially
questions.explanation: If the centripetal force disappears, the object will move tangentially to the circle in a straight line due to inertia (Newton’s first law). Without the force, there is no acceleration to keep it in the circular path.

questions.question_text: A ball is projected with a speed of \( 28 \, \text{m/s} \) at an angle of \( 45^\circ \) to the horizontal. What is the maximum height attained? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 28 \, \text{m/s}, \theta_0 = 45^\circ, \sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_0 \sin \theta_0 = 28 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 14\sqrt{2} \approx 19.8 \, \text{m/s} \). \( h_m = \frac{(19.8)^2}{2 \times 9.8} = \frac{392.04}{19.6} \approx 20 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown horizontally at \( 20 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 45 \, \text{m} \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical motion: \( y = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \), where \( y = -45 \, \text{m} \). \( -45 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \Rightarrow -45 = 5 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 9 \Rightarrow t = 3 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A boat sails east at \( 8 \, \text{m/s} \) while a current flows north at \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the boat’s velocity relative to the ground?
questions.explanation: Velocity components: \( v_x = 8 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 6 \, \text{m/s} \). Magnitude \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 50 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \). What is its speed at maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: At maximum height, speed = \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 50 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 53^\circ = 0.6 \). \( v_x = 50 \times 0.6 = 30 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 22 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is its horizontal velocity component?
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 22 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866 \). \( v_x = 22 \times 0.866 \approx 19.05 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched with a speed of 30 m/s at 30°. What is its horizontal velocity component?
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity v_x = v₀ cos θ₀. Given: v₀ = 30 m/s, cos 30° = √3/2. v_x = 30 × (√3/2) = 15 √3 ≈ 25.98 m/s.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 16 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is its time to reach maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Time to maximum height \( t_m = \frac{v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 16 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( t_m = \frac{16 \times 0.866}{10} \approx \frac{13.856}{10} \approx 1.39 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, what is true about the work done by the centripetal force?
questions.explanation: The centripetal force is always perpendicular to the velocity (tangential) in uniform circular motion. Since work is the dot product of force and displacement, and the displacement is along the velocity, the work done is zero (force and displacement are perpendicular).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 17

questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest with an acceleration of \( (4 \hat{i} + 3 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its displacement magnitude after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Displacement \( \mathbf{r} = \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{a} t^2 \) (since \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \)). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = 4 \hat{i} + 3 \hat{j}, t = 2 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{r} = \frac{1}{2} (4 \hat{i} + 3 \hat{j}) \times 2^2 = 2 (4 \hat{i} + 3 \hat{j}) = 8 \hat{i} + 6 \hat{j} \, \text{m} \). Magnitude \( |\mathbf{r}| = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: For a projectile launched at an angle, what is true about the horizontal and vertical motions?
questions.explanation: The horizontal and vertical motions in projectile motion are independent of each other. The horizontal motion is uniform (constant velocity), while the vertical motion is uniformly accelerated due to gravity, allowing separate analysis of each component.

questions.question_text: A particle’s position is given by \( x = 2t^2 + 3t \) and \( y = t^2 - 2t \) (in meters and seconds). What is the magnitude of its velocity at \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v_x = \frac{dx}{dt} = 4t + 3, v_y = \frac{dy}{dt} = 2t - 2 \). At \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \): \( v_x = 4 \times 2 + 3 = 11 \, \text{m/s}, v_y = 2 \times 2 - 2 = 2 \, \text{m/s} \). Speed \( v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{11^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{121 + 4} = \sqrt{125} \approx 11.18 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: In projectile motion, what is conserved throughout the trajectory if air resistance is negligible?
questions.explanation: With negligible air resistance, the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) is conserved in projectile motion. Energy transforms between kinetic and potential forms, but the sum remains constant as gravity is a conservative force.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown horizontally at \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \) from a height of \( 4.9 \, \text{m} \). What is its horizontal range? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \))
questions.explanation: Time to fall: \( h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \Rightarrow 4.9 = \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times t^2 \Rightarrow 4.9 = 4.9 t^2 \Rightarrow t^2 = 1 \Rightarrow t = 1 \, \text{s} \). Horizontal range \( R = v_x t = 6 \times 1 = 6 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circular path of radius \( 3 \, \text{m} \) with a speed of \( 6 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its angular speed?
questions.explanation: Angular speed \( \omega = \frac{v}{R} \). Given: \( v = 6 \, \text{m/s}, R = 3 \, \text{m} \). \( \omega = \frac{6}{3} = 2 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary factor affecting the time of flight of a projectile launched from level ground?
questions.explanation: The time of flight of a projectile depends on the initial vertical velocity component (\( v_0 \sin \theta_0 \)) and gravity (\( g \)), as given by \( T_f = \frac{2 v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). The vertical component determines how long the projectile stays in the air.

questions.question_text: A stone is dropped from a cliff 45 m high with an initial horizontal speed of 15 m/s. What is its speed on hitting the ground? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity: v_x = 15 m/s (constant). Vertical velocity: v_y = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 45) = √900 = 30 m/s. Speed v = √(v_x² + v_y²) = √(15² + 30²) = √(225 + 900) = √1125 ≈ 33.54 m/s.

questions.question_text: What is the physical significance of the time of flight being zero for a projectile?
options: It is launched horizontally from ground
questions.explanation: A time of flight of zero occurs when the initial vertical velocity component (\( v_0 \sin \theta_0 \)) is zero, meaning the projectile is launched horizontally (\( \theta_0 = 0^\circ \)) from ground level, resulting in no vertical displacement and immediate landing.

questions.question_text: A particle moves in a circle of radius \( 1.5 \, \text{m} \) with a speed of \( 3 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration \( a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} \). Given: \( v = 3 \, \text{m/s}, R = 1.5 \, \text{m} \). \( a_c = \frac{3^2}{1.5} = \frac{9}{1.5} = 6 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

tests.title: Motion in a Plane Chapter-Wise Test 18

questions.question_text: What is the significance of the angle of projection in determining the maximum height of a projectile?
options: It influences the vertical velocity component
questions.explanation: The maximum height \( h_m = \frac{(v_0 \sin \theta_0)^2}{2g} \) depends on the vertical component of the initial velocity (\( v_0 \sin \theta_0 \)). The angle of projection determines this component, with larger angles (up to 90°) increasing the height by maximizing the vertical contribution.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 14 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Time of flight \( T_f = \frac{2 v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 14 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( T_f = \frac{2 \times 14 \times 0.8}{9.8} = \frac{22.4}{9.8} \approx 2.29 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at \( 22 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 60^\circ \). What is its vertical velocity at \( t = 1.5 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: Vertical velocity \( v_y = v_0 \sin \theta_0 - g t \). Given: \( v_0 = 22 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866, t = 1.5 \, \text{s}, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( v_y = 22 \times 0.866 - 10 \times 1.5 = 19.052 - 15 = 4.05 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle starts from rest with an acceleration of \( (5 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its displacement magnitude after \( 3 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Displacement \( \mathbf{r} = \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{a} t^2 \) (since \( \mathbf{v}_0 = 0 \)). Given: \( \mathbf{a} = 5 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}, t = 3 \, \text{s} \). \( \mathbf{r} = \frac{1}{2} (5 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) \times 3^2 = \frac{9}{2} (5 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j}) = 22.5 \hat{i} - 9 \hat{j} \, \text{m} \). Magnitude \( |\mathbf{r}| = \sqrt{22.5^2 + (-9)^2} = \sqrt{506.25 + 81} = \sqrt{587.25} \approx 24.23 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: In uniform circular motion, which quantity is constant in direction?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration is centripetal and always directed towards the center of the circle. Its magnitude is constant, but its direction changes to remain radial. The speed (magnitude of velocity) is constant, while the velocity direction and acceleration direction are not.

questions.question_text: A ball is projected at \( 30 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 53^\circ \). What is the time to reach maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8 \))
questions.explanation: Time to maximum height \( t_m = \frac{v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 30 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 53^\circ = 0.8, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( t_m = \frac{30 \times 0.8}{10} = \frac{24}{10} = 2.4 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 12 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its time of flight? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6 \))
questions.explanation: Time of flight \( T_f = \frac{2 v_0 \sin \theta_0}{g} \). Given: \( v_0 = 12 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6, g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( T_f = \frac{2 \times 12 \times 0.6}{10} = \frac{14.4}{10} = 1.44 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 45 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 30^\circ \). What is its speed at maximum height? (Take \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2, \cos 30^\circ = 0.866 \))
questions.explanation: At maximum height, speed = \( v_x = v_0 \cos \theta_0 \). Given: \( v_0 = 45 \, \text{m/s}, \cos 30^\circ = 0.866 \). \( v_x = 45 \times 0.866 \approx 38.97 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched at \( 36 \, \text{m/s} \) at \( 37^\circ \). What is its horizontal range? (Take \( g = 12 \, \text{m/s}^2, \sin 74^\circ = 0.96 \))
questions.explanation: Range \( R = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta_0}{g} \), where \( 2\theta_0 = 74^\circ \). Given: \( v_0 = 36 \, \text{m/s}, \sin 74^\circ = 0.96, g = 12 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). \( R = \frac{36^2 \times 0.96}{12} = \frac{1296 \times 0.96}{12} = \frac{1244.16}{12} \approx 103.68 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: For an object moving in a plane with constant acceleration, what can be said about its path if the acceleration is perpendicular to the initial velocity?
questions.explanation: If the constant acceleration is perpendicular to the initial velocity, the path becomes a parabola. This is because the acceleration affects only one component (e.g., vertical in projectile motion), while the other (e.g., horizontal) remains uniform, resulting in a parabolic trajectory.

questions.question_text: A spring of \( k = 1000 \, \text{N/m} \) has a \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) mass. If \( E = 5 \, \text{J} \), what is the amplitude?
questions.explanation: Total energy: \( E = \frac{1}{2} k A^2 \). \( 5 = 0.5 \times 1000 \times A^2 \Rightarrow 5 = 500 A^2 \Rightarrow A^2 = 0.01 \Rightarrow A = 0.1 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A simple pendulum of length \( 0.25 \, \text{m} \) oscillates on Earth (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)). What is its period?
questions.explanation: Period: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} \). \( T = 2 \times 3.14 \sqrt{\frac{0.25}{9.8}} = 6.28 \sqrt{0.0255} \approx 6.28 \times 0.16 \approx 1.0 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A mass oscillates with \( v = -15 \sin (6t) \) (in m/s). What is its amplitude?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v = -\omega A \sin (\omega t) \). \( \omega = 6 \, \text{s}^{-1}, v_{\text{max}} = \omega A = 15 \Rightarrow A = \frac{15}{6} = 2.5 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A spring of \( k = 180 \, \text{N/m} \) has a \( 0.9 \, \text{kg} \) mass. If \( E = 0.9 \, \text{J} \), what is the amplitude?
questions.explanation: Total energy: \( E = \frac{1}{2} k A^2 \). \( 0.9 = 0.5 \times 180 \times A^2 \Rightarrow 0.9 = 90 A^2 \Rightarrow A^2 = 0.01 \Rightarrow A = 0.1 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 7 \cos (5t) \) (in m). What is its maximum acceleration?
questions.explanation: Maximum acceleration: \( a_{\text{max}} = \omega^2 A \). \( A = 7 \, \text{m}, \omega = 5 \, \text{s}^{-1} \). \( a_{\text{max}} = 5^2 \times 7 = 25 \times 7 = 175 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 4 \cos (2t + \frac{\pi}{2}) \) (in m). What is its acceleration at \( t = 0 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Acceleration: \( a = -\omega^2 x \). \( \omega = 2 \, \text{s}^{-1}, x(0) = 4 \cos (\frac{\pi}{2}) = 4 \times 0 = 0 \, \text{m} \). \( a = -2^2 \times 0 = 0 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 6 \sin (3t - \frac{\pi}{4}) \) (in m). What is its acceleration at \( t = 0 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( \cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \))
questions.explanation: Acceleration: \( a = -\omega^2 x \). \( \omega = 3 \, \text{s}^{-1}, x(0) = 6 \sin (-\frac{\pi}{4}) = -6 \sin \frac{\pi}{4} = -6 \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \approx -4.24 \, \text{m} \). \( a = -3^2 \times (-4.24) = 9 \times 4.24 \approx 38.16 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: Which of the following motions is periodic but does not exhibit oscillatory behavior about a fixed point?
options: A mass oscillating on a spring
A planet orbiting in a circular path
A pendulum swinging with small amplitude
questions.explanation: Uniform circular motion is periodic (repeats after a fixed time) but not oscillatory, as it does not involve to-and-fro motion about a mean position, unlike SHM examples.

questions.question_text: Which function represents periodic but not simple harmonic motion? (\( \omega \) is a positive constant)
questions.explanation: SHM requires \( a = -\omega^2 x \): (a) \( \sin^2 \omega t = \frac{1 - \cos 2\omega t}{2} \): Periodic (period \( \frac{\pi}{\omega} \)), not SHM (not sinusoidal). (b) \( 3 \cos (\pi - \omega t) = -3 \cos (\omega t) \): SHM. (c) \( \sin \omega t \): SHM. (d) \( e^{\omega t} \): Not periodic.

questions.question_text: What distinguishes the restoring force in SHM from that in uniform circular motion?
options: It is linear with respect to displacement
questions.explanation: In SHM, the restoring force is linear (\( F = -kx \)), varying with displacement, while in uniform circular motion, the centripetal force is constant in magnitude and radial.

questions.question_text: In SHM, when is the magnitude of acceleration equal to zero?
questions.explanation: Acceleration \( a = -\omega^2 x \) is zero when \( x = 0 \), i.e., at the mean position, where the restoring force is absent.

questions.question_text: A pendulum of length \( 0.49 \, \text{m} \) oscillates with \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Period: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{0.49}{9.8}} = 2\pi \sqrt{0.05} \approx 1.404 \, \text{s} \). Frequency: \( v = \frac{1}{T} = \frac{1}{1.404} \approx 0.712 \, \text{Hz} \).

questions.question_text: A spring of \( k = 300 \, \text{N/m} \) has a \( 1.5 \, \text{kg} \) mass. If \( E = 0.75 \, \text{J} \), what is the amplitude?
questions.explanation: Total energy: \( E = \frac{1}{2} k A^2 \). \( 0.75 = 0.5 \times 300 \times A^2 \Rightarrow 0.75 = 150 A^2 \Rightarrow A^2 = 0.005 \Rightarrow A = \sqrt{0.005} \approx 0.071 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: In SHM, if the particle’s velocity is zero, what can be inferred about its position relative to the equilibrium?
options: It is at the maximum distance from equilibrium
It is at the equilibrium position
It is halfway between equilibrium and maximum
It depends on the initial phase
questions.explanation: Velocity is zero (\( v = -\omega A \sin (\omega t + \phi) = 0 \)) at the extreme positions (\( x = \pm A \)), where the particle is farthest from the equilibrium point.

questions.question_text: A spring-mass system oscillates with \( T = 0.5 \, \text{s} \) when \( m = 0.5 \, \text{kg} \). What is the spring constant?
questions.explanation: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}} \). \( 0.5 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{0.5}{k}} \Rightarrow \frac{0.5}{2\pi} = \sqrt{\frac{0.5}{k}} \). \( (0.0796)^2 = \frac{0.5}{k} \Rightarrow k = \frac{0.5}{0.00634} \approx 78.9 \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 5 \sin (2t) \) (in m). What is its speed at \( x = 2.5 \, \text{m} \)?
A mass of \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) is attached to a spring with \( k = 300 \, \text{N/m} \). If displaced by \( 15 \, \text{cm} \), what is the total energy?
A pendulum of length \( 0.8 \, \text{m} \) oscillates with \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Period: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{0.8}{10}} = 2\pi \sqrt{0.08} \approx 1.78 \, \text{s} \). Frequency: \( v = \frac{1}{T} = \frac{1}{1.78} \approx 0.562 \, \text{Hz} \).

questions.question_text: A pendulum has \( L = 0.64 \, \text{m}, g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its angular frequency?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{L}} = \sqrt{\frac{9.8}{0.64}} \approx \sqrt{15.31} \approx 3.91 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: Two identical springs (\( k = 70 \, \text{N/m} \)) are attached to a \( 1.4 \, \text{kg} \) mass as in Fig. 13.14. What is the frequency?
questions.explanation: Effective \( k_{\text{eff}} = 2k = 2 \times 70 = 140 \, \text{N/m} \). \( \omega = \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text{eff}}}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{140}{1.4}} = \sqrt{100} = 10 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( v = \frac{\omega}{2\pi} = \frac{10}{2 \times 3.14} \approx 1.59 \, \text{Hz} \).

questions.question_text: Two identical springs (\( k = 60 \, \text{N/m} \)) are attached to a \( 1.2 \, \text{kg} \) mass as in Fig. 13.14. What is the frequency?
questions.explanation: Effective \( k_{\text{eff}} = 2k = 2 \times 60 = 120 \, \text{N/m} \). \( \omega = \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text{eff}}}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{120}{1.2}} = \sqrt{100} = 10 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( v = \frac{\omega}{2\pi} = \frac{10}{2 \times 3.14} \approx 1.59 \, \text{Hz} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 5 \cos (2t + \frac{\pi}{4}) \) (in m). What is its acceleration at \( t = 0 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( \cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \))
questions.explanation: Acceleration: \( a = -\omega^2 x \). \( \omega = 2 \, \text{s}^{-1}, x(0) = 5 \cos \frac{\pi}{4} = 5 \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \approx 3.536 \, \text{m} \). \( a = -2^2 \times 3.536 = -4 \times 3.536 \approx -14.14 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has an amplitude of \( 10 \, \text{cm} \) and a frequency of \( 2.5 \, \text{Hz} \). What is its maximum velocity? (Take \( \pi = 3.14 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum velocity: \( v_{\text{max}} = A \omega \). \( \omega = 2\pi v = 2 \times 3.14 \times 2.5 = 15.7 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( A = 0.1 \, \text{m} \). \( v_{\text{max}} = 0.1 \times 15.7 = 1.57 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Two identical springs (\( k = 100 \, \text{N/m} \)) are attached to a \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) mass as in Fig. 13.14. What is the period?
questions.explanation: Net force: \( F = -2kx \), so effective \( k_{\text{eff}} = 2k = 200 \, \text{N/m} \). \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k_{\text{eff}}}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{1}{200}} \approx 0.44 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A simple pendulum has a length of \( 0.9 \, \text{m} \) and oscillates with \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its period?
questions.explanation: Period: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{0.9}{9.8}} \approx 2 \times 3.14 \sqrt{0.0918} \approx 1.9 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: In an ideal SHM system, what happens to the kinetic energy as the particle approaches the extreme position?
options: It becomes equal to the total energy
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy decreases as the particle approaches the extreme position, where velocity becomes zero, and potential energy reaches its maximum.

questions.question_text: The projection of a particle in circular motion on the x-axis is \( x = 3 \cos (2\pi t) \) (in m). What is the radius of the circular path?
questions.explanation: For SHM as projection of circular motion, radius = amplitude. Here, \( x = A \cos (\omega t) \), so \( A = 3 \, \text{m} \). Radius = \( 3 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 2 \sin (4t + \frac{\pi}{3}) \) (in m). What is its acceleration at \( t = 0 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( \cos \frac{\pi}{3} = 0.5 \))
questions.explanation: Acceleration: \( a = -\omega^2 x \). \( \omega = 4 \, \text{s}^{-1}, x(0) = 2 \sin \frac{\pi}{3} = 2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.732 \, \text{m} \). \( a = -4^2 \times 1.732 = -16 \times 1.732 \approx -27.71 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: What property of SHM allows its displacement to be expressed as a linear combination of sine and cosine functions?
questions.explanation: The harmonic nature of SHM, driven by a linear restoring force, results in sinusoidal motion, which can be written as \( x = A \sin (\omega t) + B \cos (\omega t) \), a general solution to the SHM differential equation.

questions.question_text: A spring-mass system has \( m = 0.5 \, \text{kg}, k = 200 \, \text{N/m} \). If the amplitude is \( 4 \, \text{cm} \), what is the total energy?
A spring-mass system oscillates with \( T = 0.9 \, \text{s} \) when \( m = 0.9 \, \text{kg} \). What is the spring constant?
questions.explanation: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}} \). \( 0.9 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{0.9}{k}} \Rightarrow \frac{0.9}{2\pi} = \sqrt{\frac{0.9}{k}} \). \( (0.1432)^2 = \frac{0.9}{k} \Rightarrow k = \frac{0.9}{0.0205} \approx 43.9 \, \text{N/m} \).

questions.question_text: A simple pendulum has a period of \( 1.8 \, \text{s} \) on Earth (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)). What is its length?
questions.explanation: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} \). \( 1.8 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{9.8}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{L}{9.8}} = \frac{1.8}{2\pi} \approx 0.2865 \). \( \frac{L}{9.8} = (0.2865)^2 \Rightarrow L \approx 9.8 \times 0.0821 \approx 0.805 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A simple pendulum oscillates with a frequency of \( 0.5 \, \text{Hz} \) on Earth (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)). What is its length?
questions.explanation: Period: \( T = \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{0.5} = 2 \, \text{s} \). \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} \Rightarrow 2 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{9.8}} \). \( \sqrt{\frac{L}{9.8}} = \frac{1}{\pi} \Rightarrow \frac{L}{9.8} = \frac{1}{\pi^2} \Rightarrow L \approx \frac{9.8}{9.87} \approx 0.99 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A spring of \( k = 250 \, \text{N/m} \) has a \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) mass. If \( E = 1.25 \, \text{J} \), what is the amplitude?
questions.explanation: Total energy: \( E = \frac{1}{2} k A^2 \). \( 1.25 = 0.5 \times 250 \times A^2 \Rightarrow 1.25 = 125 A^2 \Rightarrow A^2 = 0.01 \Rightarrow A = 0.1 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A mass oscillates with \( v = -15 \cos (3t) \) (in m/s). What is its amplitude?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v = -\omega A \sin (\omega t) \), but given \( v = -15 \cos (3t) \). \( \omega = 3 \, \text{s}^{-1}, v_{\text{max}} = \omega A = 15 \Rightarrow A = \frac{15}{3} = 5 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in circular motion has its x-projection as \( x = 7 \cos (\pi t) \) (in m). What is its maximum speed?
questions.explanation: Maximum speed: \( v_{\text{max}} = \omega A \). \( A = 7 \, \text{m}, \omega = \pi \, \text{s}^{-1} \). \( v_{\text{max}} = \pi \times 7 \approx 3.14 \times 7 \approx 21.98 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle’s x-projection from circular motion is \( x = 8 \cos (2\pi t) \) (in m). What is its maximum acceleration?
questions.explanation: Maximum acceleration: \( a_{\text{max}} = \omega^2 A \). \( A = 8 \, \text{m}, \omega = 2\pi \, \text{s}^{-1} \). \( a_{\text{max}} = (2\pi)^2 \times 8 \approx 39.48 \times 8 \approx 315.84 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: What role does the phase constant play in differentiating two SHM systems with identical amplitude and frequency?
questions.explanation: The phase constant (\( \phi \) in \( x = A \cos (\omega t + \phi) \)) shifts the starting point of the oscillation, affecting the initial position and velocity, thus distinguishing the motions.

questions.question_text: What distinguishes the restoring force in a spring-mass system from that in a simple pendulum at small amplitudes?
questions.explanation: The spring-mass system uses elastic force (\( F = -kx \)), constant with displacement, while the pendulum’s force (\( F = -mg \sin \theta \approx -mg \theta \)) derives from gravity and varies with angle.

questions.question_text: A pendulum of length \( 1.8 \, \text{m} \) oscillates with \( g = 10 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Period: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{1.8}{10}} = 2\pi \sqrt{0.18} \approx 2.68 \, \text{s} \). Frequency: \( v = \frac{1}{T} = \frac{1}{2.68} \approx 0.373 \, \text{Hz} \).

questions.question_text: A spring system has \( m = 1 \, \text{kg}, k = 100 \, \text{N/m}, A = 20 \, \text{cm} \). What is the potential energy at \( x = 0 \, \text{m} \)?
questions.explanation: Potential energy: \( U = \frac{1}{2} k x^2 \). At \( x = 0 \, \text{m} \), \( U = 0 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: In SHM, when does the particle experience its maximum restoring force?
questions.explanation: The restoring force (\( F = -kx \)) is maximum at the extreme positions (\( x = \pm A \)), where displacement is greatest, coinciding with maximum potential energy.

questions.question_text: A spring of \( k = 360 \, \text{N/m} \) has a \( 1.5 \, \text{kg} \) mass. If \( E = 1.8 \, \text{J} \), what is the amplitude?
questions.explanation: Total energy: \( E = \frac{1}{2} k A^2 \). \( 1.8 = 0.5 \times 360 \times A^2 \Rightarrow 1.8 = 180 A^2 \Rightarrow A^2 = 0.01 \Rightarrow A = 0.1 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A simple pendulum has a length of \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) and oscillates with \( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \). What is its period?
questions.explanation: Period: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{0.4}{9.8}} \approx 2 \times 3.14 \sqrt{0.0408} \approx 1.27 \, \text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 6 \cos (2\pi t + \frac{\pi}{4}) \) (in m). What is its speed at \( t = 0.25 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( \sin 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \))
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v = -\omega A \sin (\omega t + \phi) \). \( A = 6 \, \text{m}, \omega = 2\pi \, \text{s}^{-1}, \phi = \frac{\pi}{4} \). At \( t = 0.25 \): \( 2\pi \times 0.25 + \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{3\pi}{4} \). \( v = -2\pi \times 6 \sin \frac{3\pi}{4} = -12\pi \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \approx -26.64 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 5 \sin (3t + \frac{\pi}{4}) \) (in m). What is its speed at \( t = 0.25 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( \cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \))
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v = \omega A \cos (\omega t + \phi) \). \( A = 5 \, \text{m}, \omega = 3 \, \text{s}^{-1}, \phi = \frac{\pi}{4} \). At \( t = 0.25 \): \( 3 \times 0.25 + \frac{\pi}{4} = 0.75 + 0.785 \approx 1.535 \, \text{rad} \approx 88^\circ \). \( v = 3 \times 5 \cos 88^\circ \approx 15 \times 0.0349 \approx 0.5235 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Two springs (\( k = 150 \, \text{N/m} \)) are attached to a \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) mass as in Fig. 13.14. What is the frequency?
questions.explanation: Effective \( k_{\text{eff}} = 2k = 2 \times 150 = 300 \, \text{N/m} \). \( \omega = \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text{eff}}}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{300}{3}} = 10 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( v = \frac{\omega}{2\pi} = \frac{10}{2 \times 3.14} \approx 1.59 \, \text{Hz} \).

questions.question_text: A mass oscillates with \( v = -9 \sin (3t) \) (in m/s). What is its displacement function?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v = -\omega A \sin (\omega t) \). \( \omega = 3 \, \text{s}^{-1}, v_{\text{max}} = \omega A = 9 \Rightarrow A = \frac{9}{3} = 3 \, \text{m} \). Displacement: \( x = A \cos (\omega t) = 3 \cos (3t) \).

questions.question_text: In SHM, what is the relationship between the magnitudes of maximum acceleration and maximum velocity?
options: \( v_{\text{max}} \) is the square of \( a_{\text{max}} \)
questions.explanation: Maximum velocity \( v_{\text{max}} = \omega A \), maximum acceleration \( a_{\text{max}} = \omega^2 A \). Thus, \( a_{\text{max}} = \omega v_{\text{max}} \), showing \( a_{\text{max}} \) is proportional to \( v_{\text{max}} \) via \( \omega \).

questions.question_text: Which function represents SHM? (\( \omega \) is a positive constant)
questions.explanation: SHM requires \( a = -\omega^2 x \): (a) \( \sin \omega t + 2 \cos 3\omega t \): Not SHM (mixed frequencies). (b) \( 5 \cos (\omega t - \frac{\pi}{3}) \): \( a = -5\omega^2 \cos (\omega t - \frac{\pi}{3}) = -\omega^2 x \), SHM. (c) \( e^{\omega t} \): Not periodic. (d) \( \sin^3 \omega t \): Periodic, not SHM.

questions.question_text: A simple pendulum has a period of \( 3 \, \text{s} \) on Earth (\( g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2 \)). What is its length?
questions.explanation: \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} \). \( 3 = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{9.8}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{L}{9.8}} = \frac{3}{2\pi} \approx 0.477 \). \( \frac{L}{9.8} = (0.477)^2 \Rightarrow L \approx 9.8 \times 0.227 \approx 2.23 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A particle executes SHM with an amplitude of \( 5 \, \text{cm} \) and a period of \( 2 \, \text{s} \). What is the maximum speed of the particle? (Take \( \pi = 3.14 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum speed in SHM: \( v_{\text{max}} = A \omega \). Angular frequency: \( \omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2 \times 3.14}{2} = 3.14 \, \text{rad/s} \). Amplitude: \( A = 5 \, \text{cm} = 0.05 \, \text{m} \). \( v_{\text{max}} = 0.05 \times 3.14 = 0.157 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the physical significance of the angular frequency in SHM?
options: It determines the rate of oscillation
It indicates the restoring force magnitude
questions.explanation: Angular frequency (\( \omega = 2\pi v \)) relates to how quickly the particle oscillates, determining the rate of phase change and thus the frequency of oscillations.

questions.question_text: A spring system has \( k = 500 \, \text{N/m}, m = 2 \, \text{kg} \). What is the maximum acceleration if \( A = 8 \, \text{cm} \)?
questions.explanation: \( \omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{500}{2}} = \sqrt{250} \approx 15.81 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( a_{\text{max}} = \omega^2 A = (15.81)^2 \times 0.08 \approx 250 \times 0.08 = 20 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( v = -10 \sin (2t + \frac{\pi}{2}) \) (in m/s). What is its displacement function?
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v = -\omega A \sin (\omega t + \phi) \). Given \( \omega = 2, v_{\text{max}} = \omega A = 10 \Rightarrow A = 5 \, \text{m} \). Comparing: \( -\omega A \sin (2t + \frac{\pi}{2}) = -10 \sin (2t + \frac{\pi}{2}) \), phase matches. Displacement: \( x = A \cos (\omega t + \phi) = 5 \cos (2t + \frac{\pi}{2}) \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has an amplitude of \( 15 \, \text{cm} \) and a frequency of \( 2 \, \text{Hz} \). What is its maximum velocity? (Take \( \pi = 3.14 \))
questions.explanation: Maximum velocity: \( v_{\text{max}} = A \omega \). \( \omega = 2\pi v = 2 \times 3.14 \times 2 = 12.56 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( A = 0.15 \, \text{m} \). \( v_{\text{max}} = 0.15 \times 12.56 \approx 1.884 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Which property of an SHM system ensures that the frequency remains constant regardless of the energy imparted?
options: The linearity of the restoring force
questions.explanation: Frequency (\( v = \frac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} \)) depends solely on mass and spring constant, not energy or amplitude, due to the linear nature of the restoring force.

questions.question_text: A particle’s displacement is \( x = 6 \cos (\pi t + \frac{\pi}{6}) \) (in m). What is its velocity at \( t = 0.5 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \))
questions.explanation: Velocity: \( v = -\omega A \sin (\omega t + \phi) \). \( A = 6 \, \text{m}, \omega = \pi \, \text{s}^{-1}, \phi = \frac{\pi}{6} \). At \( t = 0.5 \): \( \pi \times 0.5 + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{3\pi}{6} + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{4\pi}{6} = \frac{2\pi}{3} \). \( v = -\pi \times 6 \sin \frac{2\pi}{3} = -6\pi \sin 60^\circ = -6\pi \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx -16.31 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: What underlies the ability of SHM to be represented as a projection of uniform circular motion?
options: The sinusoidal nature of the displacement
questions.explanation: The sinusoidal variation of displacement in SHM (\( x = A \cos (\omega t + \phi) \)) matches the projection of a circular path’s radius, reflecting identical periodic behavior.

questions.question_text: A spring-mass system has \( m = 0.2 \, \text{kg}, k = 80 \, \text{N/m} \). If displaced by \( 5 \, \text{cm} \), what is the total energy?
questions.explanation: Total energy: \( E = \frac{1}{2} k A^2 \). \( A = 0.05 \, \text{m}, k = 80 \, \text{N/m} \). \( E = 0.5 \times 80 \times (0.05)^2 = 0.5 \times 80 \times 0.0025 = 0.1 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 6 \sin (2\pi t + \frac{\pi}{4}) \) (in cm). What is its acceleration at \( t = 0.25 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: Acceleration: \( a = -\omega^2 x \). \( \omega = 2\pi \, \text{s}^{-1}, x = 0.06 \cos (2\pi \times 0.25 + \frac{\pi}{4}) = 0.06 \cos (\frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{\pi}{4}) = 0.06 \cos \frac{3\pi}{4} \). \( \cos \frac{3\pi}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \), so \( x = -0.06 \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \approx -0.0424 \, \text{m} \). \( a = -(2\pi)^2 \times (-0.0424) \approx 39.48 \times 0.0424 \approx 1.67 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: Why does the frequency of a spring-mass system increase when a stiffer spring is used?
questions.explanation: Frequency \( v = \frac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} \) increases with a larger spring constant (\( k \)), as a stiffer spring (higher \( k \)) provides a stronger restoring force, speeding up oscillations.

questions.question_text: A particle in SHM has \( x = 3 \cos (2t + \frac{\pi}{6}) \) (in m). What is its speed at \( t = 0.5 \, \text{s} \)? (Take \( \sin \frac{4\pi}{6} = 1 \))
