questions.explanation: \( \tau = I \alpha \). \( \tau = 16 \, \text{Nm} \), \( I = 8 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{16}{8} = 2 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: Three particles of masses \( 5 \, \text{kg} \), \( 10 \, \text{kg} \), and \( 15 \, \text{kg} \) are at \( (0, 0) \), \( (2, 4) \), and \( (6, 2) \) respectively. What is the x-coordinate of their center of mass?
A solid cylinder of mass \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) rolls without slipping with a linear speed of \( 2.4 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its angular velocity?
Two particles of masses \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) are at \( (0, 5) \) and \( (10, 0) \) respectively. What is the distance of their center of mass from the origin?
A uniform circular disk of radius \( 3 \, \text{m} \) and mass \( 12 \, \text{kg} \) has its center at \( (0, 0) \). What is the position of its center of mass?
questions.explanation: For a uniform circular disk, the center of mass is at its geometric center. Given center at \( (0, 0) \), CM position = \( (0, 0) \).

tests.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
tests.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion Chapter-Wise Test 16

questions.question_text: A force \( \mathbf{F} = -3 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} - 4 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{N} \) acts at \( \mathbf{r} = 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 5 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m} \). What is the magnitude of the torque about the origin?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{\tau} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -3 & -4 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (2 \times (-4) - 5 \times (-3)) = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (-8 + 15) = 7 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{Nm} \). Magnitude = \( 7 \, \text{Nm} \).

questions.question_text: A wheel of radius \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) and moment of inertia \( 1.6 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) is accelerated by a torque of \( 8 \, \text{Nm} \). What is its angular acceleration?
questions.explanation: Torque: \( \tau = I \alpha \). \( \tau = 8 \, \text{Nm} \), \( I = 1.6 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{8}{1.6} = 5 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: Two particles of masses \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) are at \( (1, 5) \) and \( (4, 1) \) respectively. What is the distance of their center of mass from the origin?
Two particles of masses \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) are at \( (2, 0) \) and \( (0, 3) \) respectively. What is the distance of their center of mass from \( (0, 0) \)?
A disk with moment of inertia \( 1.5 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) rotates at \( 4 \, \text{rad/s} \). A torque of \( 6 \, \text{Nm} \) acts for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is its final angular velocity?
questions.explanation: \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{6}{1.5} = 4 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \). \( \Delta \omega = \alpha t = 4 \times 3 = 12 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega = \omega_0 + \Delta \omega = 4 + 12 = 16 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: Which statement is true about the axis of rotation in pure rotational motion?
options: It is perpendicular to the body
questions.explanation: In pure rotational motion, the axis of rotation is fixed, meaning it does not move or change direction, constraining the body to rotate about it.

questions.question_text: A torque of \( 21 \, \text{Nm} \) acts on a wheel with moment of inertia \( 7 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) starting from rest. What is its angular speed after \( 4 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{21}{7} = 3 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \). \( \omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t = 0 + 3 \times 4 = 12 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A wheel with moment of inertia \( 2.5 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) rotates at \( 6 \, \text{rad/s} \). A torque of \( 10 \, \text{Nm} \) acts for \( 2 \, \text{s} \). What is its final angular velocity?
questions.explanation: \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{10}{2.5} = 4 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \). \( \Delta \omega = \alpha t = 4 \times 2 = 8 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega = \omega_0 + \Delta \omega = 6 + 8 = 14 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: What is the SI unit of moment of inertia?
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia \( I = \sum m_i r_i^2 \) has units of mass times distance squared, so the SI unit is \( \text{kg m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) object moves with a velocity of \( 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} - 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the velocity of its center of mass?
questions.explanation: For a single object, the center of mass velocity equals the object’s velocity. Magnitude = \( \sqrt{(3)^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 4} = \sqrt{13} \approx 3.6 \, \text{m/s} \).

tests.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
tests.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion Chapter-Wise Test 17

questions.question_text: Three particles of masses \( 3 \, \text{kg} \), \( 6 \, \text{kg} \), and \( 9 \, \text{kg} \) are located at \( (0, 1) \), \( (2, 2) \), and \( (4, 0) \) respectively. What is the x-coordinate of their center of mass?
A solid sphere of mass \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) rotates about its center at \( 5 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its rotational kinetic energy?
A torque of \( 14 \, \text{Nm} \) acts on a wheel with moment of inertia \( 7 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) starting from rest. What is its angular speed after \( 5 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{14}{7} = 2 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \). \( \omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t = 0 + 2 \times 5 = 10 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) block slides down an inclined plane with a constant velocity of \( 2 \, \text{m/s} \). What is the velocity of the center of mass of the block?
questions.explanation: For a single body in pure translational motion, the velocity of the center of mass is the same as the velocity of the body. Given: \( v = 2 \, \text{m/s} \). Thus, \( \mathbf{V} = 2 \, \text{m/s} \) (direction along the incline).

questions.question_text: What is the condition for a rigid body to have zero angular acceleration?
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration is zero when the net torque is zero (\( \mathbf{\tau} = I \mathbf{\alpha} \)), as torque drives rotational change.

questions.question_text: A torque of \( 15 \, \text{Nm} \) is applied to a wheel with moment of inertia \( 3 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). What is its angular acceleration?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = I \alpha \). \( \tau = 15 \, \text{Nm} \), \( I = 3 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{15}{3} = 5 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A particle rotates about a fixed axis at a radius of \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) with a linear speed of \( 3 \, \text{m/s} \). What is its angular velocity?
questions.explanation: \( v = \omega r \). \( v = 3 \, \text{m/s} \), \( r = 0.6 \, \text{m} \). \( \omega = \frac{v}{r} = \frac{3}{0.6} = 5 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: Three particles of masses \( 1 \, \text{kg} \), \( 5 \, \text{kg} \), and \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) are at \( (0, 2) \), \( (3, 0) \), and \( (4, 6) \) respectively. What is the x-coordinate of their center of mass?
Which physical quantity is defined as \( \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} \) for a particle?
questions.explanation: Angular momentum of a particle is defined as \( \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} \), where \( \mathbf{r} \) is the position vector and \( \mathbf{p} \) is the linear momentum.

questions.question_text: Why can a rigid body not deform under the influence of forces in theoretical mechanics?
options: Because it is an idealization with fixed distances
questions.explanation: In theoretical mechanics, a rigid body is an idealization where inter-particle distances are fixed, preventing deformation and allowing focus on rotational and translational motion only.

tests.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
tests.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion Chapter-Wise Test 18

questions.question_text: A torque of \( 9 \, \text{Nm} \) is applied to a wheel with moment of inertia \( 3 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). What is its angular acceleration?
questions.explanation: \( \tau = I \alpha \). \( \tau = 9 \, \text{Nm} \), \( I = 3 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{9}{3} = 3 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A uniform disk of mass \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) rotates at \( 8 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its angular momentum about its axis?
questions.explanation: \( L = I \omega \). For a disk: \( I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times (0.5)^2 = 0.5 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( L = 0.5 \times 8 = 4 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A uniform disk of mass \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) rotates about its center with an angular speed of \( 10 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its rotational kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Rotational KE: \( K = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2 \). Moment of inertia of a disk: \( I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.04 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( K = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.04 \times (10)^2 = 0.02 \times 100 = 2 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a symmetric body rotating about its symmetry axis have angular momentum aligned with the axis?
options: Due to cancellation of perpendicular components
questions.explanation: Symmetry ensures perpendicular components of angular momentum cancel out, leaving \( \mathbf{L} = I \mathbf{\omega} \) aligned with the axis of rotation.

questions.question_text: A uniform rod of length \( 2 \, \text{m} \) and mass \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) lies along the x-axis with its left end at the origin. What is the position vector of its center of mass?
questions.explanation: For a uniform rod, the center of mass is at its geometric center. Length = \( 2 \, \text{m} \), so the center is at \( 1 \, \text{m} \) from the origin along the x-axis. Position vector: \( \mathbf{R} = 1 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 0 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} + 0 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} = 1 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: In rotational motion, what is the relationship between linear velocity and angular velocity for a particle?
questions.explanation: The linear velocity \( v \) of a particle in rotational motion is related to angular velocity \( \omega \) by \( v = \omega r \), where \( r \) is the perpendicular distance from the axis.

questions.question_text: A solid sphere of mass \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) has an angular momentum of \( 12 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). What is its angular velocity?
questions.explanation: \( I = \frac{2}{5} M R^2 = \frac{2}{5} \times 3 \times (0.4)^2 = 0.192 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( \omega = \frac{L}{I} = \frac{12}{0.192} \approx 62.5 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: For a body rotating about a fixed axis, what is true about particles on the axis?
options: They have the maximum linear velocity
questions.explanation: Particles on the axis of rotation have a perpendicular distance \( r = 0 \) from the axis, so their linear velocity \( v = \omega r = 0 \), meaning they remain stationary.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the angular velocity of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis?
options: It varies with distance from the axis
It is the same for all particles in the body
It is zero for points farthest from the axis
It depends on the mass of each particle
questions.explanation: For a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis, all particles have the same angular velocity, regardless of their distance from the axis, as it’s a property of the body’s rotation as a whole.

questions.question_text: A solid sphere of mass \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.1 \, \text{m} \) rolls without slipping down an incline. If its linear speed is \( 5 \, \text{m/s} \), what is its angular velocity?
questions.explanation: For rolling without slipping: \( v = \omega r \). \( v = 5 \, \text{m/s} \), \( r = 0.1 \, \text{m} \). \( \omega = \frac{v}{r} = \frac{5}{0.1} = 50 \, \text{rad/s} \).

tests.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
tests.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion Chapter-Wise Test 19

questions.question_text: Two particles of masses \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) and \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) are at \( (1, 4) \) and \( (9, 2) \) respectively. What is the distance of their center of mass from the origin?
A solid cylinder of mass \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.5 \, \text{m} \) has a kinetic energy of \( 10 \, \text{J} \). What is its angular speed?
questions.explanation: \( I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (0.5)^2 = 0.25 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( K = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2 \Rightarrow 10 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.25 \times \omega^2 \Rightarrow 20 = 0.25 \omega^2 \Rightarrow \omega^2 = 80 \Rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{80} \approx 8.94 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A hollow cylinder of mass \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) rotates at \( 5 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its angular momentum about its axis?

A solid sphere of mass \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.3 \, \text{m} \) rotates about an axis through its center. If its angular momentum is \( 9 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \), what is its angular velocity?
questions.explanation: \( L = I \omega \). For a sphere: \( I = \frac{2}{5} M R^2 = \frac{2}{5} \times 5 \times (0.3)^2 = 0.18 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( \omega = \frac{L}{I} = \frac{9}{0.18} = 50 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A uniform rectangular plate of dimensions \( 3 \, \text{m} \times 5 \, \text{m} \) and mass \( 12 \, \text{kg} \) has one corner at \( (1, 1) \) along the x- and y-axes. What is the position of its center of mass?
questions.explanation: For a uniform rectangle, the center of mass is at the centroid. Vertices: \( (1, 1), (4, 1), (1, 6), (4, 6) \). CM: \( X = 1 + \frac{3}{2} = 2.5 \), \( Y = 1 + \frac{5}{2} = 3.5 \). Position: \( (2.5, 3.5) \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: A solid cylinder of mass \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) rotates at \( 25 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its angular momentum about its axis?
questions.explanation: \( I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.08 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( L = I \omega = 0.08 \times 25 = 2 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) block moves with a velocity of \( -2 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the velocity of its center of mass?
questions.explanation: For a single object, the center of mass velocity equals the object’s velocity. Magnitude = \( \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (3)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9} = \sqrt{13} \approx 3.6 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: Which of the following best defines a rigid body?
options: A body that can only undergo translational motion
A body with a fixed shape where distances between particles do not change
A body that deforms under external forces
A body with no mass distribution
questions.explanation: A rigid body is one where the distances between all pairs of particles remain constant, even under the influence of forces. This is an idealization, as real bodies deform slightly, but it’s a key assumption in rotational dynamics.

questions.question_text: A solid sphere of mass \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) has an angular momentum of \( 8 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). What is its angular velocity?

A \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) particle moves with velocity \( \mathbf{v} = -5 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m/s} \) at \( \mathbf{r} = 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} \, \text{m} \). What is the z-component of its angular momentum?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (3 \times 2 - 0 \times (-5)) = 6 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). Z-component = \( 6 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \).

tests.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
tests.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion Chapter-Wise Test 20

questions.question_text: A wheel with moment of inertia \( 6 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) rotates at \( 3 \, \text{rad/s} \). A torque of \( 12 \, \text{Nm} \) acts for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is its final angular velocity?
questions.explanation: \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{12}{6} = 2 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \). \( \Delta \omega = \alpha t = 2 \times 3 = 6 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega = \omega_0 + \Delta \omega = 3 + 6 = 9 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) particle moves with velocity \( \mathbf{v} = 6 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} \, \text{m/s} \) at \( \mathbf{r} = 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m} \). What is the magnitude of its angular momentum about the origin?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (0 \times 0 - 2 \times 6) = -12 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). Magnitude = \( 12 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A uniform triangular lamina has vertices at \( (0, 0) \), \( (5, 0) \), and \( (0, 6) \). What is the x-coordinate of its center of mass?
questions.explanation: For a uniform triangular lamina, the center of mass is at the centroid, the average of the vertices. \( X = \frac{0 + 5 + 0}{3} = \frac{5}{3} \approx 1.67 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: Vectors \( \mathbf{a} = 8 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} - 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 7 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \) are given. What is the magnitude of \( \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} \)?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 8 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 7 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (8 \times 7 - (-3) \times 2) = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (56 + 6) = 62 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \). Magnitude = \( 62 \).

questions.question_text: What is the primary source of angular acceleration in a rigid body?
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration (\( \alpha \)) is caused by net external torque (\( \mathbf{\tau} = I \mathbf{\alpha} \)), which drives rotational change.

questions.question_text: A \( 7 \, \text{kg} \) object moves with a velocity of \( 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} - 4 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the velocity of its center of mass?
questions.explanation: For a single object, the center of mass velocity equals the object’s velocity. Magnitude = \( \sqrt{(3)^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.question_text: A uniform rod of mass \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) and length \( 1 \, \text{m} \) is pivoted at one end. What is its moment of inertia about the pivot?
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia of a rod about an end: \( I = \frac{1}{3} M L^2 \). \( M = 2 \, \text{kg} \), \( L = 1 \, \text{m} \). \( I = \frac{1}{3} \times 2 \times (1)^2 = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.67 \, \text{kg m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: Vectors \( \mathbf{a} = -4 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 5 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \) are given. What is the magnitude of \( \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} \)?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} ((-4) \times 5 - 3 \times 2) = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (-20 - 6) = -26 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \). Magnitude = \( 26 \).

questions.question_text: A hollow cylinder of mass \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.2 \, \text{m} \) has a kinetic energy of \( 2 \, \text{J} \). What is its angular speed?
questions.explanation: \( I = M R^2 = 1 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.04 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( K = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2 \Rightarrow 2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.04 \times \omega^2 \Rightarrow 4 = 0.04 \omega^2 \Rightarrow \omega^2 = 100 \Rightarrow \omega = 10 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: What characterizes pure translational motion of a rigid body?
options: All particles have the same angular velocity
All particles have the same linear velocity
Particles rotate about a fixed axis
Particles have different velocities depending on their position
questions.explanation: In pure translational motion, all particles of the rigid body have the same velocity at any given instant, with no rotation involved.

tests.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
tests.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion Chapter-Wise Test 21

questions.question_text: A solid sphere of mass \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) has an angular momentum of \( 11.52 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). What is its angular velocity?
A uniform rod of mass \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) and length \( 2 \, \text{m} \) is pivoted at its center. What is its moment of inertia about the pivot?
questions.explanation: For a rod pivoted at its center: \( I = \frac{1}{12} M L^2 \). \( M = 5 \, \text{kg} \), \( L = 2 \, \text{m} \). \( I = \frac{1}{12} \times 5 \times (2)^2 = \frac{20}{12} = \frac{5}{3} \approx 1.67 \, \text{kg m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: In the expression \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{\omega} \times \mathbf{r} \), what does \( \mathbf{v} \) represent?
questions.explanation: The equation \( \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{\omega} \times \mathbf{r} \) gives the linear velocity of a particle in rotational motion, where \( \mathbf{\omega} \) is the angular velocity and \( \mathbf{r} \) is the position vector from the axis.

questions.question_text: A thin ring of mass \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) rotates about its center at \( 5 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its rotational kinetic energy?
What happens to the angular velocity of a rigid body if the net external torque is zero?
questions.explanation: If the net external torque is zero (\( \frac{d\mathbf{L}}{dt} = \mathbf{\tau} = 0 \)), angular momentum is conserved, and for a fixed moment of inertia, angular velocity remains constant.

questions.question_text: A thin ring of mass \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.4 \, \text{m} \) has a kinetic energy of \( 8 \, \text{J} \). What is its angular speed?
questions.explanation: \( I = M R^2 = 1 \times (0.4)^2 = 0.16 \, \text{kg m}^2 \). \( K = \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2 \Rightarrow 8 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.16 \times \omega^2 \Rightarrow 16 = 0.16 \omega^2 \Rightarrow \omega^2 = 100 \Rightarrow \omega = 10 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a requirement for a rigid body to be in mechanical equilibrium?
options: Net force must be zero only
Net torque must be zero only
Both net force and net torque must be zero
questions.explanation: For mechanical equilibrium, both translational and rotational equilibrium are required: the net force (\( \sum \mathbf{F} = 0 \)) and net torque (\( \sum \mathbf{\tau} = 0 \)) must be zero.

questions.question_text: A \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) particle has a velocity \( \mathbf{v} = 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} \, \text{m/s} \) at position \( \mathbf{r} = 4 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m} \). What is the magnitude of its angular momentum about the origin?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} = \mathbf{r} \times (m \mathbf{v}) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = -8 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). Magnitude = \( 8 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A torque of \( 25 \, \text{Nm} \) acts on a wheel with moment of inertia \( 5 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) starting from rest. What is its angular speed after \( 2 \, \text{s} \)?
questions.explanation: \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{25}{5} = 5 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \). \( \omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t = 0 + 5 \times 2 = 10 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 3 \, \text{kg} \) particle moves with velocity \( \mathbf{v} = 6 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} - 4 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m/s} \) at \( \mathbf{r} = 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m} \). What is the z-component of its angular momentum?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & -4 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (0 \times (-4) - 2 \times 6) = -12 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). Z-component = \( -12 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \).

tests.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
tests.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion Chapter-Wise Test 22

questions.question_text: A force \( \mathbf{F} = 7 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{N} \) acts at \( \mathbf{r} = -2 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 1 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m} \). What is the magnitude of the torque about the origin?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{\tau} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} ((-2) \times 3 - 1 \times 7) = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (-6 - 7) = -13 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{Nm} \). Magnitude = \( 13 \, \text{Nm} \).

questions.question_text: A wheel with moment of inertia \( 5 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) rotates at \( 3 \, \text{rad/s} \). A torque of \( 10 \, \text{Nm} \) acts for \( 5 \, \text{s} \). What is its final angular velocity?
questions.explanation: \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{10}{5} = 2 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \). \( \Delta \omega = \alpha t = 2 \times 5 = 10 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega = \omega_0 + \Delta \omega = 3 + 10 = 13 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: Two vectors are given as \( \mathbf{a} = 6 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = -4 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 2 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \). What is the magnitude of \( \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} \)?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ 6 & 3 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (6 \times 2 - 3 \times (-4)) = \hat{\mathbf{k}} (12 + 12) = 24 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \). Magnitude = \( 24 \).

questions.question_text: A solid sphere of mass \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) and radius \( 0.6 \, \text{m} \) rotates about its center at \( 5 \, \text{rad/s} \). What is its rotational kinetic energy?
A wheel with moment of inertia \( 8 \, \text{kg m}^2 \) rotates at \( 2 \, \text{rad/s} \). A torque of \( 16 \, \text{Nm} \) acts for \( 3 \, \text{s} \). What is its final angular velocity?
questions.explanation: \( \alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{16}{8} = 2 \, \text{rad/s}^2 \). \( \Delta \omega = \alpha t = 2 \times 3 = 6 \, \text{rad/s} \). \( \omega = \omega_0 + \Delta \omega = 2 + 6 = 8 \, \text{rad/s} \).

questions.question_text: A uniform square lamina of side \( 4 \, \text{m} \) and mass \( 8 \, \text{kg} \) has one corner at the origin and lies along the x- and y-axes. What is the position of its center of mass?
questions.explanation: For a uniform square, the center of mass is at the centroid. Vertices: \( (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 4), (4, 4) \). CM: \( X = \frac{0 + 4}{2} = 2 \), \( Y = \frac{0 + 4}{2} = 2 \). Position: \( (2, 2) \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: What is the effect of doubling the radius of a rotating disk on its moment of inertia, assuming mass remains constant?
questions.explanation: For a disk, \( I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 \). Doubling \( R \) increases \( R^2 \) by a factor of 4, so \( I \) increases by a factor of 4 if \( M \) is constant.

questions.question_text: A \( 4 \, \text{kg} \) particle moves with velocity \( \mathbf{v} = 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 5 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m/s} \) at \( \mathbf{r} = -2 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} \, \text{m} \). What is the z-component of its angular momentum?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} ((-2) \times 5 - 0 \times 3) = -10 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). Z-component = \( -10 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 6 \, \text{kg} \) particle moves with velocity \( \mathbf{v} = 3 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m/s} \) at \( \mathbf{r} = -4 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} \, \text{m} \). What is the magnitude of its angular momentum about the origin?
questions.explanation: \( \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{p} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\ -4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{\mathbf{k}} ((-4) \times 3 - 0 \times 0) = -12 \, \hat{\mathbf{k}} \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \). Magnitude = \( 12 \, \text{kg m}^2/\text{s} \).

questions.question_text: In a rigid body undergoing both translation and rotation, what describes the motion of any point?
options: Combination of translational and rotational velocities
questions.explanation: The motion of any point is a combination of the translational velocity of the body (same for all points) and the rotational velocity about the axis, varying with distance from the axis.

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 1

questions.question_text: A silver sheet has an area of \( 1.5 \, \text{m}^2 \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is the increase in area when heated to \( 120^\circ \text{C} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( A_0 = 1.5 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( \Delta T = 120 - 20 = 100^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta A = A_0 \times 2 \alpha_l \Delta T = 1.5 \times 2 \times 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 0.0057 \, \text{m}^2 \).

questions.question_text: Why do blacksmiths heat an iron ring before fitting it onto a wooden wheel?
questions.explanation: Heating causes thermal expansion (Section 10.5), increasing the ring’s diameter (\( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \)), allowing it to fit over the wheel; it contracts upon cooling for a tight fit (Example 10.2).

questions.question_text: A gas occupies \( 4.2 \, \text{L} \) at \( 1.4 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 47^\circ \text{C} \). If the pressure is increased by \( 0.6 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature decreased by \( 20^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?
During vaporization, what does the supplied heat primarily do to the liquid?
options: Converts it to vapor without temperature change
questions.explanation: During vaporization, the supplied heat (latent heat of vaporization) breaks intermolecular bonds to convert the liquid into vapor, without changing its temperature.

questions.question_text: What happens to the volume of an ideal gas if its temperature is doubled at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas at constant pressure, Charles’ Law states that volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature. If temperature doubles, volume doubles.

questions.question_text: What is the Celsius temperature equivalent to \( 400 \, \text{K} \)?
questions.explanation: Relation: \( T_C = T - 273.15 \). Given: \( T = 400 \, \text{K} \). \( T_C = 400 - 273.15 = 126.85^\circ \text{C} \approx 127^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: A silver rod of length \( 1 \, \text{m} \) at \( 10^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 110^\circ \text{C} \). If its cross-sectional area increases by \( 0.0076 \, \text{cm}^2 \), what was its original area? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( \Delta T = 110 - 10 = 100^\circ \text{C} \), \( \Delta A = 0.0076 \, \text{cm}^2 \), \( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta A = A_0 \times 2 \alpha_l \Delta T \). \( 0.0076 = A_0 \times 2 \times 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 \). \( 0.0076 = A_0 \times 3.8 \times 10^{-3} \Rightarrow A_0 = \frac{0.0076}{3.8 \times 10^{-3}} = 2 \, \text{cm}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) copper block at \( 200^\circ \text{C} \) is dropped into \( 0.9 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \) in a calorimeter of mass \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) (specific heat = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \)). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) gold block at \( 1500^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.6 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) copper calorimeter at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of gold = \( 134 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas at \( 3.5 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 77^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 4.5 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature drops to \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) and volume increases to \( 6 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 2

questions.question_text: A gas at \( 2.4 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 87^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 7 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is lowered to \( 37^\circ \text{C} \) and pressure adjusted to \( 3 \, \text{atm} \), what is the percentage change in volume?
questions.explanation: Given: \( P_1 = 2.4 \, \text{atm} \), \( T_1 = 87^\circ \text{C} = 360 \, \text{K} \), \( V_1 = 7 \, \text{L} \), \( T_2 = 37^\circ \text{C} = 310 \, \text{K} \), \( P_2 = 3 \, \text{atm} \). \( \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \). \( V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{P_1}{P_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 7 \times \frac{2.4}{3} \times \frac{310}{360} = 7 \times 0.8 \times 0.8611 \approx 4.82 \, \text{L} \). Percentage change: \( \frac{V_1 - V_2}{V_1} \times 100 = \frac{7 - 4.82}{7} \times 100 = \frac{2.18}{7} \times 100 \approx 31.14\% \) (decrease).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to convert \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -30^\circ \text{C} \) to steam at \( 120^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))
Which of the following correctly relates the coefficients of linear and area expansion?
options: Area coefficient is half the linear coefficient
Area coefficient is twice the linear coefficient
Linear coefficient is twice the area coefficient
questions.explanation: The coefficient of area expansion is approximately twice the coefficient of linear expansion (\( \Delta A / A \approx 2 \alpha_l \Delta T \)), as area involves two dimensions.

questions.question_text: During the melting of ice at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \), why does the temperature remain constant despite heat being supplied?
options: Heat is used to change the state, not raise temperature
Ice has a high specific heat
Heat is lost to the surroundings
questions.explanation: The heat supplied during melting (latent heat of fusion) is used to change the state from solid to liquid, overcoming intermolecular forces, not to increase temperature (Section 10.8).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise \( 0.8 \, \text{kg} \) of aluminium from \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 75^\circ \text{C} \) if its specific heat capacity is \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \)?
questions.explanation: Given: \( m = 0.8 \, \text{kg} \), \( \Delta T = 75 - 25 = 50^\circ \text{C} \), \( s = 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \). \( Q = m s \Delta T = 0.8 \times 900 \times 50 = 36000 \, \text{J} = 36 \, \text{kJ} \).

questions.question_text: How much heat is needed to convert \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) of mercury at \( -39^\circ \text{C} \) to liquid at \( 357^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of solid mercury = \( 140 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 0.12 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of liquid mercury = \( 140 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: \( Q_1 = 0.1 \times 140 \times (39) = 546 \, \text{J} \) (solid from -39°C to 0°C). \( Q_2 = 0.1 \times 0.12 \times 10^5 = 1200 \, \text{J} \) (melting). \( Q_3 = 0.1 \times 140 \times 357 = 4998 \, \text{J} \) (liquid from 0°C to 357°C). Total: \( Q = 546 + 1200 + 4998 = 6744 \, \text{J} = 6.744 \, \text{kJ} \).

questions.question_text: A copper rod of length \( 80 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 40^\circ \text{C} \) is cooled until its length decreases by \( 0.0136 \, \text{cm} \). What is the final temperature? (\( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 80 \, \text{cm} \), \( \Delta L = -0.0136 \, \text{cm} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \), \( T_1 = 40^\circ \text{C} \). \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \Rightarrow -0.0136 = 80 \times 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \times \Delta T \). \( \Delta T = \frac{-0.0136}{80 \times 1.7 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{-0.0136}{1.36 \times 10^{-3}} = -10 \, \text{K} \). \( T_2 = 40 - 10 = 30^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) of water from \( 15^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 85^\circ \text{C} \) and then convert \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) to steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) silver calorimeter initially at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), silver = \( 236 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

A \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) mercury block at \( 400^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium calorimeter at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of mercury = \( 140 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which temperature scale uses absolute zero as its starting point?
questions.explanation: The Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero, the theoretical point where all molecular motion ceases, making it an absolute temperature scale.

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 3

questions.question_text: A gas at \( 1.9 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 67^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 6.5 \, \text{L} \). If the pressure is increased to \( 2.5 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature raised to \( 117^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?

How much heat is required to convert \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -15^\circ \text{C} \) to steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

A brass cube of side \( 15 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 35^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 135^\circ \text{C} \). What is the increase in its surface area if one face is \( 225 \, \text{cm}^2 \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( A_0 = 225 \, \text{cm}^2 \) (one face), total surface area = \( 6 \times 225 = 1350 \, \text{cm}^2 \), \( \Delta T = 135 - 35 = 100^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). Area expansion: \( \Delta A = A_0 \times 2 \alpha_l \Delta T \). For total surface area: \( \Delta A = 1350 \times 2 \times 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 1350 \times 3.6 \times 10^{-3} = 4.86 \, \text{cm}^2 \).

questions.question_text: A steel disc of radius \( 25 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 130^\circ \text{C} \). What is the increase in its area? (\( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( r = 25 \, \text{cm} \), \( A_0 = \pi r^2 = \pi \times 25^2 = 625\pi \, \text{cm}^2 \), \( \Delta T = 130 - 30 = 100^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta A = A_0 \times 2 \alpha_l \Delta T = 625\pi \times 2 \times 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 \). \( \Delta A = 625\pi \times 2.4 \times 10^{-3} = 1.5\pi \, \text{cm}^2 \approx 4.71 \, \text{cm}^2 \) (\( \pi \approx 3.14 \)).

questions.question_text: How much heat is needed to melt \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) of lead at its melting point of \( 328^\circ \text{C} \)? (Latent heat of fusion of lead = \( 0.25 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))
A steel cube of side \( 20 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 125^\circ \text{C} \). What is the increase in volume? (\( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 20 \, \text{cm} \), \( V_0 = 20^3 = 8000 \, \text{cm}^3 \), \( \Delta T = 125 - 25 = 100^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \alpha_v = 3 \alpha_l = 3 \times 1.2 \times 10^{-5} = 3.6 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta V = V_0 \alpha_v \Delta T = 8000 \times 3.6 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 28.8 \, \text{cm}^3 \).

questions.question_text: A gas occupies \( 2.5 \, \text{L} \) at \( 1.2 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 37^\circ \text{C} \). If the pressure is doubled and temperature increased by \( 50^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?

A \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) iron block at \( 150^\circ \text{C} \) is dropped into \( 1.5 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of iron = \( 450 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

What is the heat required to raise the temperature of \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) of copper from \( 30^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 80^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( m = 0.5 \, \text{kg} \), \( \Delta T = 80 - 30 = 50^\circ \text{C} \), \( s = 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \). \( Q = m s \Delta T = 0.5 \times 386 \times 50 = 9650 \, \text{J} = 9.65 \, \text{kJ} \).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales at the ice point?
questions.explanation: At the ice point (freezing of water at standard pressure), Celsius is \( 0^\circ \text{C} \) and Fahrenheit is \( 32^\circ \text{F} \) (Section 10.3).

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 4

questions.question_text: A \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) iron block at \( 300^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.8 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 24^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) silver calorimeter at \( 24^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of iron = \( 450 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), silver = \( 236 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
What happens to the pressure of an ideal gas if its volume is halved and temperature is kept constant?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s Law (Section 10.4) states \( P V = \text{constant} \) at constant temperature. If \( V_2 = V_1 / 2 \), then \( P_2 = 2 P_1 \), so the pressure doubles.

questions.question_text: Why can’t you open a tightly screwed metal lid until it’s heated in hot water?
questions.explanation: Heating the metal lid causes it to expand due to thermal expansion, loosening its grip on the jar, which expands less if made of glass or remains unchanged if plastic.

questions.question_text: A \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) lead block at \( 500^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 26^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) brass calorimeter at \( 26^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of lead = \( 127.7 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), brass = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which process describes the direct transition from solid to gas observed in iodine?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the process where a substance transitions directly from solid to gas, as observed with iodine under certain conditions.

questions.question_text: What happens to the temperature of an ideal gas if its volume doubles at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: Charles’ Law states that at constant pressure, \( V / T = \text{constant} \). If volume doubles (\( V_2 = 2V_1 \)), the absolute temperature doubles (\( T_2 = 2T_1 \)).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) brass block at \( 350^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) iron calorimeter at \( 27^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of brass = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), iron = \( 450 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Why does water in a calorimeter reach a steady temperature when mixed with a hot object?
questions.explanation: In calorimetry (Section 10.7), heat lost by the hot object equals heat gained by the water and calorimeter at thermal equilibrium, where no further heat transfer occurs.

questions.question_text: A \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) silver block at \( 150^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium calorimeter at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of silver = \( 236 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium block at \( 160^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 1.2 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 28^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) lead calorimeter at \( 28^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), lead = \( 127.7 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 5

questions.question_text: How much heat is needed to convert \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) to steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)? (Latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))
What is the relationship between the Celsius and Kelvin scales?
questions.explanation: The Kelvin scale is offset from the Celsius scale by \( 273.15 \), so \( T = t_C + 273.15 \) (Section 10.4), where \( T \) is Kelvin and \( t_C \) is Celsius.

questions.question_text: What is the Kelvin temperature equivalent to \( -23^\circ \text{C} \)?
What is the key difference between Celsius and Fahrenheit scales at the boiling point of water?
questions.explanation: At the boiling point of water under standard pressure, the Celsius scale reads \( 100^\circ \text{C} \), while the Fahrenheit scale reads \( 212^\circ \text{F} \), reflecting different interval sizes and zero points.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about latent heat during a phase change?
options: It changes the state without changing temperature
questions.explanation: Latent heat is the heat absorbed or released per unit mass during a phase change without a temperature change (Section 10.8.1, \( Q = m L \)).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium block at \( 120^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.8 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) copper calorimeter at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A silver sphere of radius \( 8 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 70^\circ \text{C} \) is cooled to \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is the decrease in its volume? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( r = 8 \, \text{cm} \), \( V_0 = \frac{4}{3} \pi \times 8^3 = \frac{2048}{3} \pi \, \text{cm}^3 \), \( \Delta T = 20 - 70 = -50^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \alpha_v = 3 \alpha_l = 3 \times 1.9 \times 10^{-5} = 5.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta V = V_0 \alpha_v \Delta T = \frac{2048}{3} \pi \times 5.7 \times 10^{-5} \times (-50) \). \( \Delta V = \frac{2048}{3} \pi \times (-2.85 \times 10^{-3}) \approx -6.12 \pi \approx -19.22 \, \text{cm}^3 \) (decrease of \( 19.22 \, \text{cm}^3 \)).

questions.question_text: A steel rod has a length of \( 1 \, \text{m} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What will be its length at \( 120^\circ \text{C} \) if the coefficient of linear expansion of steel is \( 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \)?
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 1 \, \text{m} \), \( T_1 = 20^\circ \text{C} \), \( T_2 = 120^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta T = 120 - 20 = 100^\circ \text{C} \). Linear expansion: \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T = 1 \times 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 1.2 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} \). New length: \( L = L_0 + \Delta L = 1 + 0.0012 = 1.0012 \, \text{m} \).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to melt \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \)? (Latent heat of fusion = \( 3.33 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

How much heat is required to convert \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -20^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 10^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 6

questions.question_text: A brass ring has an inner diameter of \( 5 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \). To what temperature must it be heated to increase the diameter to \( 5.009 \, \text{cm} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 5 \, \text{cm} \), \( L = 5.009 \, \text{cm} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \), \( T_1 = 30^\circ \text{C} \). \( \Delta L = 5.009 - 5 = 0.009 \, \text{cm} \). \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \Rightarrow 0.009 = 5 \times 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \times \Delta T \). \( \Delta T = \frac{0.009}{5 \times 1.8 \times 10^{-5}} = 100 \, \text{K} \). \( T_2 = 30 + 100 = 130^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to vaporize \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) of nitrogen at \( -196^\circ \text{C} \)? (Latent heat of vaporization of nitrogen = \( 2.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

How much heat is required to convert \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -18^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 40^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) copper calorimeter initially at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: \( Q_1 = 0.3 \times 2100 \times 18 = 11340 \, \text{J} \) (ice to 0°C). \( Q_2 = 0.3 \times 3.35 \times 10^5 = 100500 \, \text{J} \) (melting). Heat gained by water and calorimeter: \( (0.3 \times 4186 + 0.1 \times 386) \times (40 - 0) = (1255.8 + 38.6) \times 40 = 1294.4 \times 40 = 51776 \, \text{J} \). Heat lost by calorimeter: \( 0.1 \times 386 \times (25 - 0) = 965 \, \text{J} \) (assume it cools to 0°C first). Total heat supplied: \( Q = 11340 + 100500 + 51776 - 965 = 162651 \, \text{J} = 162.65 \, \text{kJ} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) gold block at \( 1200^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of gold = \( 134 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
What is the significance of the latent heat of fusion?
questions.explanation: The latent heat of fusion is the heat required per unit mass to change a substance from solid to liquid at its melting point, reflecting the energy needed to break intermolecular bonds.

questions.question_text: A \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium block at \( 80^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \). Calculate the final temperature. (Specific heat of aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas occupies a volume of \( 2 \, \text{L} \) at \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 1 \, \text{atm} \) pressure. What will be its volume at \( 127^\circ \text{C} \) if the pressure remains constant? (Use ideal gas law)
questions.explanation: Given: \( V_1 = 2 \, \text{L} \), \( T_1 = 27^\circ \text{C} = 300 \, \text{K} \), \( T_2 = 127^\circ \text{C} = 400 \, \text{K} \), \( P_1 = P_2 \). Using Charles' Law: \( \frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2} \). \( V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 2 \times \frac{400}{300} = 2 \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{8}{3} \approx 2.67 \, \text{L} \).

questions.question_text: A metal cube has a volume of \( 1000 \, \text{cm}^3 \) at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \). What will be its volume at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) if the coefficient of volume expansion is \( 5.4 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \)?
questions.explanation: Given: \( V_0 = 1000 \, \text{cm}^3 \), \( \Delta T = 100^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_v = 5.4 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta V = V_0 \alpha_v \Delta T = 1000 \times 5.4 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 5.4 \, \text{cm}^3 \). New volume: \( V = V_0 + \Delta V = 1000 + 5.4 = 1005.4 \, \text{cm}^3 \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) tungsten block at \( 250^\circ \text{C} \) is dropped into \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 18^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) silver calorimeter at \( 18^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of tungsten = \( 134 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), silver = \( 236 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas at \( 17^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 2.5 \, \text{atm} \) occupies \( 5 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is raised to \( 67^\circ \text{C} \) and the volume is adjusted to \( 7 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?
questions.explanation: Given: \( T_1 = 17^\circ \text{C} = 290 \, \text{K} \), \( P_1 = 2.5 \, \text{atm} \), \( V_1 = 5 \, \text{L} \), \( T_2 = 67^\circ \text{C} = 340 \, \text{K} \), \( V_2 = 7 \, \text{L} \). Ideal gas law: \( \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \). \( P_2 = P_1 \times \frac{V_1}{V_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 2.5 \times \frac{5}{7} \times \frac{340}{290} \). \( P_2 = 2.5 \times 0.7143 \times 1.1724 \approx 2.09 \, \text{atm} \).

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 7

questions.question_text: A copper cylinder has a volume of \( 500 \, \text{cm}^3 \) at \( 50^\circ \text{C} \). What temperature must it be cooled to for the volume to decrease by \( 0.85 \, \text{cm}^3 \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( V_0 = 500 \, \text{cm}^3 \), \( \Delta V = -0.85 \, \text{cm}^3 \), \( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \), \( T_1 = 50^\circ \text{C} \). \( \alpha_v = 3 \alpha_l = 3 \times 1.7 \times 10^{-5} = 5.1 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta V = V_0 \alpha_v \Delta T \Rightarrow -0.85 = 500 \times 5.1 \times 10^{-5} \times \Delta T \). \( \Delta T = \frac{-0.85}{500 \times 5.1 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{-0.85}{0.0255} \approx -33.33 \, \text{K} \). \( T_2 = 50 - 33.33 \approx 16.67^\circ \text{C} \approx 16.7^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: Which scale measures temperature relative to the freezing and boiling points of water with 180 intervals between them?
questions.explanation: The Fahrenheit scale uses \( 32^\circ \text{F} \) for freezing and \( 212^\circ \text{F} \) for boiling of water, with 180 intervals (\( 212 - 32 = 180 \)) between these points.

questions.question_text: Which material is preferred as a coolant in radiators due to its high capacity to absorb heat?
questions.explanation: Water is preferred as a coolant in radiators because of its high specific heat capacity, allowing it to absorb significant heat with minimal temperature rise.

questions.question_text: A \( 0.45 \, \text{kg} \) copper block at \( 200^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 1.1 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 23^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) brass calorimeter at \( 23^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), brass = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
What is the primary factor affecting the volume expansion of a gas compared to solids and liquids?
questions.explanation: Gases expand much more than solids and liquids due to their higher coefficient of volume expansion, which is temperature-dependent and significantly larger (Section 10.5).

questions.question_text: Which property of a material explains why sand heats up faster than water under the same sunlight?
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity determines how much heat is needed to raise the temperature of a material. Sand has a lower specific heat capacity than water, so it heats up faster.

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) of water from \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 80^\circ \text{C} \) and then convert \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) of it to steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

A gas at \( 300 \, \text{K} \) and \( 1 \, \text{atm} \) occupies \( 3 \, \text{L} \). If it is heated to \( 450 \, \text{K} \) while the volume is adjusted to \( 4.5 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?

A gas at \( 2.8 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 97^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 3.8 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is raised to \( 147^\circ \text{C} \) and volume reduced to \( 2.5 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?

A steel plate has an area of \( 1.2 \, \text{m}^2 \) at \( 45^\circ \text{C} \). What is the decrease in area when cooled to \( 5^\circ \text{C} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( A_0 = 1.2 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( \Delta T = 5 - 45 = -40^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). Area expansion: \( \Delta A = A_0 \times 2 \alpha_l \Delta T = 1.2 \times 2 \times 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \times (-40) \). \( \Delta A = 1.2 \times 2.4 \times 10^{-5} \times (-40) = -0.001152 \, \text{m}^2 \) (decrease of \( 0.001152 \, \text{m}^2 \)).

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 8

questions.question_text: How much ice at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \) will melt if \( 16744 \, \text{J} \) of heat is supplied? (Latent heat of fusion of ice = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( Q = 16744 \, \text{J} \), \( L_f = 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \). \( Q = m L_f \Rightarrow m = \frac{Q}{L_f} = \frac{16744}{3.35 \times 10^5} \approx 0.05 \, \text{kg} = 50 \, \text{g} \).

questions.question_text: A brass rod of length \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 220^\circ \text{C} \). If its cross-sectional area increases by \( 0.018 \, \text{cm}^2 \), what was its original area? (\( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( \Delta T = 220 - 20 = 200^\circ \text{C} \), \( \Delta A = 0.018 \, \text{cm}^2 \), \( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). Area expansion: \( \Delta A = A_0 \times 2 \alpha_l \Delta T \). \( 0.018 = A_0 \times 2 \times 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \times 200 \). \( 0.018 = A_0 \times 7.2 \times 10^{-3} \Rightarrow A_0 = \frac{0.018}{7.2 \times 10^{-3}} = 2.5 \, \text{cm}^2 \).

questions.question_text: Which property of a substance determines the amount of heat required to change its temperature by \( 1^\circ \text{C} \) per unit mass?
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity (\( s \)) is defined as the heat required per unit mass to change the temperature by \( 1^\circ \text{C} \) (Section 10.6, \( s = \frac{1}{m} \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta T} \)).

questions.question_text: A gas expands from \( 4 \, \text{L} \) to \( 6 \, \text{L} \) at constant pressure of \( 2 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature \( 300 \, \text{K} \). What is the new temperature if the volume is reduced back to \( 4 \, \text{L} \) at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, \( \frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2} \). Initial: \( V_1 = 4 \, \text{L} \), \( T_1 = 300 \, \text{K} \), \( V_2 = 6 \, \text{L} \), \( T_2 = ? \). \( T_2 = T_1 \times \frac{V_2}{V_1} = 300 \times \frac{6}{4} = 450 \, \text{K} \). Back to \( 4 \, \text{L} \): \( T_3 = T_2 \times \frac{V_3}{V_2} = 450 \times \frac{4}{6} = 300 \, \text{K} \) (original temperature).

questions.question_text: A copper cube has a side length of \( 10 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \). What is its volume at \( 130^\circ \text{C} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 10 \, \text{cm} \), \( V_0 = 10^3 = 1000 \, \text{cm}^3 \), \( \Delta T = 130 - 30 = 100^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). Volume expansion: \( \alpha_v = 3 \alpha_l = 3 \times 1.7 \times 10^{-5} = 5.1 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta V = V_0 \alpha_v \Delta T = 1000 \times 5.1 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 5.1 \, \text{cm}^3 \). \( V = V_0 + \Delta V = 1000 + 5.1 = 1005.1 \, \text{cm}^3 \).

questions.question_text: Which law explains why the volume of a gas increases when its temperature rises at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: Charles’ Law states that at constant pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (\( V / T = \text{constant} \), Section 10.4).

questions.question_text: A gas at \( 3 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 4 \, \text{L} \). If the pressure is reduced to \( 1.5 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature raised to \( 177^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Given: \( P_1 = 3 \, \text{atm} \), \( T_1 = 27^\circ \text{C} = 300 \, \text{K} \), \( V_1 = 4 \, \text{L} \), \( P_2 = 1.5 \, \text{atm} \), \( T_2 = 177^\circ \text{C} = 450 \, \text{K} \). \( \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \). \( V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{P_1}{P_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 4 \times \frac{3}{1.5} \times \frac{450}{300} = 4 \times 2 \times 1.5 = 12 \, \text{L} \).

questions.question_text: Which gas law relates pressure and volume when temperature is held constant?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s Law describes the inverse relationship between pressure and volume of an ideal gas at constant temperature (\( P V = \text{constant} \)).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) lead block at \( 400^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.7 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium calorimeter at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of lead = \( 127.7 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas at \( 1.5 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 77^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 9 \, \text{L} \). If the pressure is reduced to \( 1 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature lowered to \( 27^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Given: \( P_1 = 1.5 \, \text{atm} \), \( T_1 = 77^\circ \text{C} = 350 \, \text{K} \), \( V_1 = 9 \, \text{L} \), \( P_2 = 1 \, \text{atm} \), \( T_2 = 27^\circ \text{C} = 300 \, \text{K} \). \( \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \). \( V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{P_1}{P_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 9 \times \frac{1.5}{1} \times \frac{300}{350} = 9 \times 1.5 \times 0.8571 \approx 11.57 \, \text{L} \).

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 9

questions.question_text: A gas at \( 67^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 1.6 \, \text{atm} \) occupies \( 8 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is reduced to \( 17^\circ \text{C} \) and volume adjusted to \( 6 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?
questions.explanation: Given: \( T_1 = 67^\circ \text{C} = 340 \, \text{K} \), \( P_1 = 1.6 \, \text{atm} \), \( V_1 = 8 \, \text{L} \), \( T_2 = 17^\circ \text{C} = 290 \, \text{K} \), \( V_2 = 6 \, \text{L} \). Ideal gas law: \( \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \). \( P_2 = P_1 \times \frac{V_1}{V_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 1.6 \times \frac{8}{6} \times \frac{290}{340} \). \( P_2 = 1.6 \times 1.3333 \times 0.8529 \approx 1.82 \, \text{atm} \).

questions.question_text: Which statement is true about the ideal gas equation?
options: It applies only to real gases
It relates pressure and volume only
It relates pressure, volume, and temperature
questions.explanation: The ideal gas equation (\( PV = nRT \)) relates pressure, volume, and temperature for an ideal gas, where \( R \) is the universal gas constant and \( n \) is the number of moles.

questions.question_text: What process occurs when dry ice changes directly from solid to vapor?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct transition from solid to vapor without passing through the liquid state, as seen with dry ice (Section 10.8).

questions.question_text: A gas at \( 2 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 47^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 6 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature drops to \( -3^\circ \text{C} \) and pressure becomes \( 1.5 \, \text{atm} \), what is the new volume?
Why does a metal rod expand more than a glass rod for the same temperature increase?
options: Metals have a higher coefficient of linear expansion
Glass has a higher specific heat capacity
questions.explanation: Metals have a higher coefficient of linear expansion (\( \alpha_l \)) than glass (Section 10.5, Table 10.1). For the same \( \Delta T \), \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \) is greater for metals due to their larger \( \alpha_l \).

questions.question_text: Why does steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) cause more severe burns than water at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)?
options: Steam releases latent heat on condensing
questions.explanation: Steam releases additional latent heat of vaporization when it condenses on skin, transferring more energy than liquid water at the same temperature.

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to convert \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -15^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 60^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) iron calorimeter initially at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), iron = \( 450 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas occupies \( 5 \, \text{L} \) at \( 2 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 27^\circ \text{C} \). If the pressure is increased to \( 4 \, \text{atm} \) and volume reduced to \( 3 \, \text{L} \), what is the final temperature in Celsius?
questions.explanation: Given: \( V_1 = 5 \, \text{L} \), \( P_1 = 2 \, \text{atm} \), \( T_1 = 27^\circ \text{C} = 300 \, \text{K} \), \( P_2 = 4 \, \text{atm} \), \( V_2 = 3 \, \text{L} \). \( \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \). \( T_2 = T_1 \times \frac{P_2}{P_1} \times \frac{V_2}{V_1} = 300 \times \frac{4}{2} \times \frac{3}{5} = 300 \times 2 \times 0.6 = 360 \, \text{K} \). \( t_C = T_2 - 273.15 = 360 - 273.15 \approx 86.85^\circ \text{C} \approx 87^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: A gas at \( 1 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 5 \, \text{L} \). What will be its volume at \( 2 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 127^\circ \text{C} \)?
questions.explanation: Given: \( P_1 = 1 \, \text{atm} \), \( V_1 = 5 \, \text{L} \), \( T_1 = 27^\circ \text{C} = 300 \, \text{K} \), \( P_2 = 2 \, \text{atm} \), \( T_2 = 127^\circ \text{C} = 400 \, \text{K} \). Ideal gas law: \( \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \). \( V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{P_1}{P_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 5 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{400}{300} = 5 \times 0.5 \times 1.33 \approx 3.33 \, \text{L} \).

questions.question_text: Why does a calorimeter use a material with low specific heat capacity for its container?
questions.explanation: A material with low specific heat capacity absorbs less heat, minimizing its effect on the heat exchange between the substances being measured, ensuring accurate results.

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 10

questions.question_text: A copper block of mass \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) is dropped into \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Heat lost by copper = Heat gained by water. \( m_c s_c (100 - T) = m_w s_w (T - 20) \). \( 0.5 \times 386 \times (100 - T) = 1 \times 4186 \times (T - 20) \). \( 19300 - 193 T = 4186 T - 83720 \). \( 19300 + 83720 = 4186 T + 193 T \). \( 103020 = 4379 T \Rightarrow T \approx 23.53^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: A brass rod of length \( 2 \, \text{m} \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 125^\circ \text{C} \). Calculate the increase in length. (Coefficient of linear expansion of brass = \( 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 2 \, \text{m} \), \( \Delta T = 125 - 25 = 100^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T = 2 \times 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 3.6 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{m} = 3.6 \, \text{mm} \).

questions.question_text: A silver wire of length \( 1.2 \, \text{m} \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) is cooled until its length decreases by \( 0.0228 \, \text{cm} \). What is the final temperature? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 1.2 \, \text{m} = 120 \, \text{cm} \), \( \Delta L = -0.0228 \, \text{cm} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \), \( T_1 = 25^\circ \text{C} \). \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \Rightarrow -0.0228 = 120 \times 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \times \Delta T \). \( \Delta T = \frac{-0.0228}{120 \times 1.9 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{-0.0228}{2.28 \times 10^{-3}} = -10 \, \text{K} \). \( T_2 = 25 - 10 = 15^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: A \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium block at \( 280^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.7 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 22^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) lead calorimeter at \( 22^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), lead = \( 127.7 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Why do gases expand more than solids for the same temperature increase?
options: Gases have a higher expansion coefficient
questions.explanation: Gases have a much higher coefficient of volume expansion than solids due to weaker intermolecular forces, allowing greater volume changes with temperature.

questions.question_text: A brass ring has an inner diameter of \( 10 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 40^\circ \text{C} \). What temperature must it be cooled to for the diameter to decrease by \( 0.009 \, \text{cm} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 10 \, \text{cm} \), \( \Delta L = -0.009 \, \text{cm} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \), \( T_1 = 40^\circ \text{C} \). \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \Rightarrow -0.009 = 10 \times 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \times \Delta T \). \( \Delta T = \frac{-0.009}{10 \times 1.8 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{-0.009}{1.8 \times 10^{-4}} = -50 \, \text{K} \). \( T_2 = 40 - 50 = -10^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of \( 2 \, \text{kg} \) of water from \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 50^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat capacity of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( m = 2 \, \text{kg} \), \( \Delta T = 50 - 20 = 30^\circ \text{C} \), \( s = 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \). Heat required: \( \Delta Q = m s \Delta T = 2 \times 4186 \times 30 = 251160 \, \text{J} \).

questions.question_text: Which temperature scale uses \( 32^\circ \) and \( 212^\circ \) as the freezing and boiling points of water at standard pressure?
questions.explanation: The Fahrenheit scale defines the freezing point of water as \( 32^\circ \text{F} \) and boiling point as \( 212^\circ \text{F} \) at standard pressure (Section 10.3).

questions.question_text: What happens to the boiling point of a liquid when external pressure decreases?
questions.explanation: Decreasing external pressure reduces the energy needed for molecules to escape into the vapor phase, lowering the boiling point, as seen in high-altitude cooking.

questions.question_text: A silver ring has an inner circumference of \( 31.4 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \). What temperature must it be heated to for the circumference to increase by \( 0.0597 \, \text{cm} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( L_0 = 31.4 \, \text{cm} \), \( \Delta L = 0.0597 \, \text{cm} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \), \( T_1 = 15^\circ \text{C} \). \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \Rightarrow 0.0597 = 31.4 \times 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \times \Delta T \). \( \Delta T = \frac{0.0597}{31.4 \times 1.9 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{0.0597}{5.966 \times 10^{-4}} \approx 100 \, \text{K} \). \( T_2 = 15 + 100 = 115^\circ \text{C} \).

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 11

questions.question_text: Which substance typically has the highest specific heat capacity among common materials?
questions.explanation: Water has the highest specific heat capacity (\( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \)) among common substances listed (Section 10.6, Table 10.3), making it an effective coolant.

questions.question_text: A gas at \( 37^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 3 \, \text{atm} \) occupies \( 6 \, \text{L} \). If it is cooled to \( -13^\circ \text{C} \) while the volume is reduced to \( 4 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?
questions.explanation: Given: \( T_1 = 37^\circ \text{C} = 310 \, \text{K} \), \( P_1 = 3 \, \text{atm} \), \( V_1 = 6 \, \text{L} \), \( T_2 = -13^\circ \text{C} = 260 \, \text{K} \), \( V_2 = 4 \, \text{L} \). Ideal gas law: \( \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \). \( P_2 = P_1 \times \frac{V_1}{V_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 3 \times \frac{6}{4} \times \frac{260}{310} \). \( P_2 = 3 \times 1.5 \times 0.8387 \approx 3.77 \, \text{atm} \).

questions.question_text: A gas at \( 1.5 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 47^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 8 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is raised to \( 97^\circ \text{C} \) and pressure adjusted to \( 2 \, \text{atm} \), what is the new volume?

A \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) lead block at \( 350^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.6 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of lead = \( 127.7 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A copper plate has an area of \( 0.8 \, \text{m}^2 \) at \( 60^\circ \text{C} \). What is the decrease in area when cooled to \( 10^\circ \text{C} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( A_0 = 0.8 \, \text{m}^2 \), \( \Delta T = 10 - 60 = -50^\circ \text{C} \), \( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta A = A_0 \times 2 \alpha_l \Delta T = 0.8 \times 2 \times 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \times (-50) \). \( \Delta A = 0.8 \times 3.4 \times 10^{-5} \times (-50) = -0.00136 \, \text{m}^2 \) (decrease of \( 0.00136 \, \text{m}^2 \)).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the coefficient of volume expansion compared to the coefficient of linear expansion?
questions.explanation: The coefficient of volume expansion (\( \alpha_v \)) is three times the coefficient of linear expansion (\( \alpha_l \)), as \( \alpha_v = 3 \alpha_l \) (Section 10.5).

questions.question_text: A steel cylinder has a volume of \( 1.5 \, \text{L} \) at \( 55^\circ \text{C} \). What temperature must it be heated to for the volume to increase by \( 0.0054 \, \text{L} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Given: \( V_0 = 1.5 \, \text{L} = 1500 \, \text{cm}^3 \), \( \Delta V = 0.0054 \, \text{L} = 5.4 \, \text{cm}^3 \), \( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \), \( T_1 = 55^\circ \text{C} \). \( \alpha_v = 3 \alpha_l = 3 \times 1.2 \times 10^{-5} = 3.6 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \). \( \Delta V = V_0 \alpha_v \Delta T \Rightarrow 5.4 = 1500 \times 3.6 \times 10^{-5} \times \Delta T \). \( \Delta T = \frac{5.4}{1500 \times 3.6 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{5.4}{0.054} = 100 \, \text{K} \). \( T_2 = 55 + 100 = 155^\circ \text{C} \).

questions.question_text: What is the Fahrenheit temperature equivalent to \( 75^\circ \text{C} \)?
What happens to the volume of an ideal gas if its pressure is doubled while the temperature remains constant?
questions.explanation: According to Boyle’s Law (Section 10.4), for an ideal gas at constant temperature, \( P V = \text{constant} \). If pressure doubles (\( P_2 = 2P_1 \)), then \( V_2 = V_1 / 2 \), so the volume halves.

questions.question_text: How much heat is required to convert \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -25^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 50^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

tests.title: Thermal Properties of Matter Chapter-Wise Test 12

questions.question_text: Which temperature scale is based on the absolute minimum temperature where molecular activity theoretically ceases?
questions.explanation: The Kelvin scale is defined with its zero point at absolute zero (\(-273.15^\circ \text{C}\)), the theoretical minimum temperature where molecular activity ceases, as per the ideal gas law and thermodynamic principles (Section 10.4).

questions.question_text: What determines the final temperature when two objects of different temperatures are mixed in a calorimeter?
questions.explanation: The final temperature is determined by the principle of conservation of energy, where heat lost by the hotter object equals heat gained by the colder one, reaching thermal equilibrium.

questions.question_text: What defines the triple point of a substance?
